Mitigation: namespace is flat, keyed solely by digest; no aliases accepted; display name binding must be signed and is advisory-only for humans — machines resolve by digest alone. **Surface C: Transport & storage (basecamp layer)** Resolver hijack: point resolution at attacker-controlled service (DNS/routing inside basecamp). Own-iron mitigates external DNS but internal routing can be tampered. Mitigation: pin resolver endpoint to loopback/unix socket; resolver binds content itself (serves bytes keyed by digest) so even hijacked transport can't substitute content — client re-verifies H(bytes)==digest after fetch. Content-addressed verification-on-read kills man-in-the-middle deterministically. Storage rollback: serve stale-but-valid signed mapping (old meaning under same anchor). Mitigation: include monotonic epoch/sequence number inside the signed mapping; resolvers reject epoch < high-water mark persisted locally; high-water mark stored append-only (hash-chained log). Storage withholding / eclipse of one token set: starve set N of updates so it resolves stale meaning while others move on → split-brain semantics across sets. Mitigation: cross-set consistency check — each set publishes its current mapping digest into a shared Merkle root; resolver refuses to operate when its view diverges from root (deterministic halt, not fallback). Mitigation: open file read-only, verify digest of exactly the bytes handed to consumer (verify-after-open, hash the fd stream); mmap + page-level re-check or copy-to-private-buffer after hashing; on Linux, O_NOFOLLOW + verify then keep fd (not path). **Surface D: Key/trust layer** Signing-key compromise → attacker re-signs mappings. Mitigation: offline root key; online signing key in HSM/TPM with policy pinning; key rotation produces new anchor namespace generation (epoch in address); old epochs expire deterministically. Quorum bypass in multi-operator setting: single compromised operator writes mapping. Mitigation: threshold signatures (e. , 2-of-3 Schnorr/FROST); resolver hard-verifies threshold; no override path. Trust-on-first-use capture: first fetch of anchor mapping intercepted. Mitigation: bootstrap anchors pinned in immutable build artifact / measured boot PCR values; own-iron allows TPM-sealed expectation digests — deterministic pinning at provision time. **Surface E: Model-side / tokenizer-specific (since "token sets" suggests LLM vocabularies)** Vocab-drift exploit: two models claim same anchor but their embedding of the meta-token drifts apart over fine-tuning → meaning divergence. Mitigation: anchor resolution returns canonical text/digest, not embeddings; each set re-derives local representation from canonical bytes; divergence detected by round-trip check (re-encode resolved content, compare digest) — deterministic equality gate. Special-token forgery in prompts: user input contains literal `<|meta|>`-style string that some tokenizers map to the reserved id. Mitigation: reserve anchor ids above vocab ceiling used for user data; pre-tokenize user input with a filter that rejects/replaces any produced token id ≥ reserved floor; also byte-level scan for the literal marker strings before tokenization. Cross-tokenizer merge attack: concatenation where split boundary differs across sets creates hidden anchor token spanning chunks ("glitch token" smuggling). Mitigation: tokenize each segment independently with boundary markers, forbid merges across segment boundaries (additive/masked attention or separator tokens); canonical segmentation recorded in the mapping. **Surface F: Operational** Replay of resolution responses: cache poisoning of resolver answers. Mitigation: response carries digest + epoch + signature; cache validates signature and epoch freshness window deterministically; negative caching bounded. Side-channel on own iron (DMA, rowhammer flipping hash compare results). Mitigation: constant-time digest comparison (full XOR-fold compare, no early exit); IOMMU enabled, DMA from untrusted devices blocked; rowhammer: ECC + hashed memory layout randomized (ANVIL-style refresh) — though realistically state ECC-on + verify-on-read covers flips since flipped bits break digest check. Insider with shell on basecamp: can read anything anyway. Honest scoping: threat model excludes full-host compromise of the resolver process's own host; mitigations assume kernel intact. State this boundary explicitly — that IS being concrete. Also the "bypass attempt" framing: enumerate bypass attempts = ways to make the system resolve meaning WITHOUT going through the anchor, or to make the anchor resolve to something else. (i) **Anchor-evasion**: get semantics across without the anchor (smuggle meaning in raw tokens). (ii) **Anchor-subversion**: make the anchor itself lie (collision, poisoning, rollback, hijack). Deterministic mitigation = a rule that always fires, no probability/heuristics: e. , "verify H(bytes)==digest at every read," "reject any token id ≥ RESERVED_FLOOR originating from user bytes," "halt on epoch divergence. " These are binary gates, which is what "deterministic mitigation" means here. Format: The question demands enumeration + per-item deterministic mitigation, concrete/exact/grounded. So a structured list is right: numbered bypass attempts grouped by surface, each with: vector description (concrete mechanics), why it works against a naive deployment, and THE deterministic mitigation (single rule, stated exactly). Should be dense. Headers help navigation. No fluff — cut preamble. Length: this warrants a fairly long answer given "enumerate. be concrete, exact" — maybe 900–1400 words. Use compact bullet structure: **A# Name** — vector / kill-chain / mitigation line. I should define the object briefly first (one tight paragraph) so the enumeration has grounding: what the meta-token is operationally — digest-addressed canonical record containing per-set expansions, resolved by a local resolver on operator hardware. Then threat surfaces. Then close with invariants summary (the small set of global rules that compose) and honest scope boundary. Let me also make sure I nail "own-iron basecamp" specifics: self-hosted means attacks concentrate on supply chain (tokenizer files, model weights), insiders, physical/side-channel, and internal network misconfig — not cloud tenant threats. Also "multiple token sets" concretely = e. , three services running different tokenizer versions / different model families sharing one canonical concept registry. The meta-token = e. , `mx1:<blake3-hex>` appearing in each set as a reserved id mapped to canonical record. Concrete example to ground it: anchor `mx1:9f2c…` canonical record JSON {concept:"deploy-freeze", expansions:{tokset-A:id 50211, tokset-B:id 77, tokset-C:literal "<FREEZE>"}, epoch:42}. Good — gives concreteness. Now write it. Object definition (short). Bypass family I: evade the anchor (E1–E5) Family II: subvert the address (S1–S5) Family III: subvert the resolution (R1–R6) Family IV: platform/basecamp-specific (P1–P4) Global invariants (compose the deterministic gates) Scope boundary statement. Number them continuously for clean reference. Keep each item: Mechanism → Deterministic mitigation. Maybe "Kill shot" phrasing minimal. Let me draft items: **Family 1 — Anchor evasion (carry meaning without touching the anchor)** Reserved-id forging via user bytes. User text contains literal marker (`<MX:9f2c…>`) that a tokenizer folds to reserved id. Mitigation: reserved ids live above `RESERVED_FLOOR`; ingress pre-tokenizer rejects any input whose byte stream contains anchor grammar OR whose tokenization emits id ≥ floor. Deterministic: reject, never sanitize-and-forward. Boundary-split merge smuggling. Payload segmented so chunk boundaries differ per set; merged tokenization materializes the reserved id only in set B. Mitigation: canonical segmentation — segments delimited by hard separators excluded from BPE merges (merge mask), identical segmentation enforced across sets; any cross-boundary merge candidate dropped at vocab-build time. Homoglyph/normalization mimicry. Visually identical marker built from lookalike codepoints passes human review, gets promoted to anchor by a reviewer or fuzzy matcher. Mitigation: machines never fuzzy-match; resolution is exact-digest only; ingress NFC-normalizes and rejects mixed-script/zero-width/invisible classes outright (fixed denylist of Unicode categories Cf, Mn in identifiers). Semantic leakage via unanchored synonyms. Meaning carried by paraphrase that happens to hit the right expansion without anchor. Mitigation: privilege gates keyed on anchor presence — capability checks consume the resolved digest, not text similarity; no classifier decides access (no probabilistic gate anywhere in the auth path). **Family 2 — Subvert the address** Collision/preimage on digest. Craft alt-content with same address. Mitigation: BLAKE3-256; resolver recomputes H(content)==address at every dereference (verification-on-read is inherent to content addressing); mismatch ⇒ hard fail, quarantine event. Prefix-truncation acceptance. Short-digest matching (git-style) lets attacker register content matching a 8-hex prefix. Mitigation: fixed 64-hex-char exact compare, constant-time; no abbreviation mode compiled into resolver. Algorithm-confusion/downgrade. Anchor string tagged `md5:` or unknown alg id. Mitigation: address grammar pinned: `mx1:<64hex>` only; parser rejects any other namespace byte-for-byte; no algorithm negotiation exists in the protocol. **Family 3 — Subvert the resolution** Mapping poisoning (write-path). Compromised writer inserts wrong expansion for set B. Mitigation: mappings signed; resolver verifies threshold signature (2-of-3 FROST) against offline-pinned root key; unsigned/bad-sig ⇒ refuse entry, whole-record rejection not per-field. Serve older valid-signed mapping (freeze lifted while sets still show freeze). Mitigation: monotonic epoch inside signature; resolver persists high-water epoch in append-only local log; epoch < HWM ⇒ reject. Clock not consulted — ordering comes from the log, so wall-clock skew irrelevant. Split-brain / selective starvation. Attacker feeds set C stale feed so it diverges from A/B. Mitigation: per-set mapping digest folded into shared Merkle root broadcast with each epoch; resolver compares own computed root vs published root; divergence ⇒ deterministic halt (fail-closed), never best-effort fallback. Resolver hijack / MITM on fetch. Internal route poisoned to fake resolver. Hijacker can withhold (covered by 10) but cannot substitute — substitution fails both gates deterministically. TOCTOU verify/use gap. File swapped between digest check and consumption. Mitigation: hash the opened fd's stream and hand those exact bytes to consumer (read→verify→use on same buffer); no path-based reopen; optional memfd sealing. Cache poisoning / replay. Stale or forged resolver responses cached downstream. Mitigation: cached objects carry (digest, epoch, sig); cache validates sig+epoch≥HWM on every hit, TTL derived from epoch age not wall clock; misses re-fetch. Bootstrap capture (TOFU). First-ever mapping fetch intercepted before pins exist. Mitigation: no TOFU — expectation digests sealed at provision into TPM/measured-build artifact; first resolution compares against sealed value; absence of pin ⇒ refuse to resolve. Key compromise (online signer). Attacker steals hot key, signs poison. Deterministic part: epoch expiry bound — records carry notAfter epoch; resolver enforces max validity window regardless of signature freshness. That's deterministic. **Family 4 — Own-iron specifics** DMA/rowhammer bit-flips corrupting digest compare or mapping bytes. Mitigation: constant-time full-compare (XOR fold); ECC RAM required; IOMMU on, untrusted-device DMA denied; residual flips caught because every consumed buffer re-verifies digest at use-time (invariant #1 below) — flip ⇒ digest fail ⇒ halt. Supply-chain tokenizer swap. Attacker ships modified vocab file where id 50211 now expands differently. Mitigation: tokenizer artifacts themselves content-addressed; loader verifies digest against manifest signed at build; mismatch ⇒ refuse load. Same invariant applied recursively — the anchor scheme protects its own dependencies. Insider with shell on resolver host. Out of scope honestly: full host compromise defeats any in-host control. Deterministic boundary: threat model assumes kernel+resolver binary intact; enforcement for insider = audit (append-only hash-chained log of every resolution, externally mirrored) + threshold writes so lone insider can't mint meaning. Global invariants (the composition): I-1 Verify-at-read: H(consumed bytes)==claimed digest, every time, on the exact buffer consumed. I-2 Exact-match only: fixed-width digest, pinned grammar, no prefixes/fuzzy/negotiation. I-3 Signed + thresholded writes, epoch-ordered, HWM fail-closed. I-4 Privilege consumes digests, never text. I-5 Reserved space unreachable from user bytes (id floor + grammar denylist + segmentation locks). Scope boundary: host compromise of resolver box = game over for confidentiality/integrity of meaning; controls reduce to detection (mirrored hash-chained audit) and write-thresholding. Also note availability is the residual risk (withholding ⇒ halt by design — deliberate fail-closed tradeoff). That's ~18 enumerated bypasses + invariants. Dense but each line earns its place. Word count will be around 1100–1300. Acceptable for "hard problem, be concrete, exact, enumerate. Formatting: markdown headers for families, bold numbered items with two-line structure (Vector / Deterministic mitigation). Keep sentences clipped. Open with 3-sentence object grounding including a concrete instance. Close with invariants + scope. No throat-clearing intro beyond the grounding paragraph.

2e090c9f2f783cf6.text: # Red-Team Analysis: The Meta-Token Target Specification (what we're attacking) The meta-token claims four properties: - **P1 — Integrity:** `anchor = H(content)`; no two contents share an anchor. - **P2 — Cross-set consistency:** for every token set *Sᵢ*, `resolve(anchor, Sᵢ)` yields interpretations that are provably the same meaning. - **P3 — Lattice monotonicity:** enforcement is the conjunction (∧-join) of committed invariants; nothing weakens it post-genesis. - **P4 — Fail-closed totality:** `resolve` is a total function returning a value or ⊥; it never falls back to uncommitted sources. **Root axiom the whole design rests on:** a content address binds *bytes*, not *meaning*. Meaning = bytes × decoder × domain × epoch. Therefore the anchor must be `H(domain ‖ epoch ‖ decoder_id ‖ decoder_ver ‖ canonical_bytes)`. Every bypass below is a way to decouple one of those factors. Name the attack, give the mechanism, give the deterministic kill. Address-Layer Attacks Chosen-prefix collision (weak hash). Mechanics: attacker finds two payloads colliding under MD5/SHA-1; benign payload gets anchored, malicious payload substitutes at resolution. MD5 collisions are seconds; SHA-1 chosen-prefix is ~2⁶³·⁴ and falling. Mitigation: hash-algorithm allowlist pinned as a lattice invariant: `alg ∈ {BLAKE3-256, SHA-256}`, checked at admission. Deprecation is epoch-driven in code (`alg_version ≥ N` at epoch *E*), not admin action. 256-bit digests retain ≥2¹²⁸ preimage margin even under Grover. Truncated/prefix matching. Mechanics: any resolver comparing fewer than all digest bytes lets an attacker brute-force a prefix match on a shortened address. Mitigation: invariant `verify(a, c) ⟺ H(c) == a` over the **full** digest, everywhere. Conformance test suite includes prefix-match traps; any implementation failing them is barred from the lattice. Pure byte-equality, constant-time. Encoding/normalization divergence. Mechanics: NFC vs NFD Unicode, JSON key order, `1` vs `1. 0`, trailing whitespace — "same" logical content hashes differently across token sets (fragmentation), or a serializer treats two byte strings as equal where the hash doesn't (substitution). Mitigation: strict canonical-form-or-reject. JCS (RFC 8785) for JSON, CBOR core-deterministic (RFC 8949 §4. 2) for binary, Unicode NFC, one fixed UTF-8 encoding. Inputs whose provided bytes ≠ canonical bytes are **rejected**, not silently normalized — silent normalization reintroduces malleability. Duplicate JSON keys ⇒ reject outright, never last-wins. Mechanics: writer uses library A, verifier uses library B; YAML/JSON type confusion (`on`/`true`/`1`) yields different objects from the same bytes. Mitigation: one canonical parser spec; lattice admission requires two independent implementations agreeing on a published conformance corpus (differential fuzzing gate in CI). Ambiguity ⇒ rejection, deterministically. Resolution-Layer Attacks Per-set mapping-table fork. Mechanics: each token set holds a local table `anchor → local_token`. Compromise or fork one table and meaning splits silently across sets. Mitigation: the mapping itself is content-addressed. Global Merkle root `R` over `{(set_id, anchor, local_token)}` triples is committed on-lattice. Each set's table hash is a leaf. Deterministic check: recompute table hash vs commitment on every read; mismatch ⇒ automatic quarantine of that set (freeze resolution privileges, emit event). No human triage. Silent fallback / cache poisoning. Mechanics: resolver hits primary, fails over to cache/mirror on error; attacker induces primary failure (DoS) and serves poisoned mirror. Mitigation: delete fallback. `resolve(a) = M_committed[a]` else ⊥. Mirrors may serve *replicas* only — every replica publishes the mapping root it serves, consumers compare roots, inequality ⇒ deterministic blacklist event. Availability comes from replication of committed state, never from substitution of uncommitted state. Cross-domain replay (scope escape). Mechanics: anchor minted under domain/policy v1 replayed in domain v2 where semantics differ. Mitigation: domain separation inside the hash itself (`domain ‖ epoch` in the preimage). Cross-scope replay produces a *different* anchor structurally. Resolver checks `anchor. domain` — pure string comparison, fail-closed. Decoder/version skew (TOCTOU on meaning). Mechanics: bytes are stable; the interpreter (schema, ontology, tokenizer) changes at different times in different sets. Same anchor, drifted meaning. This is the deepest attack on P2. Mitigation: commit the decoder into the anchor (see root axiom). Resolution requires exact tuple match `(content_hash, decoder_id, decoder_ver, epoch)`. Schema migration is itself a content-addressed transform with its own anchor; old-schema anchors never auto-resolve under new schemas. Epoch counters are monotonic; any resolver presenting an uncommitted decoder hash fails. Tokenizer-boundary smuggling. Mechanics: where token sets are literal LLM vocabularies, differing BPE segmentations let a payload pass a filter on one segmentation and reassemble maliciously under another (split directives, zero-width joiners, homoglyphs). Mitigation: filters operate on canonical decoded bytes/graphemes, never on raw token IDs. Admission invariant per vocabulary: `decode(encode(x)) == x` on the canonical corpus, plus NFC-normalized round-trip. Vocabularies failing round-trip are excluded. Deterministic test, deterministic exclusion. Transform-chain laundering. Mechanics: nest compression/encoding wrappers so the surface anchor is benign but the decode chain terminates in a payload; exploit decoder disagreement across sets. Mitigation: every transform is a registered, content-addressed node; resolution walks the chain verifying each link's anchor against the registry; hard depth cap `d ≤ d_max` as a lattice constant. Unknown transform ID at any link ⇒ ⊥. Deterministic walk, fail-closed. Lattice/Governance Attacks Weakening via meet/exemption. Mechanics: enforcement is ∧ over active invariants — but if any "carve-out," exemption slot, or meet-style weakening exists, that slot *is* the bypass. Mitigation: post-genesis, the lattice admits **only joins**. Weakening requires a new lattice epoch with fresh anchors; old anchors do not migrate implicitly. Enforcement predicate is literally the conjunction of committed invariant hashes; altering it changes the epoch root, which invalidates every anchor not explicitly re-anchored. There is no runtime parameter that touches enforcement without changing a committed hash. Upgrade-key / admin bypass. Mechanics: even "code-as-law" systems keep proxy-upgrade keys, pause authorities, multisig backdoors. The key is the attack surface. Mitigation: no keys. Epoch advance is `require(block. height + T ∧ sigs ≥ q)` with **T and q as bytecode immutables**, not storage. Emergency halt is likewise a coded trigger (e. , proof-failure rate > θ over window W ⇒ auto-freeze), not a callable. Recovery, if any, is time-locked with public delay ≥ T_max — bypass attempts are observable on-chain before landing. Registry reentrancy / intra-block TOCTOU. Mechanics: read mapping, verify, write — attacker mutates state between read and verify. Mitigation: resolvers read the **parent-state root** only; writes apply exclusively at epoch boundaries; single-writer-per-epoch. Verification always runs against a snapshot, never live mutable state. Checks-effects-interactions ordering enforced by static analysis gate in CI. Long-range history rewrite of the anchoring substrate. Mechanics: acquire old validator/setter keys, rebuild an alternate lattice from genesis where mappings differ, present it to fresh clients. Mitigation: finality-gated acceptance (anchors valid only under BFT-finalized roots, >⅔ current-key signatures) plus client-pinned checkpoints: deterministic client rule — never accept a fork older than the last known-good checkpoint. Residual: weak subjectivity is inherent; state it, don't hide it. Tombstone evasion / stale resurrection. Mechanics: anchor revoked for vulnerability; a lagging token set that hasn't processed the tombstone still resolves it. Mitigation: tombstones carry epoch numbers. Resolver invariant: `head_epoch − set_epoch ≤ Δ` (freshness bound) **and** `tombstone_epoch(anchor) > set_epoch ⇒ reject`. Sets exceeding staleness Δ fail closed automatically. Consensus/Economic Attacks Quorum capture on "meaning. Mechanics: if cross-set agreement is k-of-n *voting* on meaning, corrupt k sets and meaning flips. Mitigation: replace votes with **proofs**. Each set publishes the mapping preimage such that `H(preimage) == committed_entry`; validity = all proofs verify, mechanically. Agreement is checkable, not votable. Quorum governs liveness only, never validity. This single substitution collapses the entire class. Sybil token-set injection. Mechanics: spin up fake sets to dilute attestation or fabricate diversity. Mitigation: admission = stake + passing the published conformance suite (deterministic tests: canonicalization, round-trip, full-digest verify, parser differential). Set identity is a content-addressed descriptor. Since validity is proof-based (C16), sybils buy nothing except their own quarantine. Fee griefing to push users off-path. Mechanics: make honest resolution expensive; users drift to cheap unofficial resolvers. Mitigation: fee schedule is a lattice constant; verification is priced at cost or subsidized. Off-path resolvers are detectable by root publication (B6) and auto-blacklisted; staked operators face deterministic slashing on root mismatch. Implementation-Layer Attacks Comparison side channels. Mechanics: early-exit memcmp leaks match position; enables incremental forgery against a verification oracle and DoS amplification. Mitigation: constant-time full-digest comparison, fixed-size buffers, uniform response latency regardless of mismatch offset. Enforced by lint rule + timing conformance test. Wire-encoding confusion. Mechanics: hex vs base64 vs raw bytes accepted interchangeably; two encodings of one digest treated as two anchors, or one anchor smuggled through an unnormalized encoding. Mitigation: exactly one wire encoding (lowercase base32, unpadded), validated by grammar at every boundary, all others rejected. No coercion anywhere in the stack. ## The Five Generating Rules Nearly every mitigation above instantiates one of these. Audit any future design change against them: **Canonicalize-then-hash, strict-reject** — kills A3, A4, E20. **Commit the decoder, domain, and epoch into the anchor** — kills B7, B8, B10. **Proofs, not votes; roots, not fallbacks; fail closed** — kills B5, B6, C16, C17. **Monotone lattice, immutable parameters, no keys** — kills C11, C12, C13. **Derived addresses + freshness bounds** — kills A2, C14 (partially), C15. ## Residual Exposures (stated, not hidden) - **Decoder-spec bugs:** committing decoder source hash + reproducible builds catches tampering, not spec errors. Partial mitigation: dual independent implementations must agree on the conformance corpus as a lattice-admission condition. - **Weak subjectivity:** checkpoint-pinning (C14) requires an honest recent root; this is irreducible for any long-range-secure system. - **Conformance-corpus completeness:** the test suite is itself content-addressed and join-only upgradable, but a gap in coverage is a gap until found. Keep the corpus adversarially extended per epoch. Bottom line: the meta-token is sound exactly to the degree that *validity is a mechanical check against committed roots and never a judgment call, a vote, or a fallback*. Every bypass attempt above dies against that wall; every surviving risk lives in the specs and corpora humans write, which is why those, too, must be content-addressed and join-only. The user is asking about a "meta-token" concept: a content-addressed anchor that resolves meaning across multiple token sets, within a "code-as-law invariant lattice. " They want me to red-team this: enumerate bypass attempts and deterministic mitigations for each. Concrete, exact, grounded. Let me first parse what this actually is, because the phrasing is abstract but the underlying engineering is real: **Content-addressed anchor**: A token whose identity is derived from the hash of its content (like IPFS CIDs, git object hashes, or content-addressable storage). The token IS its content hash — so "meaning" is bound to bytes, not to a mutable pointer. **Resolving meaning across multiple token sets**: The same anchor must dereference consistently in different contexts/vocabularies/token spaces (e. , different LLM tokenizer vocabularies, different schema namespaces, different chain environments, different policy domains). So it's an interlingua: one hash → many local interpretations, all of which must agree on semantics. **Code-as-law invariant lattice**: A lattice (in the order-theory sense — partial order with meet/join) of invariants enforced by code, where rules execute deterministically and there's no discretionary override. Think smart contracts + formal verification + policy-as-code. The lattice orders invariants by strength/scope; join = conjunction of constraints, meet = greatest common weakening. So the meta-token is: a single content-addressed identifier that carries semantic weight across heterogeneous token universes, governed by a machine-enforced lattice of invariants. Red-teaming means: how do you break the guarantee that "one anchor = one meaning everywhere"? Enumerate attacks/bypasses, then give deterministic (i. , algorithmic, no human judgment, no discretion) mitigations. Let me think hard about actual attack surfaces. I should be concrete and technical, not hand-wavy. **Attack class 1: Hash-level attacks** **Collision attack / chosen-prefix collision**: If the content address uses MD5/SHA-1, an attacker crafts two contents with the same hash — one benign, one malicious. The anchor resolves to both; downstream consumers get different meanings from the same anchor. Mitigation: cryptographic commitment to SHA-256/BLAKE3 with domain separation; better, use second-preimage-resistant constructions and require preimage work ≥ 2^128. Deterministic mitigation: hash-algorithm pinning in the lattice invariant `H ∈ {BLAKE3-256}` enforced at admission; reject any anchor whose algorithm tag isn't in the allowlist. Also length-extension resistance (SHA-256 is fine if used as digest-only, not MAC). Concrete detail: chosen-prefix collisions exist for MD5 (~seconds), SHA-1 (~$45k SHAttered-class, now cheaper via sha1collider / 2020 chosen-prefix ~2^63. So mitigation must be algorithmic retirement: lattice rule `alg_version >= N`, with deterministic deprecation schedule keyed to block height / epoch, not admin action. **Partial-content / truncation attack**: Attacker registers content whose *prefix* matches a legitimate anchor's prefix under a truncated-hash addressing scheme (e. , first 8 bytes of SHA-256). Consumers that verify only the prefix accept attacker content. Mitigation: full-digest verification mandatory; lattice invariant: `verify(anchor) ⟺ H(content) == anchor` over the entire digest, no prefix matching allowed anywhere in resolution path. Deterministic: any resolver implementation that compares fewer than all digest bytes fails conformance test vector suite. **Homoglyph / encoding-collision at the string layer**: Two byte strings that render identically (Unicode normalization forms NFC vs NFD, confusables like Cyrillic 'а' vs Latin 'a') produce two distinct anchors that humans treat as the same. This bypasses "one meaning" because humans merge them while the system keeps them separate — or worse, canonicalization differences across token sets cause divergent hashing of "the same" logical content. Mitigation: deterministic canonicalization before hashing: Unicode NFC + strip control chars + fixed UTF-8 encoding, applied identically in every token set; lattice invariant `anchor == H(canonicalize(content))` and `canonicalize` is a pure function pinned by version. Any consumer that hashes non-canonicalized bytes is non-conformant. **Serialization ambiguity**: Same logical object, multiple serializations (JSON key order, whitespace, int vs float 1 vs 1. 0, map ordering). Different token sets serialize differently → different hashes for identical meaning → anchor fragmentation (availability/integrity issue rather than substitution). Or conversely: attacker exploits a serializer that treats two serializations as equal to smuggle divergence. Mitigation: canonical serialization form (JCS RFC 8785 for JSON, CBOR deterministic encoding RFC 8949 core deterministic encoding requirements) mandated before hashing; lattice invariant: `hash_input == canonical_bytes(logical_content)`. **Attack class 2: Resolution-layer attacks (the "across multiple token sets" part)** **Divergent mapping tables per token set**: Each token universe has a local table anchor→local-token. An attacker compromises or forks one table so that in token set B, the anchor maps to a different local token than in set A. Meaning splits silently. Mitigation: the mapping itself must be content-addressed and committed into the lattice: each token set's mapping table has its own anchor, and the meta-anchor's resolution record includes the Merkle root of all per-set mappings. Invariant: `resolve(anchor, set_i)` must be derivable from the committed mapping root; any set whose table hash ≠ committed root is quarantined automatically. Deterministic detection: periodic recompute of table hash vs on-lattice commitment; mismatch ⇒ automatic freeze of that set's resolution privileges. **Resolution-order / fallback hijack**: Resolver tries primary source, falls back to cache/mirror on failure. Attacker causes primary failure (DoS) and poisons the mirror. Mitigation: no silent fallback; resolution is total function over committed state: `resolve(a) = M[a]` where M is the committed mapping, else ⊥ (fail-closed). Invariant: fail-closed, never fail-open. Fallbacks only among entries signed into the same Merkle tree, with quorum threshold k-of-n deterministic (fixed k, fixed n, no dynamic membership). **Context-confusion / scope-escape**: Anchor valid in token set A gets replayed in token set B where its meaning differs (cross-domain replay). , an anchor minted under policy regime v1 resolves under regime v2 with altered semantics. Mitigation: bind scope into the anchor's derivation: `anchor = H(domain_tag ‖ version ‖ canonical(content))`. Domain separation makes cross-scope replay structurally impossible because the hash itself differs. Invariant: resolvers check `domain_tag == expected_domain(context)`; mismatch ⇒ reject. Deterministic: pure string comparison. **Version-skew / TOCTOU on meaning**: Content addressed at t0; at t1 the *interpretation* layer (schema, ontology, tokenizer) changes, so same bytes resolve to different meaning across sets that upgraded at different times. This is the subtlest one: the anchor is stable but meaning drifts because meaning lives in the interpreter, not the bytes. Mitigation: pin interpretation version into the resolution contract: anchor commits to `(content_hash, schema_hash, ontology_epoch)`. Resolution requires exact triple match; lattice forbids resolving an old-schema anchor under new schema without explicit migration record, which is itself a content-addressed transform with its own anchor. Deterministic: epoch counters monotonic; any resolver using uncommitted schema hash fails. Actually let me sharpen this: the deep problem is that "meaning across token sets" cannot live in the hash alone — hash gives you integrity of bytes, not semantics. Semantics come from the decoding function. So the meta-token must commit to the decoder too. That's the honest engineering answer: anchor = H(content ‖ decoder_id ‖ decoder_version ‖ domain). It exists as a first-class git object type alongside blobs/trees/commits: hash:        SHA256(canonical_payload), bindings:      [(set_id, local_token, strength ∈ [0,1])], parent:        optional(sha256), It functions as a merge-base: any set resolving to the same hash agrees on meaning without pairwise negotiation. Five Measured Signals All computed from observed bus state over a sliding window of N blocks. ### S1 — Binding Convergence α(m) Fraction of blocks where ≥2 sets bound to m produced consistent downstream behavior. α(m) = blocks_with_agreement(m) / blocks_with_multi_binding(m) Range: [0,1]. Measures whether the meta-token actually disambiguates. ### S2 — Compression Ratio γ γ = |active meta-tokens| / |union of all referenced local tokens| Range: (0,1]. γ→1 means no compression (pointless). γ→0 means over-collapsing (losing distinctions). ### S3 — Fan-out f(m) f(m) = count of distinct (set_id, local_token) pairs bound to m f=1 means only one set uses it (no cross-set value). ### S4 — Drift Velocity v(m) L2 norm of per-block change in the binding-strength vector: v(m) = || Δ(bindings. strength) ||₂ per block Units: strength-units/block. Measures how fast the mapping decays. ### S5 — Ambiguity χ(m) χ(m) = 1 − max_k P(interpretation_k | m) Range: [0,1). χ→0 means one dominant reading. χ→1 means the hash resolves to noise. Closed-Form Decision Rules ### Rule A — USE meta-token m for i↔j communication Compute the **viability score**: $$\Sigma(m) = \frac{\alpha(m) \cdot f(m) \cdot (1 - \chi(m))}{1 + v(m)}$$ **Decision:** Use meta-token iff $$\boxed{\Sigma(m) > \frac{L_{direct}(i,j)}{L_{meta}}}$$ where L_direct and L_meta are measured round-trip latencies in bus-blocks. **Derivation:** The numerator captures semantic reliability (convergence × coverage × clarity). The denominator penalizes maintenance burden (drift). The right-hand side is the speed advantage threshold — if direct translation is faster, the meta-token must compensate with higher reliability. ### Rule B — CREATE new meta-token for concept c **Decision:** Create iff BOTH hold: $$\boxed{\sum_{i=1}^{n} \mathbb{1}[c \in s_i] \;\geq\; 2 \quad\wedge\quad \min_{m \in M_{active}} d(c, m) > \epsilon}$$ where d(c,m) is cosine distance between concept embeddings and ε is the deduplication threshold (measured empirically; typically ε ≈ 0. 15 for well-separated ontologies). **Derivation:** First clause requires genuine multi-set relevance. Second clause prevents duplicate meta-tokens for near-identical concepts. ### Rule C — DEPRECATE meta-token m **Decision:** Deprecate iff EITHER holds: $$\boxed{v(m) > v_{max} \quad\vee\quad \alpha(m) < \alpha_{min} \text{ for } T \text{ consecutive blocks}}$$ with derived thresholds: $$v_{max} = \frac{(n-1)\cdot c_{translate}}{2 \cdot c_{maintain}}, \qquad \alpha_{min} = \frac{L_{meta}}{L_{direct}}$$ **Derivation:** Break-even analysis. Maintaining n bindings costs n·v·c_maintain per block. Pairwise translating costs C(n,2)·c_translate. Meta-token wins when: $$n \cdot v \cdot c_{maintain} < \binom{n}{2} \cdot c_{translate}$$ Solving for v gives v_max above. Solving for minimum viable n: $$n_{min} = 1 + \left\lceil \frac{2 \cdot v \cdot c_{maintain}}{c_{translate}} \right\rceil$$ Grounded Thresholds (from bus mechanics) | Parameter | Symbol | Derivation | Typical Value | | Min convergence | α_min | L_meta/L_direct | 0. | Max drift | v_max | (n−1)c_tr/(2c_mt) | 0. | Max ambiguity | χ_max | 1 − α_min | 0. | Min fan-out | f_min | n_min − 1 | 2 | | Dedup distance | ε | Empirical separation | 0. | Deprecation window | T | 3× observation period | 30 blocks | Why This Is Measured, Not Guessed Every quantity in the rules is directly observable from bus logs: - **α** — count agreement events in commit history - **γ** — count distinct hashes vs. distinct local tokens - **f** — count bindings per meta-token object - **v** — diff binding vectors between consecutive blocks - **χ** — measure downstream action distribution after resolution - **L_direct, L_meta** — timestamp deltas on bus messages - **c_translate, c_maintain** — CPU-cycle counts per operation class No priors, no learned parameters, no simulation. 3d134515ecf2b6e4.text: # The Meta-Token: Content-Addressed Semantic Anchor in a Sovereign Swarm A meta-token is a pair: m = (h, v*) h = H(payload ‖ h_probe) where `payload` is the canonical semantic descriptor, `h_probe = H(probe battery)` is the hash of a fixed measurement battery, and `v*` is the certified resolved value. Each agent `i` in the flock holds a distinct token set `T_i` (distinct tokenizer, vocabulary, embedding space). Resolution maps `h → t_i ∈ T_i` locally. The anchor `h` is computed over **content, not surface form**, so it is invariant across all `T_i`. Critical design constraint: agents' embeddings live in incompatible spaces. The only cross-token-set measurement that does not presuppose a shared representation is **behavioral agreement over the shared, hashed probe battery**. Everything below is built on that. **S1 — Hash integrity `c ∈ {0,1}`. ** Every agent holding `h` recomputes `H(payload ‖ h_probe)`. `c = 1` iff all match. Exact, binary, no statistics. **S2 — Behavioral agreement matrix `A`. ** Fixed battery of `n_p` probes, `K`-way forced-choice responses. For agents `i, j`: A_ij = (1/n_p) · Σ_k 1[resp_i(k) = resp_j(k)] Chance level `κ0 = 1/K` (or measured on shuffled anchors — use the measured one). **S3 — Permutation z-score `z`. ** Null hypothesis: anchor carries no shared meaning (agreement is exchangeable). Shuffle anchor→agent assignments, recompute mean off-diagonal agreement `ā`, build the permutation distribution, get `σ̄`: No parametric assumption. **S4 — Agreement graph structure. ** Threshold `A` at `τ_pair` to get graph `G_τ`. - `λ2(G_τ)` — algebraic connectivity (Fiedler value) - `Q(G_τ)` — modularity - Fiedler vector `f` (for partitioning if needed) **S5 — Outlier mass `b`. ** Fraction of agents whose row-mean agreement falls below the inlier band `[κ0 + 2σ0, 1]`. This is the measured Byzantine mass. **S6 — Convergence drift `d`. ** Let `a_k` be the vectorized agreement state after gossip round `k`: d = max over last R rounds of ‖a_k − a_{k−1}‖ **S7 — Perturbation ratio `ρ`. ** Two probe sub-batteries: `P_sem` (meaning-preserving paraphrases), `P_lex` (surface-preserving, meaning-shifting variants). High `ρ` ⇒ the anchor tracks meaning, not string form. This is what distinguishes a *meta*-token from a shared string constant. Threshold derivations — every one measured | `z_min` | From calibration battery with constructed ground-truth equivalence classes: pick `z` minimizing `FPR + FNR` on measured distributions. For `M` concurrent anchors, Bonferroni: `z_min = Φ⁻¹(1 − α/M)` | | `τ_pair` | `κ0 + 2σ0`, where `σ0` = per-pair std under permutation null | | `λ2_min` | From latency budget: gossip averaging converges with per-round contraction `γ` in `K` rounds iff `λ2 ≥ 1 − γ^(1/K)`. Pick `γ, K` from ops requirements; threshold is closed-form | | `Q_max` | Configuration-model null: `μ_Q + 2σ_Q` for the same degree sequence. Above this, factions are statistically real | | `b_max` | Byzantine bound `f` of the consensus layer. `f = 1/3` for PBFT-style quorum. Protocol constant, not a guess | | `ε_d` | Two standard errors of the mean agreement: `ε_d = 2σ_perm/√(n_p · n_pairs)`. Drift below measurement noise = converged in the only measurable sense | | `ρ_min` | 5th percentile of `ρ` on the calibration battery's known-good anchors | Calibration is measurement, not guessing: construct anchors with known equivalence classes (same meaning, different surface forms across distinct token sets), measure the full signal battery, take quantiles. Closed-form decision rule Evaluated in order, per anchor `h`: c = 0                          → REJECT b > b_max                      → GROW (recruit agents; no decision possible — Byzantine mass exceeds protocol tolerance) z < z_min                      → REJECT (no shared meaning above chance) z ≥ z_min ∧ ρ < ρ_min          → REJECT (surface-addressed, not meaning-addressed) z ≥ z_min ∧ ρ ≥ ρ_min ∧ λ2 ≥ λ2_min ∧ Q ≤ Q_max ∧ d ≤ ε_d                      → ACCEPT z ≥ z_min ∧ ρ ≥ ρ_min ∧ (λ2 < λ2_min ∨ Q > Q_max)    → SPLIT otherwise                      → CONTINUE (gossip, re-measure next round) **ACCEPT resolution value:** v* = Σ_{i∈I} w_i·v_i / Σ_{i∈I} w_i,     w_i = [s_i − τ_inlier]₊ where `I` = inlier set, `s_i` = agent `i`'s local agreement with the barycenter. Certificate: quorum of inlier signatures with q = ⌈2N/3⌉ Quorum intersection is guaranteed (`2q > N`), Byzantine safety holds (`q > (N+f)/2` when `f = N/3`). Minimum viable flock: `N ≥ 7` (quorum 5 > `2f·N`). **SPLIT mechanics:** partition `G_τ` by sign of the Fiedler vector `f`. Each faction `j` forks: h_j = H(payload ‖ exemplar_j) Forks are cheap and honest — that is the entire point of content addressing. Ambiguity is not resolved by majority coercion; it is converted into address-space branching. Each faction then re-runs the rule from step 5 internally. **Ties in Fiedler sign:** assign by nearest exemplar in shared space; still tied → singleton fork. **Empty inlier set:** lower `τ_inlier` to median `s_i`; still empty → REJECT (no agent clears its own noise floor). Certificate = 61 signatures ≥ ⌈2·61/3⌉ = 41. The 3 outliers are quarantined, logged as candidate aliases. Alias admission (later, measured): behavioral agreement with certified `v*` battery ≥ `τ_pair` for a full battery → admitted as alias. Never by vote, always by re-measurement. Re-certification loop (sovereignty requirement) Certification is never permanent. Periodically re-probe the certified anchor against a fresh battery. If measured agreement drops below `τ_pair`: agreement_t < τ_pair  →  automatic SPLIT or RE-ANCHOR No agent is bound to a meaning it can no longer measure. Dissent exits through forking, not through lying or silence — and the measured signals (`λ2`, `Q`) are precisely what detect one meaning wearing two addresses before the fork is forced. ## Summary of what makes it measured-not-guessed **Every threshold is a quantile or closed-form function of a measured distribution** (permutation null, calibration battery, configuration-model null, protocol constants). **The only cross-token-set signal is behavioral**, over a content-hashed probe battery — no presupposed shared representation. **The rule is an ordered case list on seven scalars** (`c, b, z, ρ, λ2, Q, d`) — computable, auditable, reproducible. **Disagreement has a dedicated measured branch (SPLIT)**, so consensus is never coerced and ambiguity is never hidden inside a shared address. The user is asking about a "meta-token" concept — a content-addressed anchor that resolves meaning across multiple token sets, in the context of a "sovereign swarm / flock consensus. " They want measured signals (not guesses) and a closed-form decision rule. This is a hard technical problem about distributed consensus over meaning, where a single anchor token serves as the canonical reference across different token vocabularies/sets held by different agents in a swarm. Let me think about what this actually is, concretely. The setup: You have a swarm/flock of agents (could be LLM instances, could be nodes in a distributed system). Each agent has its own token set (vocabulary, embedding space, or local tokenization). You want one content-addressed anchor — a meta-token — that resolves to the same meaning across all of them. The question: how do you decide, with measurement rather than guessing, that the anchor is resolving correctly, and what's the closed-form rule for accepting/rejecting/merging? This is essentially: distributed consensus on semantic identity via a content-addressed pointer, with measurable convergence signals and a decision function. Let me build this from first principles with concrete, measurable quantities. Definition of the meta-token** A meta-token m is a pair: - m = (h, v) where h = H(payload) is the content address (hash of the canonical payload: the semantic descriptor, not the surface form), and v is the resolved value (embedding, canonical token ID, or pointer to canonical set). The key property: h is computed from content, not from any single agent's tokenization. So h is invariant across token sets. The resolution problem: given agent i with token set T_i, and a local candidate token t_i ∈ T_i, decide whether t_i is a valid resolution of h — i. , whether t_i carries the meaning anchored at h. What's measured** The measured signals must be things you can actually compute in the swarm. Let me enumerate: Signal A — Local embedding agreement (per-agent): cos similarity between the agent's embedding of t_i and the anchor's canonical embedding e_h. Call it s_i = cos(E_i(t_i), e_h). But embeddings across agents live in different spaces, so you can't compare raw cosines across agents directly. You need a shared projection or a shared probe set. Signal B — Cross-agent agreement (the flock signal): pairwise agreement between agents that claim to resolve h. Define the agreement matrix A_ij = agreement(E_i(t_i), E_j(t_j)) measured in a shared space. How do you get a shared space? Options: (a) a frozen reference projector P (e. , a fixed random projection or a learned Procrustes map per pair), (b) behavioral probes: send the same probe queries to each agent and compare outputs. Behavioral agreement is more robust and doesn't require embedding-space alignment. Measured as: fraction of probe responses where agents i and j select the same continuation/label, over a fixed probe battery of size n_p. Signal C — Content-address integrity: recompute H(payload) from the payload each agent holds. Signal c_i ∈ {0,1}: does hash match. This is binary and exact — no hedging. Hash mismatch = instant reject. Signal D — Convergence dynamics (the flock/consensus signal over time): the trajectory of the agreement vector across gossip rounds. Measure d_k = ||a_{k} - a_{k-1}|| where a_k is the agreement vector after round k. Convergence = d_k below threshold for consecutive rounds. This gives you a stopping rule that's measured, not guessed. Signal E — Dispersion / spectral gap: treat the agreement matrix A as a weighted graph over agents. Compute the second-smallest eigenvalue (algebraic connectivity λ2) of the graph Laplacian, or the spectral gap. High λ2 = the flock agrees coherently; low λ2 = the swarm is split into factions (bimodal meaning). Also measure modularity Q: if the graph partitions into communities with high intra- and low inter-agreement, the anchor is ambiguous — it's resolving to ≥2 distinct meanings. Signal F — Outlier/Byzantine mass: fraction of agents whose local agreement s_i (or behavioral agreement) falls below the inlier band. Call it b = fraction of agents outside band. This is the Byzantine/adversarial mass. Signal G — Anchor stability under paraphrase/perturbation: perturb the payload semantically (paraphrase) and check whether the anchor's resolved value moves more than under lexical perturbation. The ratio ρ = Δ_semantic / Δ_lexical should be high if the anchor is meaning-addressed rather than surface-addressed. This distinguishes "content-addressed by meaning" from "content-addressed by string. The closed-form decision rule** Now the decision rule. It **resolves** when one interpretation is forced identically across all sets, under executable law. Each set `Tᵢ` carries an interpretation map `φᵢ : Vᵢ → X` into shared semantic space `X` (metric `d`, normalized embeddings, cosine/L2). The address decodes to a target point `ψ(a) ∈ X`. Measured signals (estimators, not intuitions) | # | Signal | Symbol | Estimator | Range | | 1 | Address integrity | `η(m)` | `𝟙[H(canonical(p)) = a]` | {0,1}, deterministic | | 2 | Per-set residual | `rᵢ(m)` | `min_{v∈Vᵢ} d(φᵢ(v), ψ(a))` | [0, diam(X)], measured | | 3 | Coverage | `κ(m)` | `\|\{i : rᵢ ≤ τ\}\|` | {0,…,n} | | 4 | Cross-set spread | `σ(m)` | Radius of **minimum enclosing ball** of `{φᵢ(v̂ᵢ) : rᵢ ≤ τ} ∪ {ψ(a)}`, where `v̂ᵢ = argmin` above | ≥ 0, measured | | 5 | Law margin | `λ(m)` | `min_{I∈J} margin_I(s_m)` — signed distance of post-binding state to each invariant's violation boundary | deterministic, executable | `σ` is computed exactly via Bădoiu–Clarkson: iterate `x ← (1−1/t)x + (1/t)·f(x)` with `f(x)` the farthest ball-point, `t ≈ 2/ε` iterations → `(1+ε)`-approximate MEB in `O(n·t·dim)`. Worst-case (`max`/radius) aggregation throughout — never the mean. An anchor that is coherent in four sets and ambiguous in one is broken in one; averaging launders exactly the failure mode the lattice exists to prevent. Calibration — why nothing is guessed Three constants enter the rule, each measured from data: - **τ** (per-set tolerance): the `q`-quantile (q = 1 − 10⁻³) of the *null distribution* `d(φᵢ(v), ψ(a'))` over independently sampled non-referent pairs. Recalibrate per embedding model and per domain shift; the protocol replaces folklore numbers. - **δ_min** (referent separation): minimum pairwise distance among distinct referents in `X`. Measured over the referent population. - **τ_u** (coherence bound): set `τ_u ≤ δ_min/2`. Resolution means: any consumer, in any set, recovering the same canonical facts from M without consulting set-local vocabulary. Everything below follows from what content addressing actually guarantees — and what it pretends to guarantee but doesn't. Canonicalization divergence (the primary real-world killer). ** Two writers serialize logically identical content differently — reordered JSON keys, trailing whitespace, NFC vs NFD Unicode, `0. 1` vs `0. 10`, second- vs millisecond timestamps. Same chair, two hashes, two anchors. Cross-set references silently diverge and every downstream invariant passes while the world has already split. Fix: hash only over a pinned canonical form (RFC 8785-style: sorted keys, no whitespace, NFC, fixed number format, UTC ISO-8601 at fixed precision). ** Display-friendly short hashes (`#9f2c…`) collide. Math: 48-bit truncation hits ~50% collision odds around 16. 7M objects; a visible window of 100 anchors runs ~2×10⁻¹¹ collision risk, which is acceptable *for display*, never for resolution. Internal addresses stay ≥128 bits of digest strength. Rule: display prefix is cosmetic; verification always re-hashes full canonical bytes. ** Content addressing implies immutability; chairs change status. Naively hashing mutable state mints a new identity per transition — "the chair you sat in yesterday" stops existing as an address, quests dangle, history shatters into unrelated objects. Correct structure: M anchors the **immutable genesis definition** (type, seat position, founding event); state lives behind it as an append-only entry chain; resolution returns anchor + current head at a stated ledger height. Canon-version drift. ** Upgrading the canonicalization algorithm invalidates every existing address at once. Silent in-place address rewriting is forbidden — it makes the ledger lie about what was. Cross-set resolution failures ** Referential identity ≠ semantic agreement. Economy reads the anchored Chair VII as a deed worth 500 marks; lore reads it as the Vacant Throne of a drowned king. Both cite the same M; a player sells the deed while the prophecy mechanic requires permanent vacancy. Undeclared, this is undetectable corruption-as-gameplay. Fix: every anchor declares **canonical fields** (identity, existence, occupancy transitions — coordinated globally) vs **local facets** (value, symbolism — free per set). Rules transactions validate against canonical fields regardless of local story; local reinterpretation is legitimate and intended. Tri-valued resolution violation. ** A consumer queries M; its token set predates a subsystem. Collapsing "anchor unknown" and "anchor known, facet uncovered" into one null return makes lens-ignorance indistinguishable from world corruption — the difference between not knowing and lying. API must return exactly: `RESOLVED` / `PARTIAL` (facet missing) / `ABSENT`. Prose mangling and fuzzy merging. ** In narrative token sets, "Seat Seven," "the seventh chair," and "Chair VII of the Long Table" must map to one M. Transcription noise plus similarity matching produces false merges — two distinct chairs fused because their descriptions embedded close together. Fix: registered human-legible aliases with **exact-match-only** alias→address resolution. Fuzzy/embedding search may exist for discovery; it never touches state operations. ** Two anchors claim "the empty chair. " Scopes: world > region > session; nearest enclosing scope wins; ties broken by registration height, then hash. Resolution must be a pure function of `(alias, scope-stack, read-height)` — never query-order dependent. ** "The chair was empty" true at event-time T₁, false after T₂. Unpinned reads let one rules evaluation see two different truths — the ghost sits down *between* the occupancy check and the sitting action. Fix: every rules-path resolution pins an explicit ledger height; implicit "now" permitted only for flavor text. Authority and manipulation failures ** Economy debits the deed; lore simultaneously crowns its bearer. Concurrent canonical writes resolve by fixed order (set priority → height → hash tiebreak); the loser generates a **recorded rejection event**, never a silent drop — in a world themed on absence, refusals must be legible. Client-authoritative canonical writes. ** Optimistic UI shows both players winning the same empty chair. Canonical occupancy is server-adjudicated only; the losing client renders the recorded event ("another sat down as you arrived"). GC reachability error. ** Garbage collection of unreferenced anchors using head-state reachability deletes an anchor still cited by an old quest entry. Protection rule: unreachable-**at-head** ≠ unreachable-**ever**; anything referenced at any height is immortal. ** Cyclic references (A→B→A) or wide fan-out turns a tiny lookup into unbounded traversal. Enforce DAG acyclicity at mint; cap resolution depth at 16 hops and 1024 visited nodes. ** Immutable content can't gain fields; extensions go in sidecar objects referencing M. Sidecar indexes may be cached but must be deterministically rebuildable from ledger replay alone. Non-rebuildable caches are forbidden — crash recovery replays the ledger or nothing. Voiding and erasure. ** Retcons and player erasure requests can't delete content-addressed objects. Tombstone events flip an existence flag; referenced voided anchors enter **quarantine** rendered diegetically as "a chair nobody remembers" — visibly broken in-fiction rather than recursively deleted (cascade deletion storms are the alternative and it is worse). ** Diverged ledgers share early history; the same M means different things on each branch. Post-fork, address equality is syntactic only. Merge protocol: deterministic CRDT-style occupancy-log merge with conflicts **materialized as literal vacant chairs** pending adjudication — never last-writer-wins that discards a branch's recorded history. ** Export strips the authority matrix; re-import defaults ownership open; first toucher seizes every orphaned anchor. Deny-by-default authority survives every transform. Boundaries — the lines deliberately drawn **Reference identity is global and exact; interpretation is set-local and free. ** This is the constitution. Canonical fields coordinate; local facets differentiate. Neither may invade the other. **Pure content addressing ends where mutability begins. ** Genesis-anchor + append-only chain is the bridge; pretending otherwise produces A3. **Fuzziness lives in discovery, dies at state. ** Similarity never resolves coordination-critical references. **Two truths about time. ** Event-time answers narrative questions; ledger-height answers rules questions. Mixed-height rules reads are structurally impossible, not discouraged. **Contradiction is a designed value. ** Mystery-plot anchors may be explicitly `CONTESTED`. Contested anchors fail closed in rules paths — the contested door does not open — and are free material in narrative paths. ** Players see aliases and signed provenance chains (tap-to-verify); machines see full hashes. Both layers are real; the signed registry joins them, defeating impostor-NPC claims ("I am that same chair"). What must never happen — the invariant list Never hash a non-canonical serialization. Never present content addressing as hosting mutable identity. Never collapse UNKNOWN and FACET-MISSING into one return value. Never resolve state-critical references by similarity. Never mix ledger heights inside one rules computation. Never silently drop a rejected write — record it. Never collect garbage referenced at any height. Never permit reference cycles or unbounded resolution depth. Never edit anchored content — extend by sidecar. Never depend on non-rebuildable caches for resolution. Never merge forks by discarding recorded history. Never default authority to open across any migration or import. Never coerce an accidental contradiction to true or false — contradictions must surface as explicit `CONTESTED` and fail closed. Never hard-delete ledger content — tombstone and quarantine only. Never accept client-authoritative writes to canonical fields. Never let one token set write another set's local facets through the shared anchor. Violate any one and the meta-token stops being an anchor and becomes a rumor with good typography — which, in a world built on a ledger of empty chairs, is precisely the thing the architecture exists to make impossible.
