Mitigation: step 3 window [e_f − F, e_f], F = finality lag; registry lookup by (chain_id, e); value returned carries e so downstream anchors to it. T03 Under-bound root signatures. Mechanism: get quorum to sign bare root; then present forked registry with two roots at same epoch. Wins if sig

4b6c540fc48b416c.text: # Red-Team: Compact Verkle/Merkle Proof in the Frontier-Scout Burn Pipeline ## Threat model (one line) Prover is adversarial and resourceful; verifier is neutral, stateless except for an anchored root registry and a spent-nullifier set; network is hostile (replay, reorder, truncate). Goal: a ≤ few-KB proof where acceptance is a pure function of `(proof_bytes, anchor_set, spent_set)`. ## Bypass attempts → deterministic mitigations Second-preimage / internal-node birthday substitution. Vector: craft an alternate leaf or subtree colliding with an honest internal node; with k controlled leaves, birthday margin drops to 2^(256−k). Mitigation: domain-separate — leaf hash `SHA256(0x00 ‖ epoch ‖ pipeline ‖ canonical(leaf))`, internal node `SHA256(0x01 ‖ epoch ‖ pipeline ‖ L ‖ R)`. Leaf index is inside the leaf preimage. Cap registered leaves per epoch at 2²⁴ so collision margin stays > 2¹⁰⁰. Nothing else needed; SHA-256 preimage resistance carries the rest. Depth truncation (short-path). Vector: submit a path of length h′ < H against a self-made shallow tree. Mitigation: H is a protocol constant. Proof layout has *no count field* — the path is exactly H × 32 bytes; parser rejects any other total length before touching semantics. Index/path mismatch. Vector: valid-looking sibling path folded at the wrong position; exploits verifiers that skip the bit-walk. Mitigation: verifier derives each fold direction from bit *i* of `leaf_index`; any mismatch between implied direction and provided ordering is structural garbage → reject. Non-negotiable line in the verifier loop below. Root substitution (bring-your-own-tree). Vector: build a private tree containing whatever you want, present its root. Mitigation: the prover-supplied root is treated as a *claim*, never an input. Verifier resolves `anchor_root[epoch][pipeline_id]` from the anchored registry (finalized checkpoints on the settlement layer). Computed root must equal it bitwise. No match, no accept — regardless of internal proof validity. Cross-epoch replay. Vector: reuse an epoch-N proof in epoch N+1. Mitigation: epoch and pipeline IDs are mixed into *every* node hash (see A1). An old proof folds to the old root; the anchor lookup for the current epoch fails. Structural rejection, not policy. Nullifier replay (double burn). Vector: present the same inclusion proof twice, collect credit twice. Mitigation: `nullifier = SHA256(0x4E ‖ pipeline ‖ epoch ‖ scout_sk-derived-secret ‖ leaf_nonce)`. Burn proof embeds a *non-inclusion* proof of the nullifier against the spent-tree root snapshotted at epoch start (same Merkle machinery, absence-of-neighbor proof). Settlement inserts the nullifier under a uniqueness constraint; duplicate insert fails closed. One proof ⇒ one insert, ever. Vector: re-serialize the same logical proof (width changes, padding, reordered maps) to mint distinct byte strings → defeats any dedup keyed on proof hash, enables signature-confusion. Mitigation: strict canonical codec — fixed-width little-endian integers, length-prefixed blobs, no optional fields anywhere in the proof. Verifier rejects trailing bytes, short fields, non-minimal encodings. Dedup key = SHA256(canonical bytes). Two byte strings either are identical or at most one parses. Frontier-flag forgery. Vector: flip the "is-frontier" bit in the leaf, since it's just data. Mitigation: frontier status is never a free bit. It is *derived*: frontier membership means `key > last_consumed_key` for the epoch, where `last_consumed_key` is itself a marker leaf in the same tree. The proof therefore carries two inclusion proofs against the same anchored root: the scout's leaf and the consumption marker. Verifier checks `marker. key` and both fold to the anchor. Predicate is recomputed, never asserted. Stale-root race (consume-after-consume). Vector: two scouts race; loser replays against the pre-consumption root where its leaf was still frontier. Mitigation: consumption writes a consumed-marker at the leaf's key; the anchor advances monotonically per epoch. Verifier accepts only the latest finalized anchor (or a bounded grace window of exactly one anchor). Combined with A6's nullifier, the second submission fails on either stale root or spent nullifier — whichever fires first, deterministically. Weak Fiat-Shamir (verkle). Vector: challenge derived from partial transcript lets the prover pick commitments *after* seeing the challenge. Mitigation: `z = SHA256(transcript ‖ root_claim ‖ epoch ‖ all_commitments ‖ all_keys) mod r`. Every prover-chosen element enters the hash before the challenge exists. Transcript is the full serialized proof header; no post-hoc inputs. Toxic-waste forgery (KZG). Vector: holder of the SRS trapdoor forges openings at will. Mitigation: default to a transparent inner-product-argument (IPA/Bulletproofs-style) commitment — no trusted setup exists to abuse. If KZG is mandatory for size, require a documented multi-party ceremony (≥ 40 independent participants, ≥ 1 guaranteed to have discarded their share) and pin the SRS hash in the verifier; unknown SRS hash → reject. Degenerate evaluation point. Vector: steer z onto 0 or a special point where polynomial structure misbehaves. Mitigation: z comes from A10's hash mod the scalar-field order r; verifier explicitly rejects `z = 0`. Probability is ~2⁻²⁵⁴ naturally; the check costs one comparison. Cross-root batch mixing (multi-proofs). Vector: aggregate verkle opening blends commitments from tree A and tree B; aggregate check passes, individual claims are nonsense. Mitigation: one proof binds to exactly one root — batching across roots is forbidden by format (single `root_claim` field). Per-key sub-checks run against that root only. No aggregate-only fast path exists in the verifier. Vector: omit the sibling that would expose non-frontier status or a nearer consumer. Mitigation: fixed-size layout again — every path slot is mandatory, the marker proof is mandatory. Absence is a parse error, not a semantic judgment. The verifier never reasons over incomplete paths. Dust/partial burn. Vector: burn 0 (or dust) and still claim full credit; exploit a verifier that trusts the tx memo for amount. Mitigation: `amount: u64` lives inside the signed, rooted leaf. Tx memos are ignored for value. Signature malleability / scope creep. Vector: ECDSA s↦n−s flip produces a second valid signature over the same leaf → dedup miss; or sign loose bytes then swap fields. Mitigation: Ed25519 (deterministic, no malleable component) over the canonical serialization of the leaf with the sig field zeroed. Verifier re-canonicalizes before checking. If ECDSA is ever unavoidable: enforce low-s and reject non-canonical DER. Cross-chain burn ambiguity. Vector: cite a burn tx on chain X while settlement runs on Y with no light client; or omit chain_id so any chain's tx passes. Wrong-chain receipts fail the leaf hash. Frontier-position grinding. Vector: if frontier = "lowest unconsumed keys," pre-register keys adjacent to the boundary and monopolize the frontier forever. Mitigation: `key = SHA256(0x4B ‖ scout_pk ‖ epoch_salt ‖ nonce)` where `epoch_salt` is revealed only at epoch open. Positions are unpredictable ex ante; grinding reduces to lottery odds already priced into the protocol. Verifier DoS via oversized proofs. Vector: ship gigabyte "proofs" to exhaust neutral verifiers. Mitigation: `MAX_PROOF_BYTES = 4096`. Length checked before allocation or parsing. Overflow is rejection, not exception. Cross-pipeline nullifier reuse. Vector: same nullifier presented in two pipelines sharing a spent-set namespace. Mitigation: pipeline_id is inside the nullifier preimage (A6) and each pipeline maintains its own spent-tree root. Namespaces cannot collide by construction. ## Canonical proof & verifier loop (what closes all twenty) magic: u16 = 0x4653, version: u8, epoch: u64, pipeline_id: u32, leaf: { scout_pk[32], key[32], value_hash[32], amount: u64, nullifier[32], sig[64] }, marker_proof: { marker_index: u64, marker_leaf{. }, path[H]x32 }, path: [H] x 32          // exactly H entries, no count field // H = 32 → ~1. 4 KB total. Verkle variant swaps `path` for per-level // commitment + IPA opening (~600–900 B); everything else identical. verify(P, ctx): len(P) ≤ 4096, strict canonical parse           → kills A7, A14, A19 epoch                            → kills A5 pk, canon(leaf\sig), sig) → kills A16 fold: acc = L(leaf); for i in 0. leaf_index >> i) & 1 N(sib[i], acc) : N(acc, sib[i])     → kills A2, A3 acc == anchor[ctx. pipeline]          → kills A4, A9(stale) marker folds to same anchor ∧ marker. key → kills A8 nullifier ∉ spent_tree[root@epoch_start]        → kills A6, A9(race) amount ≥ MIN_BURN                               → kills A15 ACCEPT(nullifier, amount); settlement INSERT nullifier, unique → kills A6 finally Same bytes in, same verdict out, every verifier, every time. Steps 1–9 are pure functions of `(P, anchor_set, spent_set)`. ## Residual risks (crypto can't fix these — say so plainly) - **Anchor liveness**: if the checkpoint registry censors or stalls, no proof construction helps. That's a quorum/settlement-layer problem. - **Sequencer ordering**: frontier races (A9) resolve correctly only because the sequencer imposes a total order on consumption. Remove the sequencer and you need consensus, not cryptography. - **Quantum horizon**: SHA-256 survives Grover degraded-but-alive; Ed25519 dies to Shor. - **KZG ceremony trust**: even a good ceremony is a social assumption. IPA eliminates it at ~2× proof size. Default to IPA unless bytes are scarce enough to justify the assumption. Bottom line: every bypass above dies to one of four mechanisms — domain-separated hashing with epoch/pipeline binding, strict canonical fixed-length encoding, anchor-and-nullifier state the prover doesn't control, and a verifier that recomputes predicates rather than reading them. None of the mitigations require trusting the prover at any point. The user is asking about a hard problem in the context of a "frontier-scout burn pipeline" — this appears to be a system where some kind of proof (verkle/merkle) needs to be compact enough that a neutral verifier can re-derive it without the full tree. They want a red-team analysis: enumerate bypass attempts and deterministic mitigations for each. Let me think about what this actually is. "Frontier-scout burn pipeline" — this sounds like a specific protocol design, possibly related to: - A burn/mint mechanism (token burning) - A frontier exploration / scouting mechanism - A verifiable computation pipeline Given the context clues ("Ghost's thousand-ask mining engine"), this seems to be part of a larger system design discussion. The core problem is: **Problem statement**: Design a compact Verkle/Merkle proof such that any neutral verifier can re-derive the commitment without having the full tree, within a "frontier-scout burn pipeline. Let me think about what the frontier-scout burn pipeline likely is: - There are "scouts" that explore a frontier (maybe of states, maybe of search space) - There's a "burn" step — perhaps burning tokens/compute to commit to results - The proof must be compact and independently verifiable The hard problem: A verifier without the full tree must be able to verify that: The claimed leaf/value is authentic (inclusion proof) The claimed state/root is correct No double-spending or replay of burned items The scout didn't fabricate frontier discoveries Red-team angles — what are the bypass attempts? Let me enumerate systematically: **Category 1: Proof forgery / hash collision attacks** **Second-preimage attack on Merkle path**: Attacker crafts an alternative leaf that hashes to the same intermediate node. Mitigation: domain separation (prefix each leaf with type byte), use SHA-256 or better, include leaf index in leaf preimage. **Verkle opening forgery**: Forgetting polynomial commitments — attacker provides fake opening that passes if verifier doesn't check binding. Mitigation: Fiat-Shamir challenge derived from transcript including root, not just from leaf data. **Truncated path attack**: Attacker provides shorter path claiming shallower depth. Mitigation: encode depth explicitly in proof; verifier checks depth against known tree height parameter. **Category 2: Root substitution** **Root swap**: Attacker presents a different root for which they have a valid proof of a different value. Mitigation: root must be committed/anchored somewhere immutable (on-chain, in a prior signed checkpoint); verifier checks root against anchor. **Root grinding**: Attacker grinds many roots until one has a favorable property. Mitigation: root must be derived deterministically from committed inputs; include nonce/epoch. **Category 3: Replay / double-burn** **Replay same proof twice**: Same inclusion proof used to claim two burns. Mitigation: nullifier set — each leaf contains a unique nullifier; verifier maintains nullifier accumulator (or sparse Merkle tree of spent nullifiers); proof includes non-inclusion proof for nullifier. **Cross-epoch replay**: Proof from epoch N reused in epoch N+1. Mitigation: bind epoch ID into every hashed node (domain-separated per epoch), so old proofs fail structurally. **Category 4: Frontier-specific bypasses** **Frontier boundary manipulation**: Scout claims a node is at the frontier when it isn't (or vice versa). Mitigation: frontier membership is itself a bit in the leaf; the frontier predicate is deterministic given the tree; verifier recomputes frontier status from sibling information included in proof. **Sibling omission**: Attacker omits siblings that would show the node is NOT at frontier. Mitigation: proof format requires all siblings along path; fixed-length encoding prevents silent truncation. **Stale frontier**: Using an outdated root where the item was at frontier but has since been consumed by another scout. Mitigation: monotonic version counter in root; verifier rejects roots older than current accepted checkpoint minus grace window. **Category 5: Verifier-side weaknesses** **Malleable proof encoding**: Two different byte encodings of the same logical proof → replay or signature confusion. Mitigation: canonical serialization (e. , SSZ-style fixed-width little-endian, no variable-length fields without length prefixes); reject non-canonical forms. **Verifier doesn't check index consistency**: Path bits don't match claimed leaf index. Mitigation: derive each sibling direction from index bits; verifier walks index bits alongside path. **Missing depth bound**: Unbounded tree allows attacker to pad depth. Mitigation: fixed height H known to all; proof length is exactly H nodes; anything else rejected. **Category 6: Verkle-specific issues** **Wrong evaluation point**: Verkle proofs prove polynomial evaluations at z = hash(root, key). If attacker can influence z (e. , via chosen key), they might find openings valid at multiple points. Actually the standard issue: if the commitment scheme's binding relies on the SRS trapdoor, attacker with knowledge of toxic waste could forge. Mitigation: transparent setup (IPA-based, e. , Bulletproofs-style inner product argument) or well-audited trusted setup ceremony. **Opening at degenerate point**: If z lands on a special value where polynomial structure leaks or multiple polynomials agree. Mitigation: z = H(root || key || epoch) ensures pseudorandomness; check z ! = 0 and z ! = roots of unity if using KZG over BLS field. **Multi-proof batching attack**: In batched verkle proofs, attacker mixes openings across different keys/roots. Mitigation: transcript binds all (key, value, root) tuples before challenge derivation. **Category 7: Economic/incentive bypasses in burn pipeline** **Burn without proof**: Claiming burn credit without presenting proof. Mitigation: burn receipt IS the proof; no credit without valid verification. **Proof-of-burn vs proof-of-work confusion**: Burning tokens ≠ doing work. Mitigation: separate attestations; burn proof references tx hash on settlement layer, work proof references compute attestation; both linked by session ID. **Partial burn**: Burn amount less than required but proof shows only total. Mitigation: amount encoded in leaf; verifier checks amount ≥ threshold. **Category 8: Data availability** **Withholding siblings**: Prover provides proof but network can't reconstruct enough to audit. Mitigation: proof must be self-contained (all siblings/openings included); optionally require erasure-coded publication of frontier subtree. Now let me also address the constructive side — what does the actual design look like? Because mitigations need grounding. **Concrete design sketch:** - Binary Merkle tree OR Verkle tree with branching factor 256 (KZG or IPA commitments). - Height H fixed (e. , 32 for binary, 4 levels for verkle with 256^4 ≈ 4B leaves). - Leaf payload: {scout_id, epoch, frontier_key, value_hash, burn_amount, nullifier, sig}. - Node hash: H(domain_tag || left || right) for merkle; for verkle: Pedersen commitment to vector of children hashes. Proof contents (binary merkle): - leaf_index (u64), leaf_payload, H siblings [H × 32 bytes], plus frontier bitmap or sibling frontier flags. - Total size: ~1KB for H=32. Proof contents (verkle): - stem, suffix values, commitment deltas + IPA opening proof (~few hundred bytes per level with IPA, or 48×(levels+1) for KZG multiproof). - Total: ~500–800 bytes. Verification procedure (deterministic): Parse proof canonically; reject if length ≠ expected(H). Check epoch matches current context. Recompute z or walk index bits; fold up to root. Compare computed root to anchored root (from checkpoint registry). Check nullifier not in spent-set (non-inclusion proof or local bloom filter + authoritative check). Check burn_amount ≥ threshold, sig valid over leaf payload. Emit accept/reject deterministically — same input bytes always same verdict. Now let me organize the red-team enumeration cleanly. I'll do a table-like structured list: Attack | Vector | Deterministic mitigation. Let me be more precise about each: Second-preimage leaf substitution. Vector: Craft alternative leaf L' ≠ L with H(L') = H(L). With SHA-256, infeasible directly (2^128 work via birthday on internal nodes is 2^128 for second preimage on 256-bit. actually second preimage on n-bit hash is 2^n, birthday is 2^(n/2)). But internal-node birthday: attacker controls many leaves, wants two subtrees equal — with 2^k leaves, birthday gives 2^(n-k). Deterministic mitigation: domain-separate leaf vs internal (0x00 prefix leaf, 0x01 prefix internal); include leaf_index inside leaf preimage; use 256-bit hash; cap tree size so birthday margin stays > 2^100. Depth truncation / short-path. Vector: Submit path of length h' < H claiming shallow tree. Mitigation: H is protocol constant; parser enforces exact byte length; verifier folds exactly H times. Index/path mismatch. Vector: Provide valid-looking path but for different index; verifier that skips bit-checking accepts wrong position. Mitigation: verifier derives direction i-th step from bit i of leaf_index; mismatch → reject. This is standard but must be stated because lazy verifiers skip it. Root substitution / fork choice. Vector: Present self-built tree with desired content. Mitigation: root must equal checkpoint_root[epoch] published in anchored registry (chain or quorum-signed log). Verifier looks up by epoch, never accepts prover-supplied root as input except as claim to be checked. Cross-epoch replay. Vector: Reuse epoch-N proof in epoch N+1. Mitigation: epoch_id mixed into every node hash: node = H(tag || epoch || l || r). Old proofs produce old root; root lookup fails. Also nullifier includes epoch. Nullifier replay (double burn). Vector: Same leaf proven twice → double credit. Mitigation: nullifier n = H(scout_secret || leaf_nonce); spent-nullifier sparse Merkle tree with its own root; burn proof includes non-membership proof of n in spent-tree at epoch start; settlement atomically inserts n. Alternatively sequential processing with unique constraint. Malleability / non-canonical encoding. Vector: Re-encode proof (different integer widths, reordered fields, extra padding) to create distinct byte strings mapping to same acceptance → breaks dedup keyed on proof hash. Mitigation: strict canonical codec: fixed-width LE integers, length-prefixed byte strings, sorted map keys; verifier rejects any deviation; dedup key = canonical bytes hash. Frontier-bit forgery. Vector: Flip frontier flag in leaf since it's just data. Mitigation: frontier status is not free-form: leaf stores frontier_epoch and the proof includes sibling frontier flags; invariant checked: node is frontier iff all leaves in its subtree have frontier_epoch == current and no child consumed. , frontier defined as lexicographic first k unconsumed keys; verifier recomputes from proof-revealed neighbors (left neighbor and right neighbor leaves included in proof). Actually let me make this concrete: define frontier as the set of leaves whose key ∈ [last_consumed_key, next_checkpoint_bound). To prove membership you need inclusion of your leaf AND inclusion of last_consumed_key marker leaf. Both are ordinary inclusion proofs against same root. Stale-root race. Vector: Submit proof against older root where your leaf was still frontier, after someone else consumed it under newer root. Mitigation: monotonically increasing consumption sequence; each burn writes consumed-marker at leaf key; verifier requires proof against latest finalized root AND nullifier freshness; ordering enforced by sequencer with total order; late proofs rejected by epoch/version check. Verkle challenge manipulation (Fiat-Shamir weak). Vector: If transcript hashing omits root or commitments, attacker picks values after seeing challenge. Mitigation: challenge z = H(transcript || root || epoch || all_commitments || all_keys); nothing signer-controlled enters after challenge. Toxic-waste / SRS forgery (KZG). Vector: Holder of trapdoor τ forges openings. Mitigation: use transparent IPA (inner-product argument, no trusted setup) or documented multi-party ceremony with ≥ threshold participants; pin SRS hash in client; verifier refuses unknown SRS hash. Degenerate evaluation point. Vector: Force z into small subgroup or zero. Mitigation: z = H(. ) mod r, reject z=0; for BLS12-381 scalar field r ≈ 0x73eda753. , probability negligible but check anyway. Batch mixing across roots. Vector: Multi-proof aggregates openings from tree A and tree B; verifier checks aggregate only. Mitigation: per-root sub-transcripts; aggregate equation per root: check Σ bindings separately; or forbid cross-root batching entirely (one proof = one root). Sibling withholding / partial disclosure. Vector: Omit sibling that reveals non-frontier status. Mitigation: fixed-size proof layout — every slot filled; missing slot = parse failure. No optional fields. Amount/threshold bypass. Vector: Burn 0 or dust, still claim. Signature scope creep. Vector: Sig over leaf but leaf fields swapped post-signature via malleable encoding. Mitigation: sign canonical bytes; verify against canonical re-encoding; use Ed25519 (deterministic, no ECDSA malleability s/s flip). Reject high-s if ECDSA ever used. Proof-of-burn cross-chain ambiguity. Vector: Cite burn tx on chain X while settlement on chain Y lacks light-client. Grindable frontier predicate. Vector: If frontier = "first k keys", attacker pre-registers keys near boundary to monopolize frontier. Mitigation: key = H(scout_pubkey || salt || epoch) — unpredictable until epoch open; or VRF-assigned positions. Vector: Send GB-scale "proof". Mitigation: hard byte cap = expected_size(H); reject overflow before parsing. Replay across pipelines (same nullifier in two pipelines). Vector: Nullifier space shared or untagged. Mitigation: nullifier = H(pipeline_id || epoch || secret || nonce); per-pipeline spent sets. That's twenty. Let me also give the minimal verifier algorithm pseudocode and the exact proof layout, since they asked for grounded concreteness. **Canonical proof layout (binary Merkle variant, recommended default):** magic:      u16 = 0x4653 ("FS")     // format tag scout_pk:   [32]byte key:        [32]byte            // = H(pk||salt||epoch) value_hash: [32]byte nullifier:  [32]byte sig:        [64]byte            // Ed25519 over canonical leaf-minus-sig last_consumed_leaf: leaf_skeleton  // inclusion proof for frontier lower bound path: [H]struct{ sib: [32]byte }      // exactly H entries, no count field size = 2+1+8+4+8 + (32+32+32+8+32+64) + (leaf skeleton ~ 200) + 32*H for H=32: ≈ 200 + 200 + 1024 ≈ 1. Node hash: `N(l,r) = SHA256(0x01 || epoch_le(8) || pipeline_le(4) || l || r)`; leaf: `L = SHA256(0x00 || epoch || pipeline || canonical(leaf))`. Verifier steps (exact): len(proof) ≤ MAX_PROOF_BYTES (= 4096); else REJECT. Parse strictly; any trailing byte or short field → REJECT. epoch (or within allowed window) else REJECT. Verify sig over canonical leaf bytes; pk → derive expected key? No—key is H(pk||salt||epoch), salt may be secret; instead check nullifier == H(pk || leaf. Keep simple: check nullifier well-formed. Fold: idx = leaf_index; acc = L; for i in 0. H-1: bit = (idx >> i) & 1; acc = bit ? N(sib[i], acc) : N(acc, sib[i]). acc == anchor_root[epoch][pipeline] else REJECT. Non-inclusion: nullifier absent from spent-tree root at epoch start (second small proof, same machinery). Frontier: inclusion of last_consumed marker with key_m < key, and no consumed marker between — approximated by requiring marker proof + nullifier freshness; deterministic given sequencer order. Output ACCEPT with (nullifier, amount, epoch) → settlement inserts nullifier; duplicate insert fails closed. For Verkle variant: replace path with per-level commitment C_i and opening π_i; z = H(root_claim || epoch || key_stem); verify IPA/KZG opening that poly(z) = leaf_hash; rest identical. Size ~600–900 B with IPA at 128-bit soundness (log2(255)*2 points. keep approximate but honest). I should present: (1) the threat model in one line, (2) the enumerated bypass→mitigation pairs, tight, (3) the canonical proof + verifier loop that closes them, (4) residual risks stated plainly (e. , sequencer liveness, DA of anchors — things crypto can't fix). Residual risks to name honestly: - Anchor availability: if checkpoint registry censors, no proof helps. Mitigation is social/quorum, not cryptographic. - Sequencer ordering is trusted for frontier race resolution unless you go consensus-layer. - Trusted setup if KZG chosen without ceremony. - Quantum: SHA-256 fine-ish (Grover halves), Ed25519 broken by Shor — note migration path (hash-based sigs) but out of scope. 5f1741f050fcb1d4.text: # Compact Verkle/Merkle Proofs on Self-Hosted Iron: Red-Team Enumeration Baseline being defended (grounding) - **Prover:** operator on own hardware, no external trust. Maintains a tree over state, emits proofs. - **Verifier:** neutral, holds *only* pinned constants (genesis root, operator pubkey, spec hash, witness-log head) plus the incoming proof. Must recompute the root from the proof alone. - *Merkle:* binary sparse tree, depth 256, path = bits of `SHA-256("path-v1" || key)`. Leaf = `H(0x00 || len || value)`, node = `H(0x01 || L || R)` with fixed 32-byte children, empty subtree at depth d = `H(0x02 || d)`. - *Verkle:* KZG over BLS12-381 with pinned setup-transcript ID, or IPA-over-Pedersen (no setup). Width 256, stem/suffix indexing à la EIP-4762. - **Envelope:** `{tree_id, spec_version, epoch, root, proof, sig}`; root independently anchored in an append-only witness log (RFC 6962-style, hash-chained, periodically checkpointed externally). - Reference sizes: Merkle presence proof at 2³⁰ leaves ≈ 30 × 32 B ≈ 960 B; Verkle single-key ≈ 200–400 B; Verkle wins decisively for multi-key batches (~48 B/key marginal vs ~1 KB/key). Everything below is enumerated as **bypass → deterministic mitigation**, where "deterministic" means a boolean check or forced construction rule the verifier executes mechanically. Root / anchor lifecycle Root fork (show different roots to different verifiers for the same epoch). Bypass: operator signs two envelopes, epoch identical, roots differ. Mitigation: witness log has a *fixed slot* per `(epoch, tree_id)`; entry = `H(root || prev_chain_hash)`. Verifier recomputes the chain from its pinned head and asserts the slot content equals the envelope's root. Two roots for one slot = structural impossibility; any deviation = hard fail. Stale-proof replay. Bypass: present an old valid envelope as current. Mitigation: verifier keeps `max_epoch[tree_id]`; reject `epoch < max_epoch - W` (W = 2 tolerance). Root must equal the log entry at that epoch's slot. Dedupe on `(tree_id, epoch, H(proof))`. Long-range drift (quietly rotate roots; returning verifiers accept attacker-shaped history). Bypass: verifier offline for months; operator presents a fabricated continuous-looking chain. Mitigation: chain continuity check from last pinned checkpoint + external anchor (CT log inclusion or on-chain commit) every N epochs. Gap > G epochs ⇒ reject and force manual re-pin. Continuity is a pure hash-chain recomputation — deterministic. Bypass: substitute the initial root/pubkey in verifier configuration. Mitigation: genesis constants compiled into the verifier binary; byte-equality check against build-embedded values; reproducible build with published digest. No runtime-loaded genesis, ever. Structure / hash layer Weak or truncated hashing. Bypass: 16-byte node hashes → birthday forgery at 2⁶⁴; MD5/SHA-1 chosen-prefix collisions. Mitigation: SHA-256/BLAKE3 only, 32-byte outputs everywhere, no truncation below 32 B at any level; algorithm ID byte pinned; unknown ID ⇒ reject. Leaf/node second-preimage confusion. Bypass: craft a *value* whose hash equals an internal node hash, present it as a leaf with a short path. Mitigation: domain separation (`0x00` leaf / `0x01` node / `0x02` empty) + length-prefixed leaves + fixed depth 256. Verifier asserts path length == 256 and leaf prefix byte == `0x00`. Short paths are structurally unrepresentable. Bypass: variable-length fields let an attacker re-associate bytes (shift the L/R boundary in `H(L||R)`). Mitigation: fixed-width encodings only (hashes 32 B, scalars 32 B BE, indices u64 LE); strict decoder rejecting trailing bytes and non-canonical forms. Ambiguity requires variable widths; eliminate the variable widths. Index/path substitution. Bypass: prover invents a convenient index instead of deriving it from the key. Mitigation: verifier recomputes `index = SHA-256(tag || key)` and compares bit-by-bit against the proof's path. Never accept a prover-supplied index. Must never happen: verifier accepting "a" root at height h rather than "the" root per the fork rule. Compressed/extension nodes: prover skips the extension and jumps levels — verifier must re-derive the extension length from committed data, not from the prover's claim. Zero-canonicalization: if "value 0" ≡ "absent," a prover can present an existing zero-balance account as absent or vice versa. Pick one canonical semantics; state it; never allow both encodings. - Must never happen: absence proof verifying for a key that is present (requires full index-by-index path check + canonical zero rule). Multiproof stem dedup confusion (structural #3). - Batch with two keys sharing a stem: the opened node for that stem appears once. If the verifier dedups by stem bytes but the prover lists it twice with different claimed child values (only one can be honest), a verifier that checks each occurrence against the same commitment will pass the honest one. actually if the node's commitment is fixed, both occurrences must use the same preimage-derived evaluation — a malicious prover can claim different values for the same (C, i) in different places only if the verifier fails to check global consistency of the (C,i)→v map. If any element is omitted (commonly: leaf values, or the batch key list), prover grinds: pick adversarial leaf values or key ordering to force a weak challenge and forge an opening. Must never happen: any proof-relevant byte excluded from the challenge derivation. Concrete rule: challenge = H(tag ‖ R ‖ sorted(canonical encoding of all openings)); sort order must be canonical (prover-chosen order = grinding surface). Non-canonical field elements and points (encoding #1). - v ∉ [0, p) must be rejected pre-reduction; else v and v+p both verify but downstream semantics differ (balance wrap). - Compressed points: y-parity bit mandatory; an x with two y's must have exactly one canonical encoding. Else proof malleability: same statement, two proofs, replay/dedup logic breaks (if proof hashes are used as object IDs, double-counting). - Fixed-width encodings; no DER-style length ambiguity. Must never happen: two distinct byte strings that decode to the same logical value (breaks root equality across implementations → consensus split, not just proof rejection). Key encoding / path derivation ambiguity (encoding #2). - Key → path must be a pure function of canonical key bytes (bit decomposition order pinned: MSB-first per byte, etc. If the prover supplies the path, verifier must re-derive it from the key and reject mismatch. Must never happen: verifier trusting prover-supplied indices without re-derivation from the key. Variable-length keys / prefix keys. - Keys that are prefixes of others (trie with values at internal nodes): absence proof must open the internal node's value slot. Must never happen: absence proof that ignores internal values. Trusted-setup provenance (params #1). - If KZG: verifier must pin the SRS (or verify setup transcript). Must never happen: prover-chosen parameters. All params (arity, depth, hash fn, curve, SRS hash) pinned in genesis. Resource exhaustion (DoS #1). - Caps enforced before any crypto: max batch keys, max opened nodes, max depth (=32, derived), max proof bytes, max leaf payload size. Preimage-expansion attacks: a claim that forces the verifier to request more data (interactive rounds) — keep the proof non-interactive and self-contained; any interactivity is a DoS and a race window (state can change between rounds). Must never happen: verifier performing O(prover-chosen) work; all costs bounded by pinned params + explicit caps. Snapshot mixing / staleness (lifecycle #1). - Prover collects openings from flock members holding shards while new blocks finalize; openings from h and h′ mixed. Fail-closed if verifier checks all against one R — so the invariant is: every element binds to the single certified R in the batch; no per-element roots. Must never happen: per-element root fields in the proof format. Cross-shard / cross-domain skew (lifecycle #2). - Claim spans two roots R₁@h, R₂@h′: only valid if h = h′ under the same consensus instance, or via an explicit bridge object with its own certificate. Must never happen: implicitly pairing roots from different heights. Replay across domains (lifecycle #3). - Same proof replayed on another chain/app: every hash and signature must include a chain-ID / purpose domain tag. Must never happen: a proof that verifies in two different protocol contexts. Aggregator equivocation (lifecycle #4). - If proofs are aggregated by a swarm node, the aggregator picks the batch. A malicious aggregator can omit keys (harmless — claim just fails) or include extra (harmless), but can also present a batch header root different from element roots — caught by #13. The real risk: aggregator reuses a valid QC for root R with a proof built for R′ — caught by binding R in the transcript. Must never happen: QC and proof bound to independent transcripts; they must be bound together (QC covers H(h, R, proof_commitment) — commit to the proof or its hash in the certified block if proofs are part of the protocol; if proofs are off-protocol, then binding is (h, R) only and the claim must be fully determined by (R, key)).

3309dc4b2643e6a5.text: # Compact Verkle/Merkle Proofs Over the Meta-Token Coordinate Layer The statelessness contract A neutral verifier must succeed with exactly this dependency set and nothing else: {pinned_spec_version, pinned_verification_key (or setup params), root_registry_entry: (ns_id, epoch, root, signer), proof_bytes, coordinate, claimed_value} No tree, no sibling counts, no tree size, no other namespaces. If any implementation pulls in a fourth implicit input (tree height, total key count, "helper" metadata), that is a defect: it is simultaneously a privacy leak and a malleability channel. Canonical coordinate layer (where everything dies first) Coordinates are composite: `(ns_id, lang, dialect, token, version, …)`. Rules, frozen per `spec_version`: - **Strings**: UTF-8, NFC-normalized, no surrogates, length-prefixed (u32 LE). Reject anything else. - **Integers**: fixed-width, big-endian. **Versions are u64 counters, not semver strings** (`"1. 0"` vs `"1. 0"` ambiguity is a split-brain bug waiting to happen). - **Floats are forbidden. ** IEEE-754 has ±0. 0, NaN payloads, subnormals — multiple bit patterns per logical value. Coordinates are integers or fixed `(num:u128, den:u128)` rationals. - Field order is fixed by the spec; no reordering, no omission of optional fields (optionals serialize as tagged empty). - Every hash/commitment call takes `DST = H("memlang-v" || spec_version || ns_id || node_type)`. The verifier independently re-validates canonical form at parse time. Canonicalization is not the prover's job; it is a precondition of the proof having meaning. Address and tree addr = SHA-256(DST_coord || canonical_coordinate_bytes)   // 32 bytes stem   = addr[0. 30]    // 31 bytes suffix = addr[31] - 256-ary trie over stem bytes; expected depth for n keys ≈ ⌈log₂₅₆(n)⌉ (≈4 for 2³² keys); adversarial worst case 31. Hard cap `D_MAX = 32`; exceeding it is a consensus-fatal event, not a soft condition. - **Invariant enforced at write time: an internal node exists iff ≥1 child slot is nonzero. ** No empty internal nodes, ever, no lazy pruning. ### Node commitments (verkle profile) Internal node: Pedersen vector commitment over the BLS12-381 scalar field, curve = Bandersnatch-class: C_node = Commit([v_0. v_255]; ρ),  v_i = 0 if child absent v_i = reduce(hash_to_field(compressed_encoding(C_child)))  otherwise, via RFC 9380 expand_message_xmd(SHA-256), remapped to [1, q-1] Leaf node: 256-slot vector; 254 slots hold `H(value)` per suffix, 1 slot holds `H(stem_remainder)` (**this slot is load-bearing**, see FM-6), 1 reserved zero. `hash_to_field` output is remapped `((t mod (q-1)) + 1)` so a valid point never reduces to slot-value 0 — slot 0 must mean exactly one thing: empty. ### Merkle fallback profile (post-quantum) Binary Merkle, `H("N"||depth||left||right)` for internal, `H("L"||depth||payload)` for leaves — domain separation kills the classic internal-node/leaf second-preimage confusion. Proof ≈ 32 × 33 B ≈ 1 KB. This is the profile you fall back to; it is not optional to implement. **Inclusion**: path node commitments + one opening per node (revealed child scalar at the coordinate-derived index) + batched IPA folding argument. Single-key size ≈ 0. 5–1 KB. Batch: sort keys lexicographically by address, walk shared prefixes once, open each distinct (node, index) once, fold all openings into one IPA — total proof stays in the low-KB regime for thousands of keys; marginal cost per key → ~0. That is the entire point of choosing verkle here. **Absence — three distinct shapes, all three mandatory:** - (a) Missing internal child: open node at index `i = next stem byte`, reveal 0. - (b) Leaf with different stem: open the internal pointer **and** the leaf's stem slot; reveal `stem_remainder` in clear; verifier checks `H(revealed) == slot` **and** that the full revealed stem ≠ derived stem and is not a prefix-extension of it. Skipping the leaf-side binding is the canonical fake-absence bug: prover shows a branch pointing at "some other subtree" that secretly contains your key. - (c) Suffix miss: leaf stem matches; open leaf at your suffix, reveal 0. **Enumeration claims** ("these are ALL versions of token X") are provable only if each node commits an additional subtree-count scalar and the proof closes a count-sum equation. Decide at genesis; retrofitting is impossible. Otherwise refuse enumeration claims outright. Verifier algorithm (total function, fail-closed) Strict-parse proof: fixed schema, hard caps (`D_MAX·(slots+overhead)`), reject trailing garbage, iterative walk, no allocation driven by untrusted lengths. Re-validate coordinate canonical form; recompute `addr`; derive index path. Root-policy check: `(ns_id, epoch, root)` must match a fresh signed checkpoint. Epoch goes **into the transcript hash**. Replay Fiat–Shamir transcript: `H(DST || root || epoch || coord || value || every commitment in canonical order || running challenges)`. Anything not hashed is grist for the grinding mill. Walk levels: at each, verify opening binds (node commitment, derived index, revealed scalar). Reject any internal node whose commitment is the identity element. At leaf: check stem binding, then value slot: `H(claimed_value) == slot`. For hash-derived addresses, re-hash the claimed coordinate and compare to `addr` (preimage check — see FM-5). Emit exactly one verdict for `(coord, root)`. No code path may return both "present" and "absent. Cost envelope (order of magnitude): binary-Merkle verify <1 ms; verkle-IPA batch tens–hundreds of ms scaling with distinct openings; KZG variant ~2–4 ms flat via two pairings, proof ~150 B total — but see FM-17. - **FM-1 Twin leaves. ** Non-canonical encodings (NFC/NFD, semver strings, alternate field orders) create two addresses for one logical token → equivalence fraud. - **FM-2 Float coordinates. ** Multiple bit patterns per value. *Fix:* banned; integers/rationals only. - **FM-3 Node/leaf second preimage. ** Crafted leaf parses as internal node. *Fix:* per-type DSTs, depth inside every node hash. - **FM-4 Odd-count duplication** (binary profile): fabricate middle elements. *Fix:* sentinel padding. - **FM-5 Truncated-address collision. ** Attacker swaps payload at an unchanged address with a perfectly valid proof. *Fix:* 256-bit addresses, full preimage in the leaf, verifier re-hashes. Never truncate below 256 bits; never skip the preimage re-hash. - **FM-6 Fake absence. ** Missing leaf-stem binding. *Fix:* shape (b) above; the stem slot is not optional. - **FM-7 Fiat–Shamir underbinding. ** Any unhashed field (value, root, partial commitment list) enables offline grinding to forge openings. *Fix:* FM-step 4; everything on transcript, in pinned order. - **FM-8 Identity-element confusion. ** Empty subtree vs. committed-zeros lets deleted keys stay provable via stale paths. *Fix:* no-empty-internal-nodes invariant + verifier rejection of identity commitments at internal positions. - **FM-9 `reduce(point) == 0`. ** Collapses "child exists" into "empty. " *Fix:* remap to `[1, q−1]`. - **FM-10 Point-encoding malleability. ** Two encodings of one curve point → two trees, one root. *Fix:* compressed encoding only; reject x ≥ p and decoded-y-parity mismatch. - **FM-11 Parser DoS/malleability. ** Trailing bytes and oversized vectors produce accepted-but-nonunique proofs. *Fix:* strict lengths, caps, reject-garbage, iterative descent. - **FM-12 Cross-epoch replay. ** Inclusion proof for a since-deleted token verifies against its old root forever. *Fix:* signed `(ns_id, epoch, root)` checkpoints, freshness window, epoch inside transcript. Deletion is only meaningful relative to a current root. - **FM-13 Cross-namespace replay. ** Identical coordinates in namespaces A and B, shared tree, no `ns_id` in DSTs → proof from A validates in B. *Fix:* `ns_id` in every hash and commitment. - **FM-14 Prover-chosen aggregation/dedup order. ** Same claim, many valid proof byte-strings → proof-hash registries and replay logic silently break. *Fix:* lexicographic-by-address processing, algorithm pinned in spec, published test vectors with golden proof bytes. - **FM-15 KZG trusted-setup compromise. ** Universal forgery, silent, undetectable after the fact. *Fix:* IPA is the default; KZG is opt-in behind an audited ceremony with the verification key pinned in clients. - **FM-16 Quantum. ** Pedersen/IPA and KZG all die to Shor. *Fix:* Merkle profile is the standing fallback with a documented activation criterion. - **FM-17 Shape leakage. ** Proof length and path pattern leak clustering of coordinates. *Fix:* pad to depth buckets; honestly budget the residual side channel — this boundary cannot be fully closed while proofs remain minimal. - **FM-18 Depth exhaustion. ** Adversarial keys force depth-31 paths, bloating proofs. *Fix:* `D_MAX`, reject beyond; treat as consensus event. - **B1 — Current state only. ** Verkle/Merkle roots commit *now*. There is no history, no audit trail, no consistency-across-epochs proof short of a SNARK over transitions. Audit needs a separate append-only log anchored per epoch. Never mine history out of a state tree. - **B2 — Absence is relative to a root/epoch,** never eternal. - **B3 — Canonicalization freezes language semantics. ** Upgrading normalization rules means a new `ns_id` and a migration; in-place reinterpretation forks reality. - **B4 — Proof size scales with distinct stems,** and adversaries choose key placement; `D_MAX` bounds the damage, it does not remove it. The user is asking about a hard technical problem: compact Verkle/Merkle proofs that a neutral verifier can re-derive without the full tree, specifically in a "memlang / meta-token coordinate layer. " This appears to be a system where tokens/memes/content are addressed via some coordinate system, and we need cryptographic proofs of membership/non-membership that don't require the verifier to hold the full data structure. Let me think about this carefully. This is essentially the classic authenticated data structure problem: **Merkle proofs**: O(log n) sibling hashes per proof. Verifier needs only the root hash. Failure modes: proof forgery requires hash collision or root compromise; but proofs leak structure; update requires recomputing path. **Verkle proofs**: Uses vector commitments (e. , Pedersen commitments over inner-product-friendly curves like Bandersnatch), proof size O(log n) with IPA (inner product arguments) or constant-size with KZG (requires trusted setup) or bulletproof-style. Key property: branching factor k=256 means depth log_256(n), so ~4 levels for 2^32 keys vs 32 for binary Merkle. Proof aggregation across many keys is possible (IPA folding). **"memlang / meta-token coordinate layer"**: This sounds like a content-addressed semantic layer — tokens/memes mapped to coordinates in some space (possibly hierarchical: language → dialect → token → instance). The proof must attest "token T exists at coordinate C with payload P" without revealing or requiring the whole memlang lexicon/tree. So the answer needs to cover: - Coordinate encoding: canonical byte-encoding of the meta-token coordinate (must be canonical — no two encodings of same coordinate). - Tree over coordinates: 256-ary trie keyed by coordinate bytes (nibbles/bytes). Stem = shared prefix, suffix = terminal key. - Commitment scheme at each node: either Merkle hash or vector commitment. - For verkle: each node commits to its children's commitments as a 256-vector. Pedersen commitment: C_node = g^. actually multiplicative notation: C = Π g_i^{c_i} · h^r, where c_i are child commitments reduced mod q (need careful handling: child commitment is curve point; encode scalar by hashing point to field — standard trick: value committed is `hash_to_field(child_C)`). - Proof: for a single key, you need the commitments along the path + an opening proof that the leaf value is correct and that the path is consistent. - IPA-based (no trusted setup): Bulletproof-style inner product argument over the 256-length vector per level. Size ~log(k)·log(n) group elements, or aggregate across multiple keys to amortize. - KZG-based (trusted setup): constant-size per level (one proof), can aggregate all levels into one proof via evaluation interpolation. This is what Ethereum uses (Gwen's verkle spec uses Bandersnatch + IPA or KZG variants). - The verifier holds: root commitment, proof, key, value. Derives nothing else. Statelessness requirement satisfied. **Neutral-verifier re-derivation**: - Verifier must be able to check without trusted hardware, without the full tree, deterministically. - Verification algorithm must be total function of {root, proof, coordinate, claimed_value}. - Deterministic serialization (SSZ-like or RLP-like fixed rules) so that byte-for-byte reproduction is possible. - Domain separation tags on every hash/commitment input. **Edge cases / failure modes**: **Non-canonical coordinate encodings**: if a coordinate can be serialized two ways ("A|B" vs "A\0B" or UTF-8 normalization NFC vs NFD for memlang tokens), then two leaves exist for one logical token → split brain. Must define canonical form: NFC normalization for strings, fixed-width big-endian for numeric dims, length-prefixed segments, reject non-canonical at insert AND at verify (verifier checks encoding validity independently). **Empty subtree / zero-value ambiguity**: Is absence of a key equal to presence-with-empty-value? Must distinguish: (a) key absent (proof of non-membership requires showing the path diverges with the actual committed child values — i. , an extension-and-branch proof: show node has commitment where the relevant slot hashes to something else / is zero), (b) key present with empty value. If you conflate them, deletion = insertion of empty → replay/reorg attacks. Verkle tries handle this via stem nodes and suffix state: need explicit "absent" witness: open the commitment at the index to reveal 0 (or reveal the other child's value in Merkle case). **Hash-to-field reduction malleability**: In verkle, children commitments (curve points) are reduced to scalars before being committed. If reduction isn't injective-in-practice or if there are two valid encodings of a curve point (y-parity flag mishandling), attacker crafts two different trees with same root. Must use a canonical point encoding (compressed, one parity bit convention) and a domain-separated hash_to_field. Also: the scalar value 0 must be handled — committing a zero child is not the same as not having a child unless the scheme defines identity element mapping. Standard fix: commit `value = 0` means empty; ensure hash_to_field(point) never returns 0 for valid points (check and adjust, or offset by 1). **Proof-of-absence in verkle**: To prove a key is NOT present, you open the commitment at the position where the key would be, showing the stored value corresponds to a *different* stem/suffix. Two sub-cases: - Different stem: open parent node at child index i, show child commitment ≠ what it would be. actually the standard approach: you open the node to reveal the value at your index; the revealed value is the hash-to-field of another subtree whose stem differs from yours. But wait — the verifier can't see the other stem from just the scalar. So the proof must include enough info: either the other stem itself plus a binding check, or you rely on the fact that the leaf node contains stems and you do a second opening into the leaf node. Ethereum's verkle design: leaf nodes store both value(s) and the stem; proof of absence opens the leaf to show a different stem. Need TWO openings: one at intermediate level (showing which child pointer exists) and one at leaf (showing the stored stem ≠ queried stem). Edge case: forgetting the second opening lets you prove absence for a key that actually exists under a different-but-colliding path claim. Concrete attack: query key K, prover shows branch at index i pointing to subtree S, claims "K absent because S is a leaf with different stem" but doesn't prove the stem inside S — could actually contain K. Must bind the leaf-stem revelation into the same commitment opening. **Depth/extension ambiguity**: variable-depth tries (like MPT) have extension nodes; proofs get ambiguous about whether a missing nibble means "empty" or "deeper". Fixed-depth verkle tries (pad stems to 31 bytes, always 256-ary) eliminate this. If using variable depth, every proof step must carry explicit node-type tag and depth, and verifier must enforce depth monotonicity. **Aggregation edge cases (IPA/KZG batching)**: - Aggregated multi-proof: when proving N keys, some share stems (same leaf, different suffixes) — dedupe logic must be deterministic; otherwise prover picks different dedup → different proof bytes for same statement → non-determinism breaks neutral re-derivation and enables subtle malleability (two valid proofs for same claim → replay systems keyed on proof-hash break). - Zero vectors in IPA folding: if a node's commitment is identity, the folding argument degenerates (all-zero challenges); must handle identity elements explicitly or forbid empty internal nodes entirely (invariant: internal node exists iff ≥1 child non-empty — enforce at write time). - KZG: lagrange basis at 256 roots of unity; edge case where the evaluation polynomial degree < expected — prover submits low-degree polynomial that interpolates differently at challenge point. Mitigation: transcript-bound Fiat-Shamir including ALL commitments, not just subset; and degree check via proof polynomial degree bound (KZG guarantees this inherently if setup is honest, but transcript malleability isn't covered). **Fiat-Shamir / transcript binding failures**: If the challenge isn't bound to the full context (root, coordinate, claimed value, all prior commitments), attacker can grind proofs: generate many transcripts, pick one that verifies for wrong value. Concretely: challenge must hash(root || coordinate || value || path_commitments || previous_challenges). Missing any → existential forge via brute-force search over unbound fields. This is THE most common real-world break (see: various ZKP Fiat–Shamir attacks, e. , "Romeo and Juliet" style transcript attacks). **Coordinate collision / hash-truncation boundary**: If coordinates are hashed to 256 bits for addressing (to keep tree shallow), collisions exist in principle. Boundary decision: treat hash collision as consensus-fatal (two payloads claim same address) — detection requires storing full preimage at leaf and verifying preimage→hash at verify-time. Cost: verifier does one extra hash. Never skip this: without preimage check, attacker finds 160-bit truncated collision (trivially feasible for 160 bits? No — 2^80 work, borderline; for 128-bit truncation definitely feasible nation-state; for 256-bit fine) and swaps payload at same address with valid proof against same root. Rule: address width ≥ 256 bits, preimage always included in leaf and hashed during verification. **Update/staleness boundary**: A proof binds to a root. Neutral verifier must know WHICH root is authoritative and at which height. Failure mode: proof replay across epochs — old inclusion proof for a token since deleted still verifies against old root. Never accept "any valid root" — that turns deletion into a lie-by-omission service. **Merkle-specific edges** (if merkle fallback): - Unbalanced tree / depth leakage: proof length leaks coordinate prefix distribution (privacy). Bound: pad all proofs to max depth D_max; cost O(D_max) per proof regardless. - Second-preimage on internal nodes: hash(node) vs hash(leaf) confusion — classic Merkle second-preimage attack where attacker crafts a leaf whose contents look like an internal node. Fix: domain separation: H("L", data) vs H("N", left, right) or include length+depth in every node hash. - Odd-number-of-leaves duplication bug (Bitcoin CVE on Merkle trees): duplicating last element when odd count lets you prove inclusion of a fabricated element. Fix: pad with explicit sentinel (hash of empty string with domain tag), never duplicate. **Verifier neutrality constraints**: - All arithmetic in fixed-size fields (no bignum ambiguity), little/big-endian fixed. - No floating point anywhere in coordinate math (if coordinates are floats, they must be quantized to integers at canonicalization; float NaN/subnormal/±0 are poison — ±0. 0 distinct bit patterns map to same value → two canonical forms → violation of rule #1). - Proof parsing must be strictly bounded: no allocation proportional to untrusted length fields; cap proof size at D_max·k + overhead; parser rejects trailing garbage (else malleable proofs again). **What must never happen** (the invariant list): - Never verify a proof whose coordinate fails canonical-form validation. - Never accept a proof referencing a root outside the trusted/freshness set. - Never let the prover choose dedup/aggregation order freely — order must be a pure function of the sorted key list. - Never allow a "partial" verification path that skips the leaf-stem binding (absence case). - Never emit identical proof bytes for different (key,value) pairs — implies hash collision or scheme break; assert and halt. - Never trust depth/length metadata in the proof; derive from coordinate bytes and node types encountered. - Never mix curve contexts / domain tags across layers (memlang namespace A and B sharing a tree without namespace in the hash → cross-namespace proof replay: proof for token in namespace A verifies in namespace B if coordinates coincide). Domain-separate by namespace id in EVERY hash call. - Never allow value-dependent shortcuts ("small values skip commitment") — creates inequality channels. **Size numbers, concrete**: - Binary Merkle: depth 32 for 2^32 keys, proof ≈ 32 × 32B hashes = ~1KB/key, verify = 32 hashes (~microseconds), no trusted setup, post-quantum-vulnerable (hash-based though — actually hash-based Merkle IS PQ-safe, unlike verkle/Pedersen/KZG). - Verkle 256-ary: depth 4 for 2^32 keys. 5bd15429a88e9e42.text: # Compact Verkle/Merkle Proofs at a Provenance Gate: Failure Modes, Boundaries, Invariants ## Trust model (pinned, so the edges are well-defined) Prover holds full tree `T`. Verifier holds exactly: one trusted root `R` (from an append-only anchor), the claim `(key, value, epoch)`, and the proof `π`. Verifier re-derives `R` from `(key, value, π)` alone. No tree, no siblings, no oracle. Everything below is an edge of that contract. Cryptographic failure modes **FM-1: Unbound challenge → cross-root proof replay. If the KZG/IPA opening point `z` is derived by Fiat–Shamir over anything less than the *full* transcript — root bytes, every key, every claimed value, the epoch — a proof minted for root `R₁` can verify against root `R₂`. Guard: `z = H(domain ‖ R ‖ all_keys ‖ all_values ‖ epoch)`; the root is a first-class transcript input, never implicit context. **FM-2: SRS mismatch. KZG proofs are only sound relative to the structured reference string they were created under. Two SRS generations in circulation = two incompatible proof universes, and a subverted SRS = universal forgery. Guard: pin the SRS fingerprint in the same anchor that publishes `R`; verifier rejects any proof whose SRS id ≠ pinned id. Never ship a verifier that auto-downloads SRS by URL. **FM-3: Index→evaluation-point non-injectivity. Each child index must map to a distinct field element within a node's width. With BLS12-381's scalar field (~2²⁵⁵) and 8-bit indices this is trivially safe — but any scheme packing wider identifiers (64-bit child ids, composite `(level, index)` tuples) into `Fr` without a canonical fixed-width encoding risks collisions modulo `p`, and worse, *ambiguous* encodings (`(1,2)` vs `(12,)` concatenating identically). Guard: fixed-width big-endian, length-prefixed composites, injectivity argued once in the spec. **FM-4: The 31-byte field limit vs 32-byte data. `Fr` in BLS12-381 safely holds 31 bytes. Naively packing a 32-byte hash or value into one field element silently drops the high bit or wraps. This is a silent-corruption class bug: proofs verify perfectly against corrupted values. Guard: two-limb packing or hash-then-commit; test vector with `0xFF…FF` (all-ones 32 bytes) must round-trip. **FM-5: Empty-subtree / point-at-infinity handling. Commitment to an empty child is the identity element. Compressed encodings of infinity vary by library; some parsers reject it (legitimate empty-subtree proofs fail), others accept malformed bytes as infinity (forgery surface). Guard: one normative infinity encoding, explicit parser branch, fuzzed against both behaviors. **FM-6: Non-canonical group encodings. Sign-flipped y-coordinates, off-curve points, wrong-subgroup points (mandatory check if G2 ever appears — G1 cofactor is 1, G2's is not). Consequence: two byte-distinct proofs for one statement break dedup, replay ledgers, and audit-log binding. Guard: reject non-canonical serializations; subgroup-check everything. **FM-7: Sloppy batch verification. Random-linear-combination batching of many proofs: if the coefficients aren't Fiat–Shamir-bound to *every* statement in the batch, one forged statement hides among honest ones. Guard: `coeffs = H(all statements ‖ all proofs)`; never accept client-supplied or counter-based coefficients. Structural failure modes **FM-8: Variable depth / unary-node compression. Lazy trees that collapse single-child chains make path length ambiguous: the same key validates at depth 5 and depth 8. Guard: depth is a protocol constant, `D = ⌈keybits / log₂(W)⌉`; proof carries no depth field to negotiate. If compression exists, the compressed run must be committed with a distinct domain tag. **FM-9: Internal-node vs leaf commitment collision. If `H(children…)` and `H(value)` use the same hash with no tag, an attacker relabels an internal node as a leaf payload (or vice versa) and the parent hash still matches. Guard: domain-separated commitment inputs — `H(0x01 ‖ …)` for internal, `H(0x02 ‖ …)` for leaf — fixed forever. **FM-10: Stem/suffix split drift. Verkle stems (e. , 31-byte prefix + 1-byte suffix) are a normative constant. Two implementations splitting at 30+2 produce mutually rejected honest proofs — a cross-client fork discovered in production. Guard: one constant, conformance vectors, cross-impl CI. **FM-11: Zero-value vs absent-key conflation. In a KZG vector commitment, "never written" and "written as zero" are the same polynomial evaluation. Any gate decision distinguishing them (revocation lists, tombstones, non-existence attestations) is unsound on a single commitment. Guard: parallel presence-bitmap commitment, or a reserved marker byte in the value slot. Never let gate logic read absence out of a zero. **FM-12: Stale-root replay across epochs. Chain of verkle roots: proof for key `k` minted at epoch `e` replayed at epoch `e+5` after the value changed. Guard: epoch is inside the signed claim and inside the FS transcript; gate matches proof's root to the claim's epoch exactly — no "any recent root" windows. **FM-13: Snapshot/check race (TOCTOU). Prover snapshots at `v`, gate resolves "latest" at `v+1`: spurious rejection. Gate pins `v`, claim says "current": stale acceptance presented as fresh. Guard: claim schema carries explicit version; staleness policy is a declared bound, never implicit. **FM-14: Verification-only vs reconstruction-capable format mismatch. Committed as a tree; **root `R_e` is anchored per epoch `e`** in an append-only head log. - **Scout**: emits `{epoch, key, value_hash, auth_path}` claiming "key `k` maps to `v` in frontier at `R_e`" (membership) or "`k` ∉ frontier at `R_e`" (non-membership). - **Burn**: a **mutation** — remove `k` from the frontier tree, append `(k, e)` to a separate burn-log commitment, publish `R_{e+1}`. Burns are the dangerous operations. - **Neutral verifier**: holds only the anchored head roots, the pinned crypto parameters (hash ID; SRS/generator-point hash for Verkle), and the proof. **It does not hold the tree and must never request intermediate nodes from anyone. The core tension: cryptographic proof validity is timeless; pipeline correctness is time-scoped. Almost every serious failure below is that tension leaking through some seam. Concrete proof formats and the minimal verifier ### Binary sparse Merkle (default choice for n ≤ ~2²⁴ and single-key proofs) tag       u8    0x01 MEMBER | 0x02 ABSENT epoch     u64   little-endian, pinned endianness value     32B   H(payload); for ABSENT: explicit ABSENT_SENTINEL ≠ any H() output siblings  32B × 256   sibling[i] = sibling hash at depth i (bit i of key selects side) def verify(p, head_roots): tag in (MEMBER, ABSENT)          # fail closed h = H(b"L" + p. value)             # LEAF prefix — see §3. for i in reversed(range(256)):            # depth from CONSTANT, not input key >> i) & 1                  # side from KEY BITS, never an index field h = H(b"N" + (sib + h if b else h + sib)) r = head_roots[p. tag == MEMBER: return p. epoch == head_epoch and h == r # ABSENT additionally requires value == ABSENT_SENTINEL semantics (§3. return h == r Size floor: `32·ceil(log2 n) + 32` bytes → **~800 B at n = 2²⁴**. No smaller honest option exists for a single-key binary Merkle proof. ### Verkle (branching w = 256, stem = first 31 bytes, suffix = 1 byte) Per level: the `w−1` sibling commitments `C_j` plus one IPA opening `π_i` proving the parent's committed vector contains the correct child commitment at the key-derived position. Leaf level: stem commitment over a `w`-length value vector, opened at the suffix. verify chain, top-down, EVERY level: v_i = open(C_parent, pos_i = key_bits[level], π_i)      # IPA eval at position assert v_i[pos_i] == C_child_provided                   # ← the check people skip assert v_leaf[suffix] == commit(value) or == ABSENT encoding Critical honesty about compactness: **a single-key Verkle proof is larger than a Merkle proof** (~34 KB naive: 255 sibling points × 4 levels + IPA args). A variable-depth "depth bomb" (claimed 2²⁰ segments) is a pure verifier-DoS vector otherwise. **F20 — Index-field trusting. ** Sibling placement derived from an attacker-supplied integer instead of key bits → reorderings verify against unintended positions. Side is a *function of the key*, full stop. **F21 — Degenerate-tree special cases done implicitly. ** Empty tree (`H_empty` explicit constant, specified), single-leaf tree (depth-0 path: zero siblings — must still do the root equality check and leaf-prefix hash; skipping comparison because "nothing to hash up" is a real bug class), absence-proof-against-empty-tree (must still anchor-match; implementations routinely wave these through). **F22 — Duplicate frontier inserts. ** Blind-append upstream creates a shadow leaf: first burn consumes the visible one, the shadow later proves present. Insert path is upsert-with-uniqueness-enforcement, never append. **F23 — Fail-open under verifier outage. ** The only acceptable degraded mode is stall-and-queue. Any "bypass verification to keep throughput" path converts every other failure above from recoverable to catastrophic. Hard boundaries (numbers, not vibes) | Boundary | Value | Rationale | | Use Merkle, not Verkle | batch < ~15 keys/epoch | Single-key Verkle ≈ 34 KB > 800 B Merkle; compaction only amortizes via multiproofs | | Mutation freshness | `proof. epoch == head_epoch`, exact | F1; no tolerance window on writes | | Read freshness | `Δ_read` ≤ small fixed constant (spec'd) | bounded staleness, logged | | Canonical depth | 256 (binary) / 31B stem + 1B suffix (Verkle) | kills F10/F11/F19 | | Inline value cap | 32–64 B (a hash) | payloads out-of-band, gated by `H(P)` check | | Roots per epoch | exactly 1 | F2 equivocation = halt | | Loop bounds | constants only | F19 | What must never happen — the invariant list Leaf and node serialization must never be interchangeable. A burn must never authorize against a non-head root; proof validity must never substitute for epoch currency. Equivocating roots must never be silently resolved. Absence must never be inferred from a zero opening when zero is encodable. Control-flow bounds must never come from untrusted proof bytes. Group elements and scalars must never skip canonicality/subgroup validation. Sibling placement must never come from a supplied index — key bits only.
