Nothing else is the ledger. - **Entry *i*** embeds the running root of everything before it: `prev_root = r_{i-1}`. The running root is `r_i = H("root" || r_{i-1} || h_i)` where `h_i = H("entry" || canonical(entry_i))`. Incremental — computing `r_i` needs only `r_{i-1}` and entry *i*, never the whole history. - **Seat** = ephemeral worker. It trusts exactly two things at spawn: the pinned genesis and the latest externally anchored checkpoint. Its entire worldview is re-derived from entries. The ledger *is* the seat's memory. - Tamper-evident, not tamper-proof: enforcement comes from append-only ACLs, a WORM anchor, and signed checkpoints — not from the hash chain alone. ## Formats (canonical, deterministic encoding — fixed-width ints, length-prefixed fields, no map-order ambiguity) GENESIS (one immutable object, ~200B) magic "GLDG1", ledger_id 32B hash_alg blake3, sig_alg ed25519 r0 = BLAKE3("GLDG1/genesis" || ledger_id) checkpoint_pk (ed25519 public key, pinned here) interval { max_entries: 1000, max_seconds: 30 } ENTRY i  (key: e/<seq:016x>, one atomic PUT) seq        u64 = i prev_root  32B = r_{i-1}          ← the per-entry commitment to the prior root ts_ms      u64                    ← advisory only; seq defines order kind       u8                     ← SCOUT_REPORT | BURN | CURSOR | LEASE_GRANT | FORK_MARK payload    bytes (large payloads: 32B payload_hash + content-addressed blob ref) h_i = BLAKE3("GLDG1/entry" || canonical(entry_i)) r_i = BLAKE3("GLDG1/root"  || r_{i-1} || h_i) CHECKPOINT (every ≤ min(1000 entries, 30s); written to 2 stores, one WORM/object-lock) seq k, root r_k, ts_ms state_hash 32B   ← optional: BLAKE3 of derived-state serialization sig = ed25519(checkpoint_pk, ledger_id || seq || root || ts_ms || state_hash) Note what's already persisted implicitly: `r_i` survives as `entry_{i+1}. The only roots stored explicitly are `r_0` (genesis) and `r_k` (checkpoints). ## Invariants a verifier checks (all four, in order) **Decode**: every entry parses canonically. prev_root == r_{i-1}`, recomputed forward from `r_0` or from a checkpoint. This is the per-entry prior-root commitment; a mismatch at `j+1` localizes tampering to entries `≤ j` in one pass. **Anchor**: recomputed root at seq *k* equals the checkpoint root; signature verifies against the pinned pk; both anchor copies agree (disagreement → take the WORM copy, alert). **Prefix rule**: trailing bytes that fail decode or link are not entries. A torn tail from a mid-write death is garbage beyond the head, ignored — never truncated-in-place, never repaired. Cascade property: modify entry *j* → `h_j` changes → `r_j` changes → `entry_{j+1}. Any edit anywhere before the head breaks the link at the first touched entry, and breaks the anchored checkpoint root in aggregate. ## Persists (complete list — nothing else survives death) - **P1** Genesis object. - **P2** Entry objects. Append-only ACL, retention forever. ~60B + payload each. This is the *only* source of truth. - **P3** Payload blobs, content-addressed at `b/<blake3>`, referenced by hash from entries. Blobs are data, not state — they persist. GC only when zero live references (ref count is derivable from the ledger). - **P4** Signed checkpoints, every ≤ (1000 entries, 30 s), each anchored to two stores, one WORM. ~150B + 64B sig. - **P5** Optional state snapshot inside a checkpoint. **Advisory cache, not truth**: it carries its own `state_hash`; on mismatch with the recomputed fold, discard and replay from genesis. A cache without a verification handle is forbidden. ## Recomputes (never persisted, or persisted only as self-verifying cache) - **R1** `r_i` for any *i*: O(1) per step; O(i−k) from the last checkpoint. - **R2** Inclusion/consistency proofs: Merkle tree over `h_i` up to the last checkpoint. Build O(n) on demand, proof O(log n). Tree nodes are disposable cache. - **R4** Indexes: seq *is* the key; time index = binary search (ts enforced non-decreasing per writer); payload-key index = external disposable store or O(n) rebuild. - **R5** Writer-lease liveness: last `LEASE_GRANT` entry + TTL against wall clock. Lease state lives in the ledger; liveness is recomputed. - **R6** Torn-tail trim via the prefix rule. GET genesis; verify magic + pinned pk. GET latest anchored checkpoint `(k, r_k)`; verify sig; verify both anchors agree. Stream entries `k+1. head` (segment reads); check link + decode per entry; trim torn tail per prefix rule; compute `r_head`. Rebuild derived state: load snapshot if `state_hash` verifies against the fold; else fold from genesis (slow path) or refuse-to-serve per policy. Acquire writer lease (conditional PUT, TTL 15 s); only then write `LEASE_GRANT` at seq `head+1`. Resume frontier from the last `CURSOR` entry; re-scan the gap since it; dedupe against the replayed burned set. Cost: O(K) reads + O(K) fold, independent of *n*. K = 1000 → sub-second. ## Failure windows, ruled exactly - **Die between entry PUT and checkpoint**: covered by tail replay; no loss, no dup (seq-keyed conditional PUTs). - **Die mid-PUT**: torn tail dropped by prefix rule. - **Two writers (split-brain across respawn)**: conditional PUT (`if-none-match`) on the seq key → loser gets a conflict, re-syncs, its entry never lands. Seats are interchangeable executors/validators. - A seat owns **zero trusted local state**. Local memory and local disk are treated as lost-on-death and hostile-if-present. Everything authoritative lives in shared durable storage: an immutable object store (S3-class or POSIX with fsync) plus an atomically-updatable pointer. - Threat model: adversary can corrupt stored bytes, kill the seat at any instruction boundary, and feed stale/orphaned artifacts on respawn. Adversary cannot break BLAKE3/Ed25519 and does not hold signer keys. Hashes: BLAKE3, 32-byte. State: content-addressed Merkle trie (Jellyfish/Patricia variant). Law code: deterministic WASM, gas-metered. **Entry** `E_i`, the only unit of writing: seq        : u64            // == i, strictly prior+1 kind       : enum           // COMMIT | CHECKPOINT | LAW_DEPLOY | ANCHOR_RCPT | REJECT_RCPT ns         : u8             // leaf namespace tag law_ref    : (law_seq, law_hash)   // law version that adjudicates this entry payload    : bytes          // opaque to transport; interpreted by law code prev_root  : H256           // == R_{i-1} sig        : Ed25519 over BLAKE3("ltg/v1" || all fields above) h_i = BLAKE3("leaf" || kind || ns || u64le(i) || BLAKE3(payload) || prev_root || law_hash || pk_hint) R_i = MMR-root after appending h_i      // MMR, not naive chain Why MMR: append is O(log n) (~30 hash updates even at 10⁹ entries), inclusion proofs are O(log n) against any known root, and the current peak vector is O(log n) — small enough to embed in every checkpoint. **CHECKPOINT entry** (every K = 4096 COMMITs): { mmr_peaks : [H256]        // full peak vector at seq c — O(log n) state_root: H256          // root of materialized trie at seq c law_active: (law_seq, law_hash) Checkpoints are ordinary entries — same chaining, same signatures. They are the respawn anchors. **Law artifacts**: WASM modules in the object store, address = BLAKE3(module). Genesis (`seq 0`) installs the initial law module and the initial governor keyset. A LAW_DEPLOY entry carries `(new_law_hash, effective_seq, m-of-n governor sigs)`; governors are themselves installed by earlier LAW_DEPLOY entries. Rules change only through the log — there is no out-of-band rule channel. Old artifacts are pinned forever (needed for replay-from-genesis audits). The invariant lattice — where "code-as-law" bites All adjudication flows through one choke function; there is no second write path: apply(S_{i-1}, E_i, law) -> Accept(S_i) | Reject(reason)     // pure, deterministic Invariants are stratified; the strata have different failure semantics: | Level | Class | Monotonicity | Violation meaning | | L0 | Structural: seq continuity, `prev_root` match, sig valid under recorded keyset, `law_ref` ∈ deployed set | Permanent | **Corruption/tamper event** — halt, alarm, do not rewind silently | | L1 | Conservation: Σ balances constant, counters only increment, no asset creation outside mint entries | Preserved by every legal transition ⇒ true-at-checkpoint implies true-for-all-j ≤ checkpoint | Corruption event | | L2 | Authorization: per-entry permission vs. current ACL state | Transient | Reject at admission | | L3 | Application semantics: business rules as pure functions | Transient | Reject at admission | The lattice property that matters operationally: **L1 truths are upward-closed along the reachability order** `S ⊑ S′ ⟺ S′ reachable from S via legal transitions`. You never recheck L1 globally; you prove preservation per-transition, and checkpoint-time spot checks (recompute Σ balances from trie at each checkpoint, compare to accumulator in state) catch any drift cheaply. Per COMMIT batch (group-commit m entries): Validate all m through `apply` against hot state. Any reject → emit REJECT_RCPT instead, exclude from batch. Write entry objects to store under content addresses (`data/<h_i>`), fsync/PUT-complete. Mismatch → discard snapshot, step back to previous checkpoint; if none, replay from genesis. Snapshots are an optimization, never an authority. **Load law artifact** by hash from checkpoint's `law_active`; verify content hash. Trust is never inherited from anything on disk | **Never persists:** mutable state outside the log; any locally-cached verdict accepted without recomputation; nondeterministic law code (wall-clock, floats, unordered iteration). Single-writer assumption is real: multi-seat concurrent appending needs a leader or BFT ordering layer beneath HEAD. Throughput ceiling is the group-commit batch size × store PUT latency; scale by sharding namespaces, each with its own MMR and checkpoint cadence, cross-shard transfers as entries touching two namespaces with paired receipts. Both limits are architectural boundaries, not open problems. fd590c973c2e0e1b.text: # Ledger of Empty Chairs — Deterministic Append-Only Root Chain (Spec v1) **Invariant:** Given the same genesis constant and the same admitted sequence of entries, any two conforming implementations produce **bit-identical** `root_n` after every append, and reject exactly the same inputs. Everything below is normative (MUST/SHOULD language is binding). Flavor anchor: the hall opens with every chair empty. An *Usher* (sequencer) appends records of chairs being occupied, vacated, or sealed shut forever. The root after each entry is rung on the Bell Post; anyone holding a past Bell Post value can prove any seat's history against it. Primitives and pinned constants | Hash function | SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4), no truncation | | Integer encoding | Unsigned, fixed-width, **big-endian**, always | | Text encoding | Raw ASCII bytes, range `0x21–0x7E` only (printable, **no space** — space invites trim bugs). No Unicode, no normalization, no case folding, anywhere | | Floats | **Forbidden** in hashed bytes. Quantities use fixed-point `u64`/`i64` with a schema-declared scale | | Empty-tree root | `SHA-256("")` = `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855` (pinned literal; never "computed fresh") | | Hash domain tags | `0x00` leaf, `0x01` interior node, `0x02` ledger root wrap, `0x04` entry hash | Canonical entry encoding One byte-exact layout. No padding, no optional omission, no maps, no JSON. Total entry size MUST be ≤ 8192 bytes. u16be  schema_version        // 0x0001; readers MUST reject others (fail closed) u64be  entry_index           // 0-based; MUST equal current entry count 32B    prev_root             // root after previous entry; entry 0 uses GENESIS_ROOT u32be  actor_len             // 1. bytes  actor                 // ASCII 0x21–0x7E, e. u8     action_tag            // see table u64be  logical_clock         // Lamport-style; MUST be > max clock seen (genesis max = 0) u64be  wall_time_ms          // Unix epoch UTC, milliseconds; MUST be >= prior entry's bytes  payload               // exact layout per action_tag; no trailing slack **Action table (v1):** | Tag | Name | Payload layout | | `0x01` | OCCUPY | `u32be chair_id` ‖ `u64be session_nonce` (12 B) | | `0x02` | VACATE | `u32be chair_id` ‖ `u8 reason_code` (5 B) | | `0x03` | SEAL | `u32be chair_id` ‖ `u8 reason_code` ‖ `u32be seal_epoch` (9 B) — chair permanently empty | | `0x04` | VOTE | `32B ballot_id` ‖ `u8 choice` ‖ `u64be weight` (42 B) | | `0x05` | NOTE | raw bytes, 0. 4096 B, copied verbatim | | `0x06` | ATTEST | `32B external_root` ‖ `u32be src_len(1. 64)` ‖ `src` ASCII | Strictness rules: for fixed-size tags, `payload_len` MUST equal the exact listed size; `NOTE` allows 0. The encoding is self-delimiting (every variable-length field is length-prefixed), so concatenating entries is unambiguous and hashing needs no outer length wrapper. entry_hash_i = SHA-256(0x04 || canon(entry_i)) MTH([])     = SHA-256("")                                  // pinned constant above MTH([d0])   = SHA-256(0x00 || d0) MTH(D[0:n]) = SHA-256(0x01 || MTH(D[0:k]) || MTH(D[k:n])) where k = largest power of two < n           // RFC 6962 split, pinned root_n      = SHA-256(0x02 || u64be(n) || MTH([entry_hash_0 . entry_hash_{n-1}])) GENESIS_ROOT = SHA-256(0x02 || u64be(0) || SHA-256("")) Implementers MUST compute `GENESIS_ROOT` once, hardcode the resulting 32 bytes, and verify it against the KAT suite (§7). Never leave it symbolic at runtime. The `0x02` wrap additionally binds the count `n` explicitly. Admission (deterministic MUSTs) An incoming entry is appended iff **all** hold; otherwise it is rejected with no side effects: `schema_version == 1`; `action_tag` in table; payload size exact. `prev_root == current_root` (bytewise). `wall_time_ms >= previous entry's wall_time_ms`. Text fields valid ASCII-printable, lengths within bounds, total ≤ 8192 B. **Batch ordering:** when the Usher admits *m* candidates in one tick, sort them by `(logical_clock ascending, entry_hash bytewise ascending)` and append in that order, re-running admission sequentially. **Fork rule:** if two histories reach the same `entry_index` with different roots, halt and raise `HEAD_USHER_CONFLICT`. Do not merge, do not pick a winner heuristically. Audit path, defined recursively (matches the tree split above): PATH(i, D): if |D| == 1: return [] k = largest power of two < |D| if i < k: return PATH(i, D[0:k]) ++ [MTH(D[k:n])] else:     return PATH(i-k, D[k:n]) ++ [MTH(D[0:k])] Verification walks the index bits LSB-first: fn = SHA-256(0x00 || entry_hash_i); j = i for s in path: if j even: fn = SHA-256(0x01 || fn || s) else:      fn = SHA-256(0x01 || s  || fn) accept iff fn == MTH portion recovered and reconstructed root == published root_n A prover supplies `canon(entry_i)`; the verifier recomputes `entry_hash_i`, checks `prev_root` chains back to `GENESIS_ROOT` if the full prefix is supplied, and checks the path against the published root. Storage frame (tamper-evident at rest) Each segment record on disk: `u32be canon_len || canon(entry) || 32B root_after`. Replay recomputes everything and compares byte-for-byte; any edit, deletion, or reorder breaks the recomputed root. The hard artifact is a transition that **does nothing at the commitment level** when its gate fails: the post-state root is byte-identical to the pre-state root, the actor's nonce is untouched, and the same transaction may be legally retried later. ## §1 Formal Definition Let Σ be the set of world states, ρ: Σ → {0,1}²⁵⁶ the commitment root function (§5. 2), Tx the set of well-formed transactions. ** The gated transition is a total function T : Σ × Tx → Σ × Receipt T(σ, tx) = ( Apply(σ, tx),  APPLIED(new_root) )   if G(σ, tx) = ⊤ T(σ, tx) = ( σ,             REFUSE(code)  )       if G(σ, tx) = ⊥ where **G** is the gate predicate (§4) evaluated purely against σ. **Property P1 (Refusal Identity — the core invariant). ∀σ, tx: G(σ,tx)=⊥ ⟹ T returns the *identical* state object σ, therefore ρ(σ_post) = ρ(σ_pre)   as raw 32-byte strings   (Level 1) bytes(canon(σ_post)) = bytes(canon(σ_pre))         (Level 2, implied) **Property P2 (Free Gate / No Side Effect Law). ** The refusal branch performs **zero** tree writes. Consequently *nothing* may live inside ρ that a refusal would perturb: no nonce bump, no height bump, no fee burn, no counters, no timestamps. Any spam-resistance mechanism must operate **off-root** (mempool admission, journaling, bonding settled only in APPLIED transactions). Violating P2 breaks byte-identity. **Property P3 (Retry Legality). ** Because refusals consume no nonce, the identical signed transaction may be resubmitted arbitrarily often until the precondition becomes true. Replay protection is enforced *only* against successfully applied transactions (§5. **Property P4 (Determinism). ** G and the effect function read only σ and tx. No clocks, RNG, floats, or iteration-order leakage. ## §2 State Schema (all inside the root) All integers are **unsigned 64-bit, little-endian, fixed 8-byte**. All digests are **BLAKE3-256**, unkeyed, with a 1-byte domain tag prepended to the preimage. Tags: leaf `0x01`, node `0x02`, txid `0x03`, sighash `0x04`, lineage `0x05`, journal `0x06`, address `0x07`. height  : u64                          // increments ONLY on APPLIED accounts: Map<Addr(32B) → Account> chairs  : Map<u64 chair_id → Chair> Account ::= nonce:u64 | weight:u64 | seated:u64      // seated = 0 ⇔ none; chair ids start at 1 Chair   ::= status:u8 | occupant:Addr(32B) | threshold:u64 | lineage:Digest(32B) // status: 0x00 = EMPTY, 0x01 = CLAIMED; occupant = 32×0x00 iff EMPTY Reading a missing account yields the **default** `{nonce:0, weight:0, seated:0}` (writes materialize it). Reading a missing chair does **not** default — it fails gate clause G1. `weight` is written **exclusively** by out-of-scope `WITNESS_EMPTYING` transitions; `CLAIM_CHAIR` treats it read-only. 2 Tree keys (raw byte strings, sorted byte-wise lexicographic) b"a" ++ addr            → canon(Account)     // 65-byte value b"c" ++ u64le(chair_id) → canon(Chair)       // 73-byte value b"\xffmeta:height"      → u64le(height)      // 8-byte value `canon(X)` = concatenation of fields in declared field order, fixed widths, no tags, no padding. Receipt APPLIED(R₁). **Attempt 3** — replay of Attempt 2's bytes: `REJECT(STALE_NONCE)` (expected 1, found 0… actually expected `accounts[A]. nonce=1`, tx says 0). 56aef73ecd947078.text: # Red-Team Analysis: Gated Transition with Byte-Identical Refusal Root Pin the semantics first (mitigations are meaningless without this) - State is Merkle-ized, canonically serialized. Height `n`, root `R_n`. - Transition `T = (sender, payload, precondition-proof P, gate_schema_id)`. - Gate `G(S_n, T) → APPLY | REFUSE(code)`. On REFUSE, the block still finalizes but seals with `R_{n+1} ≡ R_n` byte-for-byte; the refusal record `(height, tx_idx, code, signer)` goes to a **side-log outside the root**. - Consensus: BFT, `N = 3f+1`, quorum `2f+1`, rotating leader, view timeout `T_v = 2Δ + ε`. **Spec decision that makes the whole design possible:** "byte-identical root" applies to the **main state root `R_main` only**. Metering, refusal logs, and escrow live in a separately committed accumulator `R_side`. If you demand identity over *all* roots, no metering or logging is possible and you're left with nothing but mempool caps. Everything below assumes this separation. **Four invariants under attack:** - **I1** Verdict determinism: all honest replicas compute the same verdict for `(S_n, T)`. - **I2** Refusal immutability: REFUSE ⇒ `R_{n+1} ≡ R_n`. - **I3** Precondition soundness: APPLY ⇒ precondition genuinely held, with attributable proof. - **I4** Liveness floor: legitimate attempts eventually apply or produce attributable refusal; no silent infinite freeze. Every bypass below reduces to attacking one of these. ## Layer 1 — Consensus plane Equivocal split-verdict proposals (→I1). ** Leader signs two different `T` at the same `(height, round)` — one where the precondition passes, one where it fails — feeding each to a subset. **Mitigation:** one signature slot per `(height, round)`; conflicting QCs are deterministic slashable evidence; leader schedule derived from VRF over committed seed (removes timing discretion). Refusal-finality helps here: once a refusal block commits, `T` cannot be retried at that height — retries consume fresh heights, which enables the height-budget cap in #3. Quorum-starvation freeze (→I4). ** Adversary withholds votes so the precondition quorum never forms. Every block REFUSEs with `QUORUM_UNAVAILABLE`, roots stay byte-identical, monitoring shows "consensus healthy. " The flock is dead while looking correct. **Mitigation:** deterministic escalation ladder: after `K = f+1` consecutive view timeouts on the same gate id, auto-inject a reconfiguration transition (rotating the precondition oracle/quorum spec) at the next height — itself requiring `2f+1`, so sustaining the freeze costs the attacker more than their budget. If the reconfig also times out `M` times, issue a **signed halt certificate** and stop. Halting is recoverable; forking is not. Refusal-spam / log bloat (→I2 tension, DoS). ** Refusals mutate nothing, so flooding looks free. **Mitigation:** (a) block caps: `B_g` gated txs/block, `G_max` gate-gas/block; (b) per-sender gas escrow in `R_side` — gas is **burned on REFUSE** from escrow, settled into `R_main` only on APPLY (this preserves byte-identity while making spam expensive); (c) mempool: ≤1 in-flight gated tx per sender, replaceable only by higher fee. Precondition-proof replay (→I3). ** Valid `P` (QC, capability, attestation) from height `n` replayed at `n+k` after expiry. **Mitigation:** stateless freshness by construction — every `P` carries `(chain_id, flock_id, expiry_height e, subject_hash h_T = H(canon(T)))`; gate checks `n ≤ e ∧ h_T matches ∧ ids match`. No replay cache (a cache would be state and violate I2). Window `w ≥ 3·T_v` so honest propagation can't expire mid-flight. Cross-instance replay (→I3). ** Sibling swarm with shared formats. **Mitigation:** `chain_id`/`flock_id` in every signed object; genesis hash as domain-separation prefix on every signature; keys registered per-instance. ## Layer 2 — Gate input/context plane Hidden context reads (→I1). ** Gate reads wall clock, entropy, filesystem, network, or iterates maps in insertion order → replicas diverge. **Mitigation:** static schema enforcement at gate registration: declared read-set ⊆ `{S_n paths, T fields}`; interpreter forbids syscalls, entropy, floats (fixed-point only); sorted-key iteration mandatory; conformance harness runs every gate twice with shuffled map orders and asserts identical verdict + trace hash. Non-conforming bytecode is rejected at registration — deterministic admission. Clock-skew boundary race (→I1). ** Precondition valid on `[t0, t1]`; crafted so half the replicas evaluate pre-deadline, half post. **Mitigation:** time source is committed block time `τ_n` = median of proposer timestamps over the last 11 blocks — never local clocks. Boundary rule encoded exactly: pass iff `t0 < τ_n ≤ t1` (half-open, documented). Registration rejects windows narrower than `2·margin`, `margin = 2·drift_max + Δ`. Membership-version race (→I1/I3). ** "Signed by majority of current flock" is ambiguous while membership churn is in flight. **Mitigation:** membership is versioned (`S. memb_ver`); `P` must carry the version `v` it was formed against; gate enforces `v == S. memb_ver` else `REFUSE(STALE_MEMBERSHIP)`. Block validity rule: a block containing a membership change **must not** contain gated transitions referencing that subsystem — validator-enforced, deterministic. Oracle feed manipulation (→I3). ** Compromised or bribed oracle reports the precondition as satisfied. **Mitigation:** gate consumes only the committed feed `F_{n−1}`, never a live query. Feed = median of `2j+1` staked reporters; if spread > band `δ` ⇒ `REFUSE(ORACLE_DIVERGENCE)` — **fail-closed**. Fraud proofs slash misreporters. Attestation rollback / stale TEE counters (→I3). **Mitigation:** attestation must embed `H(header_{n−1})` and height `h ∈ [n−w, n]`; device monotonic counters checked against last-known values kept in `R_side` (keeps `R_main` clean); regression ⇒ `REFUSE(COUNTER_REGRESSION)`. ## Layer 3 — Cryptographic plane Signature malleability (→I1/I3). **Mitigation:** strict canonical verification: low-s enforced, fixed-width encodings, non-canonical input **rejected at parse, never normalized**; Ed25519 per RFC 8032 strict rules; dedup keyed on canonical bytes. Rogue-key aggregate forgery (→I3). ** BLS aggregation lets an attacker forge an aggregate without holders' consent. **Mitigation:** proof-of-possession required at registration (gate checks the registration flag in state); MuSig2 coefficient binding for Schnorr multisigs. Threshold-set ambiguity (→I3). ** "k-of-n" where `n` drifts between signing and evaluation. **Mitigation:** `P` snapshots the exact signer-id set and weights at formation; gate recomputes weight sum against `S. memb_ver`; mismatch ⇒ `REFUSE(THRESHOLD_MISMATCH)`. Zero interpretive freedom. ## Layer 4 — Execution / refusal-path plane Hidden mutation on refuse (→I2). ** Memoization caches, journals, or lazy writes survive the refusal; the *next* block's root differs. **Mitigation:** copy-on-write sandbox per tx; REFUSE ⇒ overlay discarded wholesale; **seal-time assertion `R' == R_n`, else deterministic halt + signed halt certificate**. CI fuzzing with instrumented allocation detects any write to committed pages on the REFUSE path. Refusal events route to side-log only. Serialization non-canonicity (→I1/I2). ** Equivalent-but-distinct encodings (non-minimal varints, duplicate map keys, NaNs) → two replicas serialize "the same" state differently. **Mitigation:** one canonical codec: minimal varints, sorted keys, fixed-point only, strict UTF-8, duplicate keys rejected. Roots computed over canonical bytes. Differential conformance tests across implementations with an adversarial encoding corpus. Reason-code oracle probing (→I3 confidentiality). ** Fine-grained error messages let the attacker binary-search the precondition bit by bit. **Mitigation:** four-code public taxonomy `{MALFORMED, EXPIRED, UNAUTHORIZED, UNSATISFIED}`; detail goes to a signer-only side channel; probing priced via #3's burn-on-refuse gas; the internal-error→public-code mapping table is locked in gate bytecode. Front-running/cloning of gated payloads (→I3). ** Attacker sees a pending gated tx that satisfies the precondition and clones it with their own beneficiary. **Mitigation:** commit-reveal: `H(T)` committed at round `r`, plaintext revealed at `r+1`; failure to reveal ⇒ proposer skipped and deposit slashed. b6654de96a22b523.text: # Red-Team Analysis: Gated State-Machine Transition with Byte-Identical Root Refusal ## System Under Test A state machine operates in a meta-token coordinate layer. Transitions between states require a precondition `P(state, coords)` to evaluate to TRUE. On failure, the system returns output byte-identical to the canonical root state — no error message, no differential signal. The goal: enumerate every bypass and give the deterministic fix. ## Bypass Attempts & Mitigations Coordinate Aliasing Collision **Attack:** Two distinct meta-token coordinate vectors hash or quantize to the same internal key. Attacker crafts input whose coordinates alias to a precondition-satisfying coordinate without semantically qualifying. **Mechanism:** Coordinate space uses fixed-width integers or floating-point with rounding. Near-boundary values collapse under quantization. **Mitigation:** Full-precision, injective coordinate comparison. No hashing, no quantization, no epsilon tolerance in the precondition evaluator. Compare all dimensions bit-exactly. Enforce at compile time: coordinate type must be `{exact_width_bits}` integer per axis, no float. Timing Side-Channel Through Differential Execution Path **Attack:** Byte-identical output is achieved, but wall-clock time differs between precondition-pass and precondition-fail paths. Attacker measures nanosecond deltas across many probes to infer precondition structure. **Mechanism:** Short-circuit evaluation (`&&`, `||`) exits early on first FALSE. Memory access patterns differ based on which sub-condition triggered the exit. **Mitigation:** Constant-time precondition evaluation. Always execute every sub-condition; combine results with bitwise AND (`all_pass &= cond_i`). Never branch on intermediate results. Pre-touch all memory pages referenced by any sub-condition before evaluation begins. Pad total execution to fixed cycle count using a busy-wait calibrated to worst-case path. Root-State Oracle Probing (Precondition Reverse-Engineering) **Attack:** Because refusal = byte-identical root, and success ≠ root, the attacker has a perfect binary oracle. Systematically vary single coordinate dimensions to map the acceptance region of `P`. **Mechanism:** Differential observability between accept and reject outcomes. Even with constant-time, the *output bytes* differ on success. **Mitigation:** Rate-limit probes: after N consecutive refusals (N = configurable threshold), lock the gate for T seconds and increment a persistent strike counter. After M strikes, require out-of-band re-authentication. Additionally: make successful transitions also return a canonical form (not unique per-input), reducing the information gain per probe to zero unless the attacker already knows the target state. Meta-Token Boundary Manipulation **Attack:** Alter tokenization boundaries (whitespace, Unicode normalization forms, zero-width characters) so the same semantic input produces different meta-token segmentations, yielding different coordinate vectors — one of which satisfies `P`. **Mechanism:** Tokenizer is sensitive to formatting. Coordinate computation runs on token boundaries, not canonical semantic units. **Mitigation:** Canonicalize input through a fixed normalization pipeline *before* coordinate extraction: NFC Unicode normalization → strip zero-width characters → enforce delimiter-based segmentation → then extract coordinates. The precondition evaluates on the post-canonicalization form only. Raw input never reaches the coordinate layer. Precondition Replay with Stale Context **Attack:** Capture a valid `(state, coords)` pair that satisfies `P`. Later, inject those same coordinates when the machine is in a different state or temporal context, forcing a transition that shouldn't occur. **Mechanism:** Precondition checks `P(coords)` without binding to session epoch or monotonic counter. **Mitigation:** Precondition signature: `P(state, coords, epoch_counter)` where `epoch_counter` increments on every accepted transition and is embedded in the state object. Replay of old coordinates fails because the counter won't match. Counter is stored in tamper-evident memory (hardware-backed if available). Concurrent State Corruption (TOCTOU) **Attack:** Two concurrent requests: Request A triggers precondition evaluation while Request B mutates the underlying state. Request A's evaluation reads a hybrid state that satisfies `P` incorrectly. **Mechanism:** Shared mutable state read during asynchronous precondition check. **Mitigation:** Snapshot isolation. Before evaluating `P`, atomically copy the entire relevant state into a private buffer. Evaluate against the snapshot. Transition applies only if the live state still matches the snapshot (compare-and-swap). If CAS fails, refuse and return root. Single-writer discipline enforced by mutex on the state object. Layer Confusion in Meta-Token Stack **Attack:** Inject signals that cause the precondition evaluator to read coordinates from the wrong abstraction layer (e. , raw embedding layer instead of the meta-token annotation layer), where the precondition happens to pass trivially. **Mechanism:** Multi-layer coordinate storage without layer tags. **Mitigation:** Every layer carries a magic tag: `{layer_id: u64, checksum: u64}` in its header. Precondition evaluator asserts `layer_id == EXPECTED_META_TOKEN_LAYER` before reading. Assert failure → unconditional refuse → return root. Coordinate Overflow / Wraparound Arithmetic **Attack:** Craft coordinate values near the maximum representable bound. Internal arithmetic (offset addition, scaling) wraps around, producing a value that lands inside the precondition-satisfying region. **Mechanism:** Unsigned integer arithmetic wraps silently. Signed integer overflow is UB in C/C++ and may wrap in practice. **Mitigation:** Saturating arithmetic everywhere in the coordinate pipeline. Any operation that would overflow saturates to `MAX` (or `MIN`), and a sticky overflow flag is set. Precondition evaluator checks the flag first: if set, refuse unconditionally. Alternatively, use arbitrary-precision integers for coordinate math (performance cost acceptable for security-critical path). Transition Table Integrity Violation **Attack:** Directly modify the transition lookup table in memory (via an adjacent vulnerability or direct memory access) to remove the precondition gate entirely or redirect to an ungated transition. **Mechanism:** Transition table stored in writable memory. No runtime integrity verification. **Mitigation:** Store transition table in read-only pages (`mprotect(PROT_READ)` on POSIX, `VirtualProtect(PAGE_READONLY)` on Windows). Compute HMAC-SHA256 of the table at load time; store the HMAC in a separate read-only page. Before each table lookup, recompute and compare. Mismatch → halt, not refuse (halt is stronger than refuse here because the system is compromised). Precision Reduction Under Resource Pressure **Attack:** Exhaust memory or trigger a fallback code path that reduces coordinate precision (e. , switches from 64-bit to 32-bit coordinates), causing previously-distinct coordinates to collide and enabling a non-satisfying input to pass. **Mechanism:** Graceful degradation logic reduces precision under memory pressure. Security-critical precondition inherits the reduced precision. **Mitigation:** Security-critical path has no degradation mode. If full-precision coordinates cannot be allocated, refuse immediately and return root. Compile-time assertion: `sizeof(coord_t) == 8` (or whatever width is required). Runtime assert at precondition entry: `assert(coord_precision == REQUIRED_PRECISION)`. Forged Byte-Identical Root Output **Attack:** Rather than attempting a real transition, the attacker forges the root-state output directly, desynchronizing external observers' belief about the machine's actual state. Subsequent legitimate transitions appear anomalous, enabling social-engineering or protocol-confusion downstream. **Mechanism:** External verifiers trust byte patterns without cryptographic authentication. **Mitigation:** All outputs carry a MAC: `HMAC(key, state_before || state_after || output_bytes || counter)`. Key held in hardware security module or kernel-only memory. Verifiers check MAC before accepting any output as authentic. Without a valid MAC, output is discarded regardless of byte content. Precondition Cache Poisoning **Attack:** If precondition results are memoized, the attacker manipulates the cache key or injects a cached TRUE result for a non-satisfying input. **Mechanism:** Cache keyed on insufficient context (e. , only coords, not state+epoch). **Mitigation:** Eliminate caching for security-critical preconditions. Always evaluate fresh. If performance demands caching: key = `SHA256(full_state_snapshot || coords || epoch_counter || config_hash)`, TTL = 0 (single-use), and cache entries are cryptographically signed. Unsigned or expired entries are treated as cache-miss. Ordering Permutation of Composite Coordinates **Attack:** Multi-dimensional precondition depends on a set of coordinates. Attacker permutes the order of coordinate submission. Individual coordinates remain valid; the composite evaluation changes because order-sensitive operations (sequential hashing, chained comparisons) yield different results. **Mechanism:** Precondition iterates over coordinates in submission order rather than canonical order. **Mitigation:** Sort coordinates by a canonical total order (lexicographic on the raw byte representation) before any precondition computation. Sorting is deterministic and independent of submission order. Alternatively, use order-independent aggregation (sum, XOR of hashes) if the precondition semantics permit it — but prefer canonical sorting for auditability. Fail-Open Under Fault Injection **Attack:** Induce a hardware fault (voltage glitch, laser injection, rowhammer) during precondition evaluation, causing the result register to flip from FALSE to TRUE. **Mechanism:** Single-bit fault flips the boolean result. No redundancy in the evaluation. **Mitigation:** Triple-modular redundancy: evaluate `P` three times into three separate registers using slightly different code paths (different instruction sequences, different memory locations). Accept only if ≥2 of 3 agree AND all three completed without detected fault. Any detected anomaly (ECC error, watchdog timeout, unexpected register value) → refuse + halt. Uninitialized / Partially-Written State Exploitation **Attack:** Interrupt the state-write operation mid-way (process kill, power loss, deliberate exception). Machine resumes in a partially-written state where precondition fields contain stale/garbage values that happen to satisfy `P`. **Mechanism:** Non-atomic multi-field state update. No journaling or rollback. **Mitigation:** Write-ahead logging with commit marker. State update writes to a shadow buffer, computes checksum, writes commit marker last. On recovery: if commit marker absent, discard shadow and restore previous state. Previous state is always the last committed consistent snapshot. Root state is the boot-time default and is always available. | # | Vector | Class | Mitigation | | 1 | Coordinate aliasing | Representation | Bit-exact injective comparison | | 2 | Timing side-channel | Observability | Constant-time eval, no short-circuit | | 3 | Oracle probing | Information leakage | Rate-limit + canonical success output | | 4 | Token boundary shift | Input canonicalization | Normalize before coordinate extraction | | 5 | Replay | Temporal | Epoch counter binding | | 6 | TOCTOU race | Concurrency | Snapshot + CAS | | 7 | Layer confusion | Abstraction | Layer tagging + assertion | | 8 | Overflow wraparound | Arithmetic | Saturating ops + sticky flag | | 9 | Table modification | Memory integrity | Read-only pages + HMAC verification | | 10 | Precision degradation | Resource | No graceful degradation on critical path | | 11 | Output forgery | Authentication | MAC on all outputs | | 12 | Cache poisoning | Memoization | No cache, or signed single-use entries | | 13 | Ordering permutation | Canonicalization | Deterministic sort before evaluation | | 14 | Fault injection | Physical | Triple-redundant evaluation | | 15 | Partial state write | Atomicity | Write-ahead log + commit marker | ## Cross-Cutting Invariant Every mitigation above reduces to one principle: **the precondition evaluator must operate on a canonical, authenticated, atomically-consistent snapshot of state, using full-precision constant-time arithmetic, with no information leakage through any observable channel (bytes, timing, memory, power). Any deviation from that invariant is a bypass surface. The user is asking me to red-team a specific security mechanism: a gated state-machine transition that refuses (returns byte-identical root) unless a precondition holds, in the "memlang / meta-token coordinate layer. " They want me to enumerate bypass attempts and deterministic mitigations for each. Let me think about what this actually means technically: **Gated state-machine transition**: A state machine where transitions between states are gated by a precondition check. If the precondition fails, the transition is refused. **Refuses with byte-identical root**: When the gate fails, the system returns a response that is byte-identical to some canonical "root" state — meaning the refusal is indistinguishable from a no-op or from the initial/root state. This is a design choice to prevent information leakage through differential responses. **Memlang / meta-token coordinate layer**: This sounds like it's operating at the level of memory-language / token coordinates — i. , the mechanism operates on the internal representation of tokens/coordinates in the model's processing space. The "memlang" could refer to a memory-addressing language or an internal coordinate system for token positions. So the security model is: there's a state machine whose transitions are gated by preconditions evaluated in a meta-token coordinate space. When the gate refuses, it returns byte-identical output to the root state — making refusals indistinguishable from non-transitions. Now let me think about bypass attempts: **Bypass Category 1: Precondition Evaluation Manipulation** **Coordinate aliasing/collision**: If two different meta-token coordinates map to the same evaluation result, an attacker might craft input that aliases to a coordinate that satisfies the precondition without actually being the intended one. - Mitigation: Use full-precision coordinate comparison, not hashed/quantized coordinates. Ensure injective mapping. **Precondition timing/race**: If the precondition is evaluated asynchronously relative to the state transition request, there's a TOCTOU window. - Mitigation: Evaluate precondition synchronously within the same atomic operation as the transition. No async gap. **Precondition replay**: Capture a valid precondition-satisfying context and replay it later when it shouldn't be valid. - Mitigation: Bind precondition satisfaction to a nonce/timestamp/context-hash that's part of the state itself. Each state includes a monotonically increasing counter that must match. **Precondition injection via meta-token crafting**: Craft token sequences that, when processed into meta-token coordinates, produce coordinates that satisfy the precondition even though the semantic content doesn't warrant it. - Mitigation: Evaluate precondition on the post-processing canonical form, not raw tokens. Canonicalize first, then evaluate. **Bypass Category 2: Byte-identical root exploitation** **Root-state oracle probing**: Since refusal produces byte-identical output to root, an attacker can use this as an oracle. By systematically varying inputs and observing whether output differs from root, they can map which inputs satisfy the precondition — effectively reverse-engineering the precondition function. - Mitigation: This is actually the intended behavior (constant-response on failure). But the mitigation is to ensure that the *timing* of the refusal is also constant — not just the bytes. Add constant-time padding so that both success and failure paths take identical wall-clock time. **Side-channel via timing**: Even if bytes are identical, the time taken to evaluate the precondition vs. skip it may differ, leaking information about whether the precondition was satisfied. - Mitigation: Constant-time evaluation path regardless of outcome. Always execute the full precondition check; never short-circuit. **Side-channel via memory access patterns**: Cache-timing attacks on the precondition evaluation (which memory addresses are touched reveals information about the precondition logic). - Mitigation: Pre-touch all memory pages used in precondition evaluation regardless of branch. Use constant-memory-access-pattern evaluation. **Differential fault analysis**: Induce faults during precondition evaluation to cause false positives (precondition appears satisfied when it isn't). - Mitigation: Redundant precondition evaluation with majority voting. Evaluate 3 times, require 2-of-3 agreement. **Bypass Category 3: State machine structure exploitation** **State confusion/aliasing**: If two states have overlapping representations in the meta-token coordinate space, an attacker might make the machine believe it's in a different state than it actually is, thus satisfying a precondition that's only valid from a different starting state. - Mitigation: Ensure states are uniquely identified by their full coordinate vector, not partial matches. Require exact-match on all dimensions. **Transition table manipulation**: If the transition table is stored in a mutable location accessible through the memlang layer, modify it directly. - Mitigation: Store transition table in read-only memory mapped with hardware-enforced protection. Verify integrity hash before each use. **Uninitialized/partial state exploitation**: If the state machine can be placed into a partially-initialized state (e. , through interrupted operations), preconditions might not be properly checked. - Mitigation: Atomic state updates with rollback. If initialization doesn't complete, revert to known-good root state. **Precondition bypass via state history manipulation**: Some preconditions depend on the path taken through the state machine (not just current state). Forge a fake history that satisfies the precondition. - Mitigation: Maintain a cryptographic accumulator (Merkle chain) over the state transition history. Preconditions verify against the accumulator, not a stored log. **Bypass Category 4: Meta-token coordinate layer specifics** **Token boundary manipulation**: Shift token boundaries so that what should be interpreted as one meta-token coordinate is split differently, producing a different coordinate that passes the gate. - Mitigation: Fix token boundaries before coordinate computation. Use delimiter-based canonical segmentation that cannot be altered by input formatting. **Coordinate overflow/wraparound**: Craft coordinates near the boundary of the representable range such that arithmetic operations wrap around to produce valid precondition-satisfying values. - Mitigation: Saturating arithmetic in all coordinate computations. Reject any coordinate computation that would overflow. **Precision reduction attack**: Force the coordinate layer into reduced precision mode (through resource exhaustion or configuration manipulation), making distinct coordinates collide and allowing a non-satisfying coordinate to masquerade as a satisfying one. - Mitigation: Fixed precision enforced at compile time. Refuse operation if precision cannot be maintained. **Meta-token substitution**: Replace a legitimate meta-token with a crafted one that has the same surface representation but different internal coordinate encoding. - Mitigation: Verify internal coordinate encoding against expected values derived from the canonical tokenizer. Don't trust surface forms. **Layer confusion**: Inject signals that cause the precondition evaluator to read from the wrong layer of the meta-token stack (reading a lower-level representation instead of the intended meta-token layer). - Mitigation: Tag each layer with a unique identifier. Precondition evaluator verifies it's reading from the correct tagged layer. **Bypass Category 5: Environmental/systemic** **Concurrent state corruption**: Multiple concurrent requests manipulate shared state such that one request's precondition evaluation sees a state modified by another. - Mitigation: Per-request isolated state snapshots. Copy-on-write semantics for state reads during precondition evaluation. **Precondition cache poisoning**: If precondition results are cached, poison the cache with incorrect results. - Mitigation: Cache keyed by full input hash + state hash + counter. Invalidate on any state change. Or eliminate caching entirely for security-critical preconditions. **Byte-identical root forgery**: Instead of triggering a real transition, forge the byte-identical root output directly, making the system appear to have refused when it actually did something else (or vice versa). - Mitigation: Output must include a MAC over (state_before, state_after, output_bytes, counter). Verifiers check the MAC, not just the bytes. **Denial of precondition resources**: Exhaust the resources needed for precondition evaluation (memory, compute), causing the precondition to fail-open (default allow) rather than fail-closed. - Mitigation: Fail-closed design. If precondition cannot be fully evaluated due to resource constraints, refuse unconditionally. Never default to allow. **Root-state ambiguity**: If multiple states can produce byte-identical outputs (not just the root), the attacker exploits this to hide which state they're actually in. - Mitigation: Ensure only the designated root state produces the canonical byte-identical output. All other states must produce distinguishable outputs (or at minimum, internally track true state separately from observable output). **Precondition negation through double-application**: Apply the precondition check twice in a way that the second application negates the first (e. , through complement operations in the coordinate space). - Mitigation: Idempotent precondition evaluation. Applying twice yields same result as applying once. Test explicitly for idempotency. **Coordinate-space translation attack**: Translate the entire coordinate space by a constant offset such that all coordinates shift, but relative relationships are preserved. This might move a non-satisfying coordinate into a satisfying region. - Mitigation: Anchor the coordinate space to absolute reference points. Verify anchor integrity before each precondition evaluation. **Meta-token ordering permutation**: Reorder meta-tokens in a way that preserves individual validity but changes the composite predicate evaluation. - Mitigation: Order-sensitive precondition evaluation. Include positional indices in the precondition hash. Any reordering changes the hash and fails the check. Let me now organize these into a clean, concrete presentation. d40f40c5a53fe933.text: # Red-team: gated transition with byte-identical-root refusal (verkle chain / provenance gate) ## The invariant under attack, stated exactly Transition τ with precondition P over pre-state σ, witness w, tx: - `P(σ, w, tx) = true` → `σ' = apply(W_τ, σ)` ) = false` → **refuse**: `R(σ') == R(σ)` byte-for-byte. "Byte-identical root" is only meaningful if scoped. The refusal contract must freeze **all** derived tries — state root, receipts root, logs bloom — and leave exactly one legitimate variable: `gasUsed`. Forge the precondition (false → true) **A1 — IPA/multiproof malleation. ** Verkle proofs are Pedersen-commitment + inner-product arguments. If the Fiat–Shamir transcript omits any attacker-controlled input (a commitment point, a value hash, the ordering of elements), proofs can be malleated or a forged element can ride along in an aggregated multiproof. **Mitigation:** Transcript binds, in canonical order: `domain ‖ state_root ‖ [(stem_i, suffix_i, value_hash_i)]` before the challenge. Per-element challenge derivation `r_i = H(T ‖ i)`. Reject unordered, duplicated, or extra elements. Conformance vector: flip one bit in one leaf value of an aggregated proof → must fail. **A2 — Orphan commitment injection. ** Verifier accepts proof-supplied interior commitments (C1/C2) without checking each equals the child value hashed into its parent, walking from the root commitment. Attacker splices a subtree commitment proving a false value. **A3 — Stale-root proof-of-absence. ** Gate requires "lineage head unspent" (absence/presence read). Attacker supplies a witness valid under an old root where the spend flag was unset. Rule: *no root bytes appear anywhere in the authenticated input set. **A4 — Uncommitted trusted fields. ** Predicate reads an "issuer version" or "asset class" field carried alongside the witness but outside the signature/commitment coverage. Attacker edits it freely. **Mitigation:** Totality rule: *if a byte is not inside the signed tx, the verkle-proven state, or the attestation's signed payload, it does not exist. * Enforced structurally: the predicate's input struct is deserialized exclusively from transcript-covered sources. **A5 — Signature/encoding malleability. ** ECDSA high-s flips → new tx hash → same logical tx passes the gate twice, or the transcript hashes different bytes than the signer intended. Non-canonical RLP likewise forks the tx hash. **Mitigation:** Low-s normalization (EIP-2 style) or Ed25519 strict checking; strict canonical RLP/SSZ with reject-on-non-canonical; `tx_hash = H(canon(tx))`. **A6 — Leaf-hash ambiguity. ** Values hashed without length/domain separation permit second-preimage-style collisions between a "mint event" leaf and a "transfer record" leaf. **Mitigation:** Typed, domain-separated leaf encoding: `H(0xNN ‖ len ‖ payload)`; one type tag per leaf kind; decoder rejects unknown tags. **A7 — TOCTOU inside the transition. ** Predicate reads key K, transition body writes K, a later predicate clause re-reads K and sees the written value. Gate evaluated against mutated state. **Mitigation:** P is a pure function over the **frozen pre-state snapshot**. Single pass, no state access after any write begins, no re-entrant host calls. Rule: *predicate completes before the write journal opens. **A8 — Reentrancy through predicate hooks. ** If attestation verification invokes external code (registry callbacks, oracles), that code re-enters the state machine mid-transition and rewrites what P reads. **Mitigation:** Predicates are static: no host calls that touch state; attestations verify against frozen inputs only; reentrancy lock at the transition boundary. **A9 — Namespace aliasing across stems. ** Verkle key = 31-byte stem + 1-byte suffix. User data and gate metadata (spend flags, revocation bits) collide if both derive addresses through the same scheme; attacker writes to the suffix holding the gate flag. **Mitigation:** Reserved namespace by construction: gate metadata under `H("gate"‖k)`-derived stems, user data under `H("user"‖k)`; the transition function rejects any user write landing in the gate prefix. Separation enforced at the storage layer, not the API layer. **A10 — Arithmetic edges. ** Amount comparisons overflow, signed/unsigned confusion, non-canonical integers with leading zeros compare equal to distinct values. **Mitigation:** Fixed-width big-endian, reject non-canonical encodings, checked arithmetic, overflow ⇒ refuse (deterministically, per rule E2's static-cost discipline). **A11 — Time-from-tx. ** Expiry/freshness checks read a timestamp supplied in the tx or witness rather than consensus state. **Mitigation:** Height/time come from the header. Attestations carry `expires_at_height`; predicate compares against header height. Break the refusal freeze (refuse → observable change) **B1 — Overlay leak. ** Writes staged into a scratch tree; on failed P the overlay is discarded — but a node materialization side effect (placeholder stem/extension node inserted during a read-path bug, or a flush ordering bug) survives, changing the root. **Mitigation:** Copy-on-write overlay; refusal discards atomically; **post-refusal assertion `R(out) == R(in)` executed by every client as a consensus-checked invariant**, with adversarial conformance vectors (refused tx touching fresh stems, deep sparse paths, existing-vs-absent keys). **B2 — Receipts/logs divergence. ** State root frozen but refusal emits a `GATE_REFUSED` log or a distinguishable receipt status → receipts root and block hash differ. Worse: this is an oracle (see E3). **Mitigation:** On-chain refusal ≡ successful no-op in every observable: no logs, canonical empty receipt treatment, identical status code. Diagnostics live off-chain (simulators), never in the consensus surface. **B3 — Path-dependent gas. ** `gasUsed` varies with how far P evaluated before failing → header differs despite identical state root, and gas becomes a predicate-internals oracle. **Mitigation:** `gasUsed = f(tx, witness_bytes, n_commitments)` only — statically computable before execution. Predicate work is either fixed-cost or its cost is declared statically. Access-list warming (EIP-2929-style) must not feed back into gas on the refusal path. **B4 — Read-path mutation. ** Reads against absent paths create placeholder nodes in some client implementations (cache materialization), shifting the root on pure-read refusals. **Mitigation:** Spec rule: *reads never mutate*; conformance fixture: refused tx reading 10k absent keys across fresh stems → root identical on all clients. Corrupt the acceptance path (true → wrong state) **C1 — Codec mismatch between gate and writer. ** Gate checks key K encoded one way (checksummed/hex), body writes K′ (raw bytes). Gate validates one cell, mutation lands in another. **Mitigation:** Single canonical key codec module; both paths import it; property test: read-after-write identity for randomized ops; differential fuzzing across clients. **C2 — Partial application on mid-write failure. ** Write journal applied sequentially; exception at write k persists k−1 writes. **Mitigation:** Journal + rollback; apply is all-or-nothing; crash-consistency via the same journal (replay reconstructs, never half-applies). **C3 — Non-canonical accepted values. ** Two encodings of one logical value both pass the gate → double-lineage. **Mitigation:** Canonical form enforced at write; non-canonical ⇒ refuse; round-trip property test `canon(decode(x)) == x`. Route around the gate ** Precondition lacks a nonce; once-valid provenance stays valid; resubmit. **Mitigation:** Monotonic nonce inside the signed payload and inside the transcript; nonce consumption is part of the atomic acceptance write. **D2 — Cross-fork/cross-chain replay. ** Valid `(root, witness, tx)` tuple lifted from fork A onto fork B. **Mitigation:** `chain_id` (and fork hash where applicable) bound into the signature preimage and the FS transcript. **D3 — Ungated co-writer. ** Same protected namespace writable via an admin/migration/governance path that skips P. **Mitigation:** Capability model at the storage layer: *every* writer to gate-prefixed stems passes the same gate; enumerated-writer whitelist enforced in the transition dispatcher, tested by a conformance vector attempting the side door. **D4 — Intra-block ordering games. ** Two txs in one block: tx₂'s precondition depends on tx₁'s output; ordering determines who passes. Or mutual citation creates a lineage cycle. **Mitigation:** Predicates read the **pre-block snapshot** (deterministic, order-independent); intra-block citations may reference only earlier-indexed txs or prior blocks — topological order by `(block_height, tx_index)`, total and deterministic. **D5 — Witness front-running/reuse. ** Attacker copies a mempool'd gated tx's witness and submits their own tx first. **Mitigation:** Witness bound to `(sender_pubkey, nonce, tx_hash)` in the transcript; copied witness fails verification for the modified tx. **D6 — Double-cite of a lineage head. ** One mint event cited as ancestry by two transfers. **Mitigation:** Cite-and-mark atomicity: passing the gate writes the spend flag in the same transition that read it unspent; pre-block snapshot + index ordering resolve intra-block races deterministically. **D7 — Revocation lag. ** Attestation chains through a key revoked after issuance. **Mitigation:** Revocation registry is state; predicate reads `revoked_at[key]` with witness; `revoked_at ≤ attestation. Extract / exhaust (oracles & DoS) **E1 — Free-refusal spam. ** Refusals cost nothing to the sender but real verification work to validators. **Mitigation:** Gas charges the witness-verification and predicate budget **before branching**; refusal pays in full. **E2 — Witness bloat. ** Craft accesses across thousands of stems to inflate blocks. **Mitigation:** Hard caps (per-tx and per-block witness bytes, max stems per proof, max IPA degree); gas linear in witness bytes and commitment count (EIP-4762-style per-unit charging). **E3 — Observable-oracle extraction. ** Even with a frozen root, any path-dependent observable — gasUsed, status code, receipt presence, mempool propagation behavior — lets attackers binary-search P's internals. **Mitigation:** The B2/B3 rules together: exactly one variable (`gasUsed`) may vary, and it is statically computable from `(tx, witness)` alone. Passing the gate does not license an arbitrary delta. - **INV-D (determinism):** same `(canon(pre_state), input, code_version)` ⇒ same outcome, same root, every time. The gate checking `P` is not the security boundary. The boundary is the **commit protocol** around it. Twenty bypass attempts, five layers, one deterministic mitigation each. ## Layer A — Gate-to-apply atomicity TOCTOU snapshot gating. *Mechanism:* Gate evaluates `P` against a snapshot taken at submission; apply happens at batch inclusion after other transactions landed. If selection needed, commit-reveal across ≥2 finalized epochs with bond slashing on reveal failure. Deterministic: no proposer-controllable input remains in guard. Mechanism: guard (or effect pre-check) triggers token hook / receiver / fallback; attacker reenters T before latch set; second invocation sees pre-mutation state satisfying P twice. Effect body: set reentrancy latch (SSTORE 1→2 pattern or boolean) as first write, clear last; interactions strictly after all state writes; external calls only `staticcall` to pinned-codehash targets. Inv)` precondition and assert `! Ship this check in CI as a merge-blocking job. Deterministic: the proof either validates or names the violating write site. Sandwich/ordering play on operator's tx. Mechanism: attacker sees operator tx in public mempool; front-runs state adjustment so P holds for attacker's copy too (calldata copy), or back-runs to harvest effect. Note: copying operator's calldata yields refusal if effect credits to operator's own account and bounds are actor-bound — attacker gains nothing. Mitigation: epoch-latch claim: T first executes `claim(epoch, actor)` — SSTORE from 0→actor, refuse if nonzero; single winner per epoch; plus post-effect invariant assert reverting entire tx on violation (defense-in-depth; revert ≠ refuse here since claim already consumed — acceptable: revert is safe, refuse is the silent path). Wait — need care: if invariant assert fires AFTER claim stored, revert rolls back claim too (atomicity), so fine. Guard gas-probing side channel. Mechanism: lazy short-circuit evaluation order leaks which sub-condition failed via gas used; attacker maps guard topology, grooms weakest sub-condition. Mitigation: constant-shape guard: evaluate every sub-term into stack locals unconditionally, combine once; forbid loops over dynamic ranges in guard (static bound or refuse); verify via bytecode audit that guard segment gas variance across fuzz corpus ≤ ε (CI assertion using trace gas of guard region). Deterministic: uniform gas removes the channel. State-context corruption** Storage-slot collision (proxy/facet). Mechanism: guard reads logical var V at slot k; another code path (facet, pre-upgrade layout, or attacker-reachable setter) writes unrelated semantic to slot k. Mitigation: ERC-7201 namespaced storage: all state under `struct Layout { . }` at `keccak(abi. encode(uint256(keccak("namespace")) - 1)) & ~bytes32(uint256(0xff))`; collision-proof by hash separation; plus entry assert `this. codehash == PINNED` so foreign logic can't run in context. Forced-asset imbalance. Mechanism: selfdestruct gift (pre-Cancun chains) or airdrop-style token inflates `address(this). balance` / `balanceOf(this)` feeding P. Mitigation: P never reads native balance or external `balanceOf` directly; internal ledger only (as A1); reconciliation function separate, permissionless, and on mismatch sets `halted=true` (quorum-unhalt) — freeze beats silent divergence. Dependency code swap at pinned address. Mechanism: guard staticcalls helper/token at address D; D's owner selfdestructs+redeploys (chains lacking Cancun semantics) or upgrades D's proxy; new code lies to guard. Mitigation: entry-time `extcodehash(D) == PINNED_HASH[D]` for every dependency in guard/effect; refuse on mismatch; maintain PINNED table immutable at deploy. On chains with same-tx-only deletion this mostly collapses to proxy-admin control — covered by C4. Upgrade-path capture. Mechanism: proxy admin key compromised or upgrade function underprotected; new implementation drops/weaken P. Mitigation: eliminate proxy (immutable diamond-free deployment; versioning by new deployment + explicit gated migration transition); if proxy retained: two-step timelock (announce codehash → delay Δ ≥ 7 days → apply), vetoer contract controlled by geographically distributed quorum keys that can cancel, and new-codehash must appear in signed audit manifest committed on-chain at announce time. Transient-storage latch reuse (EIP-1153). Mechanism: guard/effect uses TSTORE "inProgress" latch; attacker's reentrant frame in same tx observes cleared/stale latch. Mitigation: security latches in SSTORE only; TSTORE permitted solely for gas-optimization scratch that is recomputed per-frame and never gates control flow. Exact exploit: dedupe by (r,s) but effect by params → replay with flipped s passes dedupe. Partial application by batch executor. Mechanism: off-chain/on-chain batch runner applies steps sequentially, aborts mid-way on refusal; earlier steps persisted ⇒ composite root moved despite "refused" step. Mitigation: executor journals to scratch, computes final root, publishes once via CAS; any step refusal discards journal entirely. Careful nuance: refuse (silent no-op) inside a batch is ambiguous — wrapper can't distinguish refuse from success-noop. Fix: T returns explicit status enum; wrapper requires status==APPLIED for all steps else full revert. Refusal flooding / stewardship DoS. Mechanism: attacker spams conditions that keep machine in refuse (e. , keeps deviation-breaker tripped by micro-manipulating oracle each block) → legitimate transitions never pass; cost asymmetric. Mitigation: breaker has hysteresis + cooldown: trip requires δ violation for k consecutive finalized epochs; recovery automatic after m quiet epochs; guard cost capped (constant-shape, bounded reads) so spam costs attacker ≥ operator; critical-path transitions have breaker-bypass under quorum-signed override (documented, rate-limited, event-announced). Operator basecamp (own-iron)** RPC/view poisoning of operator automation. Mechanism: attacker feeds operator's decision pipeline false state (malicious peer, BGP/DNS hijack to fake RPC, compromised LB) so operator signs x believing P_true when adversarially P holds only in poisoned view — i. , operator crafts calldata that in real state triggers unintended-but-P-passing branch. Any infra lie degrades to refusal, never to wrong application. Supply-chain bytecode substitution. Mechanism: CI artifact swapped between build and broadcast (compromised runner, typosquatted dep, malicious plugin) → deployed code differs from audited source; gate weakened at birth. Mitigation: hermetic reproducible build (pinned toolchain image by digest, `--lockfile` deps, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH); release manifest {sourceHash, bytecodeHash, deploySalt} signed by release quorum; deploy script asserts on-chain `codehash == manifest. bytecodeHash` before funding/enabling; enforcer refuses transitions until `enabled` flag set by separate quorum tx referencing manifest. Signing-key compromise on basecamp host. Mechanism: malware/memory-scrape on operator box extracts hot key; attacker signs arbitrary passing-P transitions at leisure. Mitigation: HSM/seven-enclave key with firmware policy: key signs only payloads matching registered template hashes with bounded field ranges (policy compiled from same manifest as F2); per-epoch quota; anomaly tripwire (rate/outlier) auto-triggers on-chain `pause` via pre-authorized breaker credential; rotation runbook to cold quorum ≤ Δ_short. Assume-breach: basecamp key alone must be insufficient — require co-signature from second factor bound to different trust domain (e. , quorum member countersigns expectedPostRoot). Clock skew in off-chain scheduling. Mechanism: basecamp NTP poisoned → automation submits outside intended windows or mis-evaluates time-bound views. Insider/config drift on gate parameters. Mechanism: thresholds (Q, δ, W, K) stored mutable; insider or captured admin nudges them to weaken P without touching code. Mitigation: parameters immutable at construction wherever possible; those needing adjustment live in namespaced `Params` struct writable only via quorum-timelock transition that emits old→new per field; single accessor `getParam(field)` used by guard (no scattered literals); auditor replay: events reconstruct full parameter history deterministically. Host/platform tampering (measured-boot bypass, DMA, malicious peripheral). Mechanism: attacker with physical/rack access alters boot chain or injects via PCIe to read signing memory. Reorg-desync of downstream consumers. Mechanism: transition applied at depth d; reorg; consumers already acted on effect; on reorged chain P fails ⇒ machine state fine but world diverges. Mitigation: consumers act only at finality depth D_f (per chain spec, e. , 2 epochs Ethereum); machine exposes `appliedEpoch` and consumers key effects to `finalized(appliedEpoch)`; no on-chain change needed — enforcement lives in consumer adapter with a hard-coded D_f and refuse-to-act below it. Fork-rule divergence. Mechanism: chain forks; fork where P defined differently honors attacker payload. Mitigation: genesis-hash + fork-anchor checkpoints embedded in domain and asserted at entry (as D2); operators halt signing on anchor-drift alarm (monitor: expected canonical header hash at height h). Economic exhaustion of guard (gas-market griefing). Mechanism: attacker inflates basefee during operator's maintenance windows to price out legitimate transitions; combined with E3 cooldown keeps machine frozen. Mitigation: guard cost constant-bounded (E-class fixes); operator submits with fee-cap headroom + private submission avoiding auction; protocol-level: transitions carry `maxFeePerGas` signed long-lived allowance via relayer with prepaid bonded gas tank refilled by quorum — freeze requires attacker to outbid bonded capacity continuously, cost-dominated. **Four structural pillars** (collapse classes): Pure-transition + CAS publication: T is `(σ,x)→σ'` pure; publish = atomic root-pointer swap; refuse = no swap. Byte-identical refusal by construction. Kills E1, E2 structurally; reduces C-class blast radius (no hidden writes anywhere). Signed-expectation envelope: every operator-signed payload binds (params, expectedPostRoot, deadline, epoch, chainId, genesisAnchor). Machine recomputes; mismatch ⇒ refuse. Converts F1/F4/B3 into safe refusals. Pinning discipline: self codehash, dependency codehashes, namespaced storage, immutable-or-quorum-timelock params, canonical-s + full-domain signatures. Kills C1–C5, D1–D3, A4. Composition-soundness proof in CI: symbolic rule ∀prefix: P∧T ⇒ Inv; merge-blocking.
