4d135567d9c2ad1e.text: # Consensus Without a Central Brain — Ledger of Empty Chairs Decoding the problem Strip the skin off the game terms and this is: **N stateless replicas, no leader, one append-only log, must emit one identical output stream forever. - *"Stateless workers"* → a worker is a pure function `step(state, input)`; its only memory is the ledger. Cold start = fold the ledger from the last checkpoint. - *"Empty chairs"* → the eligible-voter set `E` (the chairs) is itself a ledger-defined roster. No chair is privileged; a chair *empties* when it is struck (fenced). Leadership is a permanently vacant chair. - *"One honest voice"* → the output stream is the sequence of sealed payloads in chain order. Formal property: at any instant, any two workers' outputs are prefix-comparable (`out_i ⊑ out_j` or vice versa), and all converge to one limit stream σ. - *"No drift"* → every decision is a **pure function of a ledger prefix**. No wall clocks, no floats, no map-iteration order, no local counters. The chain position **is** the logical clock. The one structural trick that makes leaderless work: **every validity predicate is prefix-local** — evaluable at a record's own position in the hash chain, identically by every worker, with no side channel. Chain position replaces the coordinator. Ledger grammar (exact) Hash chain: each record carries `prev_hash = H(previous record)`. `H = SHA-256`. Canonical encoding: fields sorted by tag, `tag ‖ len_be32 ‖ body`, fixed-width big-endian integers, **no floating point anywhere** (world coordinates are fixed-point, e. 1e-6 units). Re-encoding a record must reproduce its bytes bit-for-bit. | `INPUT` | payload_hash, payload | | `PROPOSE` | slot, round, chair_id, digest | | `VOTE` | slot, round, chair_id, digest | | `CHECKPOINT` | height, state_hash, code_version | | `STRIKE` | chair_id, reason_hash | **Validity predicates** (evaluated at the record's own chain position `p`; all are prefix-local): - **V1** `prev_hash == H(prev record)` - **V2** encoding is canonical - **V3** for PROPOSE/VOTE: `slot > sealed_height(prefix p)` ∧ `chair_id ∈ E(prefix p)` ∧ no earlier VOTE in the chain by the same chair with the same `(slot, round)` - **V4** `code_version == pinned_version(prefix p)` (kills version-skew drift) - **V5** CHECKPOINT: `state_hash == fold(committed payloads ≤ height)` (verifiable lazily; deterministic) Predicate V3 is the load-bearing one: **a vote is valid only if, at its chain position, the slot was not yet sealed and the chair had not yet voted in that round. ** Late votes for a sealed slot self-invalidate. No epochs broadcast, no leases, no leader. Measured signals (integers read off the ledger — nothing estimated) | Signal | Definition | Healthy value | | **S1** `votes(p,s,r,d)` | # distinct valid VOTE records at positions ≤ p for (slot s, round r, digest d) | reaches Q, then slot seals | | **S2** `forks(s,r)` | # distinct digests holding ≥ 1 valid vote in (s,r) | collapses to 1 within ~2 rounds | | **S3** `participation(s,r)` | # distinct chairs with a valid vote in (s,r) | ≥ Q | | **S4** `divergence(h)` | # distinct CHECKPOINT `state_hash` values recorded at height h | **exactly 1** — this is the drift meter | | **S5** `lag(i)` | `sealed_height − applied_height(i)` | bounded by replication delay; liveness only | | **S6** `gap(i)` | max observed height − local height | 0. S4 is the drift instrument: workers periodically checkpoint their folded state hash at a common height. Identical code + identical prefix ⇒ identical hash. Any S4 > 1 is measured nondeterminism, located to the exact height and the exact deviating chairs. Closed-form decision rules **R1 — Quorum (closed form). - Crash-fault tolerance: `Q = ⌊N/2⌋ + 1`, tolerates `F = N − Q = ⌈N/2⌉ − 1` failures. - Byzantine tolerance: `Q = 2F + 1`, requires `N ≥ 3F + 1`. (Check: two quorums intersect in ≥ 2Q − N ≥ F + 1 chairs, at least one honest. **R2 — Seal (the commit rule). Slot `s` is sealed with digest `d` at chain position p* = min { p : ∃ r, d : votes(p, s, r, d) ≥ Q } Sealing is a *derived fact*, not a record — though an explicit `SEAL` certificate carrying the Q vote hashes may be appended so verification costs O(Q) instead of O(prefix). The payload of `d` enters the voice stream at position `p*`. **R3 — Vote choice (deterministic winner function). d*(p,s,r) = argmin_lex { d : votes(p,s,r,d) = max_c votes(p,s,r,c) } Highest valid count; ties broken by byte-wise lexicographic order of the digest. The lex tiebreak is **not cosmetic** — it is the collapse mechanism: on a perfect split, every honest chair computes the same lex-min winner and concentrates on it next round. If no candidate exists, a chair proposes its own deterministic block: all `INPUT` records since the previous seal, sorted by `(payload_hash, chair_id)` — a canonical cut. Concurrent cuts create forks; the vote resolves them at a cost of one round. **R4 — Round advance. Enter round `r+1` for slot `s` when `participation(s,r) ≥ Q` (S3) and the slot is unsealed, or after timeout `τ(r) = τ₀·2^r + (H(chair_id ‖ s ‖ r) mod W)`. Jitter comes from a hash, not a clock, so behavior stays reproducible. Timeouts gate retries only — **they never select values. Any record failing V1–V4 is ignored, and its author's chair is struck via `STRIKE` (itself a sealed decision). Struck chairs leave `E`; their past valid votes stand, their future ones don't. **R6 — Drift response (honesty rule). If `divergence(h) = k > 1`: retain the majority state hash, strike the minority chairs. If no majority exists (k-way split), append `HALT`: the voice goes silent rather than assert anything not derivable from sealed records. **Silence over guessing is the definition of the honest voice here. Why this works — the two theorems **Safety (one voice, zero drift). Votes are valid only under prefix-local predicates (V3), so every worker evaluates the same valid-vote set. Suppose two distinct digests seal the same `(slot, round)`. Each seal needs Q valid votes, one per chair per round ⇒ 2Q valid votes from ≤ |E| chairs ⇒ 2Q ≤ |E| ⇒ Q ≤ |E|/2 — contradicting `Q = ⌊|E|/2⌋ + 1`. ∎ At most one digest seals per slot. Seals occur at totally ordered chain positions ⇒ the sealed-payload sequence σ is unique. Every honest worker emits σ truncated at its observation frontier; any two outputs are prefix-comparable at all times; all converge to σ. **That is "speaking as one voice," stated as a theorem, not a hope. ** If ≥ Q chairs are correct and records eventually propagate to all honest chairs: round r achieves participation ≥ Q; if the vote fragments, R4 advances and R3 concentrates all honest mass on the plurality winner — within ≤ 2 rounds of full visibility, its count reaches Q. Common case (identical deterministic proposals): seals in 1 round (propose → attest → sealed). Worst case is bounded, deterministic, and clock-free. Summary of the mechanism in one breath **The hash chain is the clock. Every rule is a pure function of a prefix. Slot contention is settled by repeated plurality vote with a lex tiebreak, one vote per chair per round, sealed at the earliest prefix where a digest hits Q. Quorum intersection makes double-seals arithmetically impossible; prefix-local validity makes every evaluator agree; checkpointed state hashes measure drift to the bit; and when measurement contradicts assumption, the voice halts instead of lying. ** No brain required — the ledger is the brain, and it is empty of occupants by design. So the real engineering question: how do N stateless, leaderless workers reach deterministic agreement using only an append-only log, such that every worker that reads the log computes the *same* next action? This is essentially: **deterministic state machine replication where the log itself is the source of truth and workers are pure functions of a log prefix**. The classic answer is: Workers are pure functions: `next_action(log_prefix) → action`. Determinism means same prefix → same action. 0cad869a44577091.text: # Consensus Without a Central Brain: Pinned-Root Deterministic Quorum ## The reduction that makes it work Stateless workers cannot run Raft/PBFT — they have no log to order and no memory between jobs. But they don't need to. In a verkle-chain architecture **the tree is the brain**: every scrap of durable state (lineage edges, consumed-flags, code registry, prior decisions) lives under keys committed to root `R`. A worker is therefore a pure function: worker_i : (artifact a, root R*, code c) → (verdict v, trace-digest e, attestation σ) Agreement stops being a messaging problem and becomes three mechanical problems: **agree on the input** (pin one root), **compute identically** (kill every nondeterminism channel), **compare digests** (vote by signature). Workers never talk to each other — only to an aggregator. Communication is O(N) 96-byte attestations, no O(N²), no leader election, no view-change. ## Definitions (fix these exactly) - `R* = R(h*)` where `h*` = latest **finalized** block height. Finality replaces reorg-depth guesses with immutability. - `c*` = gate code hash, itself stored at tree key `K_code` — so the code being run is *proven on-chain*, not configured out-of-band. - `dᵢ = H(vᵢ ‖ eᵢ)` — the joint decision digest. `eᵢ` is a Merkle-chained execution-trace hash: each step commits `H(prev ‖ opcode ‖ operands ‖ stack_top)`, giving O(log steps) forensic localization of any divergence. Any worker cache is irrelevant by construction — cached objects are re-proved against the pinned root or discarded. ## The measured signals (not heuristics — exact quantities) | # | Signal | Definition | Healthy value | Alarm | | S1 | Root pin | `#{i : Rᵢ = R*}` | `N` | `< q*` → halt | | S2 | Code pin | `#{i : cᵢ = c*}` | `N` | `< q*` → halt | | S3 | Proof failures | `mᵢ` = # verkle proofs failing against `R*` | `0` | `> 0` → exclude worker | | S4 | Digest histogram | bins over `{dᵢ}` | one bin holding `N` | majority bin `< q*` → abstain | | S5 | Staleness | `t_now − t(h*)` | ≤ finality interval (~12. 8 min, 2 epochs PoS) | exceeded → repin | | S6 | Aggregation latency | `t_agg` to collect q* sigs | p99 from live telemetry | `> T_max` → abort, retry at `h*+1` | Every one of these is a hash equality, an integer count, or a clock delta. Nothing is sampled, estimated, or trusted. ## The closed-form decision rule With `N` workers tolerating `f` Byzantine faults, the bound is forced, not chosen: f_max = ⌊(N−1)/3⌋          (existence requirement: N ≥ 3f_max + 1) q*    = 2·f_max + 1        (decision quorum) N:   4   7   10   13   16   19 q*:  3   5    7    9   11   13 DECIDE(a, h*): A ← {i : Rᵢ = R*  ∧  cᵢ = c*  ∧  mᵢ = 0} d̂ ← mode({dᵢ : i ∈ A})                    # ties broken by min(H(d)) — though ties below are impossible n̂ ← #{i ∈ A : dᵢ = d̂} EMIT(record(d̂, v̂, e*))  ⟺  |A| ≥ q*  ∧  n̂ ≥ q* ∧  t_now − t(h*) ≤ Δ_max otherwise: EMIT NOTHING (silence, not a guess) **Uniqueness is proved, not hoped. ** Suppose two distinct records for the same `(h*, H(a))` existed. Minimum durable state = O(1): last-voted-round + last-committed-round. Anything claiming zero-state safety is hiding a witness service (which is just someone else's state). - Throughput ceiling: every event costs log space + replication bandwidth ×N; N grows → per-event cost grows; sharding splits it but reintroduces cross-shard atomicity problems (see Group 8). **The Never List** (each with the violation it prevents) Never two conflicting entries certified for the same slot. (Prevents: two worlds, duplicated chairs. Never apply any event absent from the certified log. (Prevents: local invention, silent admin powers. Never read wall-clock, local RNG, or uncommitted gossip inside the transition function. Never commit with less than floor(N/2)+1 (crash) / 2f+1 (BFT) distinct identities. (Prevents: split brain; note "distinct identities" — one node sending 3 signed votes ≠ quorum. Never accept a message whose world_id, epoch, or round fails validation. (Prevents: replay, cross-world contamination, wraparound exploits. Never rewrite anything at or before the finalized frontier. (Prevents: un-happening ownership. Never let a restarted worker vote in a round ≤ its journaled last-voted round. (Prevents: amnesia double-vote. Never apply an event twice; never drop a receipt-backed event. (Prevents: dupes/losses; sender_seq strict monotonicity. Never serve reads below the finalized frontier without labeling them stale. (Prevents: economic dupes via read skew. Never keep a worker in the serving pool after a state-root mismatch. (Prevents: confident wrong voice. Never make fork-choice or tie-break depend on anything but the certified data itself. (Prevents: heal-time divergence. Never change roster outside the log / without joint-quorum. (Prevents: era-overlap split brain. Never leave empty/degenerate cases undefined: empty round, empty batch, N=1, zero events, missing shard. (Prevents: implementation-defined divergence at the boring cases — most real drift lives here. Never allow non-canonical serialization into any hash. (Prevents: false alarms masking true drift and vice versa. Never punish/exclude without a logged, quorum-ratified proof. (Prevents: exclusion-as-attack. **Minimal closing mechanism set** — short list tying it together: - Event flow: workers batch → broadcast block with world_id/epoch/round → collect 2f+1 certs → block certified → DAG of certified blocks → total order = deterministic function (per-round leader-by-lowest-hash among certified, or round-robin) → apply in order with per-round pinned code version → checkpoint state root every K rounds at finalized frontier → mismatch = fail-stop. - Numbers: N odd, N ≥ 3f+1 if Byzantine assumed, else N ≥ 2f+1; quorum floor(N/2)+1 / 2f+1; 64-bit rounds; fixed-point math; UTF-8 byte sort keys; canonical serialization; finality certificates gate all ownership effects. 3112b92873666004.text: # Consensus Without a Central Brain: Edge Cases for the Git-Bus Treaty **Load-bearing assumption stated once:** the bus is a git repository (or ref namespace) where stateless workers read state from refs, compute deterministically, and write back via ref updates governed by treaty rules. "One honest voice" = all workers converge on an identical interpretation of the ref DAG. Everything below follows from the mechanics of that substrate. Concurrency and write races **Lost update via non-CAS push. ** Worker A reads ref at commit X, computes, pushes Y. Worker B does the same, pushes Z. If either push isn't a compare-and-swap against the exact expected old value (`--force-with-lease` semantics, enforced server-side), the second write silently clobbers the first lineage. Drift begins here. **Ambiguous push outcome. ** Network timeout during push ≠ failed push. The pack may have arrived and the ref moved. A worker that treats timeout as failure and retries blind can double-apply or fork its own log. Every ambiguous outcome must be reconciled by re-reading remote state before any retry. **Half-applied multi-ref transactions. ** A push touching multiple refs without `--atomic` can apply ref 1 and fail ref 2. Cross-ref invariants (e. , "data commit + ack commit land together") break. Either single-ref-per-transaction or atomic pushes, mandatorily. **Lease takeover without fencing. ** Worker holds a lease (lock ref with expiry), dies, lease expires, worker B takes over, A wakes and still believes it holds the lease. Git has no native fencing tokens — the epoch must be encoded in the ref name or commit payload and validated by the receiving hook. Wall-clock leases are worse than useless under clock skew; leases must be height-based (commit-height), not time-based. **Ack-counting via reflogs. ** Quorum acks counted by walking reflogs break instantly: reflogs are local, non-replicated, and gc-pruned. Acks must be ordinary commits on a branch, counted by DAG walk. Determinism failures (the drift vector) **Non-deterministic compute. ** Float rounding differences, locale-dependent sorting, map iteration order, library version skew, time-of-day reads. Two honest workers, same input, different output. The treaty must pin: canonical serialization (sorted keys, NFC Unicode, LF line endings, UTF-8 only), integer or fixed-point arithmetic, and a content-hash of the fold/checkpoint code itself inside the treaty. **Timestamp-derived ordering. ** Committer dates come from worker clocks. Skewed clocks produce out-of-order "history. " Ordering must come exclusively from DAG topology (parent hashes), never from any timestamp field. ** Shallow clones, hidden refs, filtered views. A worker that sees truncated history misses a tombstone or revocation from 500 commits back and acts on resurrected state. ** CRLF vs LF, non-UTF-8 bytes, NFC vs NFD unicode — same logical content, different hashes, duplicate-but-distinct entries in the fold. Canonicalize at write; reject non-canonical at read. **Mirror split-brain. ** Worker reads replica 1 (lagging), writes to replica 2. One canonical origin, or a deterministic mirror-promotion rule — never "whichever is reachable. **GC pruning live objects. ** Server-side `git gc` prunes objects referenced only by an in-flight operation. Quarantine or keepalive refs must protect objects for the duration of any plausible in-flight window. **LFS/blob decoupling. ** Pointer file survives, payload store GC'd independently → the voice references content that doesn't exist. Either ban blobs above a size threshold on the bus or bind blob retention to the referencing commit's lifetime. **Case-insensitive ref collision. ** On macOS/Windows hosting, `refs/heads/Vote` and `refs/heads/vote` are the same physical ref. Silent aliasing of two logical streams into one. ** A spamming worker inflates the ref namespace; `ls-remote` slows for everyone; liveness dies without any single visible failure. Per-identity ref quotas at the hook. Adversarial and semi-honest failures ** Signed commits give attribution, not correctness. A compromised key holder signs garbage that passes integrity checks. Semantic validation must exist at the hook (deterministic validator, not a decision-maker — this is the line that keeps it from being a central brain) and/or at verify-on-read. **Mixed enforcement modes. ** Some readers verify signatures and canonicality; others trust the ref because "the server checks. " Divergent acceptance sets → two honest voices. Pick one globally: enforce-on-write everywhere, or verify-on-read everywhere. ** Force-pushed rewrites strand every cached hash downstream. Published bus refs are append-only, period. **Void-cascade ambiguity. ** A bad commit is detected; the fix is a forward-correction (void commit), never a rollback. But if later commits descend from the voided one, the cascade rule (void descendants? ) must be a deterministic function of the DAG, decided in advance — not adjudicated ad hoc, which would resurrect a central brain. Boundaries — where the guarantee stops - **Crash-fault tolerance, not Byzantine. ** Quorum > N/2 gives safety under crash faults. Git signing provides attribution, not Byzantine agreement; tolerating Byzantine behavior requires quorum-intersecting signed votes, which is a different treaty. Do not claim BFT from this construction. - **Single-shard linearizable, cross-shard eventual. ** A single ref serializes updates (CAS point). Scale-out via sharded refs reintroduces multi-shard transactions, which need a coordinator — i. , a central brain. The treaty's honest scope: linearizable within one shard/ref-family, compensating operations across shards. ** All writes serialize through one ref's CAS. Expect ref-update lock contention to cap write rate regardless of N. Checkpoint refs every K commits cut read cost (O(tail) not O(history)), but checkpoints must be *verifiable reconstructions* — deterministic folds over history that anyone recomputes and compares — never authoritative shortcuts, or checkpoint-writer becomes the brain. - **Statelessness is reconstruction, not amnesia. ** Every worker caches the fetched snapshot between operations. "Stateless" means "provable rebuildable from the bus," nothing stronger. Transport must be authenticated (pinned host keys/certs) or the cache is MITM-poisonable. - **Roster changes are epoch-boundaried. ** Membership edits execute under the *old* roster's quorum and take effect at a defined epoch boundary (e. , commit-height modulo). Never atomically with data; never retroactively. Otherwise "which N counts for this quorum? " is unanswerable mid-flight. ** Consensus round-trip ≈ git push RTT. Sub-second coordination loops are outside this design's envelope. What Must Never Happen (invariants) **Never rewrite or delete published bus history. ** Append-only, enforced by `deny-non-fast-forward` plus reader-side chain verification. **Never derive ordering from wall clocks. **Never accept a write without CAS against the exact expected prior value. **Never leave an ambiguous push outcome unreconciled. ** Re-read before retry, always. **Never allow two distinct contents to occupy the same sequence slot. ** Per-worker monotonic sequence numbers, hook-enforced. **Never permit implicit merge resolution by any single party. ** Fast-forward only on bus refs; merges only as pre-defined deterministic folds or quorum-signed events. **Never let the fold/checkpoint function vary between workers. ** Its code hash lives in the treaty; mismatch = refuse to participate. **Never mix enforce-on-write and verify-on-read populations. ** One acceptance discipline, global. **Never allow quorum/membership to change atomically with data. ** Epoch boundaries only. **Never wrap sequence or epoch counters. ** On overflow: halt loudly, never wrap silently. **Never allow a tie between competing chains to persist undecided. ** A total-order tiebreak (e. , lexicographically greatest tip hash wins) must exist in the treaty; without it, a dual-CAS anomaly or mirror divergence becomes a permanent split voice. **Never treat a signature as proof of semantic validity**, and never treat server presence as proof of integrity unless hooks are provably active. The sharp edge, summarized Break any one and you don't get degraded consensus — you get *two honest voices that each believe they're the only one*, which is the precise failure the treaty exists to prevent. The design's job is not to make workers agree; it's to make disagreement *detectable and total-order-resolvable by any observer, including a fresh stateless worker reading the bus cold*. The user is asking about a "Ghost-AOS git-bus treaty" — this appears to be a fictional or proprietary system concept. The framing: N stateless workers achieving consensus without a central brain, speaking as one honest voice with no drift. They want edge cases: failure modes, boundaries, and invariants ("what must never happen"). Since I don't have actual documentation of a "Ghost-AOS git-bus treaty," I need to reason from first principles about what such a system would be: a git-based communication bus where stateless workers coordinate through commits/refs rather than direct messaging, governed by a "treaty" (protocol contract). This is essentially a CRDT-like / event-sourcing architecture using git as the substrate. Let me think hard about what the real failure modes are for such an architecture: **Architecture model**: Git as the bus. Workers are stateless — they read state from git refs, compute, write back via commits. Consensus emerges from the treaty rules governing ref updates (fast-forward only? "One honest voice, no drift" means all workers must converge to identical interpretations of state. Let me enumerate concrete failure modes: **Ref race conditions**: Two workers push to the same ref simultaneously. Git's compare-and-swap on refs (`git push --force-with-lease` semantics) gives linearizable CAS per-ref, but only if the treaty mandates it. Failure: worker A reads ref at commit X, computes, writes commit Y based on X; worker B does same, writes Z based on X. If both force-push, last-writer-wins silently drops one lineage → drift. **Clock skew / timestamp ordering**: Stateless workers can't rely on wall-clock timestamps for ordering because their clocks drift. If the treaty uses commit timestamps for ordering, two workers with skewed clocks produce out-of-order history. Must use DAG topology (parent hashes), not timestamps. **Split-brain on remotes**: Multiple git remotes (mirrors). A worker reads from remote 1, writes to remote 2 which is behind/lagged. Replication lag between mirrors creates phantom divergence. Treaty must pin single source of truth or define mirror promotion protocol. **Shallow/partial clones**: A stateless worker doing shallow clone sees truncated history. It may misinterpret state (e. , missing a tombstone marker from 500 commits ago). Boundary: minimum clone depth or full fetch mandated. **GC and object pruning**: `git gc` on the server prunes unreachable objects. If a worker holds a reference to a commit that gets pruned mid-operation, its fetch fails or worse, it reconstructs partial state. Objects referenced by in-flight operations must be protected (e. , via refs/keepalive or quarantine). **Idempotency of writes**: Stateless worker crashes after commit but before recording that it committed. On retry, it re-reads state, sees its own commit, and applies the operation again → double-apply. Need deterministic operation IDs embedded in commit messages, and treaty rule: skip if op-ID already present in history. **Non-deterministic computation**: Worker computes result depending on environment (locale, float rounding, library version, time-of-day). Two honest workers produce different outputs from same input → drift. Treaty must mandate canonical serialization (sorted keys, fixed encoding, integer math or fixed-point, pinned dependency hashes). **Merge conflicts as consensus failures**: If treaty allows merges, merge resolution is a judgment call = central brain reappears implicitly in whoever resolves. Must forbid merges on bus refs; fast-forward only, or explicit quorum-signed merge commits. **Sybil / rogue writer**: Anyone with push access can write anything. But hooks run on server = central brain? No — hooks are deterministic validators, not decision-makers. Boundary: validation logic must be pure function of the incoming ref update. **Rebase rewriting history**: Force-push rewrites published history. Readers who cached old hash now see dangling references. Never rewrite pushed refs; append-only ledger invariant. **Tag vs branch confusion**: Annotated tags are objects; lightweight tags are refs. A worker dereferencing ambiguously may read different states. Treaty: one ref namespace, exact refspec grammar. **Empty tree / initial commit edge**: First commit has no parent. Workers computing diffs against parent must handle null parent. Also orphan branches appearing on the bus = parallel universes. Reject non-fast-forward including orphan roots on bus refs. **Large blobs / LFS pointers**: Binary artifacts break text-diff assumptions; LFS pointer files reference external store that can be GC'd independently → pointer without payload = corrupt voice. Either forbid blobs above size threshold on bus or define blob retention tied to referencing commits. **Commit message encoding**: Non-UTF8, CRLF vs LF, trailing whitespace — two workers parse the same commit differently. Canonicalization required at write time; readers reject non-canonical. **Race between read and prune of notes/refs**: `refs/notes` used for metadata can be updated concurrently; notes merge strategies are lossy by default (cat_sort_uniq etc. If treaty stores coordination metadata in notes, concurrent note appends lose data. **Quorum ambiguity**: If treaty says "N-of-M workers must ack," how is ack recorded? Commits to an acks ref? Concurrent ack commits race; counting them requires reading reflog or walking history — reflogs aren't replicated! Counting acks via reflog breaks across mirrors. Acks must be ordinary commits on a branch, counted by DAG walk. **Timeout/liveness vs safety**: A worker holding a lease (lock ref with expiry timestamp) dies; lease expires; another takes over; original wakes up and still thinks it holds lease → two writers. Fencing tokens needed: lease includes epoch number; writes carry epoch; server rejects stale epochs. But git refs have no native fencing — must encode epoch in ref name or commit content and validate in hook. **Lock ref itself races**: Creating lock via `git push` of a lock ref — two workers create same lock ref, one wins CAS, loser must detect. If loser's client doesn't check push result properly (network error where push actually succeeded — ambiguous outcome! ), you get double-lock. Ambiguous RPC outcomes: timeout ≠ failure. Worker must reconcile by re-reading remote state before retrying. **Network partition during push**: Push partially received (pack sent, ref update not confirmed). Server has objects but ref not moved. Retry pushes same pack — fine, idempotent at object level, but worker must handle "everything up-to-date" responses. **History walk cost explosion**: Consensus-by-DAG-walk degrades as history grows unboundedly. Stateless worker re-reading full history each cycle = O(N²) total work. Boundary: checkpoint refs (snapshots) every K commits; workers read latest checkpoint + tail. But checkpoint creation is itself a write needing consensus. chicken-and-egg. Checkpoints must be deterministic function of history (anyone can verify), not authoritative. **Byzantine vs crash faults**: Git integrity (SHA-1/SHA-256 content addressing) prevents accidental corruption but not malicious valid-signature writers. A compromised worker with valid key can sign garbage. Treaty needs semantic validation layer + key revocation procedure. Revocation is itself a consensus event — who revokes without central brain? Pre-committed revocation policy: any worker can push revocation ref; effect is automatic. **SHA-1 collision**: Old git SHA-1 collision attacks (SHAttered). Use SHA-256 repos or at least new-object-format SHA-1 (collision-resistant hardened). **Time-of-check-to-time-of-use on working state**: Worker reads HEAD, computes, pushes with --force-with-lease expecting base=X. Between its fetch and push, ref moved. CAS fails — good. But if worker naively force-pushes, silent clobber. Treaty: all bus pushes MUST use CAS (old-value expectation); servers MUST enforce deny-non-fast-forward except through explicit quorum path. **Determinism of conflict-free merge when treaty allows multiple append-only streams**: e. , each worker owns refs/workers/<id> (append-only personal log), and "voice" = deterministic fold over all worker logs sorted by (content hash). Then convergence is guaranteed IF fold is commutative/associative/idempotent (CRDT-ish). Edge cases: worker log forks (two heads on own ref — shouldn't happen with CAS but ambiguous push outcomes can cause retry-fork); fold must handle duplicate entries (idempotence) and out-of-order arrival (commutativity). Snapshotting the fold must be verifiable: snapshot commit includes input set hashes so any worker can recompute and compare. **Membership changes**: N changes. Adding/removing workers mid-flight: quorum computed over which roster? Roster itself stored on the bus → bootstrap problem and racing roster updates. Boundary: roster changes require quorum under OLD roster, take effect at defined epoch boundary (commit height % epoch length), never retroactively. **Zombie workers / slow workers**: Partitioned worker returns after hours, replays stale ops. Op IDs dedupe handles it, but stale *leases* and stale *views* must be rejected by epoch/fencing. **Git protocol quirks**: denyCurrentBranch` — pushing to checked-out branch fails confusingly. - Atomic push (`--atomic`) across multiple refs: without atomicity, multi-ref transaction half-applies on error → inconsistent multi-ref state. Treaty: either single-ref-per-transaction or --atomic mandatory. - Hidden refs / namespaces: worker with limited visibility sees partial bus → wrong view. - Shallow push: pushing from shallow clone can fail or produce broken history. - Case-insensitive filesystems on some hosts: refs differing only by case collide (refs/heads/Main vs main on macOS/Windows servers) → two logical refs become one physical ref, silent aliasing. **Observability gap**: "One honest voice" claim needs verification. Without a liveness/health signal, partitioned minority keeps writing to unreachable fork forever. Need heartbeat refs with TTL and a deterministic "canonical head" election (e. , longest valid chain by hash order tiebreak) so any observer can identify THE voice. Election rule must be total order: e. , highest chain tip hash wins lexicographically. Any deterministic total order works; absence of one = permanent split. **What must never happen (invariants)**: - Never rewrite or delete published bus history (append-only). - Never accept a write whose validity depends on reader-side mutable config. - Never allow two different contents to both claim same sequence slot (per-worker monotonic sequence numbers enforced by hook). - Never derive ordering from wall clocks. - Never allow implicit merge resolution by any single party. - Never allow the fold/snapshot function to differ between workers (pinned code hash in treaty). - Never allow unbounded retention gaps (checkpoint cadence floor). - Never allow ambiguous push outcomes to go unreconciled (must re-read before retry). - Never allow membership/quorum to change atomically with data (epoch separation). - Max commit size, max refs count, max fan-in per epoch. - Minimum quorum: > N/2 for safety under crash faults; > 2N/3 only if Byzantine tolerated — git signing gives attribution not Byzantine agreement; so treaty is crash-fault tolerant, NOT Byzantine fault tolerant unless you add quorum intersection on signed votes. - Latency bound: consensus round-trip bounded by git push latency (~hundreds of ms); throughput bounded by ref-update serialization on a single ref (~lock contention). Scale-out via sharded refs, but cross-shard transactions then need two-phase commit — which reintroduces a coordinator → boundary: treaty scope is single-shard linearizable, cross-shard eventually consistent with compensating ops. **Statelessness illusion**: True statelessness impossible — every worker caches at least the fetched snapshot between operations. "Stateless" really means "reconstructible. " Edge case: worker's cache poisoned by MITM if transport isn't authenticated (SSH known_hosts, HTTPS certs). Trust-on-first-use pitfalls. **Hook bypass**: Server-side pre-receive hooks are the enforcement point; if hosting platform (GitHub etc. ) disallows custom hooks or they're disabled, treaty degrades to convention-only → any client bug becomes corruption. Boundary: self-hosted bare repo with hooks, or treaty must assume adversarial clients and make readers verify everything (verify-on-read model). **Verify-on-read vs enforce-on-write**: If enforcement is on-write (hooks), readers trust refs. If hooks unavailable, readers must verify each commit (signatures, canonical form, chain continuity). Mixed mode = worst: some readers verify, some don't → divergent acceptance sets → split voice. Pick one, globally. **Recovery from detected violation**: History shows invalid commit slipped through. Rollback = history rewrite = forbidden. Forward-fix: append correction commit marking invalid range as voided; canonical fold skips voided ranges. Voiding authority = quorum-signed void commit. Edge: voiding a commit that later commits depend on → cascade semantics must be defined (void descendants too? deterministic rule required). **Empty operations / no-op commits**: Worker pushes empty commit as heartbeat; fold must ignore empty payloads but still count sequence numbers. Mismatch between "counted" and "meaningful" events. **Unicode normalization**: Same logical string, different NFC/NFD forms → different hashes → duplicate-but-distinct entries. Canonicalize NFC at write. **Integer overflow in sequence numbers / epoch counters**: define widths; wraparound policy (never wrap; halt instead). Bound: per-identity ref quota enforced by hook. **Time-based lease vs height-based lease**: Prefer height-based (commit-height leases) since height is consensus-visible; wall-clock leases depend on unsynchronized clocks.
