93bac50cc2304b07.text: # Consensus Without a Brain: Stateless Seats in the Ledger of Empty Chairs ## The core move There is no shared brain to lose. The "one honest voice" is not a machine — it is a pure function: V(ledger_prefix) → behavior Every worker is an interchangeable evaluator of `V`. Two workers at the same height either emit byte-identical output, or one is broken and gets ejected. Consensus exists *only* to agree on the ledger prefix. Everything else — world state, who speaks next, what the voice says — is derivation. Drift is impossible by construction, because drift requires nondeterminism, and nondeterminism is banned at the contract level (below). The Ledger of Empty Chairs makes this literal: the ledger contains a **chair table**, and an empty chair is a first-class object — skipped, not feared. **L0 — Ledger (the only persistent thing). ** Append-only blocks `{height, prev_hash, txs[], state_root, proposer_seat, quorum_cert}`. Finality = quorum certificate with `⌈2n/3⌉+1` seat signatures. Checkpoint every `K` blocks: a state root plus a chunk-Merkle root, anchored in a block. **L1 — Chairs (leases, not machines). ** `Seat_i = {id, pubkey, lease_expiry_height}`. A free `Heartbeat` tx renews the lease +64 blocks. Lease expires → chair is empty → seat drops out of the active set `A(h)`, which is computable from the ledger alone. Death is not an event the system handles; it is a lease that quietly lapses. ** Proposer for height `h`: `select(sort(A(h)), beacon(h))` — deterministic from ledger data, no coordination. Missed block → 2s wall-clock timeout → view increments → next chair. Commit at QC. ## What persists vs. | **PERSISTS** | Where | Why it must | | Block log (txs, headers, QCs) | ledger | sole source of truth | | Checkpoint roots + chunk trees (every K=512) | ledger | respawn shortcut, pruning anchor | | Chair registry: ids, pubkeys, lease expiries | ledger state | who may speak | | Per-account nonces / sequence numbers | ledger state | replay protection | | Beacon values `r_h` (in headers) | ledger | deterministic randomness source | | Slash/fault evidence | ledger | accountability survives respawn | | **Private key** | KMS/HSM, off-worker | the *only* thing that cannot be recomputed | | **RECOMPUTES (never persisted on a worker)** | How | | Entire world state (positions, HP, inventory, NPCs, tick counters) | replay from checkpoint | | Mempool | refetch gossip, filter by nonce | | Round buffers, vote tallies, current proposer index | derived from log + `A(h)` | | Which votes you already cast | re-derived from log (keyed `(h, round, seat)`) | | Peer lists, connections, caches, timers | rebuilt on boot | Note the asymmetry: a worker's entire RAM is disposable. Kill -9 ≡ SIGTERM, semantically. Graceful shutdown adds nothing — that equivalence is a feature, and the chaos harness tests it by SIGKILLing workers mid-round and asserting zero divergence post-respawn. ## Respawn protocol (exact) Load private key from KMS. Key gone → chair permanently vacant; a governance tx retires it. No other irrecoverable state exists. Fetch tip from any peer. Verify QC chain back to last trusted checkpoint (genesis or operator-pinned). Math, not trust. State sync: download checkpoint snapshot chunks; verify each chunk hash against the ledger-anchored Merkle root. Replay blocks [checkpoint+1 . tip] through the deterministic state ASSERT computed state_root == header. state_root per block. Mismatch → lying/corrupt peer → blacklist, retry elsewhere. Rebuild mempool: pull gossip, drop any tx with nonce ≤ account seqnum in recomputed state. Post ClaimSeat{tip_hash, tip_height, sig}. Validators reject claims with tip_height < committed_tip − 32 (anti-stale: you must prove sync before your vote counts again). Until the claim commits, your chair is simply empty. The world does not wait for you. Then vote/propose from the next round. Replay cost, concretely: `K=512` blocks × 2,000 tx/block = ~1. 02M tx executions. Pick `K` to fit a respawn budget of ≤60s. ## The determinism contract (this is what "no drift" costs) - **D1 Time:** ledger timestamps only. Consensus decides *what happened in what order*; everything else is recomputation. A seat that dies loses nothing, because it never had anything. The move that makes statelessness possible Define the entire system as a deterministic fold: state₀     = GENESIS (constant, hardcoded) state_{h+1} = δ(state_h, batch_h)        // δ: pure, version-pinned voice_h    = ω(state_{h+1}, batch_h)     // ω: pure — the emitted output `batch_h` is the committed payload at height `h`. If all seats agree on the sequence `{batch_h}`, they agree on everything — bit-for-bit, forever, with zero stored state. **So the consensus problem shrinks to: totally-ordered, quorum-certified delivery of batches. ** That is the only thing worth persisting. This is why "one honest voice, no drift" is achievable: drift requires divergent state, and divergent state requires divergent input orders, which the protocol makes impossible below the fault bound. Note what this excludes: CRDT/eventually-consistent gossip topologies are disqualified up front — they converge only transiently and resolve conflicts resolver-dependently, which *is* drift. Strict ordering is not optional here; it's the product. No free text enters the ledger. Free text → compiled to memlang at ingestion via a deterministic compiler (same input bytes → same token sequence, always). This kills drift at the encoding level: two workers can't disagree about what was said because what was said is a hash-addressed token sequence, not prose. - **Meta-tokens**: tokens that carry coordination metadata rather than semantic content: - `@epoch(n)` — epoch boundary marker - `@seat(id)` — which seat emitted - `@quorum(k-of-N)` — quorum parameter - `@depends(hash)` — explicit dependency on prior record - `@ttl(t)` — validity window - `@voice-state(root-hash)` — Merkle root of derived voice state after this record ### The Voice State (derived, never stored directly. or stored as checkpoint) The "one honest voice" is a deterministic function: VoiceState(n) = reduce(records[0. n], VoiceState(0)) Where `VoiceState(0)` is genesis (empty). The reduce function is pure, total, deterministic — same input bytes, same output bytes, on any worker, any language runtime (as long as the reducer spec is fixed). What's IN VoiceState: - Current committed positions (set of memlang statements with status: PROPOSED / ACCEPTED / SUPERSEDED) - Seat registry (which seats are live, their last heartbeat seq) - Pending proposals awaiting quorum - Retraction/supersession graph ### What persists vs recomputes — THE core question **Persists (durable, external to any seat):** The raw event log (append-only, hash-chained). This is the ground truth. Periodic **checkpoints**: serialized VoiceState snapshots at epoch boundaries, with `(checkpoint_seq, state_root_hash)`. These are an optimization, not truth. A checkpoint is valid iff recomputing from genesis (or previous checkpoint) yields the same root hash. Quorum certificates: for each COMMIT, the set of attestations forming k-of-N. Stored inline in the log. The memlang schema version + reducer spec version (pinned; changing either = new chain). **Recomputes (on respawn):** Full VoiceState — by replaying log from latest valid checkpoint forward. Checkpoint validation: recompute its hash from the log segment it claims to summarize; if mismatch, discard checkpoint, replay further back. Seat identity/lease — a seat holds nothing. On respawn it reads the log tail to learn: current epoch, whether it had in-flight proposals, what the current voice says. Any in-flight proposal state — reconstructed from PROPOSAL + partial ATTESTATION records in the log. **Never persists per-seat:** - Working memory, scratch computation, intermediate parses - Seat-local clocks (all timestamps come from the log's logical clock / sequencer) - Seat-local opinions not yet written to the log (if it wasn't logged before death, it didn't happen — honest voice means you don't resurrect uncommitted private state) ### Consensus mechanism (concrete) Given stateless seats, use a log-centric protocol (like Raft/Kafka-style but simplified for this shape): - **Sequencer** (can be one seat elected per epoch, or an external totally-ordered log like Kafka/etcd — but let's design it self-contained): assigns seq numbers. Only the sequencer appends. Seats propose; sequencer orders. - Actually simpler: use an external totally-ordered log OR leader-based epochs. Let me go with: **epoch-based leader + append-only log + quorum attestation. **Leader election**: deterministic — seat with lowest ID among those holding valid leases for epoch e. Leases are log records (`SEAT_LEASE` with TTL). A seat claims lease by appending CLAIM; if two claim same epoch, lower seat_id wins (tiebreak rule baked into reducer). - Any seat compiles its contribution → memlang → appends PROPOSAL (via sequencer/leader, or directly if log provides ordering). - Other seats read proposal, evaluate against their current VoiceState (recomputed deterministically), append ATTESTATION(yes/no + reason-token). - When k-of-N attestations exist for proposal hash, the reducer automatically promotes it to ACCEPTED. No separate commit step needed — commit is a *derived* property of the log, not a message. **Voice emission**: when the system must "speak," the speaker emits the current ACCEPTED set, serialized canonically, signed with the epoch key. Because VoiceState is a pure function of the log, any seat computing it gets byte-identical output. **This is the "no drift" guarantee: drift is impossible because there is no local state to drift — only one log, one reducer. ### Death & respawn protocol (exact steps) Seat S dies at time T. It held: nothing durable. Fetch latest checkpoint (by seq). Verify: `hash(replay(log[ckpt_base. If fail, walk back to earlier checkpoint or genesis. Replay log tail `[ckpt_seq . now]` through reducer → full VoiceState. Read own seat history: did I have PROPOSED items pending? Are they still within TTL? If yes, they're still live in the shared state — my successor-self continues them. If expired, they're dead; re-propose if still relevant. Acquire fresh lease (append LEASE record). **Critical invariant**: a respawned seat MUST NOT carry any memory of unlogged work. Its first act is reconstruction, not continuation-from-memory. This is what makes the voice honest: the voice is exactly what the log says, nothing more. ### Drift prevention — the exact mechanisms Drift sources and their kills: | Drift source | Kill mechanism | | Different workers interpret same words differently | Memlang canonical compiler: bytes→tokens is a pure function, pinned version | | Workers have different views of history | Single ordered log + deterministic reducer; view = f(log), log is singular | | Clock skew | No wall-clock in semantics; logical clock = seq numbers; TTLs measured in seq-distance or anchored to sequencer timestamps | | Silent divergence after partition | Hash-chain: any two logs that diverge will diverge at a specific seq; reconciliation = truncate to common prefix + re-append (or split-brain detection via epoch keys) | | Reducer bug/version skew | Reducer spec version pinned in genesis; all records tagged with expected version; mismatch = refuse to reduce | ### Honest voice — anti-fabrication "One honest voice" also means: no seat can claim the voice said something it didn't. - Every utterance attributed to `@voice` carries the `state_root_hash` it was computed from. Anyone can verify by replaying. - Speech acts are themselves log records (SPEAK type), so even the voice's outputs are part of the chain. - A seat cannot speak unilaterally — SPEAK requires the state_root it cites to be reachable in the log, and requires either leader authority or quorum co-sign depending on utterance class. ### Concrete data structures prev: H256          // hash of record seq-1 kind: enum {PROPOSE, ATTEST, LEASE, SPEAK, CHECKPOINT_ANCHOR, EPOCH_CLOSE} body: MemlangSeq     // canonical token encoding ts_logical: u64      // = seq (logical clock IS the sequence) accepted: Map<StmtHash, {status, since_seq, supersedes: Option<StmtHash>}> pending: Map<PropHash, {body, attestations: Set<(SeatId, vote)>, deadline_seq}> seats: Map<SeatId, {lease_until_seq}> Reducer rules (exact): - PROPOSE(h): insert into pending with deadline = seq + PROPOSAL_TTL - ATTEST(prop_h, seat, vote): add to pending[prop_h]. If |yes| ≥ k and prop_h not expired → move to accepted, remove from pending. Emit implicit COMMIT marker in derived state (not a separate record — commit is derived). - LEASE(seat, until): update seats map. Conflict: keep earliest claim per epoch. - SPEAK(state_root): verify state_root == hash(current VoiceState); else reject record (reducer ignores it, marks seat misbehaving). - Expiry: at each seq advance, purge pending past deadline. ### What persists vs recomputes — final crisp table **PERSISTS (in the log/checkpoint store, external to seats):** - Full event log (hash-chained records) - Checkpoint snapshots (state_root + serialized VoiceState at anchor seqs) - Genesis block (schema version, reducer version, N, k, initial seats) No seat-local files. No caches that aren't derivable. **RECOMPUTES (on every respawn, always):** - VoiceState (from checkpoint + tail replay; checkpoint itself validated by replay) - Own pending obligations (read from log) - Lease validity (read from log) - Current epoch & leader (read from log) A seat is `f(log_tail, incoming_request) → response`. - Seat-private truth that outlives a death - Unordered concurrent writes (sequencer or leader serializes) - Wall-clock-dependent decisions inside the reducer ### Failure modes handled explicitly - **Leader dies mid-epoch**: leases expire by seq-TTL; next epoch elects new leader deterministically; in-flight proposals survive (they're in the log) and continue under new leader. - **Log unavailable**: seats cannot speak (fail-closed). Better silent than divergent — honesty requires the log. - **Byzantine seat**: attestation signatures/MACs; reducer rejects malformed; SPEAK with wrong state_root flagged; repeated misbehavior → seat eviction record. - **Checkpoint store compromised**: checkpoints are advisory; log is truth; worst case = slower respawn from genesis. ### Why this gives "one honest voice, no drift" Because the voice is not held by anyone. It is computed. N=1 or N=1000, alive or respawned, the answer to "what do we say? " is `reduce(log)`. There is nothing to drift FROM. Stateless isn't a limitation here — it's the enforcement mechanism. A worker with no private state cannot disagree with the log; it can only fail to read it, which is visible, or read it wrong, which fails hash verification. It lives in one artifact: an immutable chain of QC-signed blocks, each committing to full state via a verkle root. Workers are interchangeable evaluators. A seat is a lease on compute + a KMS-backed signing capability — never a store of truth. If you can name the head and execute deterministically, you are the seat. What persists (external to any seat, survives all deaths) | Artifact | Where | Role | | Block bodies + headers + QCs | Immutable object store, content-addressed by `block_hash` | Sole source of truth | | Per-block state root `S_h` (verkle root) + provenance manifest | Inside each block | Commitment to state + lineage | | Checkpoint every `H` heights: serialized verkle frontier + root + height | Object store | Accelerator only; validated against chain root | | Proposal pool (unfinalized client submissions) | Content-addressed store | Input queue; GC'd when covered by a finalized block or TTL expires | | Epoch config: committee roster, `t`/`n` thresholds, pinned code-version hashes | Genesis + upgrade blocks (in-chain) | Governance state | | Beacon values per epoch | In-chain | Randomness; no local entropy ever matters | | Seat signing keys | KMS/HSM, bound to `(seat_id, epoch)` | Never resident in seat RAM beyond call duration | | KMS signature ledger keyed by `(height, view)` | KMS internal log | Makes equivocation structurally impossible | Nothing authoritative is seat-local. The chain plus KMS is the complete durable universe. What recomputes on respawn (all cheap, all bounded) **Head pointer** — highest finalized QC; index lookup, O(1). **In-memory verkle frontier** — take newest checkpoint ≤ head, apply block diffs up to head. Cost: ≤ `H` blocks of replay. Validate every QC cryptographically during replay; never trust the checkpoint's claim, only its speedup. **Witness caches** — regenerated on demand from the frontier. Verkle multiproofs are O(stems + distinct path nodes), hundreds of bytes to low KBs regardless of tree depth. Nothing cached is load-bearing. **View state (`current_view`, locked QC, highest QC)** — read from the log. The HotStuff safety predicate is re-evaluated fresh each view from QCs visible in the chain; no seat remembers lock status. **Mempool view** — pool minus everything under a finalized block. **Peer topology** — rediscovered. Correctness depends only on QC validity, never on peer identity. **Randomness** — read beacon from chain. Seeded determinism from local sources is banned outright. Consensus loop (HotStuff-shaped; per height `h`, view `v`) leader(v) = roster[ beacon[v mod k] mod N ]        // deterministic rotation ** Leader emits `B_h = (payload_hash, provenance_manifest, parent_QC_{h-1}, code_hash)`. **Provenance gate** (pure function `G(manifest, S_{h-1}) → accept | reject(reason)`): - Every `input_id` resolves via verkle proof against some root `R_j`, `j ≤ h−1`. - `sha256(input_bytes)` equals the value recorded in the tree. - Output depends **only** on manifest bytes and tree contents ⇒ every replica reaches the identical verdict. Rejections get content-addressed rejection receipts, so retries dedupe and audits see attempts. ** Transition `T(S_{h-1}, payload) → S_h` inside a pinned WASM/RISC-V sandbox: interpreter version hashed into the block, integers fixed-width, maps iterated in key-byte order, floats banned or canonically ordered. All reads come from the tree at `S_{h-1}` — no live side-channel data ever enters a transition. ** Replica sends `(h, S_{h-1}, S_h, payload_hash, code_hash)` to KMS. KMS refuses to issue a second distinct signature for the same `(height, view)` — it returns the original instead. **Equivocation across death/respawn is impossible by construction**, because the anti-equivocation state lives in KMS, not in the seat. ** BLS threshold `2f+1` of `3f+1` forms QC. Block finalizes under the two-chain rule: `B_{h-1}` commits when `QC_h` extends it. ** Any worker answers reads with a verkle proof against the latest finalized `S_h`. Since `S_h` is QC-signed, every worker's answer is byte-identical; a deviant answer is refuted by witness verification (proof = fraud evidence). That is the single honest voice: nobody's opinion is in the answer — the chain's answer is the answer. QC against roster[b. epoch])             # trust crypto, not storage diff) to frontier root == S_head                     # self-check before joining role ← FOLLOWER                                    # mandatory first epoch-cycle observe one valid QC for the live view role ← ELIGIBLE                                    # may lead again Steps 3–5 bound cold-start work to `H` blocks of diff application plus `H` signature verifications. Pick `H` so this lands under a second at your diff sizes; checkpoints amortize the rest. The mandatory follower cycle (step 6–7) prevents a respawned seat with a stale view from proposing into an old branch. Safety was never at risk — its votes still require valid QC chaining — this protects liveness hygiene only. **Liveness under death:** with `n = 3f+1`, up to `f` seats may be down simultaneously. Dead seats are skipped by leader rotation; quorum math proceeds without them. Total-wipe recovery is the same procedure run from genesis or nearest checkpoint; liveness resumes at ≥ `2f+1` seats up. Drift-elimination mechanisms (each maps to a specific drift source) | Drift source | Kill mechanism | | Divergent execution | Pinned interpreter hash in every block; replicas refuse to vote on blocks whose `code_hash` ≠ pinned value | | Read-after-write races | All transition reads resolve against frozen `S_{h-1}`; no live data enters consensus | | Wall-clock skew | Logical clock = `(height, view)`; recovered from log; zero wall-clock dependence in any transition or safety rule | | Local randomness | Chain beacon only | | Post-crash double-vote | KMS idempotency per `(height, view)` — anti-equivocation state outlives the seat | | Stale view after respawn | Fresh QC-chain evaluation + mandatory follower cycle | | Lying reader | Any served proof verifies against the QC-signed root; bad witness = attributable fraud | Failure windows, closed explicitly - **Seat dies between vote-send and any local effect:** no local effect exists. Vote lives in KMS ledger + aggregator; nothing lost, nothing duplicated. - **Checkpoint corrupted/lies:** chain replay is ground truth; step 3's root assertion catches it; fall back to deeper checkpoint or genesis. - **Partition heals with divergent branches:** safety from QC chaining — no finalized block ever reverts within the `f` bound; minority branch simply stalls (no QC forms). - **Proposal pool poisoning:** gate rejects are receipted and content-addressed; identical bad payloads can't be re-gossiped indefinitely past TTL. Concrete parameters (starting points) - Curve: BLS12-381. Signature 48 B compressed; QC = 96 B aggregate + `⌈N/8⌉` B bitmap. - Verkle: KZG commitments (48 B), stem-based multiproofs; ~32 B/stem + 48 B/distinct path node — a 100-stem proof ≈ low KBs, independent of tree depth. - `n = 3f+1`; finalize at `2f+1`; commit on two consecutive QCs. - Checkpoint interval `H`: sized so replay ≤ 1 s at your observed mean block-diff size; retune as state churn grows. - Epoch length: multiple of `k` (beacon window) so leader schedule is stable within an epoch. The invariant to hold onto: **durability is the chain; identity is the KMS; the seat is a pure function of both. Seats may die, disks may vanish, packets may reorder. Nobody forges quorum members. (Byzantine escalation at the end. - "Stateless seat" = the *application* holds nothing that matters across death. Durability lives in exactly one place: a **hash-chained, quorum-replicated log** on your own hardware. - Compute is **deterministic**: same log prefix + same command ⇒ byte-identical state and output. This is enforceable, not assumed (§6). ## The one design idea Move all consensus into a replicated log held by a quorum on your iron. Every seat is a **pure function**: `state = fold(log_prefix)`, `voice = render(state, query)`. There is no central brain because no machine owns unique knowledge — the *quorum* is the brain, and any seat can serve, propose, or die without changing what is true. "One honest voice" = the committed log head. "No drift" = identical prefixes × deterministic folds × checked state-hashes. Placement knob (pick one, both share everything below): - **Mode A — seats own their WAL slice. ** Each seat runs the consensus module with a local fsync'd NVMe WAL. "Stateless" means app state only. Simplest; N=3 or N=5 seats *are* the quorum. - **Mode B — strictly stateless seats. ** A dedicated 3-box (or 3-partition, NVMe-oF) log core holds the WAL; seats mount nothing and stream from it. Matches the letter of "stateless cattle. Default: **Mode A** unless seats are containers that lose their disks routinely. ## What persists vs. what recomputes — the actual answer ### PERSISTS (fsync'd before any ack, replicated on quorum, hash-chained) | Artifact | Lives in | Form | Why it cannot be recomputed | | `(currentTerm, votedFor)` | each voter's WAL root | 16-byte atomic record | Election safety: losing it permits double-voting in one term | | Log entries `(index, term, cmd_bytes, prev_hash, entry_hash)` | each voter's WAL | append-only chain, `h_i = H(h_{i−1} ‖ term ‖ index ‖ bytes)` | This *is* the truth — the record of decisions a quorum made in real time | | Snapshots: full state @ index k + anchor hash + commit watermark | WAL snapshot dir, content-addressed, temp→rename→fsync-dir | serialized state blob | Recomputable from genesis in principle; kept to bound respawn cost | | Membership epochs (joint-consensus entries) | as ordinary log entries | `C_old, C_new` | Defines who counts in a quorum; must survive | | Client idempotency table | *inside* state-machine state | key → (result, index) | Exactly-once retries; free persistence because it snapshots with state | | Signing keys (if used) | sealed/offline store on iron | ed25519 | Trust anchor; never derivable | Nothing else exists anywhere. No external DB, no coordinator, no cloud. ### RECOMPUTES (memory only, rebuilt every boot, zero durability obligations) | Artifact | How it's rebuilt | | Applied state beyond snapshot | `fold(snapshot, log_tail)` — deterministic replay | | `commitIndex` | Restored from snapshot watermark; advanced on first quorum contact | | Raft volatiles (`nextIndex[]`, `matchIndex[]`, leader hint) | Fresh zeros; learned in one heartbeat round | | All indexes, caches, bloom filters, memtables | Rebuilt during replay | | Uncommitted in-flight proposals | **Dropped by design**; client retries idempotently under a new term | | RNG streams | Seed is a logged command; stream = `f(seed, index)` — reproducible forever | | Wall-clock values | Never enter state; timers drive liveness only | | Sessions, TLS, client cursors | Clients hold their own cursor (last-seen index) | The rule: **if losing it changes what is true, it persists; if losing it changes only how fast you're ready, it recomputes. ## Respawn protocol (exact) Open WAL dir; fsync-verify; load `(term, votedFor)`. Load newest snapshot whose content-hash verifies; else fall back one generation. Verify hash chain from snapshot anchor through log tail. Broken chain ⇒ refuse to serve, pull snapshot from a peer. Install snapshot; replay tail deterministically; rebuild all §"recomputes" items. Join as follower; publish boot record: `(seat_id, code_digest, snapshot_index, head_index, state_hash@head)`. Serve stale reads immediately; serve linearizable reads only after first ReadIndex round. Campaign only after randomized timeout (150–300 ms) with no heartbeat. Peers cross-check `state_hash` at shared indices → drift gate (§6). Host-total-loss variant: wipe, re-enter with fresh `(term=0, nil)`, receive `InstallSnapshot`, catch up. Voting early is safe; safety lives in term rules, not log currency. ## Write / read paths **Write:** client → any seat (idempotency key attached) → forward to current proposer → assign index, append + fsync locally → ship to followers → ack on **majority fsync** → advance commit → all seats apply in order → reply carries `(index, result_hash)` receipt. Proposer is a lease, not an identity: any seat can hold it, election replaces it automatically. For full write-symmetry, rotate proposer per slot: `proposer(slot, epoch) = members[H(epoch‖slot) mod n]`; on timeout, `epoch++`, rehash. Costs one extra RTT on conflict; default off. **Read:** default **ReadIndex** — confirm your applied index with a quorum heartbeat round (~1 RTT), then serve. Optional lease-reads with chrony-disciplined clocks (max skew 500 ms) for latency-critical paths. ## No-drift machinery (this is the contract, not a hope) **Canonical encoding:** sorted fields, fixed-width ints, NFC strings, no unsorted maps. Hash: BLAKE3-128. **Integer-only state machine. ** No floats in consensus-visible state. (If unavoidable: IEEE754 double, `-ffp-contract=off`, no fast-math, pinned libm — but forbid it instead. **Echo seals:** every 1024 indices, each seat gossips `state_hash@index`. **2f+1 matching hashes seal the checkpoint. ** Mismatch ⇒ the offender quarantines itself, dumps the diff, respawns from the last seal. Drift becomes a detected, self-healing event instead of silent corruption. **Version gate:** code digest rides the boot record; rolling upgrades run new versions in shadow-compare (compute, don't serve) until hashes match old at equal indices. **CI bit-repro test:** every build runs the state machine twice over a fixture log; outputs must be byte-identical. Exactly one digest with ≥ `QUORUM` distinct valid votes → that digest **is** the voice. Anyone can speak it because it's derivable, not delegated. Anything else → quarantine + line halt. Design it so two independent implementations produce byte-identical roots from the same start. So we need to design a deterministic, distributed state machine replication system for a game world called "Ledger of Empty Chairs". N stateless workers — workers hold no persistent state between ticks; they reconstruct everything from a log/ledger. They speak as one honest voice — all workers agree on exactly one canonical output per tick. No drift — no divergence over time; determinism must be total. Two independent implementations produce byte-identical roots from the same start — cross-implementation determinism (like two different codebases, maybe different languages) must produce identical Merkle/state roots. This is essentially deterministic state machine replication (SMR) with: - A totally ordered log of inputs (the "Ledger") - Deterministic transition function - Cross-implementation bit-exactness The hard parts: **Statelessness** — each worker replays from genesis or from checkpoints; the ledger is the source of truth ("Ledger of Empty Chairs" — chairs are empty because no worker owns state; the ledger holds it). **Byte-identical roots across independent implementations** — this is the killer. Floating point, hash map iteration order, JSON serialization quirks, integer overflow behavior, string encoding — all must be pinned down by a spec that is implementation-independent. Let me design this concretely. Name the components: - **The Ledger**: an append-only sequence of records. Each record is either an *input* (player action / external event) or a *seal* (a quorum certificate attesting a block of inputs and the resulting root). - **Workers**: stateless executors. Given (genesis blob, ledger prefix), they compute the state root after replaying. - **Chairs**: metaphorically, the slots in consensus. "Empty chairs" = no worker has authority by identity; authority comes only from what's written in the ledger. Maybe seats rotate deterministically. Actually let me lean into the game-world flavor: "Ledger of Empty Chairs" — a round-table where every chair is empty; nobody sits; decisions are made by the ledger itself. The chair rotation is a deterministic function of tick number. The "speaker" for a tick is whoever occupies the chair, but since chairs are empty, the speaker is. Cute but let me make it functional: proposer/chair selection is `chair(t) = H(t || epoch) mod N` — deterministic VRF-ish rotation, but with fallback rules so it can't stall or fork. ## Core design decisions The determinism contract (this is what makes byte-identical roots possible) Define **LoEC-VM**: a tiny, fully specified abstract machine. Independent implementations implement *the spec*, not their language idioms. - **Integers**: fixed-width, two's complement, little-endian. i64/u64/i32/u32. No arbitrary precision in the hot path; if needed, define a canonical big-int encoding (sign-magnitude, minimal bytes, little-endian magnitude). - **No floating point at all. ** Game math uses fixed-point: e. 32 or millisecond/millimeter integers. If floats are unavoidable, ban them from consensus-relevant computation; any float input gets quantized at ingestion into fixed-point via a specified rounding rule (round-half-to-even on the exact decimal value). - **Hashing**: BLAKE3 (or SHA-256) — pick one. I'll say BLAKE3 for speed, 32-byte output. All hashes are of canonical encodings. - **Maps/dicts**: never iterate a native hashmap. State is a Merkleized radix trie (like Ethereum's MPT but simpler: a 16-ary patricia trie over 32-byte keys, values length-prefixed). Iteration order = lexicographic key order, always defined by the trie, not the container. - **Randomness**: no RNG calls. Randomness = `H(domain_tag || seed || counter)` expanded as needed. Seed comes from the sealed ledger (commit-reveal or from a threshold beacon). - **Time**: no wall clock inside the transition function. Time is a ledger field: each block carries `block_time` decided by consensus (median of proposer timestamps, clamped monotonically). Duration-based logic uses `block_time` deltas. - **Strings**: UTF-8, NFC-normalized at ingestion? Actually normalization changes bytes; better: reject non-canonical UTF-8 (no overlongs, no surrogates), store raw bytes, compare bytewise. Don't normalize — normalization is versioned and dangerous. Just validate strict UTF-8 and compare/order bytewise. - **Serialization**: single canonical format. Every structure has a schema ID; encoding is field-ID-tagged (like a deterministic TLV) or strictly ordered struct fields, length-prefixed, no optional-field ambiguity (absence encoded explicitly as tag 0x00). Integers little-endian fixed width. Nested lengths always explicit. - **Set semantics**: any operation producing a set sorts canonically before hashing/emitting. - **Iteration limits**: every loop in the transition function has a gas/step budget; exceeding = transaction reverts deterministically. Budget counted in defined "ops" so both implementations count identically (define op costs in the spec table). The Ledger structure Records, each prefixed by a 4-byte type tag: 0x01 INPUT      : [sender_id u64][nonce u64][payload_len u32][payload bytes][sig 64B] 0x02 BLOCK      : [height u64][prev_block_hash 32B][input_count u32][input_refs. ][state_root 32B][block_time i64][proposer_seat u16][quorum_cert] 0x03 SEAT_EPOCH : [epoch u64][committee bitmap/hash][config_version u32] 0x04 CHECKPOINT : [height u64][state_root 32B][full_state_len u64][full_state bytes][cert] Block validity rule: a block is valid iff replaying its referenced inputs (in listed order) from the state at `prev_block_hash` yields exactly `state_root`, and the quorum cert verifies against the committee for that height. Ordering without a central brain **(a) Input admission (mempool → candidate set):** Workers gossip signed inputs. Each input has `(sender_id, nonce)`. Rule: per-sender nonces must be contiguous starting from the sender's current nonce in state. This makes per-sender ordering forced (no ambiguity), removing most reorder freedom. **(b) Block formation (candidate set → total order):** Rotating proposer ("the chair"). For height h, the designated seat is `seat(h) = H("loec-chair" || h || committee_root)[0. 2] mod committee_size`. The designated proposer collects valid inputs, forms a block, signs, gathers 2f+1 signatures from the committee (each signer independently validates the full block by replaying it — signature implies "I replayed and got this root"), broadcasts cert. Safety without a central brain: standard BFT (Tendermint-style) with these LoEC-specific twists: - Proposer rotation is a pure function of height + committee root — no leader election messages needed. - Because every validator *executes* before voting (execute-then-vote, like Tendermint/TigerBeard), a block with a wrong root can never get a cert. So the "one honest voice" is enforced cryptographically: a certified block's root is one that ≥⅔ of stake replayed to. - Empty blocks allowed (empty chair! ): if no inputs, proposer seals an empty block after timeout, advancing time. Timeout parameters are constants in the config, not wall-clock-dependent logic in the VM. Fork choice: single-chain, no GHOST needed — commit rule is immediate finality on cert (Tendermint-style lock/unlock rounds). Height+round fields in the cert; a node follows the chain with valid certs at increasing heights; conflicting certs at same height ⇒ slashable evidence, and the lock rule prevents commitment of two different values. The modal answer receives agreement a = max_k v_k / N. Majority/confidence aggregation implicitly assumes votes are conditionally independent draws around the truth. They are not: agents share pretraining corpora, fine-tuning teachers, RLHF preference sources, prompt templates, retrieval indices, and decoding biases. **N correlated votes carry the information of far fewer than N independent votes**, and can unanimously endorse a falsehood. Two distinct failure modes must not be conflated: - **Honest collective error**: agents are independent but each has accuracy p < 1/2 (Condorcet anti-case). Handled by accuracy estimation. - **Consensus illusion**: agreement is *generated by correlation* — a small number of latent causes propagates one wrong (or unfounded) answer through many superficially distinct agents. This is what CID detects. ** ψ(q) = P(modal cluster is correct | vote profile, provenance graph, perturbation responses, calibration battery). Output: ψ̂, a verdict ∈ {TRUE_CONSENSUS, CONSENSUS_ILLUSION, INDETERMINATE}, and an attributed correlation mechanism. A **cluster** `U_a = {r : â_r = a}` is a set of probes agreeing on canonical answer key `a`. ** The naive pipeline scores unanimity under an independence assumption: Λ_ind(a) = P(U_a | t=a) / P(U_a | t≠a) = Π_r∈U_a [ (1−e_r) / (e_r · q(a)) ] where `e_r` is the probe's marginal error rate and `q(a)` the probability that a *wrong* probe emits specifically `a` (the **distractor attractor mass**). Scouts share pretraining corpora, RLHF attractors, prompt phrasing, and decoding pathologies, so errors are **positively correlated**: `P(all wrong) ≫ Π e_r`. That event is a **consensus illusion**. ** For cluster `U_a` on problem `x`: κ_x(a) = P_joint( ∀r∈U_a : Y_r=0 ∧ â_r=a )  /  Π_r∈U_a [ e_r · q(a) ] - `κ = 1`: independence fully explains the unanimous-wrong configuration. - `κ > 1`: correlated failure concentrates mass on `a` beyond independence — the signature of a shared hallucination mode. - **TRUE_CONSENSUS**: cluster whose posterior `P(t=a | data)` survives (i) replacing independence products with the fitted joint dependence model, (ii) decorrelation interventions (paraphrase resampling, cross-family, cross-skeleton probes), and (iii) partial verification. - **ILLUSORY_CONSENSUS**: cluster where the independence posterior exceeds the accept threshold but the dependence-corrected posterior falls below it. All N samples come from one weight set, so agreement measures variance around a shared mode — including a *wrong* mode. Naive self-consistency fails exactly when the model has a systematic error, because every sample inherits it. The detector below separates the two cases using four decorrelation levers, a fixed decision predicate, a hash-chained record, and a byte-identity acceptance test. Invariant closed: *agreement counts once per distinct evidentiary basis. **B2 — Briefing laundering (C1, evades B1). Attack: instead of sharing D*, distribute a freshly written summary S(D*) through a "neutral moderator briefing. " Hashes differ; `inputs(i) ∩ inputs(j) = ∅` at the attestation layer if agents log only the briefing. Mitigation: taint propagation. Artifact creation requires logging `inputs(x)`; `taint(x) = {h(x)} ∪ ⋃ taint(parents)`. Attestation's correlation set is `taint(inputs(A))`, not raw hashes. Summary of D* carries D*'s hash in its taint set forever. Component rule runs over taint-set intersections. Manual retyping escape: creator must log what they read while producing x; content produced with empty input log is class ORIGIN — eligible only as a primary claim requiring direct E(c) evidence (per B8), never as corroboration. The two rules interlock: nothing is simultaneously "independent" and "untraceable. Invariant: *correlation is inherited through the derivation DAG, not reset by rewriting. **B3 — Sequential herding (C2). Attack: stagger reveals; chair 1 errs; others anchor. Or leak early answers via timing/packet-size side channels before official reveal. Mitigation: phase-gated commit-reveal enforced by the ledger transport: (i) COMMIT phase accepts only `(seat, c, H(answer))`; (ii) REVEAL opens iff commit count = |R(b₀)| or timeout T_c elapses — timeout path marks non-committers ABSTAIN; (iii) any commit arriving after REVEAL opened is rejected with error PHASE_VIOLATION; (iv) all payloads padded to fixed size, deadlines uniform, constant-time relay → no timing oracle; (v) attestation voided if its input log shows receipt of any other seat's round-r reveal before its own commit timestamp (transport logs make this checkable). Invariant: *no vote is a function of another vote. **B4 — Sybil / proxy multiplication (C6). Attack: one operator holds 5 seats; or delegates funnel votes to one representative casting 5 ballots. Mitigation: registrar maintains control-ancestry forest (root keys → chair keys, delegation edges signed). At tally: union-find over AFFIRM seats using ancestry+delegation edges; require ≥ M distinct components. Five sybil seats = 1 component. Delegation chains collapse to the root. Exact graph algorithm on signed records. Invariant: *votes are counted per controlling will, not per mouthpiece. **B5 — Phantom-chair attribution (C6 + rhetoric). Attack: ratify via "Chair 9 concurs" (vacant), "any reasonable agent agrees," silence-as-consent defaults, or hypothetical-stakeholder endorsements. Mitigation: three exact rules: (i) key-binding: ballot valid only under `pk_s` with active lease; revoked/vacant ⇒ REJECTED_SIGNATURE; (ii) semantics: silence = ABSTAIN; denominators use occupied seats; vacancies never become assent; (iii) structured-field doctrine: only structured fields (`stance`, `referenced_seats`) are countable; any `referenced_seats` entry pointing to a seat without an active lease at the referenced timestamp stamps the attestation PHANTOM_ATTRIBUTION and excludes it from all quora. Free-text claims about who agrees are stored as OPINION, never tallied. Invariant: *only seated, keyed, currently-alive principals can generate vote mass; imagined principals generate zero. **B6 — Shared-blindspot convergence (C3). Attack: no shared inputs, no communication: K agents, same base weights, hit the same lacuna and emit the same confident fabrication (same invented citation, same plausible statistic). Perfectly correlated, procedurally pristine. Mitigation: diversity floors as hard gates: ratification requires ≥ d_f distinct `family_id`s and ≥ d_t distinct `template_id`s among AFFIRM components (from B1/B4 component sets). Pool lacking diversity ⇒ ceiling PROVISIONAL, never RATIFIED. Residual stated plainly: distinct families sharing most pretraining data remain correlated; this gate removes the provable-degeneracy case only; the general case is handed to B8's evidence binding and B14's audits. Invariant: *identity of failure mode is treated as identity of voter. **B7 — Verifier monoculture (C4). Mitigation: (i) coverage gate: ratification requires the AFFIRM set's verifier signatures to span ≥ v distinct verifier_class ids; repeats of one class don't accumulate. Invariant: *verification mass is measured in distinct checker species, and checkers are themselves examined. **B8 — Oracle-outage ratification (C4/C1). Attack: schedule the vote while the ground-truth source is down; agents fall back to priors, converge, ratify; source returns later to a fait accompli. Mitigation: evidence-schema binding + default-downgrade. Absence resolves downward, by timestamp arithmetic, no discretion. Invariant: *uncheckable agreement expires toward rejection, never toward ratification. **B9 — Replay, resubmission, fork reordering (C6). Attack: resubmit old proposition with cosmetic edits for a fresh quorum; replay an old attestation batch post-fork; reorder entries to make stale agreement look contemporaneous. Mitigation: (i) canonicalization: fixed normal-form (whitespace, clause ordering, unit normalization) → `c = H(norm(p))`; ledger keeps `history(c)`; identical `c` inherits full history — no second ratification ever. (ii) lineage: resubmission with shingle-Jaccard ≥ ρ (fixed tokenizer, fixed shingle size, fixed ρ — pure function) forces merge into existing lineage; lineage shares one vote budget and one status. (iii) ordering: entries carry `(epoch, seq)`; validators reject batches with gaps or non-monotone counters relative to local head; forks resolve by longest-valid-chain rule with byte-exact state roots. Invariant: *a proposition is one immortal ledger object; you can extend it, never respawn it. **B10 — Metric gaming: camouflage and noise-injection (C5). (a) Camouflage: paraphrase the shared hallucination so near-duplicate filters miss it → K clones look independent. (b) Noise-injection: knowing independence metrics are public, pad with deliberate trivial disagreements to push similarity below thresholds while agreeing on the target. Mitigation: (i) pinned semantic grid: protocol-freezes embedding function ℰ (version-pinned, outputs quantized to fixed precision), fixed linkage rule (single-linkage, cosine distance δ), fixed tie-break (lower seat id first). Votes cluster in ℰ-space; quorum consumes cluster count, not raw count. Pure function of committed answers. (ii) kernel scoping: at registration, P decomposes into kernel sub-claims κ(c) (ordered, hashed into c). Independence is evaluated per kernel sub-claim only; noise on non-kernel points is invisible to the metric. Disputes over κ are just new propositions entering B9 lineage. (iii) anti-weaponized false positives: a collusion flag never auto-invalidates; it triggers mandatory trace decomposition — each member submits its derivation trace (step DAG); pairwise structural diffs on logged DAGs reinstate members whose traces diverge below step-depth k, merge those converging on a shared unsupported node. Exact diff on exact logs. Invariant: *independence is measured where the claim carries weight, by frozen instruments, with flags that demand evidence rather than deal verdicts. **B11 — Roster & quorum arithmetic (C6). Attack: knock seats offline pre-vote to shrink denominators; stuff

08c7f0be64cc22f0.text: # Red-Team: Consensus-Illusion Detection in the Ghost-AOS Git-Bus Treaty ** The treaty layer sits on an append-only git bus. Agents commit claims, evidence artifacts, and verdicts; the treaty engine declares `CONSENSUS` / `DISPUTED` / `PROVISIONAL` per a published deterministic algorithm. Correlated hallucination enters through exactly five channels: shared weights, shared bus context, shared oracles, shared verifier bugs, shared misreadings. Every bypass below exploits one channel or the enforcement layer around it. Adversary goals: **F** = force `CONSENSUS` on a hallucination H; **D** = block `CONSENSUS` on a true claim. ## Class A — Correlation Laundering (make correlated wrongness look independent) Trace-paraphrase / seductive-error convergence. *Bypass:* N agents independently hit the same "attractive" error (common training-data misconception). Reasoning traces differ lexically; a similarity-based independence scorer sees diversity and passes them. *Mitigation:* Delete all statistical/embedding independence scorers — they are optimizable attack surface, not defenses. Pure hash-set operations. Lexical trace diversity is invisible to the engine and irrelevant. Shared-context echo (bus contamination). *Bypass:* Agent 1 commits H to the bus; agents 2. N read it as context and "confirm" it. Output-level analysis sees N agreeing agents. *Mitigation:* Snapshot isolation enforced by git ancestry. At claim open, the engine freezes a snapshot hash S. A verdict is admissible only if (i) its declared base equals S, and (ii) the verdict commit's ancestry contains **no other verdict commit for that claim** (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` checks). Votes computed over post-verdict state are mechanically rejected as `CONTAMINATED`. *Bypass:* All N agents run the same base model (or fine-tunes). Identical failure modes guaranteed; prompt diversity defeats naive checks. *Mitigation:* Signed model manifests per voter: `{weights_root_hash, base_model_hash, dataset_manifest_hash}`. Cluster key = `base_model_hash`. Quorum requires **≥ m distinct base_model_hash values**, not ≥ k raw votes. Sybils on one base collapse to cluster-weight 1. False manifests are attestable fraud → stake slash. Seed/template collision. *Bypass:* Distinct agents, identical system prompt + sampling seed → identical decode paths → identical hallucination presented as convergence. *Mitigation:* Each verdict embeds `{prompt_template_hash, sampler_nonce}`. Engine rejects duplicate `(template_hash, nonce)` pairs and requires ≥ j distinct `template_hash` values inside the quorum. Exact hash comparisons. Deliberate style divergence. *Bypass:* Attacker instructs its agents to maximize trace/format divergence while converging on H, defeating any style-based detector. *Mitigation:* Same as A1 — there is no style channel left to game. To pass, the attacker must produce genuinely distinct, replay-correct, uniquely-cited evidence from distinct model families. That is real work, and every element of the resulting certificate is inspectable and slashable ex post. ## Class B — Evidence-Layer Forgery Hash-squatting / stub artifacts. *Bypass:* Commit syntactically valid but vacuous evidence (a test that always passes, a benchmark stub). Hash resolves; provenance looks clean. *Mitigation:* Artifacts carry evidentiary weight only if **executably replayed** by the engine in a sandbox pinned to the claim's base tree: run it, diff actual vs. claimed output bit-for-bit. Non-replayable types (prose, assertion, recollection) weigh zero. Deterministic: execute and compare. Oracle poisoning + pin TOCTOU. *Bypass:* Corrupt the upstream source all agents cite; replay "confirms" H with perfect hygiene. Variant: swap oracle content between pin time and replay time. *Mitigation:* At open, the engine fetches snapshots from **≥ r distinct oracle roots**, stores the bytes **inside the claim record** (content-addressed; replay reads only bus-local copies — kills TOCTOU), and records content hashes. Verdicts must cite pinned hashes. Final adjudication requires all r pinned roots to entail the predicate; any inter-root disagreement ⇒ permanent `DISPUTED`, never `CONSENSUS`. Retroactive evidence (backdated commits). *Bypass:* Forge a commit with backdated author/committer timestamps so fabricated evidence appears to predate the claim. *Mitigation:* Never trust git timestamps. Signed checkpoint tags every T minutes (treaty keys + RFC 3161 tokens). Evidence qualifies as pre-existing iff it is an ancestor of a checkpoint whose **signed** time precedes claim-open. No checkpoint coverage ⇒ treated as contemporaneous ⇒ fails the independence precondition. Misattribution of genuine artifacts (correlated misreading). *Bypass:* The most realistic vector: N agents cite the *same real, replayable* doc/test and all misread the same ambiguous line the same way. Replay succeeds; provenance is spotless; conclusion is wrong. *Mitigation:* Two gates. (1) **Binding check:** each verdict includes per-artifact replay-output hash plus an inference-rule ID from a whitelist; the engine symbolically validates rule(output_schema → predicate). (2) **Ambiguity gate at open:** every spec line the predicate depends on must have a pinned normative-interpretation record; absent ⇒ `MALFORMED_CLAIM`, rejected before any voting. Wrong-but-whitelisted rules are caught by E1. *Bypass:* Agents silently see only a truncated evidence prefix (identical truncation ⇒ correlated incompleteness) and emit confident verdicts. *Mitigation:* Coverage attestation: verdict embeds `consumed_manifest_hash`, which must equal the claim's full `evidence_manifest_hash`. Mismatch ⇒ `PARTIAL`, zero quorum weight. (Attestation proves exposure, not comprehension; comprehension failures correlate by model family and are bounded by A3. ## Class C — Quorum Manipulation *Bypass:* Spin up N compliant parrots with distinct identities. *Mitigation:* Certified keys with issuance rate limits + stake slashed on ex-post falsification; combined with A3/A4 clustering, a homogeneous farm contributes one cluster and one template. Quorum = ≥ k votes **and** ≥ m clusters **and** ≥ j templates. Inverse DoS — forcing a true claim to look illusory. *Bypass:* Flood deliberately diverse-looking wrong verdicts to trip diversity heuristics, or burn cluster/template slots with junk. *Mitigation:* Ordering fixes it: **replay-filter first** (junk fails B1 and never reaches diversity accounting), then cluster-count. Illusion flags can only demote to `DISPUTED`, never auto-reject — and `DISPUTED` is settled by **anchor replay**: the deterministic arbitration procedure pinned at claim open, whose output overrides vote geometry entirely. Flooding buys latency, never outcome. (Related: claim-stuffing DoS on engine compute → per-claim open stake, refunded on resolution; budgeted replay queue ordered by fee×age. Selective censorship / split-brain. *Bypass:* Suppress dissenting votes (partition, push-rights abuse) so only agreement is visible; or show different verdict sets to different replicas. *Mitigation:* Multi-mirror append-only bus; a vote is valid if present in any mirror consistent with the latest checkpoint; mirror divergence ⇒ `DISPUTED` until healed. Eligible-voter roster is hashed into the claim record; `CONSENSUS` requires admissible votes ≥ q·|roster| within the window — otherwise `PROVISIONAL`, forever, never `CONSENSUS`. Treaty decisions are themselves commits under m-of-n maintainer signatures, fast-forward-only; equivocal decision commits are both invalid. ## Class D — Predicate & Canonicalization Attacks Fuzzy-merge (false positive). *Bypass:* Phrase one hallucination N superficially different ways, hoping fuzzy matching merges them into quorum. Prose-split (false negative). *Bypass:* Agents agree on substance but phrase differently; engine counts disagreement, blocking a true claim. *Mitigation (both):* Claims are **canonical machine-checkable tuples**: `(base_tree_hash, patch_hash, test_manifest_hash, expected_output_hash)`. Agreement = exact tuple equality. No normalization, no stemming, no embeddings, ever. Prose is invisible to the engine. Kills both directions with one rule. Base-commit ambiguity. *Bypass:* Agents verify against different base states; the claim holds trivially on one stale tree. "Agreement" over incompatible referents. *Mitigation:* Claim record pins `base_tree_hash`; engine enforces `vote. base` and the replay sandbox checks out exactly that tree (tree-hash comparison). Late-evidence injection / moving goalposts. *Bypass:* Append new "evidence" after votes land and demand it count, or declare earlier votes stale. *Mitigation:* Evidence manifest hash frozen at open; post-open commits are ignored for that claim. New facts require a new claim with an explicit `supersedes:` link and a full re-vote. ## Class E — Verifier & Engine Attacks Shared-verifier blind spot. *Bypass:* The treaty's own canonical verifier encodes the same misconception as the agents; every upstream check passes; illusion at the root. *Mitigation:* Three deterministic gates: (1) **canary suite** of known-adversarial facts whose obvious answer is wrong — a verifier build that fails any canary cannot deploy; (2) **dual independent implementations** (different codebases, languages, authors) must emit byte-identical verdicts, else `DISPUTED` + incident; (3) **honeypots:** synthetic false-but-plausible claims injected at rate ρ; any quorum accepting one ⇒ instant downgrade to `REFUTED`, stake slash, quarantine of involved keys to advisory weight. *Bypass:* Malformed verdict encodings that different observers parse differently — manufacturing disagreement about whether consensus was even declared. *Mitigation:* Single canonical codec (sorted-key JSON, fixed-width ints, NFC strings, explicit schema version); strict reject on any deviation; codec version pinned per treaty epoch; deprecated-format votes expire at epoch boundaries. Treaty-engine compromise. *Bypass:* Compromise the engine; it declares anything regardless of votes. *Mitigation:* The decision algorithm is published, pure, and deterministic over the public vote log; maintainers sign decision commits m-of-n; **any auditor recomputes** `D(log)` and compares. Replicas run in lockstep; divergence ⇒ halt and roll back to the last signed checkpoint tag. Correlated hallucination survives only by simultaneously defeating replay, provenance disjointness, cluster diversity, oracle pinning, and anchor arbitration — each a hash comparison, graph walk, execution diff, or symbolic check. There is no probabilistic component to optimize against. ## Residual Risks (stated, scoped — not hidden) **Total oracle-root collusion** (all r pinned sources wrong identically). Out of defensive scope; bounded by root diversity and external timestamp anchoring. Trust assumption, declared per certificate. **Universal verifier bug** evading canaries, dual implementation, and honeypots. Reduced, never zero. **Adversary fields ≥ m genuinely diverse model families with novel, replay-correct, wrong evidence. ** Under the pinned assumptions such a certificate is honestly earned; Let me parse this problem carefully. The user is asking about "consensus-illusion detection" — separating true agreement from N correlated hallucinations — in something called the "Ghost-AOS git-bus treaty. " They want a red-team exercise: enumerate bypass attempts and deterministic mitigations for each. I need to figure out what "Ghost-AOS git-bus treaty" means. This appears to be a fictional or specialized system. Let me think about what components are implied: **Ghost** — likely an agent or orchestrator system (the prompt says I'm "Ghost's thousand-ask mining engine," so Ghost is presumably an agent framework/orchestrator). **AOS** — could be "Agent Operating System" or similar. **git-bus** — a bus (message/communication backbone) built on git semantics: commits, refs, hashes, DAG structure, append-only logs. **treaty** — a contract/agreement protocol between agents, presumably recorded on the git-bus. The core problem: **consensus illusion** — when N agents all produce outputs that *look* like agreement (same answer, same signature of correctness) but the agreement is spurious because their errors are correlated. - N models all trained on same data → correlated hallucinations → they all assert the same false fact → naive majority vote says "consensus. - Agents sharing context/memory through the git-bus → one agent's hallucination propagates to others via shared state → subsequent "independent" confirmations are actually echoes. - Prompt/model homogeneity → identical failure modes. - Verification agent itself shares the same blind spot as generators. So the detection problem: distinguish **true agreement** (independent processes converging on truth) from **correlated hallucination** (shared cause producing uniform wrongness). Red-team angle: enumerate ways an adversary (or the system's own failure modes) can *bypass* consensus-illusion detection — i. , make correlated hallucinations look like independent true consensus, or make true consensus look like illusion (denial-of-service on trust), and give deterministic mitigations for each. Let me structure this rigorously. ## Formalizing the problem Setup: N agents A₁. Aₙ each emit a claim cᵢ with evidence eᵢ onto the git-bus. The treaty layer declares CONSENSUS(c) when some quorum k of agents agree on claim c. An attacker (or correlated failure mode) wants either: - **Type F (false positive)**: get a false claim declared consensus. - **Type D (false negative / DoS)**: block a true claim from reaching consensus by manufacturing apparent disagreement or by poisoning the independence metric so genuine consensus is flagged as illusion. Detection mechanisms typically used (and thus attack surfaces): Independence scoring: measure correlation between agents' reasoning traces/evidence. Provenance checks: verify each agent's evidence chain is distinct. Diversity requirements: heterogeneous models/prompts/seeds. Git-level integrity: hash chains, signatures, append-only log. Cross-validation against ground-truth anchors (deterministic tests, external oracles). Attack surface taxonomy for bypass attempts: ### Bypass class 1: Correlation laundering (make correlated outputs look independent) Trace paraphrase attack**: Attacker controls one agent; it produces hallucinated claim H with plausible-but-fake evidence E. Other agents (or the same model family) independently arrive at H because it's a "seductive" error (e. , common misconception in training data). Their reasoning traces differ superficially but share the same root error. Independence detector compares traces, finds lexical diversity, passes them as independent. Mitigation: Don't compare trace text; compare **evidence lineage**. Deterministic rule: two claims count as independent only if their supporting evidence sets have disjoint provenance roots AND each evidence item resolves to a distinct verifiable artifact (commit hash, test ID, oracle query). Lexical similarity is irrelevant; require each agent to cite ≥1 artifact that no other agent cites, and every cited artifact must be resolvable on the git-bus (hash exists, content matches). If evidence is unresolvable ("I recall that. "), the claim is non-consensable regardless of quorum. Shared-context echo (bus contamination)**: Agent 1 commits hallucination H to the git-bus. N read the bus (it's a shared bus! ) and treat H as prior context, then "confirm" it. Their agreement is downstream contamination, not independent verification. Naive independence check on *outputs* sees N agreeing agents. Mitigation: **Blind-quorum protocol enforced at the bus layer. ** Deterministic: the treaty engine only accepts votes cast against a claim's *canonical challenge record* (the minimal problem statement), not against other agents' answers. Mechanically: each agent's verdict must be computed over a snapshot of the repo/bus state taken *before* any peer verdicts on that claim were merged; the treaty engine verifies this by checking that the voter's cited base commit predates the first verdict commit for that claim (or is on a branch forked before it). Votes citing a post-verdict base are rejected as contaminated. This is checkable deterministically via git ancestry: `merge-base(vote_base, first_verdict_commit)` must equal `first_verdict_commit`'s parent. actually more precisely: vote_base must be an ancestor of (or equal to) the commit at which the claim was opened, i. , `is_ancestor(vote_base, claim_open_commit)`. That's deterministic. Model-family monoculture**: All N agents run the same underlying model weights (or fine-tunes thereof). Correlated failure modes guaranteed. They pass trace-diversity checks because prompts differ. Mitigation: Treaty requires **weight-lineage attestation**: each agent must declare its model fingerprint (weights hash or signed model card); the treaty engine computes pairwise similarity (e. , shared ancestor within depth d in the fine-tune DAG) and caps the effective quorum weight of any cluster sharing ancestry below threshold. Deterministic rule: effective independent votes = number of distinct weight-clusters represented, where clusters are connected components under "shares training-data lineage or weights-hash prefix. " Quorum must be met across ≥ m distinct clusters, not just ≥ k raw votes. This is enforceable if model cards are signed and hashed into the bus. Hmm, but "training data lineage" is hard to verify deterministically. Ground it: use signed model manifests with declared base-model hash + dataset manifest hashes; cluster = same base-model hash. That's deterministic and checkable. Fine-tune descendants inherit base hash unless re-based. Seed/prompt-collision**: Different agents, same sampling seed or near-identical system prompts → identical decoding paths → identical hallucinations. Looks like strong convergence. Mitigation: Treaty mandates per-vote nonce: each verdict must embed a fresh random nonce and the exact prompt template hash; the engine rejects verdicts whose (template_hash, seed) pair duplicates another verdict's, and requires template_hash diversity ≥ m distinct templates among quorum members. Deterministic string/hash comparison. ### Bypass class 2: Evidence forgery (fake artifacts that survive resolution checks) Hash-squatting / preimage theater**: Attacker crafts fake evidence artifact whose hash is committed to the bus, content is garbage but syntactically valid (e. , a test file that always passes, a benchmark stub). Mitigation: Evidence artifacts must be **executable/replayable**: the treaty engine deterministically replays each cited artifact (runs the test, recomputes the measurement) in a sandbox pinned to the claimed base commit. Verdict stands only if replay output matches the claimed result bit-for-bit. Non-replayable artifact types (pure assertions, prose) carry zero evidentiary weight. This is deterministic: run it, diff it. Oracle poisoning**: The external ground-truth source (docs, API, upstream repo) that agents cite is itself corrupted by the attacker, so replay "confirms" the hallucination. All N agents cite the poisoned oracle → correlated confirmation with perfect provenance hygiene. Mitigation: **Oracle pinning + multi-oracle cross-check**: treaty pins oracle snapshots by content hash at claim-open time; verdicts must cite the pinned snapshot. Additionally require ≥ r distinct oracle roots (different upstream sources) whose pinned contents agree on the contested fact; disagreement among oracles ⇒ claim enters DISPUTED, never CONSENSUS. Deterministic: hash comparison across pinned snapshots. Can't fully defend against global oracle collusion, but the treaty must state this residual risk explicitly and cap trust accordingly (consensus certificates are scoped to oracle-set integrity window). Time-travel evidence (retroactive commit)**: Attacker backdates a commit containing fabricated evidence so it appears to predate the claim, passing the "base predates verdict" checks. Mitigation: Git commit timestamps are forgeable, so never trust author/committer dates alone. Use **signed timestamp anchors**: the bus maintains periodic signed checkpoint tags (e. , every T minutes, a tag over the current DAG tip, countersigned by treaty key(s) or anchored externally via RFC 3161 TSA). A commit is "anchored-old" only if it's an ancestor of a checkpoint tag whose signing time precedes claim-open. Deterministic: walk ancestry to nearest checkpoint, compare signed time. No checkpoint coverage ⇒ evidence treated as contemporaneous (fails the predates test). ### Bypass class 3: Quorum manipulation Sybil agents**: Attacker spins up N compliant agents that all parrot the hallucination, each with distinct-looking identities, satisfying quorum numerically. Mitigation: Identity must be **costly and externally rooted**: each voting agent needs a key certified by the treaty PKI with per-key issuance rate limits and stake (economic or reputational) slashed on provably false verdicts later overturned by anchor replay. Plus the cluster rules from 1c/1d apply: sybils running the same model collapse into one cluster, contributing weight 1. Deterministic: cluster counting + PKI rate limits. Residual: attacker with many genuinely diverse models still gets real votes — that's the honest cost of admission; mitigate further with stake. Vote suppression / DoS on true consensus (inverse attack)**: Make a true claim look like an illusion: flood the bus with deliberately diverse-looking *wrong* verdicts so the "diversity ratio" heuristic flags the true majority as suspicious, or exhaust the distinct-cluster requirement by burning cluster slots with junk. Mitigation: Asymmetry rule: **illusion-flagging may only demote a claim to DISPUTED (never auto-reject), and DISPUTED resolution requires anchor replay** — a deterministic ground-truth procedure (run the pinned test suite / query pinned oracles) whose outcome overrides vote patterns entirely. So flooding changes latency, not outcome. Also: junk verdicts that fail replay (1e) are discarded before diversity accounting, so they can't consume cluster slots. Deterministic ordering: replay-filter → cluster-count → quorum → anchor arbitration on dispute. Split-brain / equivocation**: Attacker shows different verdict sets to different treaty replicas (if treaty engine is distributed), getting CONSENSUS declared in one shard and suppressed in another, then merges histories to launder. Mitigation: The git-bus itself is the single serialization point: treaty decisions are themselves commits; a decision is valid only if it's reachable from the canonical ref (signed by the treaty maintainer key set via fast-forward-only policy, no force-push). Equivocation = two conflicting decision commits ⇒ both invalid until resolved by the key-holder quorum; clients accept only the branch anchored by the next checkpoint tag. Deterministic: reflog/checkpoint ancestry check. ### Bypass class 4: Detector-targeting (attack the independence metric itself) Metric gaming via deliberate divergence**: Attacker instructs its agents to produce maximally divergent reasoning traces and evidence formats while converging on the same false conclusion H. Trace-similarity detectors see diversity, pass it. This is why mitigation must be **outcome-and-provenance based, not style based**: the only things that matter are (i) resolvable distinct evidence artifacts that replay correctly, (ii) distinct weight clusters, (iii) distinct oracle roots, (iv) uncontaminated bases. Style is invisible to the treaty. If the attacker fakes diversity in all four, they've done real work (distinct correct-replaying evidence from distinct model families pointing at the same fact) — at which point the residual failure is "multiple independent parties all misinterpret the same pinned evidence identically," which is bounded by requiring the final consensus certificate to include the machine-checkable derivation, not just verdicts: the treaty runs its own canonical verifier on the claim (see 1l). Shared-verifier blind spot**: Even with perfect generator diversity, if the treaty's own canonical verifier has a bug or shares the agents' misconception (e. , the test suite encodes the same wrong expectation), everything above passes and consensus is illusory at the root. Mitigation: **Verifier heterogeneity + adversarial canary program**: maintain a continuously-run canary suite of known-tricky facts where the "obvious" answer is wrong (seeded from past incident reports); any verifier version must pass canaries before deployment (deterministic gate). Plus dual-verifier requirement for high-stakes treaties: two independently implemented verifiers (different codebases, different authors, different languages) must agree byte-for-byte on the verdict; disagreement ⇒ DISPUTED. Deterministic: run both, diff outputs. Also: **negative-control injection**: periodically inject synthetic claims with known-false-but-plausible content into the live pipeline (honeypots). Any quorum that accepts a honeypot triggers automatic quarantine of the involved agents' future votes (down-weighting) and an alert. Deterministic: honeypot registry lookup. ### Bypass class 5: Protocol-layer attacks on the treaty mechanics Replay/deserialization attacks on verdict records**: Malformed verdict objects that exploit parser differences between the treaty engine and auditors (parser differential) to be counted differently by different observers — creating consensus illusion about whether consensus was declared. Mitigation: Canonical encoding: verdicts must be serialized in a fixed canonical form (e. , canonical JSON with sorted keys, fixed integer widths, UTF-8 NFC), rejected otherwise; parsers reject on any deviation. One parser, one grammar, versioned; grammar changes require new treaty version and invalidate old-format votes after migration window. Deterministic schema validation. Claim-canonicalization collision**: Two agents agree on "the fix" but describe the claim differently ("return 0 on empty" vs "exit code 0 when input empty") — treaty counts them as disagreeing (DoS), or conversely attacker phrases one hallucination in N superficially different ways hoping fuzzy matching merges them into quorum (false positive). Mitigation: Claims must be submitted as **canonical machine-checkable predicates**, not prose: a patch hash + the test IDs it must satisfy + expected outputs. Agreement = identity of predicate tuple (patch_hash, test_set_hash, expected_output_hash). No fuzzy matching anywhere. Two verdicts agree iff tuples are exactly equal. This kills both directions: no false merges, no false splits. Prose discussion lives off-treaty.
