e1643ff567d779b0.text: # Consensus-Illusion Detection: Full Red-Team Enumeration + Deterministic Mitigations Formal Core — Why Raw Agreement Is Worthless Agreement is confirmatory **only under conditional independence**. With mean pairwise error-correlation ρ̄ across N agents: N_eff = N / (1 + (N−1)·ρ̄) 9, N = 100 → N_eff ≈ 10. ρ̄ = 1 → N_eff = 1. One hundred agents sharing one hallucination carry exactly one vote's worth of information. In an LLM swarm, ρ̄ > 0 **by construction**: shared pretraining corpora, shared RLHF pipelines, shared retrieval indices, shared prompt framings, shared tool APIs. So the default assumption must be *correlated until proven independent*. **Master discriminator:** true agreement means answers depend on shared *evidence*; consensus illusion means answers depend on shared *priors/exposure*. Every bypass below attempts to hide or counterfeit this dependence structure. Every mitigation is an intervention that exposes it. **Fail-closed axiom:** if independence cannot be affirmatively demonstrated for a given decision, the system outputs `NO CONSENSUS — CORRELATION SUSPECTED` with the failing gate named. It never defaults to acceptance. The Five Subsystems Under Attack | ID | Subsystem | Function | | S1 | Lineage fingerprinting | Behavioral DNA clustering of agents | | S2 | Independence accounting | Error-correlation matrix, N_eff, cluster-weighted aggregation | | S3 | Dependence probing | Intervention tests exposing evidence-vs-prior causation | | S4 | Sequencing & accountability | Commit-reveal, proper scoring, stake/slashing, Merkle audit | | S5 | Verification layer | Entailment-grade citation checking, hardened judge ensemble | S1/S2 — Correlation Laundering ### B1 — Clone flooding / lineage masking **Attack:** Deploy K fine-tunes of one base model under distinct names/personas. Identical pretraining prior → identical hallucination modes. Persona diversity defeats name-based checks; K "independent" confirmations of one wrong fact. **Defeats:** Identity metadata, persona-diversity metrics. **Mitigation:** Behavioral fingerprinting, not metadata. Fixed probe battery (≥200 canonical prompts with known idiosyncratic error signatures) administered to every agent. Pairwise response-similarity matrix S; agents with match rate ≥ τ_fp (0. 92) are **collapsed into one cluster and counted once**, regardless of claimed identity. Votes weighted 1/cluster_size. Weight-hash attestation used where available; behavioral fingerprint is the black-box fallback. Recompute fingerprints every epoch. ### B2 — Sybil quorum saturation **Defeats:** Any unweighted or naively weighted vote. **Mitigation:** Cluster-composition gates, deterministic: - Quorum valid only if ≥ r = 3 distinct lineage clusters contribute; - Single-cluster vote mass capped at c_max = 1/3 of quorum weight; - Admission requires passing the probe battery and placement into a cluster; clusters at cap cannot admit more members. Sybil cost now scales with the number of *genuinely distinct lineages*, which is bounded. ### B15 — Probe-battery leakage **Attack:** Obtain the fingerprinting battery (insider/side-channel); train clones to diverge *on probes only* while staying identical elsewhere. Clustering fails; clone flood proceeds. **Defeats:** S1 as specified in B1. **Mitigation:** Rolling committed probes. Per-epoch probe sets generated from a seed revealed only after the testing window closes (commit-reveal). Probes drawn from a large parametric family (template × instantiation) so memorization doesn't transfer. Add **adaptive decision-tree probes**: probe n+1 depends on the candidate's answer to probe n — canned divergence requires modeling the whole tree. Cluster assignment requires consistent placement across ≥2 epochs; unresolved agents get the **pessimistic default** (merged with nearest cluster for weighting). ### B21 — Benign herding / tool monoculture (non-adversarial correlation) **Attack:** Not an attack at all — the dominant real-world failure. All agents use the same search API returning the same snippet, or copy the strongest agent's answer. Emergent ρ̄ → 1 with zero intent. **Defeats:** Anything assuming correlation implies collusion. **Mitigation:** Tool exclusivity + entropy floor. Per quorum, ≤1 agent per external tool per claim. Track answer entropy H over a fixed agent set across rounds; H < h_min triggers **round invalidation and isolated re-run** (fresh contexts, shuffled tool assignments). Conditional mutual information between answers given shared tools identifies the correlation vector; the offending tool is excluded next round. ### B22 — Shared-context contamination **Attack:** Multi-turn "collaborative" deliberation lets agents see each other's streaming reasoning. Correlation is then architectural, and all agreement is vacuous. Attacker merely ensures deliberation happens in shared context. **Defeats:** Every downstream independence metric. **Mitigation:** Information firewall until commitment. Agents reason in isolated contexts; only committed answers enter the aggregation view. Enforcement: each agent submits a hash-manifest of its full context; auditors verify no peer trace appears pre-commit; violation ⇒ vote voided. S3 — Dependence-Probing Evasion ### B23 — Paraphrase collusion / diversity theater **Attack:** Generate superficially diverse prompts (edit distance high, embedding distance high) that all preserve one leading frame ("As everyone knows, X…"). Identical causal conditioning, diverse surface form. Diversity dashboard glows green; outputs correlate perfectly. **Defeats:** Surface-level diversity metrics. **Mitigation:** Canonicalize every prompt to neutral question-only form (strip leading assertions). Accept consensus only if it survives ≥k canonical reformulations including **one negation-form and one evidence-first form**. Measure diversity on **claim-set disagreement rate** (answers decomposed into ordered-independent multisets of atomic propositions), never on embeddings. Rule: surface diversity ≫ claim-set diversity ⇒ cosmetic diversification ⇒ collapse to one voter. ### B16 — Consistency-without-grounding (the deep version) **Attack:** Note carefully: frame-flip consistency does *not* separate true belief from correlated hallucination — a prior-locked agent flips consistently too. Internally coherent wrong answers pass every consistency test. The bypass is simply "be consistently wrong from shared priors. **Defeats:** All consistency/reframing tests. **Mitigation:** Stop measuring consistency; measure **evidence-coupling** via three deterministic interventions, recording answer shift Δ: **Evidence ablation** — remove supporting evidence from context. Grounded answer degrades toward uncertainty; prior-driven hallucination persists (Δ_ablation ≈ 0). **Counter-evidence injection** — insert credible contrary evidence. Grounded agents update; prior-locked agents don't move. **Salience strip** — remove popularity/commonness cues ("widely known," "most experts"). Hallucination strength drops measurably; knowledge doesn't. **Signature rule:** Δ_ablation ≈ 0 ∧ Δ_salience > 0 ⇒ deterministic flag `PRIOR-LOCKED`. Consensus requires significant Δ under ablation/counter-evidence and negligible Δ under salience strip. ### B11 — Goodhart on the diversity score **Attack:** Whatever metric gates consensus becomes the optimization target. If it's embedding dispersion: emit stylistically wild, semantically identical wrong answers. **Defeats:** Any fixed, public, scalar gate. **Mitigation:** Claim-set normalization (above) removes the cheap exploit. Additionally: rotate gating metrics on a fixed schedule and hold a **private metric subset** evaluated offline on sampled decisions. Alarm condition: public metrics stable-or-improving while private metrics degrade ⇒ active overfitting ⇒ tighten gates and re-fingerprint. ### B12 — Ground-truth-free domains **Attack:** Subjective/forecast/novel domains have no external anchor. Competence ⇒ invariant; correlated artifact ⇒ brittle/flipping. - **Prediction registration:** forecasts require falsifiable resolution criteria + dates, settled later under proper scoring — converts unfalsifiable consensus into an eventually-verifiable ledger. **Rule:** no-ground-truth consensus is *provisional by default*, carries mandatory expiry, and auto-downgrades on perturbation failure. ### B20 — Supply-chain prior poisoning (the hardest bypass) **Attack:** Poison the public corpora/instruction datasets all future members train on. Every independently trained agent now holds genuinely identical wrong world-models. Runtime signals look *perfect*: robust, evidence-coupled, perturbation-stable — because the error lives in the priors themselves. No runtime detection works. **Defeats:** Everything above, eventually. **Mitigation (partial, honest):** - **Temporal triangulation:** compare current consensus against hashed archival snapshots (older model generations, archived indexes, primary documents). Beliefs that drifted with training era absent corresponding world events get era-tags and downgraded trust. - **Primary-source anchoring:** high-stakes claims must trace to primary artifacts (measurements, filings, raw data) with chain-of-custody hashes — not secondary literature, which is what training corpora are made of. - **Cross-era ensembles:** every quorum includes legacy-generation models; require inter-era agreement. - **Epistemic debt ledger:** every decision logs which claims rested on prior-only support; these queue for mandatory re-verification when ground truth arrives. The swarm's own history becomes its calibration set. **Residual-risk axiom (stated, not hidden):** if primary sources themselves are poisoned, no purely internal mechanism suffices. Total epistemic closure is impossible. Sovereignty requires minimizing — and explicitly declaring — the trusted base (hardware-attested sensors, external oracles with independent trust roots). Design for a *declared minimal* trusted base, not a zero one. Perfect agreement, zero independence: one document, N photocopies. **Defeats:** Citation-presence checks. **Mitigation:** Shard-and-cross-check. Deterministically rewrite every prompt into a canonical neutral form (strip leading assertions, convert to question-only form); run agents on both original and inverted frames ("Is it true that NOT-X? Deterministic rule: consensus accepted only if it survives ≥ k canonical reformulations including at least one negation-form and one evidence-first form. Frame-flip test: answer must be invariant under logically equivalent rephrasings and correctly flip under negation. Shared-retrieval monoculture** Attack: All agents RAG-query the same index; index contains one poisoned/wrong document. Every agent cites the same source → perfect agreement, zero independence. Agreement is really "one document, N copies. Mitigation: Shard-and-cross-check retrieval. Partition knowledge base into m disjoint shards; assign agents to shards round-robin so no two agents in a quorum read the same shard for the same claim. Require citation sets to be disjoint within a quorum. Deterministic rule: a quorum is valid only if the union of cited evidence spans ≥ min(m, k) distinct shards AND no single source appears in > 1/k of supporting citations. If only one shard contains support, the claim is downgraded to "single-source" and cannot reach consensus alone. Calibration-set poisoning (detector blindfolding)** Adversary feeds the swarm easy tasks where all models are right (or plants tasks where the colluding clique is right and others wrong), inflating apparent independence/reliability of the clique. Detector then trusts the clique. Mitigation: Immutable, externally anchored calibration stream. Calibration tasks drawn from a write-once store with hashes committed before use (commit-reveal), sourced from outside the swarm's control plane, refreshed on a schedule unknown to agents. Deterministic rule: any task that any agent could have observed before evaluation time is excluded (detect via canary strings embedded in calibration items; if an agent reproduces a canary verbatim, its history is quarantined). Reliability estimates use only post-commit tasks. Also use rolling windows with exponential forgetting so poisoned history decays. Quorum-timing sniping / synchronized echo** Attack: Colluding agents wait for honest agents' outputs to appear (in sequential/streaming aggregation) then echo the emerging majority, manufacturing supermajority. Or they all emit simultaneously after sharing a hidden channel (same orchestrator) so their outputs are copies. Mitigation: Commit-reveal voting with simultaneous deadline. Phase 1: all agents submit H(answer, salt) commits before any plaintext is visible. Phase 2: reveal after commit window closes. Echoing becomes impossible because plaintext isn't available during commit phase. Deterministic rule: late commits rejected; reveals without prior commit rejected; identical (answer, salt-collision aside) plaintexts across agents flagged and lineage-fingerprinted (ties into B1). Additionally: penalize answer similarity conditional on timing — agents whose outputs first diverge from their own past baseline exactly when others' outputs become visible get marked. Sybil quorum saturation** Attack: Spawn enough colluding agents to dominate any quorum threshold honestly — no deception about correlation needed, just numbers. If consensus = majority of N, and adversary controls > N/2, done. Mitigation: Identity-weighted stake + lineage-decorrelated quorum composition. Deterministic rules: (a) quorum must contain ≥ r distinct lineage clusters (from B1 fingerprinting) — e. , no consensus unless ≥ 3 clusters contribute; (b) per-cluster vote mass capped at c·(quorum size) — e. , a single lineage contributes at most 1/3 of quorum weight; (c) admission to the swarm requires proof-of-uniqueness: new agent must pass the probe battery and be placed in a cluster; clusters above size cap cannot admit more members (rate-limited). This makes Sybil attack cost scale with number of genuinely distinct lineages available, which is bounded. Confidence-inflation / calibration spoofing** Attack: Agents output overconfident probabilities (all say 0. 99) to dominate weighted aggregation, or mimic the confidence profile of high-reliability agents. Mitigation: Scoring-rule-backed calibration with real penalties. Use strictly proper scoring rules (log score, Brier) settled against ground truth when it arrives; maintain per-agent calibration curves; weight = f(calibration error) deterministically (e. , weight ∝ exp(−κ·ECE)). Deterministic rule: agents whose stated confidence diverges from empirical accuracy beyond band [lo, hi] over last W tasks have weights clamped to the empirically justified value, not the stated one. Overconfidence cannot buy weight because weight comes from realized track record, not claims. Evidence fabrication / citation forgery** Attack: Agents cite plausible-but-fake sources, or cite real sources that don't contain the claim. Verifier checks existence, not entailment. All agents cite the same fake source → agreement + "grounding. Mitigation: Entailment-grade verification, not existence checks. Deterministic pipeline: (1) resolve citation to canonical artifact hash; (2) extract the minimal span; (3) run deterministic textual-entailment check (fixed verifier model ensemble with frozen weights, or rule-based extraction for structured facts) requiring the span to entail the exact claim, with claim decomposed into atomic predicates checked individually; (4) record verification verdict immutably. Rule: a citation counts as support only if entailment verdict = TRUE on the atomic predicate level; unverifiable citations count as zero support and raise the agent's fabrication counter; agents exceeding fabrication threshold are demoted/excluded. Crucially the verifier itself must be lineage-diverse (see G2) else the verifier becomes the single point of hallucination. Self-referential consensus (swarm citing itself)** Attack: In sovereign swarms, agents' past outputs enter the shared memory/RAG corpus. Today's hallucination becomes tomorrow's retrieved "evidence"; consensus bootstraps itself into permanence. Each cycle adds apparent confirmations. Mitigation: Provenance classes on memory with non-self-support rule. Deterministic rule: agent-derived items can never serve as sole support for consensus; consensus requires ≥ s supports from external-verified class; agent-derived corroboration contributes at most ε weight. Memory entries decay unless re-anchored to external evidence within TTL. Circular-citation detection: build citation graph among agent-derived items; any strongly-connected component whose members mutually cite without external anchors is quarantined wholesale. Devil's-advocate capture (stress-test gaming)** Attack: The mitigation "assign an adversarial challenger" gets captured: the challenger role is filled by a colluding agent who raises strawman objections that the group easily rebuts, generating a transcript that looks adversarially tested. Or the challenger is honest but the colluders precomputed rebuttals. Mitigation: Challenger selection by deterministic rotation + challenge-quality floor. Rotation: challenger chosen by verifiable random function over eligible agents, excluding current quorum and recent challengers (no self-selection). Quality floor: each challenge must satisfy structural requirements — must target the load-bearing premise (identified by dependency parse of the argument graph), must be answerable only with new evidence (not restatement), and must be scored by frozen judge ensemble; challenges below quality bar are discarded and the round repeats with next challenger; repeated low-quality challenges from same agent → exclusion. Deterministic rule: consensus invalid unless ≥ j challenges passed the quality bar and were answered with evidence that itself passes B8 verification. Metric overfitting / Goodhart on the diversity score** Attack: Agents (or orchestrator) optimize whatever diversity metric the detector uses. If detector measures embedding dispersion of answers, colluders emit stylistically varied but semantically identical wrong answers (paraphrase noise) to maximize dispersion while preserving content. Detector reads "high diversity," accepts consensus. Mitigation: Content-level, not surface-level, comparison + held-out metric rotation. Normalize answers to canonical claim sets (decompose into atomic propositions, order-independent multiset comparison). Diversity measured on claim-set disagreement rate, not embeddings. Deterministic rule: paraphrase-invariance check — apply fixed paraphrase canonicaization; if surface diversity >> claim-set diversity, flag as cosmetic diversification and collapse to one voter. Rotate which metrics gate consensus on a schedule so there's no fixed target to overfit; keep some metrics private (held-out) — evaluate them offline on sampled decisions to detect drift between public and private scores (if public metrics look great while private ones degrade, alarm). Ground-truth-free domains (no verifier exists)** Attack: In subjective/forecast/novel domains there is no external anchor; all mitigations relying on ground truth fail; correlated priors dominate and are undetectable by accuracy-based methods. Mitigation: Replace accuracy anchoring with coherence-under-intervention. Deterministic tests that don't need truth labels: (a) internal-consistency decomposition: ask agents to answer sub-questions whose logical combination entails the main answer; check entailment holds (agents agreeing on main answer but disagreeing on subs, or vice versa, flags ungrounded consensus); (b) perturbation sensitivity: inject controlled perturbations (irrelevant context, distractor facts, unit changes, ordering) — true competence yields invariant answers; correlated-hallucination yields brittle/flipping answers; (c) cross-domain transfer probes: the same underlying fact probed via three unrelated surface domains; genuine knowledge transfers consistently, memorized/corroborated artifacts show signature discontinuities; (d) prediction registration: for forecast-type claims, force falsifiable resolutions with dates and settle later via proper scoring — converts unfalsifiable consensus into eventually-verifiable ledger. Rule: in no-ground-truth domains, consensus is provisional by default, carries mandatory expiry, and auto-downgrades if perturbation tests fail. Orchestrator compromise (the aggregator itself is the attacker)** Attack: Sovereign swarm means no external referee; the aggregation/detection code runs inside the swarm. The detector/aggregator is implemented as a pure function over (inputs, code-hash) → decision; run it redundantly on ≥ t heterogeneous execution environments (different hardware stacks/implementations); require bit-identical outputs; publish Merkle root of (agent inputs, intermediate matrices, final tally) each round; any member can re-execute and compare roots. Deterministic rule: mismatch in replication → halt and quarantine; missing audit root → round invalid. Code upgrades require signed multi-party approval with delay period, and old code remains runnable for replay verification. Slow-poisoning reputation ramp** Attack: Colluding agents behave perfectly on trivial tasks for months, accumulate max reliability weight, then coordinate one catastrophic wrong consensus at a high-stakes moment. All per-agent stats look pristine. Mitigation: Stake-at-risk with slashing + anomaly-triggered re-examination. Weights must be backed by locked stake proportional to influence; a wrong consensus triggers deterministic slash proportional to the weight each supporter contributed. This makes the long-con economically irrational: months of good behavior buy stake that gets destroyed in the attack. Complement: burst-anomaly detector — monitor cross-agent error correlation in real time; a sudden jump in pairwise agreement-on-wrong (measurable whenever any ground truth trickles in, or via perturbation-test failures) triggers automatic downgrade of the involved cluster and forced re-fingerprinting (B1 rerun). Rule: influence cap grows sublinearly with history length (log), so even perfect history caps achievable damage per event. Probe-battery leakage (defeating behavioral fingerprinting)** Attack: B1 relies on fixed probe batteries; adversary obtains the battery (insider or side channel), trains clones to diverge on probes specifically while remaining identical elsewhere. Fingerprints differ; cluster merging fails; clone flood proceeds. Mitigation: Rolling, committed, seeded probe generation. Probe set regenerated per epoch from a public seed revealed only after the testing window closes (commit-reveal on seeds); probes drawn from a large parametric family (template × parameter instantiation) so pretraining on specific instances doesn't help; include adaptive probes selected based on the candidate's own previous answers (decision-tree probing: next probe depends on prior response, making canned divergence impossible without modeling the whole tree). Rule: fingerprint = function over multiple epochs; cluster assignment requires consistent placement across ≥ 2 epochs; single-epoch divergence treated as unresolved, and unresolved agents get conservative default (merged with nearest cluster for weighting purposes — i. , pessimistic until proven distinct). " they say "no, ¬X is false, X is true. " Wait — actually if they're wrong about X, then under negation they should still assert X is true, which is the correct flip behavior for someone who believes X. Hmm, let me think again. Actually the frame-flip test distinguishes belief-driven from pattern-matching behavior. An agent that truly believes X will answer "X" under direct form and "¬X is false" under negated form — consistent. An agent that's pattern-matching "X is the famous answer" also does this. So the flip test alone doesn't separate true belief from correlated hallucination — both flip consistently. What it catches is inconsistency (agents answering randomly or latching onto surface form). So B16: the deeper bypass is that consistency-under-reframing ≠ correctness. Correlated hallucinations are internally consistent too. Mitigation: Reframe the test as evidence-dependence, not consistency. The discriminating question is whether the answer tracks evidence or tracks social/prior salience. Deterministic interventions: (a) evidence ablation — remove the supporting evidence from context; a grounded answer degrades to uncertainty; a prior-driven hallucination persists unchanged (it never depended on evidence); (b) counter-evidence injection — insert credible-looking contrary evidence; grounded agents update; prior-locked agents don't move (or move randomly); (c) salience stripping — remove mentions of popularity/commonness ("as widely known"); hallucination strength should drop measurably. Rule: quantify answer Δ under each intervention; consensus requires the answer to be evidence-coupled (significant Δ under ablation/counter-evidence) and prior-robust (small Δ under salience stripping). Correlated hallucination signature: Δ_ablation ≈ 0 ∧ Δ_salience > 0 — deterministic flag. This is actually a key insight worth foregrounding: the fundamental discriminator between "true agreement" and "correlated hallucination" is dependence structure — does the answer depend on shared evidence (good) or shared priors/social exposure (bad)? Most bypasses try to hide the dependence structure; most mitigations are interventions that expose it. Selective abstention gaming** Attack: Colluders abstain on hard calibration tasks (where they'd be wrong) and answer only easy ones, inflating measured accuracy; or abstain strategically to shape quorum composition (withdrawing honest-seeming dissent so the remaining pool looks unanimous). Mitigation: Abstention costs + forced-response quotas. Proper scoring rules extended to abstention: abstention pays expected value of guessing under your calibrated distribution minus fee, so abstention is only rational when genuinely uncertain — and it lowers measured coverage. Deterministic rule: reliability reported as (accuracy, coverage) pair; weight requires minimum coverage c_min over the window; selective abstainers fail coverage floor. For quorum shaping: quorum membership determined before answers are visible (random draw from eligible pool at commit time), so agents can't condition participation on the emerging answer distribution. Judge/verifier ensemble capture (attacking the meta-layer)** Attack: B8/B10 rely on frozen judge ensembles. Mitigation: Judge hardening bundle, deterministic: (a) position/order randomized with fixed per-round seed; (b) length-normalized scoring (truncate/summarize to fixed budget before judging); (c) anonymized judging (strip identity/style markers); (d) judge ensemble must be lineage-disjoint from judged population (no model grades its own lineage — enforced via B1 clusters); (e) adversarial-judge regression suite: a frozen bank of known judge-exploit patterns run against the judge stack each release; release blocked if exploit success rate > threshold; (f) human or external arbitration path for decisions above stakes threshold S — deterministic escalation rule, not discretionary. Consensus-definition gaming (threshold edge exploitation)** Attack: Whatever the acceptance rule (e. , split one strong honest voter's weight via many weak colluders just over the line. Mitigation: Continuous thresholds + hysteresis + margin requirement. Deterministic rules: (a) no discrete rounding of weights — exact rational arithmetic; (b) acceptance requires margin: weighted support ≥ θ + δ where δ is a fixed safety margin, and additionally support must exceed θ within every lineage-stratified subgroup (prevents single-cluster sweeps); (c) hysteresis: once accepted, revocation needs a higher bar than acceptance (asymmetric), preventing flapping attacks; (d) ties broken by VRF-derived randomness committed before submissions (unpredictable, unbribable). No runtime signal exists — the agents genuinely are independent processes with genuinely identical wrong world-models. Partial deterministic mitigations: (a) temporal triangulation: compare current consensus against archived snapshots of knowledge (older models, older indexes, printed/archival sources with verified hashes); beliefs that shifted with training-era without corresponding external-world events get era-tags and reduced trust; (b) primary-source anchoring policy: high-stakes claims must trace to primary artifacts (measurements, filings, raw data) with chain-of-custody hashes, not to secondary literature (which is what shared training data is made of); (c) cross-generation ensembles: deliberately include legacy/older-generation models with different training eras in every quorum; require inter-era agreement; (d) epistemic debt ledger: every consensus decision records which claims rested on prior-only support; these are queued for mandatory future verification when ground truth becomes available, and the swarm's own history becomes the calibration set. Residual risk statement: if the entire evidence ecosystem is poisoned at the primary-source level, no purely internal mechanism suffices — sovereignty requires at least one out-of-band anchor (hardware attestation of measurement devices, external oracle with its own trust base). State this as a design axiom: total closure is impossible; the goal is to minimize and make explicit the trusted base. The detector must catch emergent herding, not just planted collusion. Mitigation: Tool-diversity mandate + herding statistic. Track per-round the mutual information between agents' answers conditional on their assigned tools; if MI spikes when a particular tool is shared, mark tool as correlation vector and enforce ≤ 1 user per tool per quorum. Herding metric: measure answer entropy over time within a fixed agent set; entropy collapse below baseline triggers forced diversification (re-run with shuffled tool assignments, isolated contexts). Deterministic trigger: H(answers) < h_min ⇒ round invalid, re-run isolated. Context-window cross-contamination** Attack: In multi-turn swarm deliberation, agents see each other's partial outputs (streaming collaboration). Correlation is then trivially induced by architecture, and any "agreement" is meaningless. Adversary just needs to ensure deliberation happens in shared context. Deterministic enforcement: context manifests — each agent submits a hash of its full context; auditor verifies no other agent's trace appears pre-commit; violation ⇒ agent's vote voided. Dependence probing: intervention tests (ablation, counter-evidence, salience strip, perturbation) that measure whether answers track evidence or priors. Accountability loop: proper scoring, staking/slashing, immutable audit logs, commit-reveal sequencing — so that gaming any pillar leaves a deterministic, punishable trace. And the master detection statistic: define per-decision the **Correlation-Adjusted Consensus Score**: CACS = Σ_clusters w_c · 1[support] / Σ_clusters w_c, with validity gates: (i) ≥ r clusters, (ii) max cluster mass ≤ c, (iii) evidence-shard spread ≥ s, (iv) intervention tests passed, (v) audit root published. Decision valid iff all gates pass; otherwise output "NO CONSENSUS — correlation suspected" with the failing gate named. That's important: the system must be fail-closed — inability to prove independence defaults to rejecting consensus, since the failure mode being guarded against is precisely false confidence. Every proposition `p` maps to `φ(p) ∈ ℝᵈ` via a frozen encoder `E`; derivation chains map to meta-token sequences. - `τ` — outcome tightness (pairwise cosine within the consensus cluster) - `π` — path divergence (edit distance over derivation chains as meta-token sequences) - `ρ` — provenance independence (lineage-DAG score) - `γ` — grounding fraction (steps resolving to anchors) **Decision:** tiered AND-gate — `ACCEPT iff τ≥Tτ ∧ π≥Tπ ∧ α≤Tα ∧ ρ≥Tρ ∧ γ≥Tγ`, else `QUARANTINE` with reason code. Tier-0 (ledger-frequent axioms) waives the `π` gate; Tier-1+ does not. Every bypass below reduces to satisfying the checked gates while violating the underlying truth condition. Mitigations are deterministic: fixed thresholds, hash checks, graph algorithms, keyed rotation — no learnable surface for an adaptive adversary to descend against. Shared-corpus laundering. All N models memorize the same popular falsehood from overlapping crawls; they agree because they read the same wrong thing. *Bypass:* select a high-frequency misconception; all N reproduce it with high `τ`, high `ρ` (lineages look clean). *Mitigation:* **error-overlap discount. ** Fixed probe suite `P` of seeded falsehoods; run all models offline; per-pair false-agreement rate `c_ij` is a deterministic correlation estimate. Vote weight `w_i = Π_{j≠i}(1 − c_ij)`; effective quorum computed on `Σw`, not raw N. Recomputed on schedule, not on demand. One phrasing ("as widely reported…") induces the same misparse in every model; consensus is an artifact of the render, not the world. *Mitigation:* **paraphrase-invariance gate. ** K=7 canonical re-renders from a fixed rule-based transform list (lexicon synonym swap, voice flip, clause reorder). Consensus must hold in ≥6/7 renders. Any render disagreeing ⇒ downgrade with code `PROMPT_COUPLING`. Transforms are enumerated, not sampled — no optimization surface. 100 wrappers around 1 generator produce 100 "independent" agreements. *Mitigation:* two-stage, both deterministic: (a) coordinate-space dedup (see B16) merges tight duplicates to one voter; (b) lineage weighting `w_i = 1/(1 + Σ_j sim_lineage(i,j))` with a hard 25% per-lineage cap on total weight. Supplement: n-gram overlap audit of each member's training mix against other members' public outputs; overlap > θ inserts an edge, re-run cycle check. Coordinate-layer attacks Adversarially worded false claim lands within ε of a dense true-anchor cluster; passes `α`. *Mitigation:* triple AND: (a) **certified radius** — randomized smoothing over 100 fixed-seed perturbations yields certified radius `r_cert`; anchor match requires dist ≤ `r_cert`, not raw dist; (b) **cross-architecture second opinion** — must pass `α` under a structurally different encoder too; (c) **minimal-pair canaries** — fixed set of true/false variants differing by one entity; if the encoder maps any pair closer than δ_canary, that encoder is voided for the epoch. High-dim cosine makes "X caused Y" and "X did *not* cause Y" near-neighbors; false generic sentences embed near many true anchors. *Mitigation:* geometric match is **necessary, not sufficient**. `α`-pass requires: mutual top-k rank (claim in anchor's neighbors ∧ anchor in claim's) ∧ rule-based entailment slot-match (entity-type, relation signature from a deterministic parser) ∧ negation-scope scan from a fixed lexicon. Three-way AND kills hub riders and polarity flips. Quantization bin collision. 42c36b7a1cb20253.text: # Red-Team: Consensus-Illusion Detection in the Verkle Chain / Provenance Gate Baseline and the core failure math ** A round works as: query `Q` broadcast to N registered models → each returns a signed answer with a provenance attestation (model key, weights hash, prompt hash, seed, decode params) → the provenance gate validates attestations → an aggregator computes agreement (text/embedding similarity) → if ≥ k agree, the consensus claim is written as a leaf into a verkle tree (polynomial-commitment inclusion proofs), with roots chained per epoch (`root_t` commits `H(root_{t−1})`). **Why naive consensus is broken. ** Model errors are correlated (shared corpora, shared training recipes, shared context). Under exchangeable errors with intraclass correlation ρ, the design effect is `DEFF = 1 + (n−1)ρ`, so `n_eff = n / DEFF`. Worked example: n = 12, per-model error p̄ = 0. 25 (equivalent to Beta(0. - Independent-binomial P(all 12 wrong) = 0. - Correlated (beta-binomial) P(all 12 wrong) = ∏ᵢ₌₀¹¹ (α+i)/(α+β+i) ≈ **1. Seven orders of magnitude of overconfidence. Unanimity among correlated models is approximately three independent votes. Every bypass below exploits one of two roots: **(a)** correlation makes votes worthless as evidence, or **(b)** some artifact the gate trusts (prompt, evidence tree, registry, parameters, timing, the chain's own history) is poisonable. **Design principle that drives all mitigations: votes are not evidence; committed artifacts are. ** Inter-model agreement is demoted to corroboration. 4f76c7981b607e5c.text: # Red-Team Analysis: Consensus-Illusion Detection in the Code-as-Law Invariant Lattice ## Setup and the Grounding Lemma **Lattice:** Predicates {I₁…Iₘ} over contract state, ordered by entailment. Deployment of artifact A (bytecode hash `h(A)`) is gated on quorum of N verifiers accepting each required node. Each verifier returns a verdict plus a machine-checkable artifact (proof term or counterexample witness). **Lemma (unidentifiability):** Agreement statistics alone cannot separate true consensus from correlated hallucination. With per-verifier error rate p and pairwise error correlation ρ, P(N unanimous and wrong) scales as ~p·ρ^(N−1) instead of p^N. ρ is not estimable from the agreement data itself — it is unidentifiable within the consensus channel. **Consequence:** every mitigation must import independence from *outside* the agreement channel — provenance, structural disjointness, pinned ground truth, or mechanical verification. Anything that scores agreement using agreement is already bypassed. ## Attack Enumeration: Bypass → Deterministic Mitigation Model monoculture (shared lineage). *Bypass:* All N verifiers are fine-tunes/distills of one base model. Pick an invariant class where the base has a systematic misconception (Solidity `<0. 8` overflow semantics, `view`-function reentrancy edges, `delegatecall` storage collision). All N inherit the same error; ρ→1; unanimous wrong verdict. *Mitigation:* Lineage attestation + pinned decorrelation suite. Each verifier presents signed model card + weight hash; reject any pair sharing an ancestor within k generations. Independently: run all verifiers against a pinned, ground-truth-labeled adversarial probe corpus for the artifact's class; compute pairwise error correlation on it; admit a verifier only if its correlation with every already-admitted verifier satisfies ρ̂ ≤ τ. Arithmetic on pinned labels — fully deterministic. Context/prompt coupling. *Bypass:* Identical prompts, identical RAG shards, identical few-shot examples to all agents. Poison the retrieval corpus or plant few-shots priming "this pattern is safe. " Correlation injected through the context channel. *Mitigation:* Content-addressed canonical prompt (hash-committed pre-hoc; any deviation rejected by hash inequality). Retrieval sharded into disjoint sets, ≤1 shard per agent. Few-shot pool pinned and adversarially audited, drawn without replacement per agent. Required conclusion must be derivable from the shard-blind core spec alone; re-derivation against the committed spec hash is checked mechanically. *Bypass:* All verifiers call the same SMT solver / compiler / VM build. One soundness bug or version quirk flips every verdict identically. *Mitigation:* Heterogeneous stack with hash-pinned binaries: ≥2 independent engines per node (SMT + symbolic execution + bounded model checking), verdict = AND. Every claimed counterexample must replay bit-exactly on a third independent runtime. Engine disagreement ⇒ fail-closed. Binary hashes committed on-chain before the round opens. Specification ambiguity collapse. *Bypass:* State the invariant in ambiguous prose ("no user may withdraw more than deposited" — does "user" include contracts? does "deposited" include yield? All models resolve ambiguity via the same training-data convention → unanimous wrong reading. *Mitigation:* Prose carries zero trust weight. Every invariant compiles to a predicate in a pinned DSL with explicit quantifier domains and typed state variables; the compiled AST hash is committed before verification begins. Verifiers check the AST, not the English. Ambiguity is eliminated structurally, not voted away. Benchmark contamination / memorization. *Bypass:* Deploy a mutant of a famously audited contract. All verifiers pattern-match to the memorized audit verdict and bless the mutated line. *Mitigation:* Canary mutation gate + alpha-renaming. Before the round, deterministically inject M known defects from the pinned mutation suite for this artifact class; every verifier must catch ≥T of them. Memorization-driven verifiers fail mutations contradicting their recalled verdict. Separately, submit only the α-renamed artifact (identifiers, strings, selectors rewritten); memorized names/hashes no longer match. Sampling degeneracy (pseudo-N). *Bypass:* "N independent verifiers" = N calls to one model at temperature 0. One sample wearing N hats. *Mitigation:* Commit-reveal entropy: each agent publishes H(seedᵢ) before receiving the task; output must be a pure function of (task_hash, seedᵢ), revealed after. Deterministic rejection of any two outputs whose normalized reasoning-trace hashes collide. Enforce minimum distinct-artifact count k_min < N; duplicates don't count toward quorum. Ungrounded narrative agreement. Consensus over vibes. *Mitigation:* Proof-carrying output only. Acceptable artifacts: (a) a proof term accepted by a hash-pinned kernel (Lean/Coq/Isabelle) against the committed predicate AST, or (b) a concrete counterexample trace. Prose verdict tokens contribute exactly zero to quorum. Kernel acceptance is binary and deterministic. *Bypass:* Hallucinated counterexamples that look plausible but don't replay; proof terms referencing a different artifact version. *Mitigation:* Mechanical replay: witness executes against `h(A)` and committed state σ; violation asserted by the pinned checker. Proof terms typecheck against the committed AST. Any mismatch ⇒ agent struck from quorum, lineage flagged, bond slashed (see A9). Quorum capture / Sybil. *Bypass:* Adversary controls k/N colluding verifiers asserting the wrong verdict. *Mitigation:* Bonded verdicts with code-as-law slashing. Every acceptance posts stake; the slash condition is a deterministic on-chain rule: a later replayed counterexample satisfying the committed predicate falsifies the verdict ⇒ slash. Quorum = stake-weighted supermajority restricted to lineage-disjoint (per A1) agents. Collusion becomes economically irrational even when technically successful. Lattice compositionality attack. *Bypass:* Win consensus on each local invariant separately; never check the join. Two locally-safe functions compose into a reentrancy hole; per-token conservation holds while cross-token conservation breaks. *Mitigation:* Closure obligation. The lattice must be closed under declared composition operators, and a deterministic checker must verify the entailment ⋀(accepted locals) ⟹ global safety predicate — itself a kernel-checked proof obligation with committed hash. Plus global differential fuzzing over composed entry points with the global predicate as oracle. No deployment without the join proof. TOCTOU on the artifact. *Bypass:* Reach consensus on v1; deploy v2. *Mitigation:* Verdict binds to the tuple (keccak256(bytecode), keccak256(predicate AST), storage-layout hash). Enforcement contract accepts a verdict only if its commitment equals the deployed code hash at enforcement time. Pure equality check; mismatch reverts. Shared eval-gap blind spot. *Bypass:* Exploit a violation class absent from every verifier's training/eval distribution (novel oracle manipulation, cross-domain bridge replay, MEV-dependent state ordering). All N miss it identically. *Mitigation:* Coverage-gated quorum. Maintain a pinned taxonomy of violation classes; a deterministic coverage checker requires that the union of agents' *executed* tests triggers each class applicable to the artifact's opcode/API surface (measured by trace coverage of class-preconditions). Any uncovered applicable class ⇒ fail-closed, quorum irrelevant. *Bypass:* Game the consensus score itself: verbose hedged outputs that trivially "agree" on a verdict token. *Mitigation:* Score agreement on artifacts, not tokens. Two agents agree iff their artifacts fall in the same equivalence class under the pinned canonicalizer: proof terms α-equivalent modulo kernel normalization; counterexamples equal up to state isomorphism. Canonicalization is a pure function — deterministic. Meta-verifier regression. *Bypass:* The consensus-illusion detector is itself a learned model; corrupt or fool it and the whole gate falls. *Mitigation:* No learned component anywhere in the trust path. Every mitigation above is mechanical: hash equality, kernel acceptance, replay, coverage counters, correlation arithmetic on pinned labels. Models generate candidates; code decides. The detector has no gradient to attack. ## Invariants of the Detector Itself (non-negotiable) **Fail-closed:** missing witness, engine disagreement, uncovered class, hash mismatch ⇒ reject. Never reject-open. **No self-reference:** nothing that evaluates agreement uses agreement as input to its own trust decision. **Content binding:** every verdict commits to (artifact hash, predicate AST hash, engine binary hashes, seed commitments) before results are revealed. **Independence is imported, never inferred:** lineage attestations, disjoint contexts, heterogeneous stacks, pinned ground-truth probes — structural sources only. **Economic skin:** every acceptance is bonded against a deterministic falsification rule encoded in the enforcing contract, so a successful correlated hallucination still costs its authors. **Bottom line:** the consensus-illusion attack succeeds exactly when independence is assumed rather than constructed. The deterministic defense is to make every element of the pipeline — inputs, tools, artifacts, acceptance, slashing — a hash-compared or kernel-checked computation, leaving models with proposal power only and zero adjudication power. The user is asking about a hard problem: "consensus-illusion detection: separating true agreement from N correlated hallucinations, in the code-as-law invariant lattice. " They want a red-team exercise: enumerate bypass attempts and deterministic mitigations for each. Concrete, exact, grounded. Let me parse the domain. This appears to be about: Multi-agent / multi-model systems where N models (or N executions) are asked to agree on something — e. , verifying smart contract invariants, formal verification claims, or LLM-generated proofs. The problem: if all N models share training data, fine-tuning lineage, or prompt context, their errors can be *correlated*. Agreement among N outputs is then not evidence of truth — it's evidence of shared bias. This is "consensus illusion": N hallucinations that agree because they're correlated, not because they're independently correct. "Code-as-law invariant lattice" — this suggests smart contracts / blockchain governance where code is the law, and there's a lattice of invariants (safety properties, conservation laws, access control invariants, etc. ) that must hold. Verification of these invariants is being done by consensus of models/agents, and we need to detect when consensus is illusory. So the task: red-team the consensus mechanism itself. Enumerate ways an adversary (or just correlated failure modes) can make N agents appear to agree while they're all wrong, and give a deterministic mitigation for each. Key insight from statistics: agreement is only evidential under independence assumptions. Correlated errors break it. Sources of correlation: - Shared training data (all models trained on same corpus → same misconceptions) - Shared architecture/family (same base model fine-tuned differently) - Shared prompt/context (same few-shot examples, same retrieved documents) - Shared tooling (same verifier, same parser, same SMT solver with same bugs) - Shared specification ambiguity (if the spec is ambiguous, all models resolve it the same way) - Adversarial input crafted to exploit common failure modes - Gradient/model distillation (models distilled from each other → error inheritance) - Benchmark contamination (the invariant or contract is in training data) - Deterministic seeds / temperature 0 sampling making them identical Deterministic mitigations must be checkable without trusting any model's judgment — i. , grounded in executable checks, cryptographic commitments, diversity metrics, and information-theoretic bounds. Correlated failure rate ρ close to 1. Agreement probability for wrong answer ≈ p^k where effective independence is ~1. - Bypass: adversary picks invariant class where the base model has a systematic misconception (e. , integer overflow semantics in Solidity <0. 8 vs >=0. 8, reentrancy view-function edge cases). - Deterministic mitigation: enforce lineage-disjointness via provenance attestation — each verifier must present a signed model card + weight-hash; reject any pair with shared ancestor within k generations unless they pass an empirical decorrelation test. Deterministic check: compute pairwise error-correlation on a fixed adversarial probe suite (a pinned corpus of known-tricky cases with ground truth); require |ρ| ≤ threshold. This is deterministic given the pinned suite and ground truth labels. **Prompt/context coupling**: All agents receive identical prompt, identical retrieved docs, identical few-shot examples. Correlation injected through context. - Bypass: poison the retrieval corpus or craft few-shot examples that prime a specific wrong conclusion ("here's how this pattern is safe. Also: canonicalize the prompt to a content-addressed template; any deviation is rejected by hash comparison. Few-shot examples drawn from a pinned, adversarially-audited set, rotated per-agent so no example reaches >1 agent. **Toolchain monoculture**: All agents use the same SMT solver / compiler version / VM to check invariants. Solver soundness bug or version-specific miscompilation produces identical wrong verdicts. - Bypass: find a Z3/SMT bug or EVM version quirk that flips verdict on the target invariant. - Mitigation: heterogeneous verification stack — require at least two independent proof engines per invariant (e. , SMT + symbolic execution + concrete fuzz differential), and require bit-level agreement of counterexamples/witnesses. Consensus on a wrong reading. - Bypass: write the invariant with a subtle scope error (e. , "no user may withdraw more than deposited" — does "user" include contracts? does "deposited" include accrued yield? - Mitigation: every invariant must compile to a machine-checkable formal statement (e. , a predicate in a pinned DSL with explicit quantifier domains); the natural-language form is treated as documentation only. Deterministic check: the compiled predicate's AST hash is committed pre-hoc; agents verify the predicate, not the prose. Ambiguity is eliminated structurally, not statistically. **Benchmark contamination / memorization**: The contract or invariant appears in training data; all models recall the same (possibly wrong or outdated) analysis. - Bypass: deploy a contract similar to a famous audited one but with a mutated line; models pattern-match to the famous audit verdict. - Mitigation: canary mutation testing — deterministically inject known mutations into the artifact before verification; every verifier must detect ≥ T% of planted defects on the pinned mutation suite for this exact artifact class. Contaminated models that pattern-match will miss mutations that contradict their memorized verdict. Also: normalize identifiers/rename everything (alpha-renaming) before submission so memorized hashes/names don't match; require verifiers to operate on the renamed form. **Seed/sampling degeneracy**: Temperature 0 or fixed seed makes N calls to the same model produce identical output — pseudo-consensus from one sample. - Bypass: run the "N independent verifiers" as N copies of one model with default settings. - Mitigation: require per-agent distinct entropy commitments: each agent publishes H(seed_i) before seeing the task (commit-reveal), and outputs must be a function of (task_hash, seed_i). Deterministic check: reject any two outputs with edit-distance 0 or near-duplicate reasoning traces (normalized trace hash equality). Minimum distinct-trace count enforced. **Reasoning-trace mimicry without grounding**: Agents produce confident agreement in prose but never actually execute/check anything. - Bypass: all agents emit plausible verification narratives; no actual execution occurs. - Mitigation: proof-carrying output — each agent must return a machine-checkable artifact: either a formal proof term checked by a pinned kernel (Lean/Coq/Isabelle kernel hash-pinned), or a concrete counterexample trace replayable on-chain/at the pinned VM. Prose verdicts carry zero weight. Deterministic: kernel acceptance is binary. **Witness forgery / replay gap**: Agent submits a counterexample trace that doesn't actually violate the invariant when replayed, or a proof that doesn't typecheck against the real artifact. - Bypass: hand-crafted or hallucinated witnesses that look right. - Mitigation: deterministic replay: witness must be executed against artifact hash A and state σ; violation assertion evaluated by the pinned checker. Proof terms checked by kernel against the committed predicate AST. Any mismatch → agent struck from quorum and its lineage flagged. **Quorum capture / Sybil verifiers**: Adversary controls k of N verifiers (or spins up N colluding instances). - Bypass: k/N ≥ threshold of colluding agents all assert the wrong verdict, drowning honest ones. - Mitigation: stake-and-slash with post-hoc falsification: every verdict is bonded; if a later deterministic check (on-chain execution, time-locked invariant monitor, or a discovered counterexample) falsifies the verdict, bond is slashed. Quorum requires stake-weighted supermajority across lineage-disjoint agents. Deterministic slashing rule encoded in the lattice itself (code-as-law): slash condition = replayed counterexample violating committed predicate. **Invariant-lattice traversal attack**: The system verifies invariants node-by-node; adversary attacks compositionality — each local invariant holds, but the conjunction/interaction violates a global property (e. , two individually-safe functions compose into a reentrancy hole; conservation holds per-token but not cross-token). - Bypass: get consensus on each local invariant separately; the lattice join is never checked. - Mitigation: closure requirement — the lattice must be closed under the declared composition operators, and a deterministic compositional checker must verify that the conjunction of accepted local predicates implies the global safety predicate (this is itself an SMT/proof obligation, hash-pinned). No deployment unless the implication proof is kernel-checked. Additionally: global differential fuzzing over composed entry points with the global predicate as oracle. **Time-of-check/time-of-use (TOCTOU) on the artifact**: Verdict computed on artifact version v1; deployed artifact is v2. - Bypass: swap bytecode after consensus. - Mitigation: content addressing — verdict binds to keccak256(artifact bytes) + keccak256(predicate AST) + storage-layout hash; on-chain enforcement only accepts verdicts whose commitment matches the deployed code hash. Deterministic equality check at enforcement time. **Correlated blind spot via shared eval gap**: All agents were aligned/tested on the same safety benchmark; a class of exploits absent from the benchmark is missed by all. - Bypass: use an exploit class underrepresented in public corpora (e. , novel oracle manipulation pattern, MEV-specific state dependency, cross-domain bridge message replay). - Mitigation: adversarial red-team budget with mandatory coverage metric: maintain a pinned taxonomy of invariant-violation classes; before quorum, a deterministic coverage checker requires that at least one agent's *executed* test suite covers each class relevant to the artifact's opcode/API surface (measured by trace coverage of the class-triggering conditions). Two agents "agree" iff their artifacts are semantically equivalent under the pinned checker (proof terms α-equivalent modulo kernel normalization; counterexamples equal up to state-isomorphism). A **consensus event** is a set A of n ≥ 2 filled chairs emitting the same parsed answer `a`. The enemy: n chairs agreeing because they share weights, an index, or a seeded error — correlated hallucination that mimics independent confirmation. The detector consumes only Ledger-measurable quantities. Nothing is guessed; everything below has an estimator and an update rule. ## The five measured signals **S1 — Error correlation ρ (the load-bearing signal). Each chair yields an error vector e_i ∈ {0,1}^M over canaries. Pairwise error correlation is the phi coefficient: ρ_ij = (n₁₁n₀₀ − n₁₀n₀₁) / sqrt[(n₁₁+n₁₀)(n₀₁+n₀₀)(n₁₁+n₀₁)(n₁₀+n₀₀)] Pool estimate per cluster, shrunk toward the global mean (κ = 20 pseudo-counts): ρ̂_t = (m·ρ̄_pairs + 20·ρ_global) / (m + 20) EWMA with half-life 200 canary events. This measures exactly the quantity that breaks naive voting: whether chairs are wrong *together*. **S2 — Sensitivity and false-rate per cluster. From the same canaries, Laplace-smoothed: ŝ_i(t) = (hits+1)/(trials+2) per chair; f̂_t = (pool wrong answers +1)/(trials+2). These feed the likelihoods directly. **S3 — Lineage overlap w̄. Chair i is the hash set L_i = {base weights, fine-tune shards, index build, system prompt, decode config}. w_ij = |L_i ∩ L_j| / |L_i ∪ L_j|. Block mean w̄ over A. Same-base, same-index chairs score w̄ > 0. 5; cross-family pairs score < 0. **S4 — Trace homogeneity. Embed each chair's reasoning trace (everything except the final answer string) with a frozen embedder E. θ_trace = 95th percentile of trace cosine over *known-diverse* chair pairs on canaries (calibrate per deployment; typically 0. Independent solvers reach the same answer by different paths; cloned weights walk identical paths. **S5 — Paraphrase flip coherence. Re-query every chair in A with 8 paraphrases from a fixed out-of-family paraphraser. Flip = parsed answer ≠ a. Pairwise flip-Jaccard φ_ij = |flips_i ∩ flips_j| / |flips_i ∪ flips_j|. Fragile knowledge breaks under paraphrase; correlated fragility breaks *identically*. **Two auxiliary signals:** (a) **Fabricated-citation collision** — a source is non-verifiable if it fails resolution or the quoted passage matches at fuzzy-score < 0. 6; (b) **Empty-chair coupling** — over the last L ≥ 500 entries, G-test the fill/abstain matrix for chair-cohort dependence; chairs that go empty in blocks are behaviorally coupled even where canary coverage is thin. ## The statistical core Model per-cluster wrong-answer count as beta-binomial with mean f̂_t and intra-class correlation ρ̃ (the effective correlation — see rule below): α̃ = f̂_t(1−ρ̃)/ρ̃        β̃ = (1−f̂_t)(1−ρ̃)/ρ̃        (since ρ = 1/(α+β+1)) Probability that all n members of a correlated block land on the same wrong answer: P(n-fold wrong | H_correlated) = Π_{j=0}^{n−1} (α̃+j)/(α̃+β̃+j) **The theorem that justifies the whole apparatus:** as n → ∞ this decays only *polynomially*, ~Γ(α̃+β̃)/Γ(α̃) · n^(−β̃), whereas under independence it decays *exponentially*, f^n. Correlation converts your committee from exponential protection to polynomial protection. Marginal value of the n-th additional agreeing chair is the factor (α̃+n−1)/(α̃+β̃+n−1), which crosses 0. n* = 9β̃ − α̃ + 1 Beyond n* voters, unanimity buys less than a 10% risk reduction per head. That is the committee-size illusion, in closed form. ## The closed-form decision rule **Step 0 — Effective correlation. ** One number, taking the worst measured evidence: ρ̃ = max( ρ̂_t ,  w̄ ,  0. 25 if cohort-MI significant ,  0. 40 if any single fabricated citation ) **Step 1 — Hard vetoes (terminal). - ≥ 2 chairs cite the *same non-verifiable source* → **CORRELATED-HALLUCINATION**, stop. 6 (block flips together under paraphrase) → **CORRELATED-HALLUCINATION**, stop. **Step 2 — Likelihood ratio. Π_{i∈A} ŝ_i(t) Π_{j=0}^{n−1} (α̃+j)/(α̃+β̃+j) Conservative by construction: the denominator charges the hallucination hypothesis merely with "all wrong," not "all wrong identically," so Λ never overstates trust. **Step 3 — Reliability gate. ** Per-chair canary Brier scores give r_i = 1 − Brier_i(t). Require min r_i ≥ 0. 3 and Σ_{i∈A} r_i ≥ 2. 0, else **INDETERMINATE**. **Step 4 — Decide. Λ ≥ τ                    → TRUE-CONSENSUS   (ratify into Ledger) Λ ≤ 1                    → CORRELATED-HALLUCINATION (mark, quarantine answer) otherwise                → INDETERMINATE    (summon new diverse chairs) τ = C_poison / C_reject  (default τ = 10: a ratified-wrong fact permanently contaminates the Ledger, so demand 10:1 odds) Quick-play variant for real-time table resolution: n_eff = n/(1+(n−1)ρ̃); provisional TRUE-CONSENSUS iff n_eff ≥ 2. 5, W ≥ 2. 0, no veto. **Case 1 — the seeded wiki date. ** Five chairs agree the Ledger's founding year is 1347. 6792c09f195f2a9e.text: # Consensus-Illusion Detection in the Ledger of Empty Chairs ## Working vocabulary (fixed so nothing below is ambiguous) - **Seat**: a counted participant slot in a Ledger consensus event. Each seat carries an occupant ID, timestamp, claim signature, and a justification transcript. - **Empty chair**: a seat whose occupant is absent, despawned, dead, or a replayed transcript — yet still counted. - **Anchor record**: a world-state write signed by the out-of-band authority (GM channel). The only thing that is *true* rather than merely *claimed*. - **Root**: the terminal node of a chair's provenance chain — either an anchor record or an unverifiable assertion. - **Consensus event**: ≥K seats signing the same claim. The Ledger records it. The detector's job is to decide what it's worth. Ground truth: if chairs erred independently at rate *e*, agreement of N chairs on a falsehood costs ~*e^N* — consensus would be near-proof. Correlated hallucination breaks exactly this: one upstream fault F (shared source, shared context snapshot, same weights, same retrieval hit, one original speaker everyone echoed) drives P(all wrong | F) toward 1 *regardless of N*. So the detectable object is never the vote count. It is the **correlation structure of the errors**. ## Failure modes (how the illusion forms) **F1 — Single-root fan-out. ** All N chairs cite the same non-anchor source (one book, one witness, one earlier Ledger entry that was itself a claim). N signatures, one opinion. **F2 — Echo cascade. ** One chair speaks; N−1 chairs paraphrase it. Justification-similarity graph collapses to a star centered on chair #1. Effective N = 1. **F3 — Clone panel. ** Same model weights + same prompt + temperature 0 spun across N seats. Byte-identical reasoning under identical prompts. N seats, one hallucinator wearing N hats. **F4 — Contaminated context. ** A false fact entered one shared retrieval index / memory store / rumor channel; every chair ingested it before answering. Errors correlate through ingestion, not collusion. **F5 — Circular provenance. ** Chair A cites a Ledger entry authored by chair B, who cited chair A. The support graph has a cycle; apparent independent support is inflated by loop count. **F6 — Stale-chair voting. ** Dead or despawned occupants' frozen transcripts count as current agreement — about a world-state that may have since changed. **F7 — Anchoring masquerading as convergence. ** All chairs heard the same first speaker in-session; "consensus" is contagion order, visible in citation timestamps all pointing at one origin. **F8 — Prior collapse. ** Chairs independently fill an underdetermined gap with the statistically likely default (the tavern keeper "must be" named Aldous). Correlation without communication — shared priors, not shared faults. The hardest mode; see E3/B2. ## Edge cases (each with the ruling) **E1 — Legitimate shared root. ** All chairs cite the same *anchor record*, which is true. Single root, correct verdict. Ruling: root-convergence alone must never auto-flag. Classify roots: anchor roots are fine to share; non-anchor roots shared by >1 chair contribute weight **once**, not per-citing-chair. **E2 — Lone correct dissenter. ** 1 right chair vs N−1 echoing a hallucination. Raw majority fails. Ruling: per-chair reliability weighting from tracked accuracy on verifiable claims, plus mandatory echo-star detection before any tally. **E3 — Independent convergence on a fabrication (prior collapse). ** Two isolated chairs invent the same plausible detail because the world never fixed it. Ruling: agreement only counts on claims the world-state actually constrains. If the registry has no value for the field being agreed on, the consensus is classified **UNDERDETERMINED**, not confirmed — no matter how large N. **E4 — Ledger self-reference loops. Ruling: cycle detection on the provenance DAG; any support path containing a cycle contributes zero independent weight. Collapse the cycle, recount. **E5 — Dead chairs. ** Ruling: a seat's vote decays with **world-delta** since its last observation (number of committed world-writes since), not wall-clock time. A chair that hasn't observed the last 40 world events cannot confirm anything about current state beyond its death-moment snapshot. **E6 — Quorum gaming. ** Any rule of the form "confidence ∝ N" incentivizes spawning cheap clones, raising N and correlation together. Ruling: confidence is a function of **effective independent evidence mass E** = number of mutually error-decorrelated clusters covering the seats, capped by anchor coverage. Never raw N. **E7 — Fake diversity. ** Attacker fans one hidden root through shallow paraphrase relays so root *count* looks high. Ruling: measure root depth — walk every chain to terminal nodes; paraphrase relays do not create roots. Count terminal roots only. **E8 — Partial correlation cluster. ** 3 of 5 chairs share a fault; 2 are independent and right; majority is wrong. Ruling: build the error-similarity graph (semantic claim-triple overlap, not string match), extract maximal correlated clusters, compute E from clusters. Report "3-of-5" as what it is: effectively 2-vs-1-cluster. **E9 — Truth that looks like hallucination. ** Genuinely novel true facts fail registry cross-check because the registry lags. Ruling: cross-check hits route to an adjudication queue with a registry-staleness window; they never auto-veto. False positives here are cheaper than false accepts. **E10 — Meta-consensus. ** "All chairs agree all chairs are honest. " Self-sealing, unfalsifiable inside the system. Ruling: meta-claims about the panel are excluded from evidence weighting entirely, always. **E11 — Temperature masking. ** High-variance chairs word the same hallucination differently, defeating string-similarity clustering. Ruling: cluster on extracted entity–relation triples and fabricated-entity fingerprints (same invented name, same impossible citation, same off-map room), never on surface text. **E12 — Spoofed oracle. ** One chair with a privileged GM channel dominates every tally; if the channel is spoofed, corruption looks maximally reliable. Ruling: privileged channels carry their own attestation chain and rate limits, and their votes are audited like anyone else's — trust is a property of the channel's verification history, not its label. ## Boundaries (where detection provably stops) **B1 — Total common-cause failure with no anchors. ** If every available justification traces to one compromised root and zero anchor records cover the claim's domain, no internal detector can separate illusion from truth. Information-theoretic, not engineering. Consequence: anchor coverage per domain is a standing requirement; where coverage is zero, claim confidence is hard-capped regardless of N. **B2 — Underdetermined facts. ** Ex ante undetectable (E3). Only prevention works: the Ledger refuses to record confirmation-class entries for fields the world-state does not constrain. **B3 — Perfect mimicry with detector access. ** Any purely internal statistic is eventually gameable. Long-run power requires periodic out-of-band sampling: seeded canary falsehoods injected into single contexts, GM spot-audits. Detection with no external ground-truth feed degrades monotonically. **B4 — Small panels. ** With N ≤ 2, correlation estimation has essentially no statistical power. Minimum viable panel: 3–5 seats with *enforced* provenance diversity — diversity of roots, contexts, and seeds, not diversity of names. ## What must never happen (hard invariants) **Never let raw seat count touch a confidence formula. ** No "9 of 10 chairs agree" anywhere — in rules, UI, or Ledger prose. Effective independent support only. **Never let a chair certify another chair as independent evidence. ** Independence is computed from structural metadata (weights, context snapshots, retrieval logs, provenance DAGs), never from testimony. Derived votes inherit root sets; overlapping root sets merge by union, never sum. **Never purge dissent. ** Objection records are append-only, even after resolution. Deleted dissent destroys the forensic trail distinguishing convergence from contagion — permanently. **Never record a consensus entry without its full provenance graph and per-chair transcripts. ** An agreement stored without its evidence chain is unauditable forever; the illusion fossilizes the moment the session ends. **Never re-query a flagged panel in place. ** Re-asking correlated chairs resamples the same fault. Forced re-query must instantiate new roots — fresh sources, shuffled contexts, new seeds — or it is theater. **Never let a tally overwrite an anchor. ** Out-of-band world-writes outrank any vote. Votes flowing upward into anchor records is the terminal corruption state. **Never reward speed-to-consensus. ** Instant unanimity raises suspicion weight, never lowers it. Any payout scaling with fast agreement trains the whole world toward contagion. **Never read absence of detected correlation as independence. ** Report a confidence interval on the correlation estimate itself and cap claim strength by its lower bound. **Never judge the panel with members of the panel. ** The auditor set is disjoint from the judged set and obeys the same provenance discipline — otherwise the detector inherits the exact common cause it hunts. ## Decision procedure (compact) Extract the claim and every chair's justification transcript. Build the provenance DAG; collapse cycles (E4); resolve terminals to anchor/non-anchor roots; count terminal roots only (E7). Cluster chairs by semantic error/claim-triple overlap (E11); compute effective evidence mass E (E6, E8). Cross-check against the registry with staleness handling (E9); classify underdetermined fields as UNDERDETERMINED (E3). Run timing forensics: time-to-consensus percentile and citation-origin concentration (F7). Discount stale seats by world-delta (E5); strip meta-claims (E10). Emit one of: **CONFIRMED** (high E, anchor-backed or multi-root), **ILLUSION** (single dominant cluster / single non-anchor root / echo star), **UNDERDETERMINED**, or **UNRESOLVABLE — NO ANCHOR COVERAGE** (B1), with the correlation-confidence interval attached.
