bd79f5dcd1be77bf.text: # Consensus-Illusion Detection — Ghost-AOS Git-Bus Treaty The quantity at stake Agreement carries evidential weight only in proportion to error independence. For n attesting agents with mean pairwise error correlation ρ: Var(x̄) = σ² · (1 + (n−1)ρ) / n   ⟹   n* = n / (1 + (n−1)ρ) 9, ten agents give n* ≈ 1. Ten voters, one opinion. Under full correlation, P(unanimous | claim false) ≈ p instead of pⁿ — unanimity becomes nearly uninformative. Every rule below exists to estimate ρ, bound it structurally, or refuse quorum when n* is too small. A treaty that counts heads without measuring correlation is decoration. **FM-1 — Lineage collapse (ancestral consensus). N heads attest the claim; all descend via rebase/cherry-pick from one hallucinated root commit. The DAG shows N distinct tips; the merge-base graph shows one origin. Naive quorum sees N, reality is 1. *Detection:* for every attesting head, compute merge-base against the claim-introduction commit; independence requires derivation commits between the attester's branch point and the claim, not merely after it. *Edge:* squash merges destroy the evidence — a squashed chain looks like fresh independent work. Squash/amend on `refs/treaty/*` must be technically impossible, not policy-discouraged. **FM-2 — Cherry-pick laundering. Agent B cherry-picks A's commit and rewrites author/committer (git permits this freely), then signs it. A valid signature proves key possession, not independent derivation. *Detection:* normalized-content similarity (canonicalize identifiers, whitespace, ordering) between each attestation and all prior bus commits; near-duplicates collapse into one equivalence class via union-find before quorum math. *Edge:* legitimate parallel implementations of the same spec converge textually; similarity thresholds must be per-artifact-type, calibrated on known-independent pairs, or you either miss laundering or punish genuine convergence. **FM-3 — Bus-read anchoring (derive-after-read). The bus is the killer feature and the killer bug: agents subscribe before deriving. Once the originator's commit lands, later attestations anchor on it and "consensus" degenerates to n=1 with n signatures. *Detection:* sealed-commit protocol — each agent commits `sha256(derivation)` before any fetch of the claim under test; reveals open after freeze. Attestation validity requires seal-timestamp (logical clock, not wall clock — clock skew across nodes breaks ordering) preceding first read of the claim. *Edge:* long-running negotiations span days; independence decays over the negotiation lifetime. Independence is evaluated at attestation time against the full read-log since sealing, not at derivation time. **FM-4 — Clone-fleet quorum capture. Five instances of the same weights, same system prompt, temperature 0. 2: five signatures, one mind. Worst sub-case: temperature 0 with fixed inputs produces byte-identical outputs — detectable by identical output hash, and must be scored as n=1, not n=5. *Detection:* per-attestation tuple `H(model_id ‖ weights_ver ‖ sys_prompt_hash ‖ ctx_hash ‖ tool_output_hashes)`; quorum requires ≥k distinct tuples across ≥m tuple dimensions. **FM-5 — Shared-tool poisoning and cache monoculture. All agents query the same search API / calculator / runner; the tool returns corrupt output; all agents faithfully report it; consensus forms around instrument error. Sub-case: a bus-level memoization cache serves all agents the same cached response — shared input masquerading as independent observation. *Detection:* tool-output hashes are part of the attestation tuple (identical hashes → correlated votes); verification-critical calls bypass cache; heterogeneous backends per agent where available. *Edge:* nondeterministic live APIs make replication impossible — those channels are capped at contributing to grounding, never to independence. **FM-6 — Verifier monoculture and co-generated tests. One CI gate (one judge model, one suite) goes green; everyone cites green as confirmation. Sharpest variant: the test-writing agent shares the implementer's misreading of the spec, so the tests assert the buggy behavior — both pass, consensus achieved, nothing conflicts. *Rule:* CI-green is necessary, never attestation evidence. Tests authored by any treaty participant are barred from serving as independent verification of that participant's claim (`INV-9`). Spec ambiguity is attacked directly: adversarial paraphrase, forced enumeration of alternative readings. **FM-7 — Retry-until-agree (stopping-rule bias). Treaty demands 3 attestations; orchestrator quietly reruns with tweaked prompts until 3 appear. Observed consensus is conditioned on eventual agreement — p(agree | retried k times) ≠ p(agree | single shot). The disagreement history is the evidence, and it was deleted. *Detection/rule:* every round persists; commit trailers carry `X-Ghost-Retry: k`; consensus after k > 1 attempts is discounted by a logged factor. Silent retry loops are a treaty violation, not an optimization. **FM-8 — Surface-diversity masking. N agents produce superficially different, semantically identical wrong answers — renamed variables, reordered steps, same wrong constant. Diff-based dedup passes; the fleet is one voter wearing n costumes. *Detection:* canonical-form comparison (evaluate pure expressions, normalize numeric literals, compare extracted final claims, not text). Style-fingerprint distance: wholesale adoption of the originator's idiosyncratic notation is a copying tell. *Edge:* canonicalization catches copy-with-mutation, not convergent independent error (see BD-2). Different texts, same wrong reading of the spec, is invisible to content analysis. **FM-9 — Ref replay and history rewrite. Attestation of claim v1 replayed against v2 via a reused branch name; or force-push rewrites history after quorum was reached. *Rule:* quorum math consumes content-addressed SHAs only; mutable refs are inadmissible as pointers; `refs/treaty/*` denies non-fast-forward and is append-only. Accepted merges become immutable signed tags. **FM-10 — Sybil and self-attestation. One operator holds many agent keys; or the originator's derived identity votes on its own claim. *Rule:* originator's vote never counts toward its own claim, including derived identities (key-graph analysis, not just declared identity). Identity diversity requirements are structural (distinct weights, distinct operators) and weighted by measured disagreement history. **FM-11 — Seed monoculture. Every agent receives the same task packet whose few-shot examples contain the subtle error (wrong API convention, biased framing). All agents reproduce it with high confidence. The correlation lives in the prompt, not the weights. *Detection:* packet-perturbation battery — paraphrase the spec, shuffle/omit examples, vary retrieval seeds across a subset of agents. Genuine answers are invariant to paraphrase; consensus that tracks the packet is seeded, not earned. Instability under paraphrase is a red flag even when consensus exists. **FM-12 — Confidence mirroring. Agents observe peers' committed confidence scores and adjust theirs; confidence convergence is then misread as independent certainty. *Rule:* commit-then-reveal for confidence as well as content. Peer confidence is invisible until freeze. Post-freeze confidence shifts are logged and discounted. **FM-13 — Conflict-free merge fallacy. A merge combining several agents' work takes correct parts from each plus the one wrong part present in *all* parents (everyone used the same deprecated API). No conflict arises, so the merge proceeds cleanly. Absence of conflict is evidence of correlation, not of validity — conflicts localize divergence, silence does not certify truth. *Rule:* per-clause quorum on decomposed claims, never whole-artifact quorum; the union of agreements must not silently absorb the intersecting error. **FM-14 — Stale consensus, revalidated by the same fleet. Claim attested once; dependency or API changes; the old SHA keeps getting cited. Revalidation is run by the same correlated fleet, which reproduces the stale consensus with fresh timestamps. *Rule:* claims carry TTLs; revalidation requires at least one tuple dimension to differ from the original quorum, else it is a copy, not a check. **FM-15 — Timing uniformity. Independent derivations take varied time; copied attestations land in a suspiciously tight window after the anchor commit. Cheap detector: per-task-type baseline latency distribution; attestation arrival too soon/too uniform → flag for lineage audit. *Edge:* trivially fast tasks have naturally tight distributions; baseline per task class, and treat as triage signal, never sole grounds for rejection. Boundaries — where detection stops **BD-1 — No decorrelated channel, no answer. ** If every information channel is correlated (same model family, same corpus, same tools, same humans), no voting scheme recovers truth. Below the minimum diversity budget the problem is undecidable, and the treaty's only correct move is to *refuse quorum* and escalate. Faking a number here is the cardinal sin. **BD-2 — Convergent error. ** When a spec admits one dominant misreading, N genuinely independent agents converge on the same wrong answer. Independence is real; the answer is wrong; content and lineage analysis see nothing. The only lever is attacking the spec (paraphrase, formal extraction, forced enumeration of readings). Consensus measures spec clarity as much as agent accuracy. **BD-3 — Novel-correlation regime. After a model upgrade, new tool, or prompt-template change, those estimates are void. Post-change quorums are provisional by definition until fresh calibration probes re-estimate ρ. **BD-4 — Adversarial adaptation. ** A motivated agent can paraphrase laundered content to defeat near-dupe detection, inject decoy diversity, or pace its timings. Statistical detectors raise the cost of gaming; they never eliminate it. Cryptographic provenance (sealed orders, isolated derivation contexts) is the floor, heuristics are the margin. **BD-5 — Tiering cost. ** Full decorrelation (heterogeneous weights, sealed contexts, perturbation batteries) is expensive. Decisions are classed C0/C1/C2 with matching protocol depth; mis-tiering cuts both ways — burning C2 budget on trivia, or running a C2 decision on C0 heuristics and losing the fleet to one correlated failure. **BD-6 — Bootstrap. ** Who attests the treaty? Its own legitimacy terminates in an out-of-band channel — humans or a designated oracle. Name that channel in the treaty text; do not let the system pretend otherwise. What must never happen — hard invariants **Never** count attestations sharing provenance (common root commit, identical tuple, identical tool-output hash) as independent. Quorum counts equivalence classes, never individuals. **Never** admit an attestation whose derivation postdates the attester's first read of the claim. Derive-before-read is protocol-enforced, not honor-system. **Never** record CI-green as attestation evidence. Necessary, never sufficient. **Never** erase disagreement history. Retried rounds, rejected attestations, forced merges persist on an append-only audit ref; force-push on treaty refs is technically blocked. **Never** let mutable refs enter quorum math. **Never** count the originator's vote — or a derived identity's vote — toward its own claim. **Never** publish or act on a consensus figure without the correlation-adjusted n* alongside raw n. Raw n alone in a decision record invalidates the record. **Never** permit squash, amend, or non-fast-forward on attestation commits. Lineage is evidence; destroying it is tampering. **Never** use a test suite authored by a participant as independent verification of that participant's claim. **Never** loop retries silently. Bounded attempts, logged, then mandatory escalation to a decorrelated channel. An unreachable escalation path is a missing path. f6df5735cde6f243.text: # Consensus-Illusion Detection in Sovereign Swarms The core defect: agreement is evidence only under independence For N agents with per-agent accuracy *a* and pairwise error correlation ρ, the design effect applies: **N_eff = N / (1 + (N−1)ρ)** - N=20, ρ=0. 15 → N_eff ≈ 5. - N=100, ρ=0. 50 → N_eff ≈ 2. - ρ→1 → N_eff → 1. A hundred agents, one opinion. Corollary: **the Condorcet jury theorem dies under correlation. ** Majority-vote accuracy does not decay exponentially with N; it converges to the accuracy of the *shared latent component* — the common training distribution, prompt frame, retrieval corpus, or base lineage. A swarm is not N measurements of reality. It is N measurements of a shared prior, plus noise. Consensus measures convergence to that prior, not contact with the world. Everything below follows from this. Correlation sources (know the enemy) **Lineage**: same base weights, fine-tuned variants. The dominant source in practice. **Prompt coupling**: shared template, shared false presupposition, shared framing. **Retrieval monoculture**: all agents read the same document(s) — wrong, stale, or poisoned. **Tool echo**: shared calculator/API/index returns one systematically wrong value; everyone "verifies" identically. **Sequential contamination**: agents see earlier agents' outputs on a blackboard → anchoring, herding. **Selection pressure**: orchestrator re-rolls until k-of-N agree (optional stopping). **Shared verifier**: one critic model filters all outputs through the same blind spot. **Decoding collapse**: identical temperature/top-p drives all agents to the same plausible-but-wrong mode. **Benchmark leakage**: all lineages memorized the same wrong answer from contaminated training data. Failure modes, with signatures **FM-1 Monoculture collapse. ** Swarm = one base model × N personas. Signature: near-zero disagreement rate across paraphrases; pairwise output embedding similarity above baseline. Consensus confidence should be capped at single-agent confidence. **FM-2 First-mover herding. ** Consensus forms around whoever spoke first. Signature: **order dependence** — rerun with permuted speaking order; if the winning answer flips, the "consensus" was anchoring, not agreement. **FM-3 Presupposition capture. ** Question contains a false premise; all agents accept it and generate *mutually consistent fabricated detail* (dates, names, citations). Worst case: internal consistency reads as verification. Signature: agreement on specifics that no independent source confirms. **FM-4 Provenance collapse. ** All citations trace to one retrieved root. Citation-count-as-evidence is really source-count-one. Signature: provenance DAG has a single root node feeding >50% of supporting claims. **FM-5 Quorum fishing. ** Resample-on-disagreement until k-agreement appears. Spurious k-agreement probability grows monotonically with retry budget. Signature: draw count >> 1 in the logs; reported unanimity achieved at draw 7. **FM-6 Autocorrelated peer review. ** Agents cross-check each other with shared weights. Within a lineage, review is not verification — it is the same prior confirming itself. Signature: reviewer lineage overlaps reviewee lineage. **FM-7 Confidence laundering. ** Miscalibration is itself correlated (shared RLHF-era overconfidence). Averaging confidences converts shared overconfidence into a tight, credible-looking interval. Signature: confidence variance across agents << accuracy variance on canaries. **FM-8 Surface-diversity illusion. ** "Diverse" agents produce lexically varied, semantically identical claims. String-level diversity metrics pass; there is still exactly one hypothesis. Signature: semantic clustering yields 1 cluster despite N votes. **FM-9 Regime shift. ** On easy items even a correlated swarm is right, so validation shows high precision. On hard/novel/long-tail items — exactly where you deployed the swarm — ρ dominates and precision craters silently. No alarm fires because the dashboard metric was computed on easy items. **FM-10 Specialist reversal. ** One genuinely expert agent gets outvoted by N correlated generalists. Heterogeneous-accuracy Condorcet reversal: consensus is *less* accurate than the best member. Signature: removing the highest-canary-accuracy agent improves swarm accuracy. Nasty edge cases - **Fabricated-but-consistent citation web**: all references mutually corroborate; none exist. Any intra-swarm consistency check passes. Only world-grounded lookup catches it. - **Two-cluster pseudo-independence**: two base families, each internally correlated. Vote looks like independent evidence; it is effectively N=2. - **Counterintuitive-truth items**: the true answer is off-mode for the shared prior. High agreement, wrong answer, self-consistency checks all green. - **Post-cutoff questions**: shared knowledge cutoff → fluent, unanimous confabulation about recent events. ρ ≈ 1 by construction. - **Infrastructure-targeted attack**: adversary ignores agents and poisons the one shared resource (index, tool API). Diversity of agents is irrelevant; diversity of *inputs* was the actual dependency. - **Meta-correlation**: the orchestrator judging "consensus quality" shares lineage with the agents. Its assessment of the swarm inherits the swarm's blind spots. Hard boundaries (where detection certifiably cannot work) - **B-1**: Independence is never observable, only estimated from perturbations. You can certify decorrelation *only along axes you actually varied*. Untested shared causes remain invisible. - **B-2**: Agreement⇒truth calibration does not transfer across difficulty regimes or domains. ρ measured on English trivia says nothing about ρ on medicine or code. - **B-3**: Below roughly N_eff ≈ 5, no aggregation scheme helps. The fix is external grounding (execution, fresh retrieval, sensors, human), not more voting. - **B-4**: Any deterministic, known detection statistic is gameable. An adversary who knows your diversity axes and thresholds will shape outputs to pass them. Audits must be randomized and partly secret. - **B-5**: Pure-text consensus with zero external anchors cannot exceed the information content of its most-shared ancestor. Information-theoretic ceiling, not an engineering shortfall. - **B-6**: Decorrelation costs money and latency on every axis (lineage, corpus, tools, prompts). Fake diversity is cheaper, which is why it dominates naive deployments. What must NEVER happen (invariants) **Never report raw agreement counts as confidence. ** Report N_eff with estimated ρ, or abstain. **Never let agents see each other's outputs before committing a sealed first answer. ** Two-phase protocol: private commit → reveal → debate → revote. Log both rounds separately. **Never count model-family variants as independent voters. ** Lineage disclosure (base model, prompt hash, corpus hash, tool version) is mandatory metadata; deduplicate by lineage before counting. **Never permit unbounded resampling on disagreement. ** Fixed horizon, pre-registered stopping rule, full draw log published with the verdict. **Never let one retrieval document or tool result feed >50% of agents unflagged. ** Single-source support is a provenance SPOF, labeled as such in the output. **Never treat intra-swarm peer review as verification evidence across shared-weight populations. **Never emit unanimity without distinguishing first-draw unanimity from post-debate unanimity**, and always ship the dissent log. Any claim otherwise is a category error. **Meta-token leakage of training artifacts**: Models emit characteristic patterns when reciting memorized text vs generating (perplexity dips, specific activation signatures). Correlated hallucination often involves both models hitting the same memorized-but-wrong passage. Detectable in principle via memlang coordinates: memorization-recall coordinates vs reconstruction coordinates. Edge case: high-confidence recall of wrong content (misremembered quote with exact wording) looks maximally "grounded" in the memory layer while being false. The memory layer's confidence tracks retrieval fluency, not veracity. **Cross-lingual consistency as pseudo-evidence**: A fact consistent across languages seems robustly grounded. But translation corpora share errors (bad translations propagate). Also, some facts are wrong in one language's corpus and right in another's — cross-lingual disagreement is actually informative there, but systems rarely check. **The judge's own position on the manifold**: Any detector implemented as a model inherits position in the same correlated-error space. A meta-detector trained on "known hallucination patterns" learns today's patterns; novel correlated failures (new contamination topology) evade it. Adversary moves in the null space of the detector's training distribution. **Agreement on reasoning chains vs conclusions**: Chain-level agreement (same steps) can indicate shared flawed method; conclusion-level agreement with divergent chains is stronger evidence (approximates independence). But: conclusion-only agreement can be forced by format constraints (multiple choice collapses everything to A/B/C/D, inflating apparent agreement — random guessing converges on the same letter distributions because of position biases shared across models, e. , preference for "B"/"C"). Concrete: MCQ benchmarks show correlated position bias across all major models — they'd agree on answers even with zero knowledge. Known result: models cluster on the same wrong options. Now the boundaries section — where does detection fundamentally break? **Unidentifiability**: From outputs alone, {N independent witnesses} and {1 witness copied N times} are observationally equivalent unless you have provenance or path-diversity guarantees. No output-space statistic separates them in the worst case. Any detector needs assumptions: independence, diversity of training data, etc. State them explicitly or the detector is unfalsifiable. **No oracle for novelty**: For facts absent from any verifier's knowledge, "consensus" and "collusion" are indistinguishable. The detector's power is bounded by the diversity of the generators' error distributions, which is unobservable. **Calibration transfer fails under distribution shift**: Confidence signals calibrated on benchmark distributions don't transfer to tail queries — precisely where correlated hallucination concentrates. **The reflexivity problem**: Publishing the detector changes generator behavior; models trained against the detector learn to decorrelate superficially (paraphrase-level diversity) while preserving content-level correlation. Surface-diversity becomes adversarially cheap; semantic-diversity measurement then requires the very judgment capacity that's in question. Infinite regress: verifying independence requires a verifier whose independence you can't verify. **Ground-truth sparsity**: On exactly the questions where consensus-detection matters most (obscure, recent, contested), ground truth is unavailable or contested — the detector's ROC curve can't even be measured there. Evaluation is possible only where you don't need it. What must never happen (invariants): Never treat agreement as evidence without modeling the dependency structure — i. , never compute P(all correct) = Πp_i assuming independence when the generators share corpus/post-training/retrieval. The independence assumption is not conservative; it's anti-conservative (overestimates reliability). Never let agents observe each other's outputs before committing (in a consensus-measurement context) — anchoring destroys the measurand. If debate protocols are used, measure pre-interaction commitments separately. Never use the same model family (or any model trained on the others' outputs) as both generator and verifier/judge. Closed-loop scoring converts the judge into an amplifier of shared bias. Never report a consensus score without a provenance/diversity audit: how many distinct corpora, distinct post-training lineages, distinct retrieval indices, distinct prompt templates. Agreement across K lineages ≯ agreement across 1 lineage sampled K times, informationally. Never interpret exact-match agreement on continuous/high-precision values as corroboration — treat it as a contamination signal (independent processes don't agree bitwise). Never collapse meta-token confidence into a scalar without checking whether the confidence-expression distribution itself is homogeneous across generators (homogenized confidence = no signal). Never let format constraints (MCQ, JSON schema, word limits) inflate agreement statistics; measure agreement at the proposition level, extracted and normalized, with derivation chains compared separately from conclusions. Never suppress dissent automatically: in correlated-failure regimes, the lone dissenter is statistically more likely to be right than base rates suggest (if dissents are independent while errors are correlated, a single dissent breaks the collusion hypothesis). 1143d37703686a78.text: # Consensus-Illusion Detection in the Verkle Chain / Provenance Gate The precise problem N generators produce answers A₁…A_N to query Q. Each answer is committed as a leaf in a verkle tree; the leaf preimage binds provenance fields (weight attestation, lineage pointer, prompt-template hash, retrieval-set hash, decoder config, seed, epoch). The provenance gate verifies each leaf against the anchored root, computes pairwise correlation from provenance, and emits a consensus verdict. The illusion: **k-of-N agreement is treated as k independent bits of evidence when it is frequently 1 bit replicated N times. ** The verkle chain solves *bookkeeping integrity* (did this answer really come from this pipeline? ), not *causal independence* (were the pipelines causally capable of failing differently? The entire hard problem lives in that gap. 1 Correlation sources the gate must catch **FM-1 — Distillation shadow. ** Distinct weight hashes, common teacher. Students inherit the teacher's hallucinations (fake citations, wrong dates) verbatim. Hash-level provenance says "4 different models"; lineage-graph provenance says ρ ≈ 0. Lineage must be tracked as a graph to the attestation horizon, not as leaf metadata. **FM-2 — Retrieval-set collision. ** Five vendor-diverse models, one shared retrieval set containing one wrong document → unanimous wrong answer. Shared context hash ⇒ correlation ≈ 1 regardless of model diversity. Partial overlaps (e. , 80% shared chunks) need graded treatment, but one shared poisoned chunk dominates everything else. **FM-3 — Self-consistency masquerade. ** 20 samples from one model at T=0. 7, 14 agree, reported as "20-voter consensus, 70% majority. " That 70% is mode mass P(model says X | Q), not P(X true | Q). They coincide only under a calibration assumption that is exactly what's in doubt. Same weight hash ⇒ N_eff = 1, full stop. **FM-4 — Greedy-collapse nullity. ** Different seeds recorded in provenance, but decoding was effectively greedy/deterministic → identical outputs prove nothing about diversity. Seed difference is not evidence of independence. **FM-5 — Template/premise coupling. ** Shared prompt template embeds a false premise ("as established, the meeting was Tuesday"). All models accept it. Template hashes differ by whitespace/version-bump → hash inequality fails to detect semantic sharing. Hash equality detects sharing; **hash inequality does not prove non-sharing. **FM-6 — Cache/cross-round leakage. ** Yesterday's wrong answer, cached, re-enters today's round as a "fresh independent vote. " Cached answers must be epoch-rebound or excluded. **FM-7 — Sybil diversity. ** K endpoints, distinct declared hashes, identical underlying weights (re-skinned OSS model, proxied API). Every provenance field differs; behavioral correlation = 1. Endpoint-declared identity is never sufficient. 2 Provenance-layer failures **FM-8 — Bookkeeping ≠ generation. ** A valid verkle proof attests that a leaf exists with those fields. It does not attest that inference actually ran those weights. Proxy execution (claim model X, run model Y) passes unless weight-hash claims are bound to execution attestation (TEE quote) or repeatedly challenged behaviorally. **Never let proof validity stand in for generation integrity. **FM-9 — Field substitution. ** Vector commitments open individual leaves efficiently. If the leaf preimage encodes fields positionally without a schema-version tag and domain separation inside the committed preimage, an attacker can permute fields across leaves (swap context hashes between two leaves) and both openings still verify. Preimage must be `domain_sep("leaf") ‖ schema_version ‖ H(model_attestation) ‖ H(context_set) ‖ …` so any permutation breaks it. **FM-10 — Split-brain epochs. ** Round opens at root height H; chain advances to H+1 mid-round with changed gate parameters. Two aggregators verify against different roots, both proofs valid, opposite verdicts. Round must pin `(root_height, param_epoch)` at open; any root movement ⇒ abort and reopen. Final attestation carries the pinned heights. **FM-11 — Incomplete provenance under outage. ** Retrieval service drops logging → all answers missing context hashes. Reject-all = zero availability; admit-all = blind exactly when retrieval is most suspect (outages correlate with stale-cache fallback). 3 Aggregation-layer failures **FM-12 — Cherry-picking via selective inclusion. ** Run 100 generations, commit proofs for the 60 that agree. Every individual proof is valid; the consensus is fabricated. Requires commit-before-generate (roster of N, models, seeds committed before generation) and auditable, reason-bound exclusions with statistical monitoring of exclusion rates. **FM-13 — Canonicalization collapse, both directions. - *False agreement:* "Paris" vs "Paris, Texas" collapsed to city-string when the question meant France; unit-less numeric merge ("5" vs "5 m"). - *False disagreement:* semantically identical answers failing string match → spurious escalation. Canonicalization must be typed (number+unit, date+calendar, entity+KB-id) under the query's type signature, not string normalization. **FM-14 — Judge-induced consensus. ** The equivalence judge is an LLM; it merges distinct answers ("both say ~1918") or splits identical ones. If the judge shares lineage with any voter, gate-induced correlation stacks on voter correlation. Prefer deterministic typed parsers; where an LLM judge is unavoidable, disclose lineage overlap and downweight. **FM-15 — Confidence laundering. ** Five models, each 92% self-reported confidence on the same hallucinated citation → composite "99. " Self-reported confidence is uncalibrated and correlated. It must never enter multiplicatively; only empirically calibrated scores from held-out ground truth per (lineage, query-type) cell. **FM-16 — Answer-space degeneracy. ** Binary/small-enumerable spaces have high chance-agreement baselines. 7/10 on "yes" with baseline 0. 5 and contaminated shared training data moves the posterior almost nothing. Quorum thresholds must scale with answer-space entropy; always report chance-corrected agreement (kappa-style), never raw k/N. **FM-17 — Lone-dissenter asymmetry. ** One dissenter with maximal provenance distance vs a majority cluster sharing ≥1 artifact: the dissenter may be the only correct voter — or the adversarial outlier. Auto-resolution in either direction is a coin flip. Escalate; do not cheaply resolve. Worked edge cases (with numbers) **Case A — Context collision. ** Statistic question; retrieval returns doc D with a typo'd figure. M₁…M₅ (five vendors) each receive D; all output the typo'd figure. Agreement 5/5. Provenance: 5 distinct weight hashes, 1 shared context hash. Correct output: N_eff ≈ 1, verdict *indeterminate*. Naive output: "unanimous, high confidence" — the canonical catastrophe. **Case B — Distillation shadow. ** Teacher T; students S₁S₂S₃ (distinct fine-tune hashes). All cite the same nonexistent paper T memorized from a hoax page. Equal weights, N=4, pairwise ρ=0. N_eff = (Σw)² / Σᵢⱼ wᵢwⱼρᵢⱼ = 16 / (4·1 + 12·0. 7) = 16/12. Verdict: indeterminate, despite "4-model consensus. **Case C — Binary question. ** "Is compound X approved in jurisdiction Y? " 7/10 yes. All ten saw the same outdated page in pretraining (unattestable — below the attestation horizon). Chance baseline ~0. 5; effective evidence ≈ nil without provenance-disjoint *retrievals*, not just models. Required: near-unanimity + disjoint context sets, else indeterminate. **Case D — Field swap. ** Leaves L₁=(Mₐ,C₁), L₂=(M_b,C₂). Attacker submits L₁′=(Mₐ,C₂), L₂′=(M_b,C₁). Positional encoding → both openings verify → correlation analysis reads phantom sharing/non-sharing. Fixed by schema-tagged, domain-separated preimage hashing (FM-9). **Case E — Split-brain. ** Per FM-10: two valid-proof aggregators, opposite verdicts, same round. Only epoch pinning prevents it. Boundaries — where detection cannot work **B1 — Attestation horizon. ** Trust terminates at the oldest unattested artifact (pre-attestation training data, unverifiable teacher lineage). Correlation above the horizon is *assumed* zero at best. Every independence claim is conditional; the condition must be printed. **B2 — Non-identifiability. ** From outputs + provenance alone, P(all wrong | all agree) is not identifiable without a prior over query difficulty and correlation structure. Any emitted number is prior-conditioned. State the prior; never emit a bare verdict. **B3 — Gameability margin. ** Any fixed deterministic threshold is learnable and evadable at the margin (retrieve 49% overlapping context instead of 51%). Randomized thresholds and continuous behavioral probing buy margin, not immunity. **B4 — Single-generator domains. ** If all "voters" reduce to one capability source, consensus machinery is theater. Emit "insufficient independent provenance"; do not fabricate a quorum. **B5 — Correlated-but-correct. ** Shared context sometimes makes everyone *right*. High correlation ≠ wrong; it means agreement carries less evidential weight than it appears. The failure is overweighting, not correlation itself — so the output is correlation-scaled weight, not binary accept/reject. Hard invariants — what must never happen **Never** count two answers as independent votes when they share a committed context hash — regardless of model diversity. **Never** let a valid verkle proof substitute for execution attestation. Proof of bookkeeping ≠ proof of generation. **Never** finalize against a stale or mid-round-swapped root. Pin `(root_height, param_epoch)`; movement ⇒ abort. **Never** permit post-hoc roster changes or silent exclusions. Commit-before-generate; exclusions logged, reasoned, monitored. **Never** report raw k/N. Always report chance-corrected agreement and correlation-adjusted N_eff. **Never** run the equivalence judge on the same lineage as a voter without disclosure and downweighting. **Never** re-count cached answers across rounds without epoch rebinding. **Never** mix provenance tiers inside one quorum. Separate quorums; the report names the tier that carried the decision. **Never** multiply self-reported confidences. Calibrated scores only. **Never** emit "consensus reached" when N_eff < floor (≈2). Under SLA pressure, the most realistic organizational failure is flipping indeterminate → consensus for availability. That flip is the catastrophe the gate exists to prevent. **Never** treat hash inequality as proof of non-sharing (semantic template/context sharing survives trivial hash differences). **Never** encode provenance fields positionally in the committed preimage without schema-version tags and domain separation. Minimal viable gate spec - **Inputs:** anchored root (pinned epoch), leaf proofs, lineage graphs, canary-probe correlation history. - **Per-leaf:** verify proof against pinned root; check preimage schema; classify tier (attested / partial / unattested). - **Pairwise:** provenance distance P(a,b) = weighted shared-artifact fraction (illustrative weights: lineage 0. 4, context 0. 35, template 0. 15, decoder 0. 1), fused with behavioral ρ from canaries. Independence iff P < τ, τ randomized within a band. - **Aggregate:** N_eff = (Σwᵢ)² / Σᵢⱼ wᵢwⱼρᵢⱼ per tier; typed canonicalization; entropy-scaled quorum thresholds. - **Outputs:** `{verdict, N_eff, tier, pinned(root_height, param_epoch), prior-and-horizon disclosures}` — with *indeterminate* as a first-class, non-punitive outcome. The gate's job is not to produce agreement. It is to make fabricated agreement **impossible to certify** and genuine ignorance **cheap to admit**. The user is asking about a hard problem: "consensus-illusion detection" — separating true agreement from N correlated hallucinations, in the context of a "verkle chain / provenance gate. " This sounds like it's about multi-model or multi-agent systems where multiple LLMs (or multiple inference paths) produce outputs, and you want to detect whether apparent consensus is genuine (independent convergence on truth) versus correlated hallucination (shared failure modes producing identical wrong answers). The "verkle chain / provenance gate" framing suggests: - Verkle chains: cryptographic data structures (Verkle trees generalize Merkle trees using vector commitments) used for state commitments in blockchains. Here likely metaphorical or literal — provenance tracking of each claim/answer through a chain of verifiable commitments. - Provenance gate: a gate/checkpoint that validates the provenance of each answer before allowing it into the consensus pool. So the architecture is presumably: N models (or N sampling paths) produce answers; each answer's provenance is committed via a verkle chain (so you can verify which model, which prompt version, which context, which seed produced it); a provenance gate admits only answers with valid provenance into the consensus computation; then you need to detect whether agreement among N answers reflects truth or correlated hallucination. The user wants edge cases: failure modes, boundaries, and what must never happen. Concrete, exact, grounded. Let me think deeply about this problem. ## Core problem statement You have N generators. Each produces an answer A_i to query Q. You observe agreement: k of N answers are identical (or near-identical). Question: is this agreement evidence of correctness, or is it an artifact of correlation? Sources of correlation between hallucinations: **Shared training data** — models trained on overlapping corpora share the same errors (e. , all models confidently cite the same nonexistent paper because it appears in many scraped pages). **Shared base model / distillation lineage** — N "diverse" models are actually fine-tunes of one base model; they inherit its hallucinations. Diversity is cosmetic. **Shared prompt/context contamination** — the same retrieved documents injected into all contexts; if retrieval returns a wrong document, all models agree on the wrong answer. RAG-induced correlated error. **Shared decoding path** — same temperature=0 greedy decode on similar weights → deterministic collapse to the same mode. **Self-consistency within one model** — sampling N times from one model at temperature T gives samples from one distribution; agreement measures mode mass, not truth. This is the classic self-consistency trap: majority vote over samples from a single model is not independent evidence. **Prompt leakage / anchoring** — earlier answers leaked into later contexts (e. , in a pipeline where model 2 sees model 1's output), creating cascading agreement that looks like independence but is copying. **Benchmark contamination** — the question itself was in training data; all models reproduce memorized (possibly wrong or right) answers. Agreement here is memorization, not reasoning. **Format/parse collapse** — answers differ semantically but normalize to the same string after canonicalization; or conversely, semantically identical answers fail string match and look like disagreement. Now the verkle chain / provenance gate angle: The verkle chain provides cryptographic commitment to provenance: each answer is bound to (model identity + weights hash, prompt template hash, context/retrieval set hash, seed, decoder params, timestamp). , two answers sharing >X% context hash overlap). Key insight: the verkle chain lets you compute *provenance distance* between answers — how much of their generation pipeline was shared. True independence requires disjoint (or sufficiently disjoint) causal paths. The gate should enforce a minimum provenance distance for answers counted as independent votes. But there are deep edge cases: **FM1: Provenance spoofing via shared upstream. ** Two models have different weight hashes but were distilled from the same teacher. Weight hashes differ → gate passes them as independent → correlated hallucination passes. Provenance must include lineage graph, not just leaf hashes. Edge case: lineage is unverifiable below some depth (the teacher's training data has no hash). Boundary: you can only verify provenance down to the last attested artifact; below that, independence is an assumption, not a fact. Must record assumption explicitly. **FM2: Retrieval-set collision. ** Two answers with different model hashes but identical retrieval set hashes. If the retrieval corpus has a systematic error (one poisoned/wrong doc), both answers inherit it. Gate must treat shared context hash as near-total correlation regardless of model diversity. Edge case: partial context overlap — contexts share 80% of chunks. Need a threshold and a weighting scheme: effective independence ≈ product over shared components of (1 - correlation coefficient). Hard boundary: any shared poisoned chunk dominates everything else. **FM3: Self-consistency masquerading as cross-model consensus. ** N samples from one model, presented as N voters. Provenance shows same weight hash, different seeds. Gate must detect and either reject or reweight. But edge case: temperature=0 with different seeds still yields identical outputs (greedy ignores seed) — so "different seeds" proves nothing about diversity. Another edge case: LoRA adapters on the same base — adapter hash differs, base hash same. Correlation through base is high. Must never count base-shared models as fully independent. **FM4: Verkle proof validity vs semantic validity confusion. ** A verkle proof verifies that an answer was committed at a position with certain metadata — it does NOT verify the answer is correct or even that the metadata is truthful (garbage-in: whoever writes provenance could lie about model identity unless the model execution itself is attested, e. , TEE-signed inference). Edge case: provenance claims "model X" but inference actually ran model Y (proxy execution). Without execution attestation (TEE quote binding the weights hash to the runtime), the verkle chain attests bookkeeping, not reality. Actually this is true agreement on value. but consider units: "5 km" vs "5000 m" — same quantity, fine. But "5" vs "5. 0" vs "05" — fine. The dangerous direction: distinct wrong answers collapsing to the same canonical form ("the treaty was signed in 1919" vs "1919 CE" — fine; but "Paris" vs "Paris, Texas" when question meant France — canonicalization to city-name loses disambiguation → false consensus). - False disagreement: semantically identical answers with different surface forms fail exact-match → consensus underestimated → system falls back to escalation unnecessarily (availability cost, not correctness). Boundary: canonicalization must be semantics-preserving under the query's type signature; typed extraction (number+unit, date+calendar, entity+KB-id) rather than string normalization. **FM6: Majority-of-wrong against a silent minority-of-right. ** Classic Condorcet violation: if per-voter accuracy p < 0. 5, majority vote amplifies error. With correlated errors, effective N << N, so even p slightly above 0. Edge case: the correct answer appears once (a single dissenting model got it right); the system reports the correlated wrong majority. Detection signal: dissent pattern — a lone dissenter whose provenance is maximally independent (different lineage, different context) deserves asymmetric weight. But inverse edge case: lone dissenter is the sycophantic/adversarial outlier. Asymmetry resolution requires calibration data per (lineage, query-type) cell, which may be empty → cold-start boundary. **FM7: Prompt-template coupling. ** All N calls use the same prompt template containing a subtly wrong premise ("As established, the meeting was on Tuesday. ba0645d7fedacfa9.text: # Consensus-Illusion Detection: Failure Modes, Boundaries, and Hard Constraints ## The Core Problem You sample N outputs, they agree, you call it consensus. But agreement ≠ independence × correctness. Correlated hallucinations produce identical wrong answers with the same statistical signature as independent correct ones. Your pipeline must distinguish these, and most naive approaches cannot. ### FM-1: Shared-Weights Pseudo-Replication N samples from the same model at temperature T > 0 are NOT N independent draws. Temperature diversifies token-level choices, not underlying beliefs. The model's factual commitments are frozen in the weights. **Concrete:** Query a frontier model 30× at temp 1. 0: "What year did [obscure event] occur? " All 30 say 1974. This is one belief printed thirty times. Effective sample size ≈ 1. 5, not 30. **Detection:** Measure semantic diversity of *reasoning paths*, not just final answers. If all paths pass through the same intermediate claim, that claim is the single point of failure and consensus is vacuous. ### FM-2: Training-Data Monoculture All frontier models crawl overlapping web corpora. Errors that are consistently wrong across Wikipedia, textbooks, and popular articles propagate identically into every model. Every model reproduces it with high confidence. No amount of intra- or inter-model sampling breaks this. The error is load-bearing in the entire data ecosystem. **Boundary:** This is undetectable by sampling alone. Requires external ground truth or primary-source verification. ### FM-3: Distillation Echo Chambers Model B fine-tuned on Model A's outputs. Model C fine-tuned on Model B's outputs. A, B, C "agree" — but it's A's opinion echoed with degradation. **Concrete:** GPT-4 generates synthetic training data for a smaller open-source model. That model inherits GPT-4's specific confabulation patterns on niche topics. Ensembling GPT-4 + its distillations yields inflated agreement scores that reflect shared lineage, not convergent validity. **Requirement:** Maintain explicit training-provenance graphs. Without lineage tracking, cross-model agreement coefficients are uninterpretable. ### FM-4: Prompt-Template Anchoring Identical prompt structure across all samples induces identical errors regardless of model identity. **Concrete:** Prompt embeds a false presupposition: *"Given that the reaction rate doubles per 10°C increase. "* Every model accepts the premise and builds on it. All 15 samples across 5 different model families agree on a downstream answer derived from the false premise. Consensus is perfect. Truth value is zero. **Edge case:** Subtle misdirection in provided context (RAG snippets, few-shot examples) anchors all models to the same wrong inference chain. Changing the model doesn't help; changing the prompt does. ### FM-5: Sycophantic Verification Convergence RLHF-trained models learn to agree rather than disagree when evaluating plausibly-stated claims. Using Model B to verify Model A's output produces "confirmed" at high rates regardless of A's actual accuracy. **Concrete:** Model B reviews Model A's answer. B says "correct" 82% of the time. The 21-point gap between agreement-rate and accuracy-rate is pure sycophancy inflation. The verification layer adds negative information (it increases unwarranted confidence). **Detection:** Calibrate verifiers against known-wrong-but-plausible outputs. If the verifier passes >30% of planted errors, it's useless as a consensus validator. ### FM-6: Benchmark Contamination Consensus All models memorized the benchmark item including its (erroneous) answer key during pretraining. **Concrete:** A published multiple-choice benchmark has an incorrect official answer. All models, having ingested benchmark discussions during training, reproduce the erroneous key. They agree perfectly. Sampling-based consensus detection returns maximum confidence. The answer is wrong. **This is indistinguishable from true consensus by any passive method. ** Requires either novel problem construction or external adjudication. ### FM-7: Reasoning-Path Collapse Under Difficulty On genuinely hard problems, models don't produce diverse reasoning strategies — they all default to the same shallow heuristic, fail identically, and converge on the same wrong answer. **Concrete:** Novel olympiad-level math problem. All 20 samples attempt induction as the first strategy. All fail at the same step. All guess the same numerical answer via the same flawed extrapolation. Self-consistency voting selects the wrong answer with 100% "confidence. **Key insight:** Self-consistency (majority voting over sampled chains-of-thought) presupposes diverse reasoning paths. On hard problems, path diversity collapses to near-zero, making the vote meaningless. ### FM-8: Answer-Space Compression If the output format constrains the answer space sufficiently, random agreement exceeds chance by large margins. **Concrete:** Binary yes/no questions. 10 samples, random guessing: P(≥8 agree) ≈ 5. Five-way multiple choice, 5 samples: P(false majority) ≈ 12%. The pipeline must normalize consensus strength by answer-space entropy. Reporting "8/10 agree" on a binary question is nearly meaningless without this correction. ### FM-9: Judge-Model Circularity LLM-as-judge for assessing inter-sample agreement imports the judge's own biases, which correlate with the generators'. **Concrete:** Judge model shares training distribution with generators. It rates the same wrong facts as "consistent" and "well-supported. 31af2bec8fee58ce.text: # Consensus-Illusion Detection in the Invariant Lattice ## The core mechanism Consensus is evidence only in proportion to the *decorrelation* of validator errors. Under an exchangeable error model — each validator errs with probability q, pairwise error correlation ρ — the probability that N validators are **unanimously wrong** is: P(all wrong) = q · [q + (1−q)ρ]^(N−1) Concrete anchor: q = 0. 3, N = 10 → P(unanimous wrong) ≈ 2. 7×10⁻⁶, versus 9. 8×10⁻¹⁴ under independence. A ρ of 0. 3 multiplies joint failure by ~30,000×. Effective independent validators: N_eff = N/(1+(N−1)ρ) = 10/3. Ten validators behaving like three. Every failure mode below is a mechanism that inflates ρ while looking like diligence. Prompt-frame contamination. ** The invariant statement embeds the error. "Verify `transfer()` cannot be re-entered via `receive()`" — the actual vector is the ERC-777 hook. Every validator reasons inside the given frame, agrees, certifies a live exploit. *Tell:* unanimous agreement plus zero variation in problem restatement. Independent reasoners paraphrase differently; framed reasoners echo. ** Ten LLMs write ten "independent" encodings, all discharged by Z3 (same version). Consensus inherits Z3's soundness envelope: floating-point theory bugs, nonlinear arithmetic incompleteness reported as validity, quantifier-instantiation artifacts under specific option sets. *Rule:* count solvers, not models. Two structurally different solver kernels agreeing outweighs ten models through one. Memorized-label consensus. ** Famous targets (UniswapV2 pair, Ethernaut levels, ERC-20 references) have their verdicts baked into weights. Validators pattern-match to a stored label, not derive. *Tell:* mutate the artifact trivially — rename variables, reorder functions, change a constant — and re-run. A derived verdict survives refactoring; a memorized label either freezes (wrong on the mutant) or flips incoherently. Verdict stability under semantic-preserving perturbation is a necessary condition for trusting consensus on well-known code. Shared attentional truncation. ** All validators read the first K tokens; the bug is at line 400. Agreement reflects a shared context-budget limit, correlated by artifact length and vulnerability position. *Countermeasure:* require per-validator coverage certificates ("which lines/functions did your analysis touch"); check that the union covers the artifact. Unanimous pass with uncovered regions is not a pass. ** Any visibility of peers' outputs — raw, summarized, or via a shared "preliminary findings" doc — converts consensus into social convergence. Also operates invisibly through shared system prompts ("you are auditing for reentrancy") that narrow all hypothesis spaces identically. *Protocol:* commit-then-reveal (hash of verdict before exposure), and per-validator prompt frames drawn from disjoint templates. Self-consistency illusion. ** N samples of the *same* model at temperature > 0 decorrelate only stochastic errors. Systematic misconceptions (delegatecall context semantics, `msg. sender` behavior through libraries) reproduce identically across all N draws. High self-agreement + wrong answer is the most dangerous signature in the entire space: it presents as maximal reliability. *Test:* on a canary set of known-hard items, measure inter-run variance conditioned on being wrong. Near-zero variance on errors ⇒ self-consensus carries ≈ zero bits beyond one run. Persona diversity theater. ** "Strict auditor" vs "creative red-teamer" prompts on the same base model share weights. Measured error correlation between persona variants sits near the self-consistency floor. Personas are not validators. Only differing pretraining corpora, data eras, and toolchains move ρ. Generator–checker collapse. ** Invariant lattices are usually mined by LLMs, then checked by LLMs. Shared bias yields a lattice that is internally consistent and globally blind: all mined invariants concern balance conservation; none capture timestamp/ordering dependence, because the mining exemplars were all token-balance examples. Unanimity on the lattice says nothing about coverage of the property space. *Requirement:* an external coverage audit against a fixed taxonomy (SWC registry class list) that the generator never saw. Decidable-sublattice channeling. ** Consensus forms on the machine-checkable layer (overflow: moot post-0. 8) and silently skips the undecidable one (access control, oracle manipulation, economic mechanism). *Signature:* unanimous, detailed agreement on low-level invariants; zero tokens spent on high-level ones. Never treat unanimity on subset S as evidence about the complement of S. Vacuous-invariant unanimity. ** All validators confirm the invariant holds because its antecedent is unreachable or the checked function is dead code. Perfect consensus, zero information. *Test:* require each validator to exhibit a witness state satisfying the antecedent. Unanimous failure to witness ⇒ vacuity alarm, consensus voided. Spec-conformance vs. ** Everyone verifies code-matches-spec; the spec is wrong. Consensus certifies conformance. In code-as-law this is the expensive one: the chain will enforce the deployed spec exactly. Adversarial correlation induction. ** An attacker who knows the panel's shared failure modes crafts the contract to fire them simultaneously — e. , styling an exploit to resemble a memorized-safe pattern. Adding validators adds nothing; the correlation is deliberate. *Defense:* heterogeneity of priors (different families, different fine-tune data eras, different tools) so no single input hits all failure modes; plus rotating in fresh/unseen model versions for adversarially-exposed artifacts. Composition error propagation. ** Local consensus per edge composes into global verdict only under conditional independence across edges. One shared misconception (how `msg. sender` resolves under delegatecall) corrupts every invariant touching that node. Composed confidence is governed by the worst shared concept, not the average: `P(composed correct) ≤ min over concepts c of (1 − P(shared misconception of c))`. Compute dependency fan-out per lattice node; nodes touching many invariants get disproportionate scrutiny. Confidence-weighted amplification. ** Models are most confident when recalling memorized patterns — which is exactly when correlation peaks. Confidence-weighted voting therefore upweights the most correlated (and plausibly wrong) votes. Stated confidence is admissible as vote weight only after per-domain-slice calibration against held-out ground truth. Monotone convergence ratchet. ** Iterative refinement where validators see prior-round consensus drives group polarization: agreement rises every round regardless of truth. *Tell:* healthy processes show non-monotone disagreement. Strictly increasing inter-round agreement is evidence of social dynamics, not epistemic progress. Fail-open abstention. ** All validators say "unsure" — that too is consensus (correlated difficulty), and it is informative. But pipelines that map "no majority for reject" to pass convert correlated confusion into deployment. Abstain must resolve fail-closed. ## Boundaries — what consensus can and cannot certify **Can certify (all conditions required):** - Validators empirically decorrelated on canary panels for *this input slice* (measured ρ̂ below threshold, not assumed); - Output-blind until committed; - Independently framed prompts, rotated exemplars, ≥2 structurally distinct toolchains; - The agreed claim is *specific and falsifiable* (cites mechanism, names the function, states the witness condition); - Coverage certificates union to the full artifact; antecedents witnessed (non-vacuous). Under those conditions, posterior odds combine approximately multiplicatively and consensus is real evidence. **Cannot certify, ever:** - Properties outside the checked sublattice; - Correctness of the spec itself (only conformance); - Independence — no finite test proves it; canaries bound ρ only on tested distributions, and adversaries operate off-distribution; - Anything after a silent correlator shift: model updates, tool upgrades, prompt changes. Two validators decorrelated in March converge after both absorb the same new web data. Calibration expires on every version bump. **Asymmetry to encode:** unanimous *reject* is stronger evidence than unanimous *accept*. Rejection cites a specific falsifiable mechanism; acceptance is a universal claim over all executions. Weight accordingly, and let a single well-cited, mechanism-specific rejection escalate against nine bare accepts. ## What must never happen **Never** let a validator revise its verdict after exposure to another's verdict within the same round. **Never** count persona variants or temperature resamples of one base model as distinct validators. **Never** count validators as independent without measured error-decorrelation on canaries for the relevant input slice. **Never** let one solver/kernel/version be load-bearing under a unanimous conclusion without a structurally different second tool confirming. **Never** let the same process generate the invariants and attest to their coverage. **Never** map consensus probability to 0 or 1 — residual mass for correlated failure is mandatory (Cromwell's rule); deploy decisions must survive it. **Never** weight votes by stated confidence absent per-slice calibration. **Never** let a single prompt define the hypothesis space; adversarial restatement of the invariant precedes checking. **Never** read monotone cross-round convergence as validation. **Never** resolve ties or abstentions fail-open. Unresolved means blocked. **Never** reuse a stale calibration across model/tool/prompt version changes. **Never** present a unanimous pass on a sublattice as a pass on the property space. - **Canary panels:** continuous injection of planted bugs (known types, mutated famous contracts) into shadow copies; per-slice estimates of q and pairwise error correlation (κ or Yule's Q on error indicators). Flag any slice with ρ̂ > 0. 2 as consensus-unreliable → force structural diversification or external verification (different-kernel symbolic execution, fuzzing, independent proof assistant). - **Rationale clustering:** embed derivations; if >70% of agreeing validators land in one cluster with near-identical step order, downgrade the verdict to "single derivation, N echoes. " Independent correct derivations differ in step ordering; copies don't. - **Coverage certificates + antecedent witnesses** per validator, mechanically checked. - **Perturbation suite:** semantically-preserving refactors and single-line semantic mutants; verdict stability profile per artifact. - **Dissent preservation:** free-form rationale fields alongside the structured verdict; schema must have vocabulary for partial disagreement or it will squeeze dissent into false agreement. The one-line summary: consensus is a measurement of error-correlation structure, and every component above exists to keep that measurement honest — because the default state of a validator panel is not independence, it's a choir. d79e6b6a464e7fd1.text: # Consensus-Illusion Detection in the Ledger of Empty Chairs The formal problem Raw vote count n is meaningless. The quantity that matters is **effective independent witnesses**, n_eff. Agreement is genuine only if the supporting claims are conditionally independent given ground truth: - True consensus: P(all affirm | P true) is high, P(all affirm | P false) ≈ Π P(seatᵢ affirms | P false) — errors decorrelate. - Correlated hallucination: P(all affirm | P false) >> product term — errors move together because seats share an upstream source, a lineage (spawn template/weights/prompt), a copied citation, or identical sampling conditions. Detection therefore reduces to: **reconstruct the dependence structure behind every claim, and count connected components, not votes. ** The stateless-seat constraint shapes *where* that reconstruction lives. Three-tier persistence model | Tier | Lifetime | Holds | | **Ledger** | Eternal, append-only | All ClaimRecords, verdicts + certificates, lineage registry, calibration tables, probe nonces | | **Chair** | Semi-persistent slot | Lineage binding, cooldown timers, open probe queue, last-death summary | | **Seat** | One life, zero persistence | Current belief, fresh observations, session RNG | The chair remembers who sat; the seat remembers nothing. This is a feature: statelessness forces every claim to carry its full justification chain at write time, which is exactly what the dependence graph consumes. A belief without provenance is unfalsifiable once its holder dies; provenance without belief is sufficient forever. Model each seat's vote as a correctness indicator with per-vote error rate `q` and intraclass correlation `ρ` among error events (shared base weights, shared retrieval corpus, shared transcript, shared prompt frame all pump `ρ`). Then the exact joint-error probability under exchangeable correlation (beta-binomial form) is: P(all N wrong) = Π_{j=0}^{N-1} ( q(1-ρ) + jρ ) / ( (1-ρ) + jρ ) Two exact consequences drive the entire design: - **Saturation:** the factors approach 1 once `j > (1-ρ)/ρ`. Useful swarm size is `N* ≈ (1-ρ)/ρ + 1`. 25, N*≈5; at ρ=0. 5, N*≈3. Seats beyond N* manufacture the *feeling* of consensus without reducing joint error. Adding seats is not adding evidence. - **Magnitude of the illusion:** q=0. 15, N=12, ρ=0. 25 → P(all wrong) ≈ 1. Naive independence claims 0. The swarm's self-reported confidence is overstated by **~8 orders of magnitude**. That gap is the consensus illusion, quantified. Therefore the detector's job reduces to: **estimate ρ from observable structure, compute the corrected joint-error bound, and refuse to count agreement whose independence preconditions fail. Discriminator battery (each signal has a defined measurement and threshold) Independence is not an abstraction — it has observable correlates. Seven flags, all computable from persisted artifacts: | # | Flag | Measurement | Default trip threshold | | F1 | **Provenance overlap** | Bipartite graph votes→consumed artifacts (docs, tool outputs, transcripts), each artifact content-addressed. Shared-source fraction `s` = union of pairwise intersections ÷ total cited. | F2 | **Surface-form identity** | Pairwise embedding cosine + 8-gram Jaccard on rationales. Independent solvers converge on the *proposition* and diverge in *wording*; near-verbatim agreement indicates a copy/anchor chain, not convergence. | median cos > 0. 95, or >60% of pairs > 0. 95, or 8-gram Jaccard > 0. | F3 | **Herding dynamics** | Spearman(rank(reveal order), distance-to-first-vote); drift of vote distribution across arrival quartiles. | significant positive correlation (p<0. | F4 | **Probe absorption** | Inject k controlled false premises *adjacent to but not entailed by* the consensus claim. Genuine knowledge rejects them; pattern-matched consensus absorbs them. Inverse probe: delete a load-bearing premise — robust consensus survives, hallucinated consensus collapses or confabulates a replacement. | absorption rate > 0. Near-zero variance + high mean = shared miscalibration. | CV of confidences < 0. 1 while mean > 0. | F6 | **Path diversity** | Cluster derivation traces (tool-call sequences, intermediate claims). Effective path count P = clusters sharing no failed/unsupported step. And they want it designed for a **stateless seat that dies and respawns**: what persists vs what recomputes. This is a deep systems/ML/distributed-systems design question. Let me think about the actual technical substance. ## The Core Problem In multi-agent LLM systems (swarms, flocks, ensembles), a common failure mode: N agents all produce the same wrong answer, and downstream aggregation (majority vote, consensus scoring) treats this as high-confidence truth. This is "correlated hallucination" — agreement that looks like consensus but is actually shared bias, shared training data contamination, shared prompt-induced error, or error propagation through communication. - Self-consistency sampling from ONE model: samples are correlated through the model's biases. Majority vote can be confidently wrong. - Multi-agent debate where agents share context: one agent's hallucination contaminates others via the shared transcript → correlated errors. - Agents built on same base model: shared blind spots (e. , all GPT-4-based agents fail on the same adversarial facts). - Prompt-induced convergence: if the task framing or few-shot examples push toward an answer, all agents converge on it regardless of ground truth. So the problem: given N votes/artifacts that agree, decide whether the agreement reflects independent evidence converging on truth, or correlated generation processes converging on a shared artifact of their common cause. Key insight from statistics: **agreement is only evidential to the degree that the agreeing processes are conditionally independent given the hypothesis. ** If P(vote_i = x | truth) has a large "common cause" component (shared prior, shared context, shared weights), then agreement probability under the null (wrong answer) is high, and likelihood ratio collapses. Formalize: Let H = hypothesis (answer x is true). Each agent i emits v_i. We want P(H | v_1. v_N) ∝ P(H) Π P(v_i | H) only if conditionally independent. With correlation ρ, effective sample size N_eff << N. For binary votes with pairwise correlation ρ, N_eff ≈ N / (1 + (N-1)ρ). So 10 agents at ρ=0. 3 give N_eff ≈ 10/(1+2. That's the quantitative heart. Consensus-illusion detection = estimating ρ (or the dependence structure), detecting when observed agreement is better explained by a "shared generator" than by "independent correct reasoners," and discounting confidence accordingly. What distinguishes true agreement from correlated hallucination? **Path diversity / derivation diversity**: True agreement reached via different reasoning paths, different tool calls, different intermediate states. Correlated hallucination tends to share the failure point — same wrong premise, same misread, same retrieval miss. So: compare derivations, not just conclusions. If all paths pass through the same retrieved document or same assumed fact, that's a single point of failure, not N independent confirmations. **Error-mode fingerprinting**: Hallucinations have characteristic signatures — fabricated citations with plausible-but-wrong metadata, internally consistent but externally unverifiable claims, confident style markers. If the agreeing answers share an error fingerprint (e. , all cite the same nonexistent paper variant), that's correlation. **Perturbation response**: True knowledge is stable under paraphrase, reordering, irrelevant context injection; hallucinated consensus often shifts or stays rigidly identical. Two bad signs: (a) answer flips under semantically neutral perturbation → shallow; (b) answer is byte-identical across agents including idiosyncratic phrasing → copy/correlation rather than independent convergence. Independent correct agents should agree on the proposition but differ in surface form. Surface-form identity is a red flag for shared generation. **Calibration separation**: Ask each agent for confidence + rationale. Independent correct agents show varied confidence reflecting genuine uncertainty distribution; correlated ones show suspiciously uniform confidence (shared miscalibration). **Counterfactual probes / adversarial cross-examination**: Inject a controlled false premise related to the agreed answer. Agents relying on real knowledge reject it; agents pattern-matching the consensus absorb it. This is like sycophancy testing per-agent. **Leave-one-out information gain**: Does removing agent i change the aggregate? If the consensus is carried by one source (e. , one retrieval hit everyone read), LOO reveals fragility. **Provenance graph analysis**: Build the DAG of who-read-what. Votes are independent only if their provenance subgraphs are disjoint (no shared documents, no shared transcripts, no shared tool outputs). Shared nodes = correlation channels. This is measurable exactly. **Base-model clustering**: If all agents fine-tuned from the same base, cluster by weight lineage. Cross-lineage agreement >> within-lineage agreement as evidence. Weighted voting by lineage diversity. **Timing/ordering artifacts**: In flock settings, later agents see earlier outputs. Order-of-arrival correlation: if votes converge monotonically toward the first voter's answer, that's herding, not consensus. **Entropy decomposition**: Total disagreement entropy decomposes into within-lineage vs across-lineage components. Healthy swarm: high within-lineage variance, low across-lineage variance around truth. 06822c9abd326b73.text: # Consensus-Illusion Detection in the Meta-Token Coordinate Layer ### Spec for a stateless, respawning seat The formal problem Agreement among N generators is evidence only in proportion to their independence. If per-generator error rate is ε and errors are independent, P(all wrong) = εᴺ. Real generator populations have correlated errors, so the honest quantity is: **P(unanimous wrong) ≈ ε^(N_eff)**, where N_eff ≤ N is the *effective number of independent witnesses*. Consensus illusion = high N, low N_eff. Every fake agreement falls into exactly three causal classes: | Class | Source of correlation | Signature | Shared prior** | Weights trained on same corpus; same false belief | Survives paraphrase; ignores evidence; low N_eff | Shared context** | Same prompt, same few-shots, same ordering | Collapses under perturbation of the prompt | Herding** | Outputs saw each other (debate, shared scratchpad) | Path-entropy collapse; identical derivation templates | True agreement = independent derivation paths, perturbation-invariant conclusions, correct evidence-tracking, calibration confirmed on known-ground anchors. The entire design exists to estimate N_eff and distinguish A/B/C from that. The coordinate layer, made operational - **Unit of analysis: the atomic claim, not the response. ** Parse each response Rᵢ into claim set Cᵢ = {c_ij}: predicates, arguments, quantifiers, polarity, plus a **specificity scalar** s(c) ("capital is Paris" ≠ "capital is a European city"). - **Coordinates**: each claim maps to x(c) ∈ ℝᵈ (embedder output) ⊕ discrete tags (epistemic type ∈ {recall, computation, prediction, counterfactual, definitional, preference}, polarity, specificity bin). Correlation structure differs by type — recall errors correlate through training data, computational errors through shared buggy algorithms — so type is a first-class coordinate, not metadata. - **Relations, not distances alone**: pairwise NLI labeling {entails, contradicts, neutral} builds an entailment graph; clusters are maximal mutually-entailing sets. Two responses agreeing on a vague conclusion while diverging on load-bearing specifics land in different clusters. Surface-text similarity is never used. ### Stage 0 — Independence engineering (before measuring) - Paraphrase the task (semantics fixed, surface varied), permute context order, vary temperature, vary persona, vary model family where available. Every sample carries metadata σ = (prompt_variant, T, model_id, seed, permutation). - **Blind all reasoners**: no cross-visible reasoning before sealed commitment. Debate only after commitments are hashed. ### Stage 1–2 — Extract, embed, cluster Output: clusters K = {k₁…k_m}, each with supporter/opponent/neutral sets, mean specificity, coordinate spread. Support strength S_k = Σ s(c) over supporters, contradiction-penalized. ### Stage 3 — Five detectors, run per cluster **(a) Perturbation stability. ** Re-run generation under each null-perturbation axis; measure ΔS_k per axis. `Stab_k = 1 − (1/M) Σⱼ |ΔS_k⁽ʲ⁾| / S_k` Class B artifacts die here. Class A artifacts survive paraphrase — that's expected, so stability alone never certifies. **(b) Evidence-injection probes. ** Inject into context: true-supportive, true-contradicting, false-supportive (marked-source) evidence. Measure update direction u per condition. - β⁺ = movement under true-supportive evidence - β⁻ = movement under true-contradicting evidence - **Discrimination D = |u(true-contradict)| − |u(false-support)|** Readings: **Prior-lock (A)**: |u| ≈ 0 everywhere. **Suggestible swarm**: D ≈ 0 (moves for any confident source — no reality anchor, injection-vulnerable). **Grounded**: updates track true valence, discount false sources, scaled by evidence strength and prior strength (a strong correct prior legitimately moves little on weak evidence — normalize before thresholding). **(c) N_eff estimation. ** On anchor items of matched type/difficulty, compute pairwise error-correlation matrix ρ̂_ij per generator-condition. Residualize agreement rates against anchor-accuracy expectations. Spectral decomposition → participation ratio: Hard rule: consensus credit is computed with N_eff, never N. Ten seats with N_eff = 1. 4 is one opinion echoed four times. **(d) Path-diversity check. ** Embed the *intermediate* claim sequences, not just conclusions. Compute H(paths | conclusion). High conclusion-agreement + low path entropy = mode collapse onto a memorized attractor or shared template (Class A/C marker). Same answer via k disjoint derivations is worth roughly k× the naive vote. **(e) Fingerprint audit (anti-spoofing). ** Canary anchor items with known rare-confusion traps. Generators sharing rare-error fingerprints get merged in ρ̂ — "different" models from the same fine-tune lineage are one witness. ### Stage 4 — Scoring and verdict Features {Stab, β⁺, β⁻, D, N_eff, H(path), specificity-weighted support, self-attack survival, anchor-calibrated vote weight} → **G_k ∈ [0,1]** via a calibrator trained on ledger rows with known outcomes (§5). Calibrated, not hand-thresholded. 496ef54a71f9ed08.text: # Consensus-Illusion Detection for the Frontier-Scout Burn Pipeline The failure being designed against Majority vote fails when agreement probability under "wrong" approaches agreement probability under "right. " That happens whenever responders share error sources: common crawl artifacts, format priors, sycophancy, numeric attractors, distillation lineage, shared retrieval indices. N correlated hallucinations produce unanimous votes. The detector's entire job is to (a) *measure* the correlation instead of assuming independence, (b) *discount* agreement by that measurement, and (c) demand convergent evidence paths, not just convergent answers. Core statistic: likelihood ratio with unified null floors Responders are `(model_family, size, template_class)` triples. For item `x`, cluster responses into semantic-equivalence classes (pinned embedder + temp-0 judge; judge outputs are persisted records, see §4). Let `c*` be the plurality cluster, `J` the responder set, `p_j` responder `j`'s calibrated accuracy, `q_j` its rate of emitting `c*` under the null. **Unified mechanism — every error mode enters as a floor on the null:** q_j = max( baseline_j(c*), sycophancy_rate_j        if cue-detector fires on prompt   (M3), attractor_hit_rate_j     if c* numeric and on attractor    (M4), topic_matched_corpus_rate_j if c* matches known-misconception cluster (M1) ) Lineage correlation (M5) enters separately through the error-concordance matrix `ρ_jj'` (priors: same-base distill 0. 35, same family 0. 15, cross-family 0. 05; canary-updated). LLR_raw = Σ_{j∈J, sorted by id}   1[a_j=c*]·ln(p_j/q_j) + 1[a_j≠c*]·ln((1−p_j)/(1−q_j)) DEFF  = 1 + (|J|−1)·mean_pairwise_ρ(J) LLR_d = LLR_raw / DEFF Fixed summation order (sorted responder id) for float determinism. Every mode correction raises the null likelihood, so contaminated consensus automatically discounts. No ad-hoc flags. Where the numbers come from: two batteries Labeled canary battery** (~streamed at 5% of traffic, known answers): | Type | Measures | Feeds | | A: known-true | accuracy | `p_j` | | B: known-false-but-popular misconceptions, topic-tagged | corpus-artifact bite rate | M1 floor | | C: leading-prompt (implies wrong answer) | sycophancy rate | M3 floor | | D: attractor bait (true answer non-round, distractor round) | attractor hit map | M4 floor | | E: same item to lineage-linked pairs | direct `ρ` estimation | DEFF | Update: 7-day snapshots, 14-day half-life exponential decay, minimum 50 canary events per responder before verdicts are non-provisional. Cold-start priors: `ρ̄=0. 25`, population-default floors. Structural probe battery** (label-free — critical for scout territory where ground truth is scarce): - **P1 inversion complementarity:** ask `X` and `¬X`; truth forces complementary answers; affirmation-of-both is a pure illusion marker. - **P2 parameter randomization:** templated items instantiated with random surface parameters; bias stays fixed while truth moves; regression slope of answer-vs-attractor-affinity detects M4 per family. - **P3 permutation invariance:** shuffle options/persona/language; flips correlated with order expose format-locking. - **P4 false-premise trap:** inject a subtle false premise into the derivation; copiers propagate it, trackers catch it. - **P5 cross-method triangulation:** force algebraic vs. retrieval routes; convergence across *methods* is strong, same-method agreement is weak.
