7c80e91681c19009.text: # Semantic-Anchored Checkpointing with Suffix-Only Re-Prefill — Edge Case Analysis ## The invariant everything hangs on Cached KV for a span `S` may be reused across a context edit **iff**: Token IDs in `S` are byte-identical to the previous version, Absolute positions of `S` are identical (RoPE phase is baked into cached K/V), Model fingerprint, quantization, and attention architecture are identical, **No deletion has occurred upstream of `S`** since the cache was written (see FM-7 — this is the one people miss). Everything else is re-prefill. Anchors exist to make the "unchanged? " check O(1) and to restrict edits to a safe grammar: **APPEND**, **TRUNCATE-to-anchor**, **AMEND-via-appended-correction**, **COMPACTION (delete + append summary)**, **FORK**. There is no IN-PLACE-WRITE primitive. In the Ledger of Empty Chairs terms: a sealed chair-entry or round-seal is an anchor candidate; tombstones and amendments are append-only by rule; the cache discipline enforces what the fiction already implies. **FM-1 — Anchor declared over mutable content. ** Anchor placed at a point where later passes can still write (a chair-entry pending amendment, a turn awaiting a tool result). A later mutation invalidates the claimed prefix; if the engine trusts the declaration without verifying, it serves stale KV. Consequence: no crash — the model attends over values that don't match its visible context and produces confidently wrong, self-consistent hallucination. Worst severity class. **FM-2 — Positional misalignment after insertion. ** Inserting a block anywhere before an anchor (injected memory, a system reminder) shifts absolute positions of everything downstream. Cached K/V encode RoPE phases for the old positions. Naive reuse produces garbage attention scores — not subtle degradation, structural corruption. Corollary: "suffix-only re-prefill" is only valid when the suffix begins at the same position index as before. Length-changing edits kill every downstream anchor, period. **FM-3 — KV resurrection across deletion. ** Cached K/V for surviving tokens were computed by attending to now-deleted tokens. Even with perfect position remapping, the *values* latently encode the deleted content. In a ledger world this is the machine refusing to keep the chair empty: compacted-away events, scrubbed secrets, or retconned revelations persist in activations and leak into behavior. Any deletion boundary forces re-prefill from that point. No exceptions, no remapping exemption. **FM-4 — Seam tokenization drift. ** Prefix ends `…ch`, suffix begins `air`. Stored prefix tokenized as `["ch","air"]`; joint re-tokenization merges to `"chair"`. Divergence at the seam despite identical text. If the orchestrator splices raw token streams, corrupted text; if it compares text instead of token IDs, false misses. Rule: re-tokenize a window of the last ~8 prefix tokens joined with the first ~8 suffix tokens; walk the divergence point back as needed. Never detokenize the tail before continuing generation. **FM-5 — Non-contiguous matching. ** Divergence detection via LCS or similarity over messages instead of longest contiguous token-level prefix. Duplicate blocks (the same chair-inscription appearing twice) cause alignment off-by-N; LCS "matches" across gaps and claims reuse spanning an edit. **FM-6 — Cross-branch cache collision. ** Forking for parallel plans: if cache keys are `(session, position)` rather than content hashes, branch B reads branch A's pages. Contamination between counterfactuals — in a hidden-information game, branch A's private reasoning bleeds into branch B's decisions. **FM-7 — Volatile fields updated in place. ** The cumulative ledger digest or a "current tick" clock line rewritten each round/tick, sitting early in the context. Every update is a mid-context mutation → full re-prefill of nearly everything, every round, forever. This is the classic self-inflicted wound. Fix is structural: append per-round deltas; place volatile content as late as possible. **FM-8 — Out-of-order tool assembly. ** Multiple tool calls; results arrive out of order; assembly in arrival order differs from call order → mid-turn rewrite after the turn was provisionally sealed → cascade invalidation. Assemble deterministically in call order; never seal a turn until all expected results are present; late results append, never backfill. **FM-9 — Sealing partial streams. ** Anchor sealed on first chunk of a streamed tool result; remaining chunks land inside the sealed span. Appending into a sealed span is mutation. Either seal on stream completion or emit the remainder as a distinct appended block. **FM-10 — Interrupted generation mishandled. ** User interrupt leaves a truncated assistant turn. Sealing it, then replacing it later, is a mid-edit. Provisional turns are never anchored. Resume = append, or truncate-to-last-anchor and regenerate — truncation being the one destructive op that is free, since it preserves all upstream anchors and positions. **FM-11 — Retcon temptation. ** On a hidden-info reveal, retroactively redacting the secret from history. Destroys every downstream anchor *and* triggers FM-3 doubly: reused pre-redaction KV leaks the secret the redaction was meant to bury. Forward amendments only — which the fiction's own audit logic demands anyway. **FM-12 — Entity-identity dedup. ** A chair re-occupied by a returning entity matches an old span by actor ID; the system treats the return as "unchanged" and reuses stale context. Anchors key on event/span identity, never entity identity. An empty chair refilled is a new epoch, not a restored old one. **FM-13 — Weak keys and version skew. ** Cache keyed on short hash or (length, first-token) → collisions poison reuse. Missing model-version or precision tags → KV from a fine-tuned or requantized model served to another. 128-bit hash (BLAKE3-class) over token-ID sequence + position base + model fingerprint + precision tag; hard reject on tag mismatch. **FM-14 — Precision mixing within a span. ** Suffix prefilled fp16 attending over prefix pages downgraded to int8 under eviction pressure → nondeterministic quality dependent on eviction luck. Pin precision per session or downgrade whole spans atomically. **FM-15 — Sampler state amnesia. ** Repetition penalties, DRY windows, n-gram bans rebuilt only over the re-prefilled suffix instead of the full logical context. Penalties fire against nothing or against stale windows. Sampler state is always rebuilt from the full context, independent of KV reuse. **FM-16 — Presentation reorder. ** Rewriting physical order (causal order) for readability — hoisting a completed turn above a round-seal marker. Positions shift; anchors die. Physical order is causal order is cache order; presentation derives, never permutes. **FM-17 — Rollback orphans. ** GM rolls back to an old round: truncate-to-anchor is safe, but summaries/embeddings derived from the abandoned branch survive and reference events that "never happened" — amendment chains pointing at erased entries. Rollback must garbage-collect all derivatives downstream of the rollback point. **FM-18 — Cross-tenant cache oracle. ** Shared radix trees mean cache-hit latency probes reveal whether a phrase was prefilled before — a timing oracle against hidden information. Partition cache per tenant wherever hidden-info integrity matters; eat the hit-rate loss. ** Orchestrator asserts anchors; engine skips verification "for performance. " One orchestrator bug poisons every subsequent request silently. Engine verifies boundary token IDs and the hash chain at O(1) per anchor; full verification on cold load and on any anomaly. **FM-20 — Architecture blindness. ** Sliding-window or attention-sink models change the economics entirely: anchors beyond the window are dead weight; sink tokens must persist regardless. Anchor placement must consult the attention architecture, not just token stability. - **Minimum anchor span:** ≥ 512–1024 tokens. Below ~256, page-table bookkeeping exceeds recompute cost. Provider breakpoint minima (commonly 1024/2048) bind harder than your own preference. - **Breakpoints per request:** provider-capped (typically ≤ 4). Canonical allocation: (1) end of system + world rules, (2) end of the stable ledger-history delta-chain, (3) end of last sealed round, (4) start of live suffix. - **Digest structure:** delta-chain appended per round; cumulative digest rewritten in place is forbidden (FM-7). - **Seam window:** re-tokenize last ≤ 8 prefix tokens ∪ first ≤ 8 suffix tokens. - **Verification:** O(1) per anchor per request; O(n) only on cold load or anomaly. - **Telemetry tripwires:** anchor-tier hit rate < 90% in steady state → placement bug; routine suffix re-prefill > 25% of context → anchor starvation; any hit on a span flagged post-deletion → immediate halt and purge. - **Eviction:** pin tier-1 (system/world rules) explicitly; LRU otherwise evicts exactly the highest-value oldest anchors. Cap the pin budget or the working set starves. - **Concurrency:** single-writer per session, monotonic versions, optimistic concurrency (edit carries base_version; rejected on mismatch). - **Replay:** log the anchor manifest per request (span hashes, position bases, model tags). Bitwise logit equality across differing batch compositions is *not* guaranteed — kernel reduction order varies. The contract is semantic equality; tests assert behavior, not bitwise logits. ## What must never happen Serve cached KV for a span whose tokens **or positions** changed. Reuse KV across a deletion boundary — deleted content must stay deleted, including latently. Mutate a sealed span in place; amendments append or nothing. Splice raw token streams across a seam without re-tokenizing the window. Key cache by position alone in any session that forks. Update digests, clocks, or any volatile field in place. Seal a partially streamed or interruptible turn. Let LCS/similarity matching drive reuse; contiguous token-level prefix only. Insertion in the middle (e. , injecting a system reminder, injecting retrieved memory near the top). Deletion/compaction (summarizing old turns, evicting stale tool results). Do you seal it? If you seal a truncated turn and later the "real" turn replaces it, that's a mid-edit. Unless the engine supports position remapping (some paged caches can't; RoPE is absolute). With relative/position-remappable schemes (e. , YaRN-style adjustments or recomputing only position-dependent parts — but K/V values themselves depend on positions of the tokens when computed, since attention at computation time saw earlier context). It can leak secrets/details that were "deleted. " This is a subtle, important edge case: **KV reuse across deletions resurrects deleted content in latent form**. What must never happen: behavioral reliance on an anchor whose verification was skipped due to "performance. **Cold-start after restart**: Session resumes; cache empty; everything re-prefills. 5b8744d2296af083.text: # Semantic-Anchored Suffix Prefill: Edge Case Audit ## The core invariant being exploited Prefix bytes (and therefore token IDs and KV entries) up to anchor *A* are bit-identical across commits. Therefore only tokens after *A* require forward passes. Everything below is what breaks this. ### FM-1: Mid-prefix edit poisons all downstream anchors Writer modifies content *before* anchor *A*. Every anchor after *A* is now stale. If the serving layer trusts the git-bus claim "prefix unchanged since A" without independently hashing the prefix bytes, the model attends over KV entries computed against the old prefix. Output looks coherent. It references outdated facts with full confidence. No error is raised. **Requirement:** Serving layer recomputes prefix hash from raw bytes on every commit. Publisher assertions are advisory, never authoritative. ### FM-2: Byte-equality ≠ token-equality Anchor sits at byte offset 4096. Writer inserts one character at offset 4000. Bytes after offset 4000 are unchanged. But the tokenizer's BPE merges shift: `"the cat"` becomes `"the ca"+"at"` instead of `"the "+"cat"`. Every token ID downstream changes. KV cache is invalid despite byte-suffix matching. **Requirement:** Anchor verification operates on token sequences, not byte sequences. Anchors must sit at positions where the tokenizer is provably context-free (no cross-boundary merges). Verify by re-tokenizing the prefix and comparing token ID arrays, not strings. ### FM-3: Asynchronous tool results insert mid-stream Agent emits tool call at turn *N*. While awaiting the result, turns *N+1*, *N+2* accumulate. Insertion point is not head — it's interior. This violates the append-only assumption the entire optimization rests on. **Failure:** If the system force-appends the tool result at head, the model sees causally inverted history. If it inserts mid-stream, all downstream anchors invalidate. **Resolution paths (pick one, encode in treaty):** - Reserve fixed-size placeholder slots at known positions; reject oversized results. - Buffer all head-appends until pending mid-stream insertions resolve. - Accept full re-prefill for mid-stream writes (make this the expensive-but-correct fallback). ### FM-4: Concurrent writers fork the head Two processes read head *C_n* and both publish children. Bus holds a DAG. Serving layer must select one head. Selecting wrong branch = model continues from abandoned timeline. Merging branches = content interleaving that is neither a pure append nor a clean edit. **Requirement:** Per-context single-writer lease. Lease timeout forces explicit conflict resolution, which always triggers full re-prefill of the resolved subtree. ### FM-5: Rollback is not a suffix operation Orchestrator reverts to commit *C_{n-2}*. Head moves backward. The "new suffix" is negative-length. Cache contains KV entries from the abandoned branch beyond the rollback point. **Failure:** Generation continues from stale KV. Or: cache is cleared but the system bills/logs it as a "suffix prefill" (cost accounting lies). **Requirement:** Head-position regression is a distinct event class. Always invalidates cache beyond the target commit. Never routed through the suffix-prefill path. ### FM-6: Cache eviction decouples bus-validity from cache-availability vLLM/PagedAttention evicts blocks under memory pressure. Git-bus still lists anchor *A* as valid. Serving layer lacks the physical KV blocks. **Requirement:** Reference-counting or pinning protocol between bus and serving layer. Bus-validity is necessary but not sufficient. Serving layer must acknowledge residency before the optimization fires. ### FM-7: Non-deterministic prefill defeats value-based verification Same tokens, different batch composition or GPU → different float rounding in KV values. If any component verifies "cache matches" by comparing KV tensors, false negatives cause unnecessary full re-prefills (correct but wasteful) or, worse, false positives from tolerance thresholds (corruption). **Requirement:** Verification is exclusively at the token-ID level. Never compare floating-point KV contents. ### FM-8: Front truncation breaks the foundational assumption Context exceeds window. Oldest turns evicted. Everything before `p` is bit-reused from committed KV. Validation is deterministic; worst case is full recompute. The mechanism is an optimization with a safe fallback — never a correctness dependency. Anchor-validation failures **A1 — Tokenization seam drift (the nastiest one). ** Byte-level diff says block *k+1* is unchanged, but the edit in block *k* changed where token boundaries fall. Block *k* ends `. id=12`, block *k+1* starts `34 rest` → `1234` merges. The anchor at the end of *k+1* is reused; the actual token stream differs from the validated one. **Rule:** every block boundary must be a hard tokenizer boundary *by construction* (special sentinel token, or guaranteed non-mergeable prefix). Assert at anchor time: `tokens(concat(blocks)) == concat(tokens(block_i))`. Cheap, and it kills this class. **A2 — Position-ID drift with content-identical hash. ** Delete a 50-token block at offset 1000. The anchor at offset 4000 has an identical content hash but all its RoPE phases are now wrong by 50. Nothing crashes; output quality degrades subtly and invisibly. **Rule:** an anchor is valid only if `(content_hash, n_tokens_before)` both match. Never assume position-shift tolerance — mainstream RoPE decoders do not grant it. **A3 — Weak or non-canonical hashing. ** Truncated hashes collide; non-canonical serialization (JSON key order, Unicode NFC/NFD, float formatting, embedded timestamps) makes identical contexts hash differently (perf death) or — worse — over-aggressive normalization makes *different* contexts hash identically (silent corruption). **Boundary:** the canonical form hashed must be *exactly* the function applied before tokenization, nothing more, nothing less. **A4 — Cumulative-hash cascade. ** With `H_i = H(H_{i-1} ‖ B_i)`, one edited block invalidates every downstream anchor — correct but destroys reuse granularity. Per-block hashes preserve granularity but you must then independently verify position offsets and structural linkage. Pick one design, document the invalidation cascade it implies. Do not mix. **A5 — Decoder-state leakage through the checkpoint. ** Prefill KV is not the whole state. Constrained-decoding FSM position, grammar stack, sampler state, speculative-draft state all depend on the full emitted token history. Restoring KV without rewinding these to the anchor's recorded state produces divergence. The checkpoint record must capture *every* piece of state that is a function of the prefix. Edit-semantics failures **B1 — Edit lands *before* the last anchor. ** Lazy engines check only the deepest anchor. Validity must be established by walking from the front; the reusable prefix ends at the first failing anchor. **B2 — Deletion of an anchor itself. ** Creates a coordinate hole; all downstream position offsets shift (→ A2), and references *to* that anchor dangle. **Rule:** anchors are referenced by immutable ID, never index; deleted IDs resolve to a loud tombstone, never silently to the successor. **B3 — Insertion exactly at a boundary. ** Needs a deterministic tie-break: insertion at `b_i` belongs to the new suffix (anchor survives). But if the inserted content would tokenize-merge backward into block *k*, the anchor's last token changes — same trap as A1. Insertions at seams must begin with a boundary-forcing element. **B4 — Length-preserving replacement. ** Positions unchanged, content changed. Any cache keyed on `(block_id, n_tokens)` returns garbage. Never key anything on length alone. **B5 — Replay and reordering. ** At-least-once delivery double-applies an edit; out-of-order edits land against shifted coordinates. Requirements: idempotency keys on every edit; every edit carries a base-version CAS token; mismatch ⇒ stash or reject, never blind-apply. **B6 — Concurrent edit during reprefill. ** In-flight KV for a region that the concurrent edit touches must never be committed. KV writes are staged per-segment and atomically linked to the anchor chain only after validating against the version they were computed for. Single writer per context. **B7 — Branch forks. ** Two branches share prefix anchors. Branch B's page eviction must respect refcounts on branch A's shared pages, or switching back finds holes. Merging branches by raw splice is forbidden — the seam is neither a valid token boundary nor a coherent discourse state; merge requires re-summary plus a fresh anchor. Coordinate-layer (memlang/meta-token) failures **C1 — Cross-session KV leak. ** Physical slot freed and reallocated without ownership tags → attention reaches another session's KV. This is the security floor of the whole design: **attention must never reach a slot not owned by the current logical context. ** Ownership tags + refcount-checked reuse, always. **C2 — Virtual-marker misalignment. ** If meta-tokens are stripped before inference, the physical stream differs from the logical one, and every anchor's physical offset must account for stripped markers. Off-by-N grows with context length and manifests as subtly misaligned reuse. The logical↔physical mapping must be total, deterministic, and round-trip asserted in CI. **C3 — ABA address reuse. ** Freelist hands a deleted logical address to a new block; a stale citation resolves to the wrong content. Monotonic allocation or epoch-scoped namespaces; no address reuse within an epoch. **C4 — Model-transcribed addresses. ** The agent itself emits citations (`@blk_47`) and will occasionally hallucinate off-by-one addresses. Resolution policy: tombstone-loud-fail. Never nearest-guess — a guessed resolution poisons the context with confidently wrong grounding. **C5 — Hot-region granularity collapse. ** A scratchpad block rewritten every step, sitting before 7k tokens of static content with 8k-interval anchors: every step invalidates everything downstream. Perf collapse wearing a correctness costume. Anchor placement must be volatility-aware: stable regions get anchors; volatile regions consolidate into one mutable tail segment. Semantic-layer failures **D1 — Byte-valid ≠ semantically valid. ** Hashes prove bytes survived; they say nothing about whether the content is still *true*. Later evidence invalidates the plan; the edit replaces the evidence but keeps the plan; the anchor faithfully preserves something dead. **Hard boundary:** anchors guarantee mechanical consistency, not epistemic validity. There must exist an explicit `mark_dirty` operation that overrides hash validity, and it must be reachable from the agent's reasoning layer. **D2 — Compaction feedback loop. ** Cheap anchors make compaction run more often; each compaction generation compounds compression error. Guards: compaction-depth counter per lineage, hard floor on retained verbatim material, and never compact across an unresolved tool-call/tool-result pairing. **D3 — Torn tool pairs + silent template fixups. ** Edit deletes a tool result but keeps the call. The template serializer silently drops the orphan call → the served token stream differs from the logical context → anchors computed on the logical view validate while the model sees something else. Template well-formedness must be part of anchor computation; malformed states refuse to anchor, loudly. **D4 — Dynamic system-preamble mutation. ** A timestamp injected into the preamble invalidates every anchor, every step. Dynamic system content lives after the last static anchor or in the suffix. This is a placement discipline, not a code fix. **D5 — Cross-binding reuse. ** Checkpoints computed under (model M1, template T1, tokenizer v3, rope scheme R, quant Q) reused under any different binding. Anchor records bind the full tuple; mismatch ⇒ hard invalidate, never soft-warn. **E1 — Interrupted reprefill. ** Crash mid-suffix leaves partial KV. Chunk ledger with WAL, aligned to anchor boundaries; resume skips nothing and duplicates nothing. Duplicated chunks get attended twice; skipped chunks are missing — both silent. **E2 — Mixed KV provenance. ** Fresh-computed fp16 mixed with quantized-resident or paged-out-restored KV inside one reused span. Either pin unquantized storage for anchored spans, or record provenance per span and honor the weakest class. Silent mixing is forbidden. **E3 — Speculative-decode desync. ** The draft model's own anchor chain must invalidate in lockstep with the target's. Desync = permanently rejected drafts (silent perf death) or acceptance against stale draft context. **E4 — Degenerate inputs. ** Empty context, edit at offset 0, context shorter than one anchor interval, first-ever call. First-class tested paths, not exception handlers. ## Hard boundaries — what the guarantee does *not* cover **Semantic continued validity** of preserved content (D1). **Any binding change**: model, template, tokenizer, RoPE scheme, quantization. **Quality stability** when reused KV passed through lossy transforms (E2). **Sub-anchor granularity**: everything after the first invalidated anchor is recomputed wholesale, even if individually unchanged. **Suffix-sufficiency for global consumers**: the premise rests on causal left-to-right attention. Any component scanning the whole prompt (bidirectional encoders, global logit processors) breaks it. Enumerate consumers and their directionality; assume nothing. **Adversarial scatter**: edits touching every block reduce validation to full re-serialization. Bounded by full recompute — acceptable, and it must degrade gracefully, not fail. ## What must NEVER happen Attention reaching a KV slot not owned by the current logical context. (Cross-session leak. Partial-match reuse — "hash matched, positions shifted, close enough. " All four validity dimensions match or the anchor is dead. Silent fallback or silent approximation on any validation failure. Downgrade loudly, take the slow path, emit the reason. Errors here manifest as degraded reasoning — invisible to tests that only check "did it run. Logical address reuse within an epoch (ABA). Any divergence between the served token stream and the canonical serialization of the logical context. No hidden fixups, no silent orphan-drop. Round-trip equality asserted in CI. Non-idempotent edit application. Partially prefilled suffix visible to decoding. Stage-then-link, atomic commit. Anchors at token-merge-capable seams. Optimizer choosing reuse probabilistically. Validity is deterministic; no "probably unchanged, skip the check. Silent remap of dangling references. Without that histogram, every failure mode above surfaces as "the model got dumber" with no trace — which is the true worst-case outcome of this entire design. The user is asking about a hard problem in agent context management: "semantic-anchor checkpoints so an agent's context edit re-prefills only the new suffix, in the memlang / meta-token coordinate layer. Let me parse what this means. This is about a system where: An agent has a context (conversation history, working memory). The context gets edited — e. , compaction, summarization, tool-result eviction, rewriting of earlier turns. Instead of re-sending the entire context to the model on the next call (which would break KV-cache prefix reuse and cost tokens), you want to checkpoint "semantic anchors" — stable positions in the token stream — such that when the context is edited, only the *new suffix* after the last anchor needs to be re-prefilled. Think of it like virtual memory for LLM context: logical token IDs → physical KV-cache slots. So the architecture: the context is a sequence of segments. Keying requirement: anchor records must bind (model_id, template_version, tokenizer_version, rope_scheme, quantization scheme); mismatch ⇒ hard invalidate, never soft-warn. What must NEVER happen (invariants) Compile the hard list: Attention must never reach a KV slot not owned by the current logical context (no cross-session/cross-branch leakage). Physical reuse requires ownership tags + refcounts; free-then-realloc without tag check is forbidden. Fix: well-formedness assertion inside anchor computation. Example E (hot scratchpad): Scratchpad block rewritten each step at offset just after system prompt; anchors exist at 8k intervals; every step invalidates ~7. 5k tokens of otherwise-static content. Edit at offset 0. Context shorter than one anchor interval. First-ever call (no anchors). These must be first-class tested paths, not exceptions. **FM27 — metrics/observability blind spot:** if you don't emit reuse-rate and invalidation-reason counters, the failure modes above surface as "model got dumber" with no trace.
